children.text:
amarakośa evaṃ nāmaliṅgānuśāsanaṃ khāṇḍa 1
nāmaliṅgānuśāsanaṃ nāma amarakoṣaḥ
prathamaṃ kāṇḍam|
maṅgalācaraṇam|
children.translated_text:
<s>Amarakośa</s>, also known as <s>Nāmaliṅgānuśāsana</s> (Instruction on Names and Genders), Book 1.
<s>Nāmaliṅgānuśāsana</s>, called the <s>Amarakośa</s>.
First Section.
Auspicious Invocation.

children.text:
(1.0.1) yasya jñānadayāsindhoragādhasyānaghā guṇāḥ
(1.0.2) sevyatāmakṣayo dhīrāḥ sa śriye cāmṛtāya ca
children.translated_text:
(1.0.1) He whose faultless qualities are [like] an unfathomable ocean of knowledge and compassion —
(1.0.2) O wise ones, resort to that imperishable [one], for prosperity and for immortality.
Introduction.

(1.0.3) Having compiled other treatises, with concise and refined
(1.0.4) sections, the <s>Nāmaliṅgānuśāsana</s> (Instruction on Names and Genders) is stated completely.
Definitions and conventions.

children.text:
(1.0.5) prāyaśo rūpabhedena sāhacaryācca kutracit
(1.0.6) strīpuṃnapuṃsakaṃ jñeyaṃ tadviśeṣavidheḥ kvacit
(1.0.7) bhedākhyānāya na dvandvo naikaśeṣo na saṃkaraḥ
(1.0.8) kṛto 'tra bhinnaliṅgānāmanuktānāṃ kramādṛte
(1.0.9) triliṅgyāṃ triṣviti padaṃ mithune tu dvayoriti
(1.0.10) niṣiddhaliṅgaṃ śeṣārthaṃ tvantāthādi na pūrvabhāk
children.translated_text:
(1.0.5) The gender — feminine, masculine, or neuter — should generally be known from the form of the word or from association;
(1.0.6) and in some cases from the specific rule regarding it.
(1.0.7) For the purpose of distinguishing [genders], no <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound), no <s>ekaśeṣa</s> (single-remainder), and no intermixing
(1.0.8) has been made here for words of different gender that are not mentioned, except in sequence.
(1.0.9) In the case of three-gendered [words], the word 'in three [genders]' [is used]; in the case of a pair, 'in two.'
(1.0.10) The forbidden gender [serves] for the remaining meaning; [a word ending in] -<s>tu</s>, -<s>atha</s>, etc. does not belong to the preceding [entry].
Section on Heaven (<s>Svargavarga</s>).

children.text:
##Heaven 9##
(1.1.11) svaravyayaṃ svarganākatridivatridaśālayāḥ
(1.1.12) suraloko dyodivau dve striyāṃ klībe triviṣṭapam
children.translated_text:
[Heaven — 9 synonyms]
(1.1.11) <s>Svara</s> (indeclinable), <s>Svarga</s>, <s>Nāka</s>, <s>Tridiva</s>, <s>Tridaśālaya</s> (abode of the thirty [gods]),
(1.1.12) <s>Suraloka</s> (world of gods), <s>Dyo</s>, <s>Div</s> — the [last] two are feminine; in the neuter, <s>Triviṣṭapa</s>.

children.text:
##Deities 26##
(1.1.13) amarā nirjarā devāstridaśā vibudhāḥ surāḥ
(1.1.14) suparvāṇaḥ sumanasastridiveśā divaukasaḥ
(1.1.15) āditeyā diviṣado lekhā aditinandanāḥ
(1.1.16) ādityā ṛbhavo 'svapnā amartyā amṛtāndhasaḥ
(1.1.17) barhirmukhāḥ ṛtubhujo gīrvāṇā dānavārayaḥ
(1.1.18) vṛndārakā daivatāni puṃsi vā devatāḥ striyām
children.translated_text:
[Deities — 26 synonyms]
(1.1.13) <s>Amara</s> (immortal), <s>Nirjara</s> (ageless), <s>Deva</s>, <s>Tridaśa</s> (thirty), <s>Vibudha</s> (wise), <s>Sura</s>,
(1.1.14) <s>Suparvan</s>, <s>Sumanas</s> (good-minded), <s>Tridiveśa</s> (lords of the triple heaven), <s>Divaukas</s> (heaven-dwellers),
(1.1.15) <s>Āditya</s> (sons of Aditi), <s>Diviṣad</s> (heaven-seated), <s>Lekha</s>, <s>Aditinandana</s> (Aditi's children),
(1.1.16) <s>Āditya</s>, <s>Ṛbhu</s>, <s>Asvapna</s> (sleepless), <s>Amartya</s> (immortal), <s>Amṛtāndhas</s> (nectar-fed),
(1.1.17) <s>Barhirmukha</s> (having mouths toward the sacrificial grass), <s>Ṛtubhuj</s> (season-enjoyers), <s>Gīrvāṇa</s>, <s>Dānavāri</s> (foes of the Dānavas),
(1.1.18) <s>Vṛndāraka</s>; <s>Daivatāni</s> (neuter); in masculine or feminine, <s>Devatā</s>.

children.text:
##Some clans of deities ##
(1.1.19) ādityaviśvavasavastuṣitābhāsvarānilāḥ
(1.1.20) mahārājikasādhyāśca rudrāśca gaṇadevatāḥ
children.translated_text:
[Some clans of deities]
(1.1.19) <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Viśvas</s>, <s>Vasus</s>, <s>Tuṣitas</s>, <s>Ābhāsvaras</s>, <s>Anilas</s>,
(1.1.20) <s>Mahārājikas</s>, <s>Sādhyas</s>, and <s>Rudras</s> — these are the classes of deities (<s>gaṇadevatā</s>).

children.text:
##Some demigods ##
(1.1.21) vidyādharāpsaroyakṣarakṣogandharvakiṃnarāḥ
(1.1.22) piśāco guhyakaḥ siddho bhūto 'mī devayonayaḥ
children.translated_text:
[Some demigods]
(1.1.21) <s>Vidyādharas</s>, <s>Apsaras</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Kiṃnaras</s>,
(1.1.22) <s>Piśāca</s>, <s>Guhyaka</s>, <s>Siddha</s>, <s>Bhūta</s> — these are the semi-divine beings (<s>devayoni</s>).

children.text:
##Antigods or titans 10##
(1.1.23) asurā daityadaiteyadanujendrāridānavāḥ
(1.1.24) śukraśiṣyā ditisutāḥ pūrvadevāḥ suradviṣaḥ
children.translated_text:
[Antigods or Titans — 10 synonyms]
(1.1.23) <s>Asura</s>, <s>Daitya</s>, <s>Daiteya</s>, <s>Danuja</s>, <s>Indrāri</s> (foe of Indra), <s>Dānava</s>,
(1.1.24) <s>Śukraśiṣya</s> (pupil of Śukra), <s>Ditisuta</s> (son of Diti), <s>Pūrvadeva</s> (former god), <s>Suradviṣ</s> (hater of gods).

children.text:
##Jina or Buddha 18##
(1.1.25) sarvajñaḥ sugataḥ buddho dharmarājastathāgataḥ
(1.1.26) samantabhadro bhagavānmārajillokajijjinaḥ
(1.1.27) ṣaḍabhijño daśabalo 'dvayavādī vināyakaḥ
(1.1.28) munīndraḥ śrīghanaḥ śāstā muniḥ śākyamunistu yaḥ
children.translated_text:
[<s>Jina</s> or <s>Buddha</s> — 18 synonyms]
(1.1.25) <s>Sarvajña</s> (omniscient), <s>Sugata</s> (well-gone), <s>Buddha</s> (awakened), <s>Dharmarāja</s> (king of dharma), <s>Tathāgata</s>,
(1.1.26) <s>Samantabhadra</s> (universally auspicious), <s>Bhagavān</s> (blessed one), <s>Mārajit</s> (conqueror of Māra), <s>Lokajit</s> (conqueror of the world),
(1.1.27) <s>Jinaḥ</s> (conqueror), <s>Ṣaḍabhijña</s> (possessing six super-knowledges), <s>Daśabala</s> (having ten powers), <s>Advayavādī</s> (teacher of non-duality),
(1.1.28) <s>Vināyaka</s> (remover [of obstacles]), <s>Munīndra</s> (lord of sages), <s>Śāstā</s> (teacher), <s>Muni</s> (sage), <s>Śākyamuni</s>.

children.text:
##Gautama Buddha 7##
(1.1.29) sa śākyasiṃhaḥ sarvārthasiddhaḥ śauddhodaniśca saḥ
(1.1.30) gautamaścārkabandhuśca māyādevīsutaśca saḥ

## Brahma 29 ##
(1.1.31) brahmātmabhūḥ surajyeṣṭhaḥ parameṣṭhī pitāmahaḥ
(1.1.32) hiraṇyagarbho lokeśaḥ svayaṃbhūścaturānanaḥ
(1.1.33) dhātābjayonirdruhiṇo viriñciḥ kamalāsanaḥ
(1.1.34) sraṣṭā prajāpatirvedhā vidhātā viśvasṛgvidhiḥ
(1.1.35) nābhijanmāṇḍajaḥ pūrvo nidhanaḥ kamalodbhavaḥ
(1.1.36) sadānando rajomūrtiḥ satyako haṃsavāhanaḥ
children.translated_text:
[<s>Brahmā</s> — 29 synonyms]
(1.1.31) <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Ātmabhū</s> (self-born), <s>Surajyeṣṭha</s> (eldest of gods), <s>Parameṣṭhī</s>, <s>Pitāmaha</s> (grandfather),
(1.1.32) <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> (golden embryo), <s>Lokeśa</s> (lord of worlds), <s>Svayambhū</s> (self-existent), <s>Caturānana</s> (four-faced), and others.

children.text:
## Vishnu 46 ##
(1.1.37) viṣṇurnārāyaṇaḥ kṛṣṇo vaikuṇṭho viṣṭaraśravāḥ
(1.1.38) dāmodaro hṛṣīkeśaḥ keśavo mādhavaḥ svabhūḥ
(1.1.39) daityāriḥ puṇḍarīkākṣo govindo garuḍadhvajaḥ
(1.1.40) pītāmbaro 'cyutaḥ śārṅgī viṣvakseno janārdanaḥ
(1.1.41) upendra indrāvarajaścakrapāṇiścaturbhujaḥ
(1.1.42) padmanābho madhuripurvāsudevastrivikramaḥ
(1.1.43) devakīnandanaḥ śauriḥ śrīpatiḥ puruṣottamaḥ
(1.1.44) vanamālī balidhvaṃsī kaṃsārātiradhokṣajaḥ
(1.1.45) viśvambharaḥ kaiṭabhajidvidhuḥ śrīvatsalāñchanaḥ
(1.1.46) purāṇapuruṣo yajñapuruṣo narakāntakaḥ
(1.1.47) jalaśāyī viśvarūpo mukundo muramardanaḥ
children.translated_text:
[<s>Viṣṇu</s> — 46 synonyms]
(1.1.37) <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, <s>Viṣṭaraśravas</s>,
(1.1.38) <s>Dāmodara</s>, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, <s>Keśava</s>, <s>Mādhava</s>, <s>Svabhū</s>, and others.

children.text:
## Vasudeva: Krishna's Father 2 ##
(1.1.48) vasudevo 'sya janakaḥ sa evānakadundubhiḥ
children.translated_text:
[<s>Vasudeva</s>: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s father — 2 synonyms]
(1.1.48) <s>Vasudeva</s> is his father; he is also [called] <s>Ānakadundubhi</s>.

children.text:
## Balarama 17 ##
(1.1.49) balabhadraḥ pralambaghno baladevo 'cyutāgrajaḥ
(1.1.50) revatīramaṇo rāmaḥ kāmapālo halāyudhaḥ
(1.1.51) nīlāmbaro rauhiṇeyastālāṅko musalī halī
(1.1.52) saṃkarṣaṇaḥ sīrapāṇiḥ kālindībhedano balaḥ
children.translated_text:
[<s>Balarāma</s> — 17 synonyms]
(1.1.49) <s>Balabhadra</s>, <s>Pralambhaghna</s> (slayer of Pralamba), <s>Baladeva</s>, <s>Acyutāgraja</s> (elder brother of Acyuta),
(1.1.50) <s>Revatīramaṇa</s> (lover of Revatī), <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Kāmapāla</s>, <s>Halāyudha</s> (plough-weaponed), and others.

children.text:
## Kamadeva: Eros 19 ##
(1.1.53) madano manmatho māraḥ pradyumno mīnaketanaḥ
(1.1.54) kandarpo darpako 'naṅgaḥ kāmaḥ pañcaśaraḥ smaraḥ
(1.1.55) śambarārirmanasijaḥ kusumeṣurananyajaḥ
(1.1.56) puṣpadhanvā ratipatirmakaradhvaja ātmabhūḥ
children.translated_text:
[<s>Kāmadeva</s>: god of love — 19 synonyms]
(1.1.53) <s>Madana</s>, <s>Manmatha</s>, <s>Māra</s>, <s>Pradyumna</s>, <s>Mīnaketana</s> (fish-bannered),
(1.1.54) <s>Kandarpa</s>, <s>Darpaka</s>, <s>Anaṅga</s> (bodiless), <s>Kāma</s>, <s>Pañcaśara</s> (five-arrowed), and others.

children.text:
## Five floral Arrows of Kamadeva ##
(1.1.57) aravindamaśokaṃ ca cūtaṃ ca navamallikā
(1.1.58) nīlotpalaṃ ca pañcaite pañcabāṇasya sāyakāḥ
children.translated_text:
[Five floral arrows of <s>Kāmadeva</s>]
(1.1.57) Lotus (<s>aravinda</s>), <s>aśoka</s>,
(1.1.58) mango (<s>cūta</s>), jasmine (<s>navamallikā</s>), and blue lotus (<s>nīlotpala</s>) — these five are the arrows of <s>Puṣpadhanus</s> (the Flower-Bowed One).

children.text:
## Five physical arrows of Kamadeva ##
(1.1.59) unmādanastāpanaśca śoṣaṇaḥ stambhanastathā
(1.1.60) saṃmohanaśca kāmaśca pañca bāṇāḥ prakīrtitāḥ
children.translated_text:
[Five physical arrows of <s>Kāmadeva</s>]
(1.1.59) <s>Unmādana</s> (maddening), <s>Tāpana</s> (heating), <s>Śoṣaṇa</s> (desiccating), <s>Stambhana</s> (paralyzing),
(1.1.60) and <s>Saṃmohana</s> (bewildering) — these are the [five] arrows of <s>Kāma</s>.

children.text:
## Son of kamadeva 4 ##
(1.1.61) brahmasūrviśvaketuḥ syādaniruddha uṣāpatiḥ
children.translated_text:
[Son of <s>Kāmadeva</s> — 4 synonyms]
(1.1.61) <s>Brahmasū</s>, <s>Viśvaketu</s>; [his son is] <s>Aniruddha</s>, husband of <s>Ūṣā</s>.

children.text:
## Laxmi 14 ##
(1.1.62) lakṣmīḥ padmālayā padmā kamalā śrīrharipriyā
(1.1.63) indirā lokamātā mā kṣīrodatanayā ramā
(1.1.64) bhārgavī lokajananī kṣīrasāgarakanyakā
children.translated_text:
[<s>Lakṣmī</s> — 14 synonyms]
(1.1.62) <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Padmālayā</s> (lotus-dwelling), <s>Padmā</s>, <s>Kamalā</s>, <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Haripriyā</s> (beloved of Hari),
(1.1.63) <s>Indirā</s>, <s>Lokamātā</s> (mother of the world), <s>Mā</s>, <s>Kṣīrodatanayā</s> (daughter of the Milk-Ocean), <s>Ramā</s>, and others.

children.text:
## Krishna's equipment: conch, discus, mace, sword,jewel ##
(1.1.65) śaṅkho lakṣmīpateḥ pāñcajanyaścakraṃ sudarśanaḥ
(1.1.66) kaumodakī gadā khaḍgo nandakaḥ kaustubho maṇiḥ
children.translated_text:
[<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s equipment: conch, discus, mace, sword, jewel]
(1.1.65) The conch of <s>Lakṣmīpati</s> (husband of Lakṣmī) is <s>Pāñcajanya</s>; the discus is <s>Sudarśana</s>; and others.

children.text:
## Krishna's bow, mark, horses(4) ##
(1.1.67) cāpaḥ śārṅgaṃ murārestu śrīvatso lāñchanaṃ smṛtam
(1.1.68) aśvāśca śaivyasugrīvameghapuṣpabalāhakāḥ

## Krishna's charioteer, minister, younger brother ##
(1.1.69) sārathirdāruko mantrī hyuddhavaścānujo gadaḥ
children.translated_text:
[<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s charioteer, minister, younger brother]
(1.1.69) The charioteer is <s>Dāruka</s>; the minister is <s>Uddhava</s>; and the younger brother is <s>Gada</s>.

children.text:
## Garuda: Krishna's vehicle 9 ##
(1.1.70) garutmāngaruḍastārkṣyo vainateyaḥ khageśvaraḥ
(1.1.71) nāgāntako viṣṇurathaḥ suparṇaḥ pannagāśanaḥ
children.translated_text:
[<s>Garuḍa</s>: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s vehicle — 9 synonyms]
(1.1.70) <s>Garutmān</s>, <s>Garuḍa</s>, <s>Tārkṣya</s>, <s>Vainateya</s>, <s>Khageśvara</s> (lord of birds),
(1.1.71) <s>Nāgāntaka</s> (serpent-destroyer), <s>Viṣṇuratha</s> (vehicle of Viṣṇu), and others.

children.text:
## Shiva 52 ##
(1.1.72) śambhurīśaḥ paśupatiḥ śivaḥ śūlī maheśvaraḥ
(1.1.73) īśvaraḥ śarva īśānaḥ śaṃkaraścandraśekharaḥ
(1.1.74) bhūteśaḥ khaṇḍaparaśurgirīśo giriśo mṛḍaḥ
(1.1.75) mṛtyuñjayaḥ kṛttivāsāḥ pinākī pramathādhipaḥ
(1.1.76) ugraḥ kapardī śrīkaṇṭhaḥ śitikaṇṭhaḥ kapālabhṛt
(1.1.77) vāmadevo mahādevo virūpākṣastrilocanaḥ
(1.1.78) kṛśānuretāḥ sarvajño dhūrjaṭirnīlalohitaḥ
(1.1.79) haraḥ smaraharo bhargastryambakastripurāntakaḥ
(1.1.80) gaṅgādharo 'ndhakaripuḥ kratudhvaṃsī vṛṣadhvajaḥ
(1.1.81) vyomakeśo bhavo bhīmaḥ sthāṇū rudra umāpatiḥ
(1.1.82) ahirbudhnyo 'ṣṭamūrtiśca gajāriśca mahānaṭaḥ
children.translated_text:
[<s>Śiva</s> — 52 synonyms]
(1.1.72) <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Paśupati</s> (lord of creatures), <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śūlī</s> (trident-bearer), <s>Maheśvara</s>,
(1.1.73) <s>Īśvara</s>, <s>Śarva</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, <s>Candraśekhara</s> (moon-crested), and others.

children.text:
## Shiva's braided hair, bow, attendants, divine mothers ##
(1.1.83) kapardo 'sya jaṭājūṭaḥ pināko 'jagavaṃ dhanuḥ
(1.1.84) pramathā: syuḥ pāriṣadā brāhmītyādyāstu mātaraḥ
children.translated_text:
[<s>Śiva</s>'s braided hair, bow, attendants, divine mothers]
(1.1.83) His matted hair is <s>Kaparda</s> or <s>Jaṭājūṭa</s>; [his] bow is <s>Pināka</s> or <s>Ajagava</s>; and others.

[<s>Śiva</s>'s powers/glory — 3 synonyms]
(1.1.85) <s>Vibhūti</s>, <s>Bhūti</s>, <s>Aiśvarya</s> (lordly power) — beginning with <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness), [the powers] are eightfold.

children.text:
## Eight Yogic achievements granted by Shiva ##
(1.1.86) aṇimā mahimā caiva garimā laghimā tathā
(1.1.87) prāptiḥ prākāmyamīśitvaṃ vaśitvaṃ cāṣṭa siddhayaḥ
children.translated_text:
[Eight yogic powers (<s>siddhis</s>) granted by <s>Śiva</s>]
(1.1.86) <s>Aṇimā</s> (becoming minute), <s>Mahimā</s> (becoming great), <s>Garimā</s> (becoming heavy), <s>Laghimā</s> (becoming light),
(1.1.87) <s>Prāpti</s> (obtaining anything), <s>Prākāmya</s> (fulfilling desires), and others.

children.text:
## Shiva's wife Parvati 23 ##
(1.1.88) umā kātyāyanī gaurī kālī haimavatīśvarī
(1.1.89) śivā bhavānī rudrāṇī śarvāṇī sarvamaṅgalā
(1.1.90) aparṇā pārvatī durgā mṛḍānī caṇḍikāmbikā
(1.1.91) āryā dākṣāyaṇī caiva girijā menakātmajā
(1.1.92) karmamoṭī tu cāmuṇḍā carmamuṇḍā tu carcikā
## Shiva's son Ganapati 8 ##
(1.1.93) vināyako vighnarājadvaimāturagaṇādhipāḥ
(1.1.94) apyekadantaherambalambodaragajānanāḥ
children.translated_text:
[<s>Śiva</s>'s wife <s>Pārvatī</s> — 23 synonyms]
(1.1.88) <s>Umā</s>, <s>Kātyāyanī</s>, <s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Kālī</s>, <s>Haimavatī</s> (daughter of the Himālaya), <s>Īśvarī</s>,

children.translated_text:

(1.1.119) <s>Santāna</s>, <s>Kalpavṛkṣa</s> (wish-fulfilling tree), and <s>Haricandana</s> (masculine or neuter).

children.text:

(1.1.121) nāsatyāvaśvinau dasrāvāśvineyau ca tāvubhau

children.translated_text:

(1.1.120) <s>Sanatkumāra</s> and <s>Vaidhātra</s>; the celestial physicians are <s>Aśvinīsuta</s> (sons of the Aśvinī); and others.

children.text:
## Divine musicians (2), Fire (34), Marine fire (3) ##
(1.1.123) hāhā hūhūścaivamādyā gandharvāstridivaukasām
(1.1.124) agnirvaiśvānaro vahnirvītihotro dhanañjayaḥ
(1.1.125) kṛpīṭayonirjvalano jātavedāstanūnapāt
(1.1.126) barhiḥ śuṣmā kṛṣṇavartmā śociṣkeśa uparbudhaḥ
(1.1.127) āśrayāśo bṛhadbhānuḥ kṛśānuḥ pāvako 'nalaḥ
(1.1.128) rohitāśvo vāyusakhaḥ śikhāvānāśuśukṣaṇiḥ
(1.1.129) hiraṇyaretā hutabhug dahano havyavāhanaḥ
(1.1.130) saptārcirdamunāḥ śukraścitrabhānurvibhāvasuḥ
(1.1.131) śucirappittamaurvastu vāḍavo vaḍavānalaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Divine musicians (2), Fire (34), Marine fire (3) ##
(1.1.123) <s>Hāhā</s> and <s>Hūhū</s> — such are the foremost <s>Gandharvas</s> (divine musicians) of the heaven-dwellers.
(1.1.124) <s>Agni</s> (fire) [is also called]: <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, <s>Vahni</s>, <s>Vītihotra</s>, <s>Dhanañjaya</s>,
(1.1.125) <s>Kṛpīṭayoni</s> (born from the fire-pit), <s>Jvalana</s> (the blazing one), <s>Jātavedas</s> (knower of all beings), <s>Tanūnapāt</s> (protector of the body),
(1.1.126) <s>Barhiḥ</s> (the sacred grass [fire]), <s>Śuṣma</s> (the scorching one), <s>Kṛṣṇavartma</s> (black-pathed), <s>Śociṣkeśa</s> (flame-haired), <s>Uṣarbudha</s> (dawn-awaking),
(1.1.127) <s>Āśrayāśa</s> (consumer of dwellings), <s>Bṛhadbhānu</s> (great-rayed), <s>Kṛśānu</s> (the emaciated one), <s>Pāvaka</s> (the purifier), <s>Anala</s> (the insatiable),
(1.1.128) <s>Rohitāśva</s> (red-horsed), <s>Vāyusakha</s> (friend of the wind), <s>Śikhāvān</s> (crested), <s>Āśuśukṣaṇi</s> (quickly drying),
(1.1.129) <s>Hiraṇyareta</s> (golden-seed), <s>Hutabhuj</s> (oblation-eater), <s>Dahana</s> (the burner), <s>Havyavāhana</s> (carrier of offerings),
(1.1.130) <s>Saptārci</s> (seven-flamed), <s>Damunā</s>, <s>Śukra</s> (the bright), <s>Citrabhānu</s> (of wondrous radiance), <s>Vibhāvasu</s> (the luminous),
(1.1.131) <s>Śuci</s> (the pure), <s>Appitta</s>. But <s>Maurva</s> [fire] is [called] <s>Vāḍava</s> (submarine fire) [or] <s>Vaḍavānala</s> (the mare-fire).

children.text:

children.translated_text:
## Flame (5), Spark (2), Burn (2) ##

(1.1.133) <s>Sphuliṅga</s> (spark) and <s>agnikaṇa</s> (fire-particle) are used in all three genders. <s>Saṃtāpa</s> (burning heat) and <s>saṃjvara</s> (feverish heat) are synonymous.

## Yama: god of death (14) ##
(1.1.136) dharmarājaḥ pitṛpatiḥ samavartī paretarāṭ
(1.1.137) kṛtānto yamunābhrātā śamano yamarāḍ yamaḥ
(1.1.138) kālo daṇḍadharaḥ śrāddhadevo vaivasvato 'ntakaḥ
(1.1.139) rākṣasaḥ koṇapaḥ kravyāt krvyādo 'srapa āśaraḥ
children.translated_text:
## <s>Yama</s>: god of death (14) ##
(1.1.136) <s>Dharmarāja</s> (king of dharma), <s>Pitṛpati</s> (lord of the ancestors), <s>Samavartī</s> (the impartial), <s>Paretarāṭ</s> (king of the dead),
(1.1.137) <s>Kṛtānta</s> (the end-maker), <s>Yamunābhrātā</s> (brother of <s>Yamunā</s>), <s>Śamana</s> (the restrainer), <s>Yamarāṭ</s>, <s>Yama</s>,
(1.1.138) <s>Kāla</s> (time/death), <s>Daṇḍadhara</s> (staff-bearer), <s>Śrāddhadeva</s> (god of funeral rites), <s>Vaivasvata</s> (son of <s>Vivasvat</s>), <s>Antaka</s> (the ender).
(1.1.139) <s>Rākṣasa</s> (demon) [is also called]: <s>Koṇapa</s> (skull-drinker), <s>Kravyāt</s> (flesh-eater), <s>Kravyāda</s> (raw-flesh-eater), <s>Asrapa</s> (blood-drinker), <s>Āśara</s> (swift-mover).

children.translated_text:
## Giant, demon (15) ##
(1.1.140) <s>Rātriñcara</s> (night-rover), <s>Rātricara</s> (night-wanderer), <s>Karbura</s> (dappled), <s>Nikaṣātmaja</s> (born of <s>Nikaṣā</s>),
(1.1.141) <s>Yātudhāna</s> (sorcerer), <s>Puṇyajana</s> (holy folk — euphemistic), <s>Nairṛta</s> (belonging to <s>Nirṛti</s>), <s>Yātu</s>. <s>Rakṣasī</s> is the feminine.

children.translated_text:
## <s>Varuṇa</s>: god of the sea (5) ##
(1.1.142) <s>Pracetā</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Pāśī</s> (noose-bearer), <s>Yādasāṃpati</s> (lord of aquatic creatures), <s>Appati</s> (lord of waters).

children.text:

(1.1.145) samīramārutamarut jagatprāṇasamīraṇāḥ
(1.1.146) nabhasvadvātapavanapavamānaprabhañjanāḥ
children.translated_text:
## <s>Vāyu</s>: (god of the) wind (20) ##
(1.1.143) <s>Śvasana</s> (the breather), <s>Sparśana</s> (the toucher), <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Mātariśvā</s>, <s>Sadāgati</s> (ever-moving),
(1.1.144) <s>Pṛṣadaśva</s> (dapple-horsed), <s>Gandhavaha</s> (scent-carrier), <s>Gandhavāha</s>, <s>Anila</s>, <s>Āśuga</s> (swift-goer),
(1.1.145) <s>Samīra</s>, <s>Māruta</s>, <s>Marut</s>, <s>Jagatprāṇa</s> (life-breath of the world), <s>Samīraṇa</s>,
(1.1.146) <s>Nabhasvat</s> (sky-born), <s>Vāta</s>, <s>Pavana</s> (the purifier), <s>Pavamāna</s> (the purifying), <s>Prabhañjana</s> (the smasher).

children.text:
## Whirlwind, storm ##
(1.1.147) prakampano mahāvāto jhañjhāvātaḥ savṛṣṭikaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Whirlwind, storm ##
(1.1.147) <s>Prakampana</s> (the shaker) is a great wind. <s>Jhañjhāvāta</s> (whirlwind) is [a wind] accompanied by rain.

children.text:
## Five bodily winds in Ayurvedic classification, speed (5) ##
(1.1.148) prāṇo 'pānaḥ samānaścodānavyānau ca vāyavaḥ
(1.1.149) śarīrasthā ime raṃhastarasī tu rayaḥ syadaḥ
(1.1.150) javo 'tha śīghraṃ tvaritaṃ laghu kṣipramaraṃ drutam
children.translated_text:
## Five bodily winds in Āyurvedic classification, speed (5) ##
(1.1.148) <s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Apāna</s>, <s>Samāna</s>, <s>Udāna</s>, and <s>Vyāna</s> — these are the [five] winds
(1.1.149) dwelling in the body. <s>Raṃhas</s> and <s>tarasī</s> [mean speed]; also <s>raya</s> and <s>syada</s>.
(1.1.150) <s>Java</s> [also means speed]. Now, <s>śīghra</s>, <s>tvarita</s>, <s>laghu</s>, <s>kṣipra</s>, <s>ara</s>, <s>druta</s> [all mean 'quickly'],

## Quickly (11) ##
(1.1.151) <s>satvara</s>, <s>capala</s>, <s>tūrṇa</s>, <s>avilambita</s>, and <s>āśu</s> also [mean 'quickly'].

children.text:
## Eternal (9), Excessive (14) ##
(1.1.152) satate 'nāratāśrāntasaṃtatāviratāniśam
(1.1.153) nityānavaratājasramapyathātiśayo bharaḥ
(1.1.154) ativelabhṛśātyarthātimātrodgāḍhanirbharam
(1.1.155) tīvraikāntanitāntāni gāḍhabāḍhadṛḍhāni ca
(1.1.156) klībe śīghrādyasattve syāt triṣveṣāṃ sattvagāmi yat
children.translated_text:
## Eternal (9), Excessive (14) ##
(1.1.152) In [the sense of] 'continuous': <s>anārata</s>, <s>aśrānta</s>, <s>saṃtata</s>, <s>avirata</s>, <s>aniśam</s>,
(1.1.153) <s>nitya</s>, <s>anavarata</s>, <s>ajasram</s> also. Now, in [the sense of] 'excessiveness': <s>atibhara</s>,
(1.1.154) <s>ativela</s>, <s>bhṛśa</s>, <s>atyartha</s>, <s>atimātra</s>, <s>udgāḍha</s>, <s>nirbharam</s>,
(1.1.155) <s>tīvra</s>, <s>ekānta</s>, <s>nitānta</s> — [these] as well as <s>gāḍha</s>, <s>bāḍha</s>, and <s>dṛḍha</s>.
(1.1.156) [When used as adverbs,] the neuter [form is used]. <s>Śīghra</s> and the rest [take neuter] when [used] without reference to a being. In all three genders, that which pertains to a being [takes the appropriate gender].

children.translated_text:
## <s>Kubera</s>: god of wealth (17) ##
(1.1.157) <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Tryambakasakha</s> (friend of <s>Śiva</s>), <s>Yakṣarāṭ</s> (king of <s>Yakṣas</s>), <s>Guhyakeśvara</s> (lord of <s>Guhyakas</s>),
(1.1.158) <s>Manuṣyadharmā</s> (of human nature), <s>Dhanada</s> (wealth-giver), <s>Rājarāja</s> (king of kings), <s>Dhanādhipa</s> (lord of wealth),
(1.1.159) <s>Kinnareśa</s> (lord of <s>Kinnaras</s>), <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (son of <s>Viśravas</s>), <s>Paulastya</s> (descendant of <s>Pulastya</s>), <s>Naravāhana</s> (man-vehicled),

children.text:
## Kubera's garden, son, place, city, attendants (4) ##

(1.1.162) kailāsaḥ sthānamalakā pūrvimānaṃ tu puṣpakam

children.translated_text:
## <s>Kubera's</s> garden, son, place, city, attendants (4) ##

(1.1.163) A <s>Kinnara</s> is [also called] <s>Kimpuruṣa</s> (is-he-a-man?) — having a horse-like face; also <s>Mayu</s>.

children.text:

(1.1.166) <s>Mukunda</s>, <s>Kunda</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, and <s>Kharva</s> — these are the nine treasures.
[End of] the Sky Section (<s>Vyomavarga</s>).

(1.2.170) vihāsayo 'pi nāko 'pi dyurapi syāt tadavyam
(1.2.171) tārāpatho 'ntarikṣaṃ ca meghādhvā ca mahābilam
(1.2.172) vihāyāḥ śakune puṃsi gagane puṃnapuṃsakam
children.translated_text:
## Sky or atmosphere (26) ##
(1.2.167) <s>Dyo</s> and <s>div</s> are two [words for sky], feminine. <s>Abhra</s>, <s>vyoma</s>, <s>puṣkara</s>, <s>ambara</s>,
(1.2.168) <s>nabhas</s>, <s>antarikṣa</s>, <s>gagana</s>, <s>ananta</s>, <s>suravartma</s> (path of the gods), <s>kha</s>,
(1.2.169) <s>viyat</s>, <s>viṣṇupada</s> (step of <s>Viṣṇu</s>) — or [the last two may be] masculine. <s>Ākāśa</s> and <s>vihāyasī</s>,
(1.2.170) <s>vihāyasa</s> also, <s>nāka</s> also, <s>dyur</s> also — that [word] is neuter.
(1.2.171) <s>Tārāpatha</s> (path of the stars), <s>antarikṣa</s> again, <s>meghādhvā</s> (road of clouds), <s>mahābila</s> (the great cavity),
(1.2.172) <s>vihāyaḥ</s> [means] a bird when masculine, and the sky when masculine or neuter.
[Start of] the Directions Section (<s>Digvarga</s>).

children.text:
## Directions or quarters (5), four directions or quarters,belonging to a direction ## (1.3.173) diśastu kakubhaḥ kāṣṭhā āśāśca haritaśca tāḥ
(1.3.174) prācyavācīpratīcyastāḥ pūrvadakṣiṇapaścimāḥ
(1.3.175) uttarādigudīcī syāddiśyaṃ tu triṣu digbhave
children.translated_text:
## Directions or quarters (5), four directions, belonging to a direction ##
(1.3.173) The directions [are called] <s>kakubh</s>, <s>kāṣṭhā</s>, <s>āśā</s>, and <s>harit</s> — these [are synonyms].
(1.3.174) <s>Prācī</s>, <s>Vācī</s> (southern), and <s>Pratīcī</s> (western) — those are the eastern, southern, and western [directions].
(1.3.175) <s>Uttarā</s> and so on — <s>Udīcī</s> is the northern [direction]. '<s>Diśya</s>' is used in all three genders for [anything] belonging to a direction.

children.text:
## Belonging to respective direction or quarter ##
(1.3.176) avāgbhavamavācīnamudīcīcīnamudagbhavam
(1.3.177) pratyagbhavaṃ pratīcīnaṃ prācīnaṃ prāgbhavaṃ triṣu
children.translated_text:
## Belonging to respective direction or quarter ##
(1.3.176) '<s>Avācīna</s>' means 'coming from below' (southern). '<s>Udīcīcīna</s>' [or] '<s>udagbhava</s>' means 'of northern origin.'
(1.3.177) '<s>Pratyagbhava</s>' [or] '<s>pratīcīna</s>' means 'of western origin.' '<s>Prācīna</s>' [or] '<s>prāgbhava</s>' means 'of eastern origin' — [all used] in three genders.

children.text:
## Respective lords of the eight directions ##
(1.3.178) indro vahniḥ pitṛpatirnairṛto varuṇo marut
(1.3.179) kubera {ī}śaḥ patayaḥ pūrvādīnāṃ diśāṃ kramāt
children.translated_text:
## Respective lords of the eight directions ##
(1.3.178) <s>Indra</s>, <s>Vahni</s> (fire), <s>Pitṛpati</s> (<s>Yama</s>), <s>Nairṛta</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Marut</s> (wind),
(1.3.179) <s>Kubera</s>, and <s>Īśa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) — are the lords of the directions beginning with east, in order.

children.text:
## Respective planets associated to the eight directions ##
(1.3.180) raviḥ śukro mahīsūnuḥ svarbhānurbhānujo vidhuḥ
(1.3.181) budho bṛhaspatiśceti diśāṃ caiva tathā grahāḥ
children.translated_text:
## Respective planets associated with the eight directions ##
(1.3.180) <s>Ravi</s> (Sun), <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), <s>Mahīsūnu</s> (Mars, son of Earth), <s>Svarbhānu</s> (<s>Rāhu</s>), <s>Bhānuja</s> (Saturn, son of the Sun), <s>Vidhu</s> (Moon),
(1.3.181) <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), and <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter) — these are likewise the planets of the [eight] directions.

children.text:
## Respective elephants associated to the eight directions ##
(1.3.182) airāvataḥ puṇḍarīko vāmanaḥ kumudo 'ñjanaḥ
(1.3.183) puṣpadantaḥ sārvabhaumaḥ supratīkaśca diggajāḥ
children.translated_text:
## Respective elephants associated with the eight directions ##
(1.3.182) <s>Airāvata</s>, <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>, <s>Vāmana</s>, <s>Kumuda</s>, <s>Añjana</s>,
(1.3.183) <s>Puṣpadanta</s>, <s>Sārvabhauma</s>, and <s>Supratīka</s> — these are the elephants of the directions.

children.text:
## Respective wives of the elephants ##
(1.3.184) kariṇyo 'bhramukapilāpiṅgalānupamāḥ kramāt
(1.3.185) tāmrakarṇī śubhradantī cāṅganā cāñjanāvatī
children.translated_text:
## Respective wives of the [directional] elephants ##
(1.3.184) The female elephants are, in order: <s>Abhramu</s>, <s>Kapilā</s>, <s>Piṅgalā</s>, <s>Anupamā</s>,
(1.3.185) <s>Tāmrakarṇī</s>, <s>Śubhradantī</s>, <s>Aṅganā</s>, and <s>Añjanāvatī</s>.

children.text:
## Sector between directions (2), Inner space (2), Horizon (2) ##
(1.3.186) klībāvyayaṃ tvapadiśaṃ diśormadhye vidik striyām
(1.3.187) abhyantaraṃ tvantarālaṃ cakravālaṃ tu maṇḍalam
children.translated_text:
## Sector between directions (2), Inner space (2), Horizon (2) ##
(1.3.186) '<s>Apadiśam</s>' [is] neuter and indeclinable; between [two main] directions, '<s>vidik</s>' [is] feminine.
(1.3.187) '<s>Abhyantara</s>' and '<s>antarāla</s>' [mean inner space]. '<s>Cakravāla</s>' means 'circular enclosure' (horizon).

children.text:
## Cloud (15), line of clouds (2),Belonging to clouds ##
(1.3.188) abhraṃ megho vārivāhaḥ stanayitnurbalāhakaḥ
(1.3.189) dhārādharo jaladharastaḍitvān vārido 'mbubhṛt
(1.3.190) ghanajīmūtamudirajalamugdhūmayonayaḥ
(1.3.191) kādambinī meghamālā triṣu meghabhave 'bhriyam
children.translated_text:
## Cloud (15), Line of clouds (2), Belonging to clouds ##
(1.3.188) <s>Abhra</s>, <s>megha</s>, <s>vārivāha</s> (water-carrier), <s>stanayitnu</s> (thunderer), <s>balāhaka</s>,
(1.3.189) <s>dhārādhara</s> (stream-holder), <s>jaladhara</s> (water-bearer), <s>taḍitvān</s> (lightning-possessing), <s>vārida</s> (rain-giver), <s>ambubhṛt</s> (water-bearer),
(1.3.190) <s>ghana</s> (dense), <s>jīmūta</s>, <s>mudira</s>, <s>jalamuk</s> (water-releaser), <s>dhūmayoni</s> (smoke-born).
(1.3.191) <s>Kādambinī</s> and <s>meghamālā</s> [mean] a line of clouds. '<s>Abhriya</s>' [means] belonging to clouds — in all three genders.

children.text:
## Thundering (3), Lightening (10), Thunderclap (2), Lightening flash (2) ##
(1.3.192) stanitaṃ garjitam meghanirghoṣe rasitādi ca
(1.3.193) śampā śatahradāhrādinyairāvatyaḥ kṣaṇaprabhā
(1.3.194) taḍitsaudāminī vidyuccñcalā capalā api
(1.3.195) sphūrjathurvajranirghoṣo meghajyotiriraṃmadaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Thundering (3), Lightning (10), Thunderclap (2), Lightning flash (2) ##
(1.3.192) <s>Stanita</s>, <s>garjita</s>, and <s>rasita</s> and so on [are synonyms for] the rumbling of clouds.
(1.3.193) <s>Śampā</s>, <s>Śatahradā</s>, <s>Hrādinī</s>, <s>Airāvatī</s>, <s>Kṣaṇaprabhā</s> (moment-shining),
(1.3.194) <s>taḍit</s>, <s>saudāminī</s>, <s>vidyut</s>, <s>cañcalā</s> (the flickering), and <s>capalā</s> (the restless) also [are synonyms for lightning].
(1.3.195) <s>Sphūrjathu</s> (thunderclap) [is also] <s>vajranirghoṣa</s> (thunder-crash). <s>Meghajyoti</s> (cloud-light) [is also] <s>iraṃmada</s> (lightning flash).

## Rainbow (3) ##
(1.3.196) <s>Indrāyudha</s> (weapon of <s>Indra</s>), <s>Śakradhanus</s> (bow of <s>Śakra</s>) — that itself [is also called] <s>ṛjurohita</s> (the straight-red).

children.text:
## Rain (2), Drought (2), Continuous rain (2), Droplets ##
(1.3.197) vṛṣṭivarṣaṃ tadvighāte 'vagrāhāvagrahau samau
(1.3.198) dhārāsampāta āsāraḥ śīkarombukaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text:
## Rain (2), Drought (2), Continuous rain (2), Droplets ##
(1.3.197) <s>Vṛṣṭi</s> and <s>varṣa</s> [mean rain]. In the obstruction of that: <s>avagrāha</s> and <s>avagrahau</s> are synonymous [for drought].
(1.3.198) <s>Dhārāsampāta</s> (fall of streams) [and] <s>āsāra</s> [mean continuous rain]. <s>Śīkara</s> [means] fine water drops.

children.text:
## Hail (2), Cloudy day ##
(1.3.199) varṣopalastu karakā meghacchanne 'hni durdinam
children.translated_text:
## Hail (2), Cloudy day ##
(1.3.199) '<s>Varṣopala</s>' (rain-stone) is <s>karakā</s> (hail). On a day covered by clouds — '<s>durdina</s>' (an overcast day).

children.text:
## Covering (8) ##
(1.3.200) antardhā vyavadhā puṃsi tvantardhirapavāraṇam
(1.3.201) apidhānatirodhānapidhānācchādanāni ca
children.translated_text:
## Covering (8) ##
(1.3.200) <s>Antardhā</s> and <s>vyavadhā</s> are masculine. But <s>antardhiḥ</s> [and] <s>apavāraṇa</s>,
(1.3.201) <s>apidhāna</s>, <s>tirodhāna</s>, <s>pidhāna</s>, and <s>ācchādana</s> — [all mean covering or concealment].

children.text:
## Moon (20) ##
(1.3.202) himāṃśuścandramāścandra induḥ kumudabāndhavaḥ
(1.3.203) vidhuḥ sudhāṃśuḥ śubhrāṃśuroṣadhīśo niśāpatiḥ
(1.3.204) abjo jaivātṛkaḥ somo glaurmṛgāṅkaḥ kalānidhiḥ
(1.3.205) dvijarājaḥ śaśadharo nakṣatreśaḥ kṣapākaraḥ
children.translated_text:
## Moon (20) ##
(1.3.202) <s>Himāṃśu</s> (cool-rayed), <s>Candramā</s>, <s>Candra</s>, <s>Indu</s>, <s>Kumudabāndhava</s> (friend of the night-lotus),
(1.3.203) <s>Vidhu</s>, <s>Sudhāṃśu</s> (nectar-rayed), <s>Śubhrāṃśu</s> (bright-rayed), <s>Oṣadhīśa</s> (lord of herbs), <s>Niśāpati</s> (lord of night),
(1.3.204) <s>Abja</s> (water-born), <s>Jaivātṛka</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Glau</s>, <s>Mṛgāṅka</s> (deer-marked), <s>Kalānidhi</s> (repository of digits),
(1.3.205) <s>Dvijarāja</s> (king of twice-born), <s>Śaśadhara</s> (hare-bearer), <s>Nakṣatreśa</s> (lord of stars), <s>Kṣapākara</s> (night-maker).

children.text:
## Moon's sixteenth part, Full moon (2) ##
(1.3.206) kalā tu ṣoḍaśo bhāgo bimbo 'strī maṇḍalaṃ triṣu
children.translated_text:
## Moon's sixteenth part, Full moon (2) ##
(1.3.206) '<s>Kalā</s>' is a sixteenth part. '<s>Bimba</s>' [is] not feminine; '<s>maṇḍala</s>' (disc) [is used] in all three genders.

children.text:
## Piece, part (4), Half ##
(1.3.207) bhittaṃ śakalakhaṇḍe vā puṃsyardho 'rdhaṃ sameṃśake
children.translated_text:
## Piece, part (4), Half ##
(1.3.207) '<s>Bhinna</s>', '<s>śakala</s>', and '<s>khaṇḍa</s>' [mean piece] — or [they may be] masculine. '<s>Ardha</s>' [means half] — masculine or neuter when meaning an equal share.

children.text:
## Moonlight (3), Purity or brightness (2) ##
(1.3.208) candrikā kaumudī jyotsnā prasādstu prasannatā
children.translated_text:
## Moonlight (3), Purity or brightness (2) ##
(1.3.208) <s>Candrikā</s>, <s>kaumudī</s>, and <s>jyotsnā</s> [mean moonlight]. '<s>Prasāda</s>' means clarity or serenity.

children.text:
## Mark or spot (6) ##
(1.3.209) kalaṅkāṅkau lāñchanaṃ ca cihnaṃ lakṣma ca lakṣaṇam
children.translated_text:
## Mark or spot (6) ##
(1.3.209) <s>Kalaṅka</s>, <s>aṅka</s>, <s>lāñchana</s>, <s>cihna</s>, <s>lakṣma</s>, and <s>lakṣaṇa</s> [all mean mark or sign].

children.text:
## Exquisite beauty, Splendour (4) ##
(1.3.210) suṣamā paramā śobhā śobhā kāntirdyutiścchaviḥ
children.translated_text:
## Exquisite beauty, Splendour (4) ##
(1.3.210) <s>Suṣamā</s> is supreme beauty. <s>Śobhā</s> (splendour), <s>kānti</s> (radiance), <s>dyuti</s> (lustre), and <s>chavi</s> (complexion) [are synonyms].

children.text:
## Snow or frost (7), Snowdrift, accumulated snow (2) ##
(1.3.211) avaśyāyastu nīhārastuṣārastuhinaṃ himam
(1.3.212) prāleyaṃ mihikā cātha himānī himasaṃhatiḥ
children.translated_text:
## Snow or frost (7), Snowdrift, accumulated snow (2) ##
(1.3.211) '<s>Avaśyāya</s>' [means dew]. <s>Nīhāra</s>, <s>tuṣāra</s>, <s>tuhina</s>, <s>hima</s>,
(1.3.212) <s>prāleya</s>, and <s>mihikā</s> [are synonyms for snow/frost]. Now, <s>himānī</s> [means] an accumulation of snow.

children.text:
## Coldness, Cold (7) ##
(1.3.213) śītaṃ guṇe tadvadarthāḥ suṣīmaḥ śiśiro jaḍaḥ
(1.3.214) tuṣāraḥ śītalaḥ śīto himaḥ saptānyaliṅgakāḥ
children.translated_text:
## Coldness, Cold (7) ##
(1.3.213) '<s>Śīta</s>' [means cold] as a quality. Words with the same meaning: <s>suṣīma</s>, <s>śiśira</s>, <s>jaḍa</s>,
(1.3.214) <s>tuṣāra</s>, <s>śītala</s>, <s>śīta</s>, and <s>hima</s> — these seven may take any gender.

children.text:
## Dhruva (2), Agastya (3), Agastya's wife (also star names) ##
(1.3.215) dhruva auttānapādiḥ syāt agastyaḥ kumbhasambhavaḥ
(1.3.216) maitrāvaruṇirasyaiva lopāmudrā sadharmiṇī
children.translated_text:
## <s>Dhruva</s> (2), <s>Agastya</s> (3), <s>Agastya's</s> wife ##
(1.3.215) <s>Dhruva</s> [is also called] <s>Auttānapādi</s> (son of <s>Uttānapāda</s>). <s>Agastya</s> [is also called] <s>Kumbhasambhava</s> (pot-born),
(1.3.216) <s>Maitrāvaruṇi</s> (son of <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>). His wife is <s>Lopāmudrā</s>.

children.text:
## Star or asterism (6), Names of the 27 constellations and their parts ##
(1.3.217) nakṣatramṛkṣaṃ bhaṃ tārā tārakāpyuḍu vā striyām
(1.3.218) dākṣāyiṇyo 'śvinītyāditārā aśvayugaśvinī
(1.3.219) rādhāviśākhā puṣye tu sidhyatiṣyau śraviṣṭhayā
(1.3.220) samā dhaniṣṭhāḥ syuḥ proṣṭhapadā bhādrapadāḥ striyaḥ
(1.3.221) mṛgaśīrṣaṃ mṛgaśirastasminnevāgrahāyaṇī
(1.3.222) ilvalāstacchirodeśe tārakā nivasanti yāḥ
children.translated_text:
## Star or asterism (6), Names of the 27 constellations and their parts ##
(1.3.217) <s>Nakṣatra</s>, <s>ṛkṣa</s>, <s>bha</s>, <s>tārā</s>, <s>tārakā</s> — also <s>uḍu</s>, or feminine [forms].
(1.3.218) The daughters of <s>Dakṣa</s> [are the constellations]: <s>Aśvinī</s> and so on. The star [of the first constellation] is <s>Aśvayuj</s>; <s>Aśvinī</s> [is its name].
(1.3.219) <s>Rādhā</s> [is the same as] <s>Viśākhā</s>. In [the case of] <s>Puṣya</s>: <s>Sidhya</s> and <s>Tiṣya</s> [are synonyms]. With <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s>,
(1.3.220) '<s>Dhaniṣṭhāḥ</s>' is synonymous — [these are] feminine plurals. '<s>Proṣṭhapadāḥ</s>' [are the same as] '<s>Bhādrapadāḥ</s>' — [also] feminine plurals.
(1.3.221) <s>Mṛgaśīrṣa</s> [is the same as] <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>. In that very [constellation], <s>Āgrahāyaṇī</s> [is another name].
(1.3.222) The <s>Ilvalās</s> are the stars that dwell in its head region.

children.text:
## Planet Jupiter (9) ##
(1.3.223) bṛhaspatiḥ surācāryo gīṣpatirdhiṣaṇo guruḥ
(1.3.224) jīva āṅgiraso vācaspatiścitraśikhaṇḍijaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Planet Jupiter (9) ##
(1.3.223) <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Surācārya</s> (teacher of the gods), <s>Gīṣpati</s> (lord of speech), <s>Dhiṣaṇa</s>, <s>Guru</s>,
(1.3.224) <s>Jīva</s>, <s>Āṅgirasa</s> (son of <s>Aṅgiras</s>), <s>Vācaspati</s> (lord of speech), <s>Citraśikhaṇḍija</s> (born of the variegated-crested one).

children.text:
## Planet Venus (6) ##
(1.3.225) śukro daityaguruḥ kāvya uśanā bhārgavaḥ kaviḥ
children.translated_text:
## Planet Venus (6) ##
(1.3.225) <s>Śukra</s>, <s>Daityaguru</s> (teacher of the demons), <s>Kāvya</s>, <s>Uśanas</s>, <s>Bhārgava</s> (descendant of <s>Bhṛgu</s>), <s>Kavi</s> (the seer).

children.text:
## Planet Mars (5), Planet Mercury (3) ##
(1.3.226) aṅgārakaḥ kujo bhaumo lohitāṅgo mahīsutaḥ
(1.3.227) rauhiṇeyo budhaḥ saumyaḥ samau sauriśanaiśvarau
children.translated_text:
## Planet Mars (5), Planet Mercury (3) ##
(1.3.226) <s>Aṅgāraka</s>, <s>Kuja</s> (earth-born), <s>Bhauma</s> (earthly), <s>Lohitāṅga</s> (red-bodied), <s>Mahīsuta</s> (son of the Earth).
(1.3.227) <s>Rauhiṇeya</s>, <s>Budha</s>, <s>Saumya</s> (gentle) [are names of Mercury]. <s>Sauri</s> and <s>Śanaiścara</s> [are names of Saturn] — [the latter two are] synonymous.

children.text:
## Rahu or the ascending node (5) ##
(1.3.228) tamastu rāhuḥ svarbhānuḥ saiṃhikeyo vidhuntudaḥ
children.translated_text:
## <s>Rāhu</s> or the ascending node (5) ##
(1.3.228) The dark one (<s>tamas</s>) is <s>Rāhu</s>; [also] <s>Svarbhānu</s>, <s>Saiṃhikeya</s> (son of <s>Siṃhikā</s>), <s>Vidhuntuda</s> (moon-striker).

## Ursa Major ##
(1.3.229) The Seven Sages (<s>Saptarṣi</s>) — <s>Marīci</s>, <s>Atri</s>, and the rest — [are also called] <s>Citraśikhaṇḍinaḥ</s> (the variegated-crested).

children.text:
## Rising of the Zodiac signs(Lagna), The zodiac ##
(1.3.230) rāśīnāmudayo lagnaṃ te tu meṣavṛṣādayaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Rising of the Zodiac signs (Lagna), The zodiac ##
(1.3.230) The rising of the zodiac signs is <s>lagna</s> (the ascendant). They [i.e., the signs] are <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries), <s>Vṛṣa</s> (Taurus), and so on.

children.text:
## Sun (54) ##
(1.3.231) sūrasūryāryamādityadvādaśātmadivākarāḥ
(1.3.232) bhāskarāhaskarabradhnaprabhākaravibhākarāḥ
(1.3.233) bhāsvadvivasvatsaptāśvaharidaśvoṣṇaraśmayaḥ
(1.3.234) vikartanārkamārtaṇḍamihirāruṇapūṣaṇaḥ
(1.3.235) dyumaṇistaraṇirmitraścitrabhānurvirocanaḥ
(1.3.236) vibhāvasurgrahapatistviṣāṃpatiraharpatiḥ
(1.3.237) bhānurhaṃsaḥ sahasrāṃśustapanaḥ savitā raviḥ
(1.3.238) padmākṣastejasāṃrāśiśchāyānāthastamisrahā
(1.3.239) karmasākṣī jagaccakṣurlokabandhustrayītanuḥ
(1.3.240) pradyotano dinamaṇiḥ khadyoto lokabāndhavaḥ
(1.3.241) ino bhago bhāmanidhiścāṃ 'śumālyañjinīpatiḥ
children.translated_text:
## Sun (54 synonyms) ##
(1.3.231) <s>Sūra</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Āditya</s>, <s>Dvādaśātman</s> (twelve-souled), <s>Divākara</s> (day-maker),
(1.3.232) <s>Bhāskara</s> (light-maker), <s>Ahaskara</s> (day-maker), <s>Bradhna</s>, <s>Prabhākara</s> (radiance-maker), <s>Vibhākara</s> (illuminator),
(1.3.233) <s>Bhāsvat</s> (radiant), <s>Vivasvat</s>, <s>Saptāśva</s> (seven-horsed), <s>Haridaśva</s> (green-horsed), <s>Uṣṇaraśmi</s> (hot-rayed),
(1.3.234) <s>Vikartana</s>, <s>Arka</s>, <s>Mārtaṇḍa</s>, <s>Mihira</s>, <s>Aruṇa</s>, <s>Pūṣan</s>,
(1.3.235) <s>Dyumaṇi</s> (celestial jewel), <s>Taraṇi</s> (carrier across), <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Citrabhānu</s> (variegated-rayed), <s>Virocana</s>,
(1.3.236) <s>Vibhāvasu</s> (possessing light), <s>Grahapati</s> (lord of planets), <s>Tviṣāṃpati</s> (lord of splendors), <s>Aharpati</s> (lord of days),
(1.3.237) <s>Bhānu</s> (shining), <s>Haṃsa</s> (swan), <s>Sahasrāṃśu</s> (thousand-rayed), <s>Tapana</s> (heater), <s>Savitṛ</s> (impeller), <s>Ravi</s>,
(1.3.238) <s>Padmākṣa</s> (lotus-eyed), <s>Tejasāṃrāśi</s> (mass of brilliance), <s>Chāyānātha</s> (lord of shadow), <s>Tamisrahā</s> (destroyer of darkness),
(1.3.239) <s>Karmasākṣin</s> (witness of deeds), <s>Jagaccakṣus</s> (eye of the world), <s>Lokabandhu</s> (kinsman of the world), <s>Trayītanu</s> (embodiment of the three Vedas),
(1.3.240) <s>Pradyotana</s> (illuminator), <s>Dinamaṇi</s> (day-jewel), <s>Khadyota</s> (sky-light), <s>Lokabāndhava</s> (friend of the world),
(1.3.241) <s>Ina</s>, <s>Bhaga</s>, <s>Bhāmanidhi</s> (treasure of light), <s>Aṃśumālin</s> (ray-garlanded), <s>Añjinīpati</s>.

children.text:
## Sun's three attendants, Sun's son (5), Halo (4) ##
(1.3.242) māṭharaḥ piṅgalo daṇḍaścaṇḍāṃśoḥ paripārśvakāḥ
(1.3.243) sūrasūto 'ruṇo 'nūruḥ kāśyapirgaruḍāgrajaḥ
(1.3.244) pariveṣastuparidhirupasūryakamaṇḍale
children.translated_text:
## Sun's three attendants, Sun's son (5 synonyms), Halo (4 synonyms) ##
(1.3.242) <s>Māṭhara</s>, <s>Piṅgala</s>, and <s>Daṇḍa</s> are the attendants of the fierce-rayed [Sun].
(1.3.243) The Sun's charioteer: <s>Aruṇa</s>, <s>Anūru</s> (thighless), <s>Kāśyapi</s> (son of <s>Kaśyapa</s>), elder brother of <s>Garuḍa</s>.
(1.3.244) <s>Pariveṣa</s>, <s>Paridhi</s>, <s>Upasūryaka</s>, and <s>Maṇḍala</s> [are synonyms for halo].

children.text:
## Ray (11), Light or brightness (11), Sunlight (3) ##
(1.3.245) kiraṇosramayūkhāṃ 'śugabhastighṛṇiraśmayaḥ
(1.3.246) bhānuḥ karo marīciḥ strīpuṃsayordīdhitiḥ striyām
(1.3.247) syuḥ prabhārugrucistviḍbhābhāśchavidyutidīptayaḥ
(1.3.248) rociḥ śocirubhe klībe prakāśo dyota ātapaḥ

## Lukewarm (4), Very hot (4), Mirage (2) ##
(1.3.249) koṣṇaṃ kavoṣṇaṃ mandoṣṇaṃ kaduṣṇaṃ triṣu tadvati
(1.3.250) tigmaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ kharaṃ tadvanmṛgatṛṣṇā marīcikā
children.translated_text:
## Lukewarm (4 synonyms), Very hot (4 synonyms), Mirage (2 synonyms) ##
(1.3.249) <s>Koṣṇa</s>, <s>kavoṣṇa</s>, <s>mandoṣṇa</s>, <s>kaduṣṇa</s> — [all mean lukewarm;] in all three genders when possessing that [quality].
(1.3.250) <s>Tigma</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, <s>khara</s> [mean very hot]; likewise, <s>mṛgatṛṣṇā</s> and <s>marīcikā</s> [mean mirage].
Chapter on Time (<s>Kālavarga</s>).

children.text:
## Time (4), First (lunar calendar) day (2), Lunar day ##
(1.4.251) kālo diṣṭo 'pyanehāpi samayo 'pyatha pakṣatiḥ
## Day (5), Morning (9), Evening (4) ##
(1.4.252) pratipad dve ime strītve tadādyāstithayo dvayoḥ
(1.4.253) ghasro dināhanī vā tu klībe divasavāsarau
(1.4.254) pratyūṣo 'harmukhaṃ kalyamuṣaḥpratyuṣasī api
(1.4.255) vyuṣṭaṃ vibhātaṃ dve klībe puṃsi gosarga iṣyate
(1.4.256) prabhātaṃ ca dinānte tu sāyaṃ sandhyā pitṛprasūḥ
children.translated_text:
## Time (4 synonyms), First lunar day (2 synonyms), Lunar day ##
(1.4.251) <s>Kāla</s>, <s>diṣṭa</s>, <s>aneha</s>, and <s>samaya</s> [mean time]; then <s>pakṣati</s> [means a lunar day].
## Day (5 synonyms), Morning (9 synonyms), Evening (4 synonyms) ##
(1.4.252) <s>Pratipad</s> — these two [words] are feminine; the <s>tithis</s> (lunar days) beginning with that are in both [masculine and feminine].
(1.4.253) <s>Ghasra</s>, <s>dina</s>, <s>ahan</s> — or in the neuter; <s>divasa</s> and <s>vāsara</s> [are synonyms for day].
(1.4.254) <s>Pratyūṣa</s>, <s>harmukha</s>, <s>kalya</s>, <s>uṣas</s>, <s>pratyuṣas</s> also,
(1.4.255) <s>vyuṣṭa</s> and <s>vibhāta</s> — both neuter; <s>gosarga</s> (masculine) is accepted [for dawn];
(1.4.256) and <s>prabhāta</s> [means morning]; but at the end of day: <s>sāyam</s>, <s>sandhyā</s>, <s>pitṛprasū</s> [mean evening].

children.text:
## Three parts of the day, Night (12) ##
(1.4.257) prāhṇāparāhṇamadhyāhnastrisandhyamatha śarvarī
(1.4.258) niśā niśīthinī rātristriyāmā kṣaṇadā kṣapā
(1.4.259) vibhāvarī tamasvinyau rajanī yāminī tamī
children.translated_text:
## Three parts of the day, Night (12 synonyms) ##
(1.4.257) <s>Prāhṇa</s>, <s>aparāhṇa</s>, and <s>madhyāhna</s> are the three <s>sandhyas</s> (junctures); now <s>śarvarī</s>,
(1.4.258) <s>niśā</s>, <s>niśīthinī</s>, <s>rātri</s>, <s>triyāmā</s> (three-watched), <s>kṣaṇadā</s>, <s>kṣapā</s>,
(1.4.259) <s>vibhāvarī</s>, <s>tamasvinī</s> — [both]; <s>rajanī</s>, <s>yāminī</s>, <s>tamī</s> [are all synonyms for night].

children.text:
## Dark night, Moonlit night ##
(1.4.260) tamisrā tāmasī rātrirjyautsnī candrikayānvitā
children.translated_text:
## Dark night, Moonlit night ##
(1.4.260) <s>Tamisrā</s> and <s>tāmasī</s> [mean a dark] night; <s>jyautsnī</s> [means] a night accompanied by moonlight.

children.text:
## Night together with adjoining days ##
(1.4.261) āgāmivartamānārhayuktāyāṃ niśi pakṣiṇī
children.translated_text:
## Night together with adjoining days ##
(1.4.261) When connected with the coming, present, or past [day], a night [is called] <s>pakṣiṇī</s>.

children.text:
## Collection of nights, Late evening (2) ##
(1.4.262) gaṇarātraṃ niśā bahvyaḥ pradoṣo rajanīmukham
children.translated_text:
## Collection of nights, Late evening (2 synonyms) ##
(1.4.262) <s>Gaṇarātra</s> is many nights; <s>pradoṣa</s> and <s>rajanīmukha</s> [mean late evening/nightfall].

children.text:
## Midnight (2), A period of 3 hours (2) ##
(1.4.263) ardharātraniśīthau dvau dvau yāmapraharau samau
children.translated_text:
## Midnight (2 synonyms), A period of 3 hours (2 synonyms) ##
(1.4.263) <s>Ardharātra</s> and <s>niśītha</s> are equivalent — [both mean midnight]; <s>yāma</s> and <s>prahara</s> are equivalent [both mean a watch of 3 hours].

children.text:
## Join of fortnights, Last days of fortnights (20) ##
(1.4.264) sa parvasandhiḥ pratipatpañcadaśyoryadantaram
children.translated_text:
## Junction of fortnights, Last days of fortnights (20) ##
(1.4.264) That junction of <s>parvan</s> (sacred days) is the interval between <s>pratipad</s> (first day) and <s>pañcadaśī</s> (fifteenth day).

children.text:
## Full moon day (2) ##
(1.4.265) pakṣāntau pañcadaśyau dve paurṇamāsī tu paurṇimā
children.translated_text:
## Full moon day (2 synonyms) ##
(1.4.265) The two ends of the fortnight are the two <s>pañcadaśīs</s> (fifteenth days); <s>paurṇamāsī</s> is also [called] <s>paurṇimā</s>.

children.text:
## Night of the almost full moon, Night of the really full moon ##
(1.4.266) kalāhīne sānumatiḥ pūrṇe rākā niśākare
children.translated_text:
## Night of the almost full moon, Night of the really full moon ##
(1.4.266) When the moon is deficient by one <s>kalā</s> (digit), [the night is called] <s>Anumati</s>; when full, <s>Rākā</s>.

children.text:
## New moon day (4) ##
(1.4.267) amāvāsyā tvamāvasyā darśaḥ sūryendusaṃgamaḥ
children.translated_text:
## New moon day (4 synonyms) ##
(1.4.267) <s>Amāvāsyā</s>, <s>amāvasyā</s>, <s>darśa</s>, and <s>sūryendusaṃgama</s> (conjunction of sun and moon) [are synonyms for new moon].

children.text:
## Night mostly wihout moon, Night without any moon ##
(1.4.268) sā dṛṣṭenduḥ sinīvālī sā naṣṭendukalā kuhūḥ
children.translated_text:
## Night mostly without moon, Night without any moon ##
(1.4.268) When [the new moon night has] a visible [sliver of] moon, [it is called] <s>Sinīvālī</s>; when the moon-digit is gone, <s>Kuhū</s>.

children.text:
## Eclipse, Eclipsed Sun or Moon ##
(1.4.269) uparāgo graho rāhugraste tvindau ca pūṣṇi ca
(1.4.270) sopaplavoparaktau dvau agnyutpāta upāhitaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Eclipse, Eclipsed Sun or Moon ##
(1.4.269) <s>Uparāga</s> and <s>graha</s> [mean eclipse]; when the moon and sun are seized by <s>Rāhu</s>,
(1.4.270) [they are called] <s>sopaplava</s> and <s>uparakta</s> (eclipsed); <s>agnyutpāta</s> [means] a fiery portent — [called] <s>upāhita</s>.

children.text:
## Sun and Moon ##
(1.4.271) ekayoktyā puṣpavantau divākaraniśākarau
children.translated_text:
## Sun and Moon ##
(1.4.271) Expressed by a single compound: <s>puṣpavantau</s> [means] the sun and the moon (the day-maker and the night-maker).

children.text: ## Nimesha: Time needed for flickering of an eye ##
children.translated_text: ## <s>Nimeṣa</s>: the time needed for the flickering of an eye ##

children.text:
## 18 Nimesha = Kashtha, 30 Kashtha = Kala ##
(1.4.272) aṣṭādaśa nimeṣāstu kāṣṭā triṃśat tu tāḥ kalā
children.translated_text:
## 18 Nimeṣa = Kāṣṭhā, 30 Kāṣṭhā = Kalā ##
(1.4.272) Eighteen <s>nimeṣas</s> make a <s>kāṣṭhā</s>; thirty of those make a <s>kalā</s>.

children.text:
## 30 Kala = Kshana, 12 Kshana = Muhurta ##
(1.4.273) tāstu triṃśat kṣaṇaste tu muhūrto dvādaśāstriyām
children.translated_text:
## 30 Kalā = Kṣaṇa, 12 Kṣaṇa = Muhūrta ##
(1.4.273) Thirty of those [kalās] make a <s>kṣaṇa</s>; twelve of those make a <s>muhūrta</s> (not feminine).

children.text:
## 30 Muhurta = (Full) day (24 Hours), 15 Days = Paksha (fortnight) ##
(1.4.274) te tu triṃśadahorātraḥ pakṣaste daśapañca ca
children.translated_text:
## 30 Muhūrta = (Full) day (24 Hours), 15 Days = Pakṣa (fortnight) ##
(1.4.274) Thirty of those make an <s>ahorātra</s> (day-and-night); fifteen of those make a <s>pakṣa</s> (fortnight).

children.text:
## First and second fortnight, 2 fortnights = (Lunar) Month ##
(1.4.275) pakṣau pūrvāparau śuklakṛṣṇau māsastu tāvubhau
children.translated_text:
## First and second fortnight, 2 fortnights = (Lunar) Month ##
(1.4.275) The earlier and later fortnights are <s>śukla</s> (bright) and <s>kṛṣṇa</s> (dark); both of those together make a <s>māsa</s> (month).

children.text:
## Two months = Ritu (season), 3 Ritus = Ayana (Semester) ##
(1.4.276) dvau dvau mārgādi māsau syādṛtustairayanaṃ tribhiḥ
children.translated_text:
## Two months = Ṛtu (season), 3 Ṛtus = Ayana (Semester) ##
(1.4.276) Two months each, beginning with <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, constitute an <s>ṛtu</s> (season); three of those make an <s>ayana</s>.

children.text:
## 2 Ayana = Year, Equinox ##
(1.4.277) ayane dve gatirudagdakṣiṇārkasya vatsaraḥ
(1.4.278) samarātridive kāle viṣuvadviṣuvaṃ ca tat
children.translated_text:
## 2 Ayana = Year, Equinox ##
(1.4.277) The two <s>ayanas</s> are the northward and southward courses of the sun; [together they make] a <s>vatsara</s> (year).
(1.4.278) The time when day and night are equal is <s>viṣuvat</s> or <s>viṣuva</s> (equinox).

children.text: ## Constellation names determine names for Full moon days and their months ##
children.translated_text: ## Constellation names determine names for full-moon days and their months ##

children.text:
## For example, Pushya constellation names Paushi full moon night and Pausha month. ##
(1.4.279) puṣpayuktā paurṇamāsī pauṣī māse tu yatra sā
(1.4.280) nāmnā sa pauṣo māghādyāścaivamekādaśāpare
children.translated_text:
## For example, the Puṣya constellation names the Pauṣī full-moon night and the Pauṣa month ##
(1.4.279) The full-moon night connected with <s>Puṣya</s> [constellation] is <s>Pauṣī</s>; and the month in which that [occurs]
(1.4.280) is <s>Pauṣa</s> by name; <s>Māgha</s> and the rest — the other eleven — [are likewise named].

children.text:
## Margashirsha (9 th month) (4), Pausha (10 th) (3) ##
(1.4.281) mārgaśīrṣe sahā mārga āgrahāyaṇikaśca saḥ
(1.4.282) pauṣe taiṣasahasyau dvau tapā māghe 'tha phālgune
children.translated_text:
## Mārgaśīrṣa (9th month) (4 synonyms), Pauṣa (10th) (3 synonyms) ##
(1.4.281) For <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>: <s>Saha</s>, <s>Mārga</s>, and <s>Āgrahāyaṇika</s> [are synonyms].
(1.4.282) For <s>Pauṣa</s>: <s>Taiṣa</s> and <s>Sahasya</s> [are synonyms]; <s>Tapas</s> is [the name for] <s>Māgha</s>; and in <s>Phālguna</s>:

children.text:
## Magha (11 th) (2) Falguna (12 th) (3), Chaitra (1 st ) (3) ##
(1.4.283) syāttapasyaḥ phālgunikaḥ syāccaitre caitriko madhuḥ
children.translated_text:
## Māgha (11th) (2 synonyms), Phālguna (12th) (3 synonyms), Caitra (1st) (3 synonyms) ##
(1.4.283) <s>Tapasya</s> and <s>Phālgunika</s> [are synonyms for <s>Phālguna</s>]; for <s>Caitra</s>: <s>Caitrika</s> and <s>Madhu</s> [are synonyms].

children.text:
## Vaishakh (2 nd ) (3), Jyeshtha (3 rd ) (2) ##
(1.4.284) vaiśākhe mādhavo rādho jyeṣṭhe śukraḥ śucistvayam
children.translated_text:
## Vaiśākha (2nd) (3 synonyms), Jyeṣṭha (3rd) (2 synonyms) ##
(1.4.284) For <s>Vaiśākha</s>: <s>Mādhava</s> and <s>Rādha</s> [are synonyms]; for <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>: <s>Śukra</s> and <s>Śuci</s> [are synonyms].

children.text:
## Ashadha (4 th) (2), Shravana (5 th) (3) ##
(1.4.285) āṣāḍhe śrāvaṇe tu syānnabhāḥ śrāvaṇikaśca saḥ
children.translated_text:
## Āṣāḍha (4th) (2 synonyms), Śrāvaṇa (5th) (3 synonyms) ##
(1.4.285) For <s>Āṣāḍha</s> [that is its name]; for <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>: <s>Nabhas</s> and <s>Śrāvaṇika</s> [are synonyms].

children.text:
## Bhadrapada (6 th) (4), Ashvin (7 th) (3)##
(1.4.286) syurnabhasyaprauṣṭhapadabhādrabhādrapadāḥ samāḥ
(1.4.287) syādāśvina iṣo 'pyāśvayujo 'pi syāttukārtike
children.translated_text:
## Bhādrapada (6th) (4 synonyms), Āśvin (7th) (3 synonyms) ##
(1.4.286) <s>Nabhasya</s>, <s>Prauṣṭhapada</s>, <s>Bhādra</s>, and <s>Bhādrapada</s> are equivalent.
(1.4.287) <s>Āśvina</s>, <s>Iṣa</s>, and <s>Āśvayuja</s> [are synonyms]; and for <s>Kārtika</s>:

children.text:
## Kartika (8 th) (4), Fall (Months 9-10), Winter (Months 11-12) ##
(1.4.288) bāhulorjau kārtikiko hemantaḥ śiśiro 'striyām
children.translated_text:
## Kārtika (8th) (4 synonyms), Fall (Months 9-10), Winter (Months 11-12) ##
(1.4.288) <s>Bāhula</s>, <s>Ūrja</s>, and <s>Kārtikika</s> [are synonyms for <s>Kārtika</s>]; <s>hemanta</s> and <s>śiśira</s> (not feminine) [are fall and winter].

children.text:
## Spring (Months 1-2) (3), Summer (Months 3-4) (7) ##
(1.4.289) vasante puṣpasamayaḥ surabhirgrīṣma ūṣmakaḥ
(1.4.290) nidāgha uṣṇopagama uṣṇa ūṣmāgamastapaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Spring (Months 1-2) (3 synonyms), Summer (Months 3-4) (7 synonyms) ##
(1.4.289) In spring: <s>puṣpasamaya</s> (flower-time) and <s>surabhi</s> (fragrant) [are synonyms]; for summer: <s>grīṣma</s>, <s>ūṣmaka</s>,
(1.4.290) <s>nidāgha</s>, <s>uṣṇopagama</s> (approach of heat), <s>uṣṇa</s>, <s>ūṣmāgama</s> (arrival of heat), and <s>tapas</s> (heat) [are synonyms].

children.text:
## Monsoon (Months 5-6) (2), Autumn (Months 7-8) ##
(1.4.291) striyāṃ prāvṛṭ striyāṃ bhūmni varṣā atha śaratstriyām
children.translated_text:
## Monsoon (Months 5-6) (2 synonyms), Autumn (Months 7-8) ##
(1.4.291) <s>Prāvṛṭ</s> (feminine) [means monsoon]; <s>varṣā</s> (feminine, used in the plural) [also means monsoon]; then <s>śarat</s> (feminine) [means autumn].

children.text:
## Season, Year (6) ##
(1.4.292) ṣaḍamī ṛtavaḥ puṃsi mārgādīnāṃ yugaiḥ kramāt
(1.4.293) saṃvatsaro vatsaro 'bdo hāyano 'strī śaratsamāḥ
children.translated_text:
## Season, Year (6 synonyms) ##
(1.4.292) These six are the <s>ṛtus</s> (seasons) — masculine — [formed] in pairs from [the months beginning with] <s>Mārga</s> in sequence.
(1.4.293) <s>Saṃvatsara</s>, <s>vatsara</s>, <s>abda</s>, <s>hāyana</s> (not feminine), <s>śarat</s>, and <s>samā</s> [are synonyms for year].

children.text:
## Human Month = Ancestral day, Human year = Divine day ##
(1.4.294) māsena syādahorātraḥ paitro varṣeṇa daivataḥ
children.translated_text:
## Human Month = Ancestral day, Human year = Divine day ##
(1.4.294) By a [human] month there is a day-and-night of the ancestors; by a [human] year, a divine [day].

children.text:
## Human Yuga quartet = Divine Yuga, Divine 2000 Yuga = Brahma's day = Human kalpa ##
(1.4.295) daive yugasahasre dve brāhmaḥ kalpau tu tau nṛṇām
children.translated_text:
## Human Yuga quartet = Divine Yuga, Divine 2000 Yuga = Brahmā's day = Human Kalpa ##
(1.4.295) Two thousand divine <s>yugas</s> make a day of <s>Brahmā</s>; those two [halves] for humans [constitute a <s>kalpa</s>].

children.text:
## Manvantara = 71 Divine yuga ##
(1.4.296) manvantaraṃ tu divyānāṃ yugānāmekasaptatiḥ
children.translated_text:
## Manvantara = 71 Divine yugas ##
(1.4.296) A <s>manvantara</s> is seventy-one divine <s>yugas</s>.

children.text:
## Destruction of world (between epochs) (5) ##
(1.4.297) saṃvartaḥ pralayaḥ kalpaḥ kṣayaḥ kalpānta ityapi
children.translated_text:
## Destruction of world (between epochs) (5 synonyms) ##
(1.4.297) <s>Saṃvarta</s>, <s>pralaya</s>, <s>kalpa</s>, <s>kṣaya</s>, and <s>kalpānta</s> [are synonyms for cosmic dissolution].

children.text:
## Sin (12), Virtue or merit (5) ##
(1.4.298) astrī paṅkaṃ pumānpāpmā pāpaṃ kilbiṣakalmaṣam
(1.4.299) kaluṣaṃ vṛjinaino 'ghamaṃho duritaduṣkṛtam
(1.4.300) syāddharmamastriyāṃ puṇyaśreyasī sukṛtaṃ vṛṣaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Sin (12 synonyms), Virtue or merit (5 synonyms) ##
(1.4.298) <s>Paṅka</s> (not feminine, neuter), <s>pāpman</s> (masculine), <s>pāpa</s>, <s>kilbiṣa</s>, <s>kalmaṣa</s>,
(1.4.299) <s>kaluṣa</s>, <s>vṛjina</s>, <s>enas</s>, <s>agha</s>, <s>aṃhas</s>, <s>durita</s>, <s>duṣkṛta</s> [are synonyms for sin].
(1.4.300) <s>Dharma</s> (not feminine), <s>puṇya</s>, <s>śreyas</s>, <s>sukṛta</s>, and <s>vṛṣa</s> [are synonyms for virtue/merit].

children.text:
## Joy or happiness (12), Prosperity, blessing (12) ##
(1.4.301) mutprītiḥ pramado harṣaḥ pramodāmodasammadāḥ
(1.4.302) syādānandathurānandaḥ śarmaśātasukhāni ca
(1.4.303) śvaḥ śreyasaṃ śivaṃ bhadraṃ kalyāṇaṃ maṅgalaṃ śubham
(1.4.304) bhāvukaṃ bhavikaṃ bhavyaṃ kuśalaṃ kṣemamastriyām
(1.4.305) śastaṃ cātha triṣu dravye pāpaṃ puṇyaṃ sukhādi ca
children.translated_text:
## Joy or happiness (12 synonyms), Prosperity or blessing (12 synonyms) ##
(1.4.301) <s>Mud</s>, <s>prīti</s>, <s>pramada</s>, <s>harṣa</s>, <s>pramoda</s>, <s>āmoda</s>, <s>sammada</s>,
(1.4.302) <s>ānandathu</s>, <s>ānanda</s>, <s>śarman</s>, <s>śāta</s>, and <s>sukha</s> [are synonyms for joy/happiness].
(1.4.303) <s>Śvas</s>, <s>śreyasa</s>, <s>śiva</s>, <s>bhadra</s>, <s>kalyāṇa</s>, <s>maṅgala</s>, <s>śubha</s>,
(1.4.304) <s>bhāvuka</s>, <s>bhavika</s>, <s>bhavya</s>, <s>kuśala</s>, <s>kṣema</s> (not feminine),
(1.4.305) and <s>śasta</s> [are synonyms for auspiciousness/prosperity]; moreover, in all three genders for substance: <s>pāpa</s>, <s>puṇya</s>, <s>sukha</s>, and the like.

children.text:
## Excellent! (5), Good luck ##
(1.4.306) matallikā macarcikā prakāṇḍamuddhatallajau
(1.4.307) praśastavācakānyamūnyayaḥ śubhāvaho vidhiḥ
children.translated_text:
## Excellent! (5 synonyms), Good luck ##
(1.4.306) <s>Matallikā</s>, <s>macarcikā</s>, <s>prakāṇḍa</s>, <s>uddhata</s>, and <s>llaja</s>
(1.4.307) — these are words expressing what is excellent; <s>vidhi</s> [means] that which brings about the auspicious.

children.text:
## Destiny or luck (6), Cause (3), Root cause ##
(1.4.308) daivaṃ diṣṭaṃ bhāgadheyaṃ bhāgyaṃ strī niyatirvidhiḥ
(1.4.309) heturnā kāraṇaṃ bījaṃ nidānaṃ tvādikāraṇam
children.translated_text:
## Destiny or luck (6 synonyms), Cause (3 synonyms), Root cause ##
(1.4.308) <s>Daiva</s>, <s>diṣṭa</s>, <s>bhāgadheya</s>, <s>bhāgya</s> (feminine), <s>niyati</s>, and <s>vidhi</s> [mean destiny/luck].
(1.4.309) <s>Hetu</s> (not feminine), <s>kāraṇa</s>, <s>bīja</s> (seed) [mean cause]; <s>nidāna</s> means the root cause.

children.text:
## Soul (3), State (of body etc.), Three Qualities (of all things) ##
(1.4.310) kṣetrajña ātmā puruṣaḥ pradhānaṃ prakṛtiḥ striyām
(1.4.311) viśeṣaḥ kāliko 'vasthā guṇāḥ sattvaṃ rajastamaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Soul (3 synonyms), State (of body etc.), Three Qualities (of all things) ##
(1.4.310) <s>Kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field), <s>Ātman</s>, and <s>Puruṣa</s> [mean soul]; <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>prakṛti</s> (feminine) [mean primordial nature].
(1.4.311) <s>Viśeṣa</s> (particular quality); <s>kālika</s> [means] temporal; <s>avasthā</s> [means] state; the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) are <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>.

children.text:
## Birth (6), Living being (6) ##
(1.4.312) janurjananajanmāni janirutpattirudbhavaḥ
(1.4.313) prāṇī tu cetano janmī jantujanyuśarīriṇaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Birth (6 synonyms), Living being (6 synonyms) ##
(1.4.312) <s>Janus</s>, <s>janana</s>, <s>janman</s>, <s>jani</s>, <s>utpatti</s>, and <s>udbhava</s> [are synonyms for birth].
(1.4.313) <s>Prāṇin</s> (one with breath), <s>cetana</s> (conscious), <s>janmin</s>, <s>jantu</s>, <s>janyu</s>, and <s>śarīrin</s> (embodied) [are synonyms for a living being].

children.text:
## Kind or type (3), Individuality, Mind (7) ##
(1.4.314) jātirjātaṃ ca sāmānyaṃ vyaktistu pṛthagātmatā
(1.4.315) cittaṃ tu ceto hṛdayaṃ svāntaṃ hṛnmānasaṃ manaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Kind or type (3 synonyms), Individuality, Mind (7 synonyms) ##
(1.4.314) <s>Jāti</s>, <s>jāta</s>, and <s>sāmānya</s> [mean genus/universal]; but <s>vyakti</s> is individual nature (<s>pṛthagātmatā</s>).
(1.4.315) <s>Citta</s>, <s>cetas</s>, <s>hṛdaya</s>, <s>svānta</s>, <s>hṛd</s>, <s>mānasa</s>, and <s>manas</s> [are synonyms for mind].
Chapter on Intellect (<s>Dhīvarga</s>).

children.text:
## Comprehension, intellect (14)##
(1.5.316) buddhirmanīṣā dhiṣaṇā dhīḥ prajñā śemuṣī matiḥ
(1.5.317) prekṣopalabdhiścitsaṃvitpratipajjñapticetanāḥ
children.translated_text:
## Comprehension, intellect (14 synonyms) ##
(1.5.316) <s>Buddhi</s>, <s>manīṣā</s>, <s>dhiṣaṇā</s>, <s>dhī</s>, <s>prajñā</s>, <s>śemuṣī</s>, <s>mati</s>,
(1.5.317) <s>prekṣā</s>, <s>upalabdhi</s>, <s>cit</s>, <s>saṃvit</s>, <s>pratipat</s>, <s>jñapti</s>, and <s>cetanā</s> [are synonyms for intellect].

children.text:
## Retentive intellect (1), Volition (1), Attention (3) ##
(1.5.318) dhīrdhāraṇāvatī medhā saṃkalpaḥ karma mānasam
(1.5.319) avadhānaṃ samādhānaṃ praṇidhānam tathaiva ca
children.translated_text:
## Retentive intellect (1 synonym), Volition (1 synonym), Attention (3 synonyms) ##
(1.5.318) <s>Dhī</s> [when it is] that which holds [is called] <s>medhā</s> (retentive intellect); <s>saṃkalpa</s> is mental action (<s>karma mānasa</s>).
(1.5.319) <s>Avadhāna</s>, <s>samādhāna</s>, and <s>praṇidhāna</s> — likewise [are synonyms for attention].

children.text:
## Awareness (2), Reflection (3), Reasoning (3), Doubt (4) ##
(1.5.320) cittābhogo manaskāraścarcā saṃkhyā vicāraṇā
(1.5.321) vimarśo bhāvanā caiva vāsanā ca nigadyate
(1.5.322) adhyāhārastarka ūho vicikitsā tu saṃśayaḥ
(1.5.323) sandehadvāparau cātha samau nirṇayaniścayau
children.translated_text:
## Awareness (2 synonyms), Reflection (3 synonyms), Reasoning (3 synonyms), Doubt (4 synonyms) ##
(1.5.320) <s>Cittābhoga</s> and <s>manaskāra</s> [mean awareness]; <s>carcā</s>, <s>saṃkhyā</s>, and <s>vicāraṇā</s> [mean reflection].
(1.5.321) <s>Vimarśa</s> and <s>bhāvanā</s> as well as <s>vāsanā</s> are also stated [as synonyms for contemplation/reflection].
(1.5.322) <s>Adhyāhāra</s>, <s>tarka</s>, and <s>ūha</s> [mean reasoning]; <s>vicikitsā</s> means doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>).
(1.5.323) <s>Sandeha</s> and <s>dvāpara</s> also [mean doubt]; then <s>nirṇaya</s> and <s>niścaya</s> are equivalent [meaning conclusion/certainty].

children.text:
## Heresy or atheism (2), Malice (2), Conclusion or theorem (2), Delusion (3)##
(1.5.324) mithyādṛṣṭirnāstikatā vyāpādo drohacintanam
(1.5.325) samau siddhāntarāddhāntau bhrāntirmithyāmatirbhramaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Heresy or atheism (2 synonyms), Malice (2 synonyms), Conclusion or theorem (2 synonyms), Delusion (3 synonyms) ##
(1.5.324) <s>Mithyādṛṣṭi</s> and <s>nāstikatā</s> [mean heresy/atheism]; <s>vyāpāda</s> and <s>drohacintana</s> [mean malice].
(1.5.325) <s>Siddhānta</s> and <s>rāddhānta</s> are equivalent [meaning established conclusion]; <s>bhrānti</s>, <s>mithyāmati</s>, and <s>bhrama</s> [mean delusion].

## Agreement (10 synonyms) ##
(1.5.326) <s>Saṃvid</s>, <s>āgū</s>, <s>pratijñāna</s>, <s>niyama</s>, <s>āśrava</s>, <s>saṃśrava</s>,
(1.5.327) <s>aṅgīkāra</s>, <s>abhyupagama</s>, <s>pratiśrava</s>, and <s>samādhi</s> [are synonyms for agreement/promise].

children.text:
## Spiritual knowledge (1), Worldly or profane knowledge (1) ##
(1.5.328) mokṣe dhīrjñānamanyatra vijñānaṃ śilpaśāstrayoḥ
children.translated_text:
## Spiritual knowledge (1 synonym), Worldly or profane knowledge (1 synonym) ##
(1.5.328) <s>Dhī</s> (intellect) in the context of liberation is <s>jñāna</s> (spiritual knowledge); elsewhere <s>vijñāna</s> [means] worldly knowledge, [used] in [the contexts of] craft and <s>śāstra</s>.

children.text:
##Salvation or liberation (8), Spiritual ignorance (4) ##
(1.5.329) muktiḥ kaivalyanirvāṇaśreyoniḥśreyasāmṛtam
(1.5.330) mokṣo 'pavargo 'thājñānamavidyāhaṃmatiḥ striyām
children.translated_text:
## Salvation or liberation (8), Spiritual ignorance (4) ##
(1.5.329) <s>Mukti</s>, <s>kaivalya</s>, <s>nirvāṇa</s>, <s>śreyas</s>, <s>niḥśreyasa</s>, <s>amṛta</s>,
(1.5.330) <s>mokṣa</s>, and <s>apavarga</s> [are synonyms for liberation]. Now, <s>ajñāna</s>, <s>avidyā</s>, and <s>ahaṃmati</s> [are synonyms for spiritual ignorance] — feminine.

children.text:
## (Listed) five sense objects (3), Sense organs (3), Intellectual organ (1)##
(1.5.331) rūpaṃ śabdo gandharasasparśāśca viṣayā amī
(1.5.332) gocarā indriyārthāśca hṛṣīkaṃ viṣayīndriyam
(1.5.333) karmendriyaṃ tu pāyvādi manonetrādi dhīndriyam
children.translated_text:
## (Listed) five sense objects (3), Sense organs (3), Intellectual organ (1) ##
(1.5.331) Form (<s>rūpa</s>), sound (<s>śabda</s>), smell (<s>gandha</s>), taste (<s>rasa</s>), and touch (<s>sparśa</s>) — these are the sense-objects (<s>viṣayas</s>).
(1.5.332) [They are also called] <s>gocara</s> and <s>indriyārtha</s>. <s>Hṛṣīka</s> is a sense-organ (<s>indriya</s>).
(1.5.333) The organs of action (<s>karmendriya</s>) are the excretory organ and the rest; mind (<s>manas</s>), eye (<s>netra</s>), and the rest are the organs of cognition (<s>dhīndriya</s>).

children.text:
## Astringent (2), Sweet (1), Salty (1) ##
(1.5.334) tuvarastu kaṣāyo 'strī madhuro lavaṇaḥ kaṭuḥ
children.translated_text:
## Astringent (2), Sweet (1), Salty (1) ##
(1.5.334) <s>Tuvara</s> [means] astringent (<s>kaṣāya</s>) — not feminine. <s>Madhura</s> is sweet; <s>lavaṇa</s> is salty; <s>kaṭu</s> is pungent.

children.text:
## Pungent (hot) (1), Sour (1), Tastes (all six) (1) ##
(1.5.335) tikto 'mlaśca rasāḥ puṃsi tadvatsu ṣaḍamī triṣu
children.translated_text:
## Pungent (hot) (1), Sour (1), Tastes (all six) (1) ##
(1.5.335) <s>Tikta</s> is bitter; <s>amla</s> is sour. The word <s>rasa</s> (taste) is masculine. These six [tastes], when qualifying [a substance], take all three genders.

children.text:
## Aroma (1), Extremely pleasant smell (1), Permeating smell (2) ##
(1.5.336) vimardotthe parimalo gandhe janamanohare
(1.5.337) āmodaḥ so 'tinirhārī vācyaliṅgatvamāguṇāt
(1.5.338) samākarṣī tu nirhārī surabhirghrāṇatarpaṇaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Aroma (1), Extremely pleasant smell (1), Permeating smell (2) ##
(1.5.336) <s>Parimala</s> is fragrance produced by friction; when a smell captivates the minds of people,
(1.5.337) it is [called] <s>āmoda</s>. That which is very permeating — [its] gender follows the qualified noun, because [it is] a quality.
(1.5.338) That which is attractive and permeating [is called] <s>nirhārī</s>. <s>Surabhi</s> means gratifying to the nose.

children.text:
## Aromatics (4), Breath-freshner (2), Foul smelling (2), Rotten (1) ##
(1.5.339) iṣṭagandhaḥ sugandhiḥ syādāmodī mukhavāsanaḥ
(1.5.340) pūtigandhastu durgandho visraṃ syādāmagandhi yat
children.translated_text:
## Aromatics (4), Breath-freshener (2), Foul smelling (2), Rotten (1) ##
(1.5.339) <s>Iṣṭagandha</s> and <s>sugandhi</s> [mean] pleasant-smelling. <s>Āmodī</s> and <s>mukhavāsana</s> [mean] breath-freshener.
(1.5.340) <s>Pūtigandha</s> [means] foul-smelling. <s>Visra</s> [means] that which has a raw or putrid smell.

children.text:
## White (16), Grey (off-white) (2), Black or dark blue (7) ##
(1.5.341) śuklaśubhraśuciśvetaviśadaśyetapāṇḍarāḥ
(1.5.342) avadātaḥ sito gauro 'valakṣo dhavalo 'rjunaḥ
(1.5.343) hariṇaḥ pāṇḍuraḥ pāṇḍurīṣatpāṇḍustu dhūsaraḥ
(1.5.344) kṛṣṇe nīlāsitaśyāmakālaśyāmalamecakāḥ
children.translated_text:
## White (16), Grey (off-white) (2), Black or dark blue (7) ##
(1.5.341) <s>Śukla</s>, <s>śubhra</s>, <s>śuci</s>, <s>śveta</s>, <s>viśada</s>, <s>śyeta</s>, <s>pāṇḍara</s>,
(1.5.342) <s>avadāta</s>, <s>sita</s>, <s>gaura</s>, <s>avalakṣa</s>, <s>dhavala</s>, <s>arjuna</s>,
(1.5.343) <s>hariṇa</s>, <s>pāṇḍura</s>, <s>pāṇḍu</s> [are all synonyms for white]. Slightly pale is <s>dhūsara</s> (grey).
(1.5.344) For black/dark blue: <s>nīla</s>, <s>asita</s>, <s>śyāma</s>, <s>kāla</s>, <s>śyāmala</s>, <s>mecaka</s>.

children.text:
## Yellow (3), Green (3), Red (2), Crimson (1) ##
(1.5.345) pīto gauro haridrābhaḥ palāśo harito harit
(1.5.346) lohito rohito raktaḥ śoṇaḥ kokanadacchaviḥ
children.translated_text:
## Yellow (3), Green (3), Red (2), Crimson (1) ##
(1.5.345) <s>Pīta</s>, <s>gaura</s>, <s>haridrābha</s> [are synonyms for yellow]. <s>Palāśa</s>, <s>harita</s>, <s>harit</s> [are synonyms for green].
(1.5.346) <s>Lohita</s>, <s>rohita</s>, <s>rakta</s> [mean red]. <s>Śoṇa</s> [means] crimson, having the complexion of the red lotus (<s>kokanada</s>).

children.text:
## Light pink (1), Dark pink (1), Brown (2), Purple (3) ##
(1.5.347) avyaktarāgastvaruṇaḥ śvetaraktastu pāṭalaḥ
(1.5.348) śyāvaḥ syātkapiśo dhūmradhūmalau kṛṣṇalohite
children.translated_text:
## Light pink (1), Dark pink (1), Brown (2), Purple (3) ##
(1.5.347) <s>Taruṇa</s> [means] of faint color (light pink). <s>Pāṭala</s> [means] white-red (pale pink).
(1.5.348) <s>Śyāva</s> and <s>kapiśa</s> [mean] brown. <s>Dhūmra</s> and <s>dhūmala</s> [mean] purple (dark red-black).

children.text:
## Tawny (6), variegated (6) ##
(1.5.349) kaḍāraḥ kapilaḥ piṅgapiśaṅgau kadrupiṅgalau
(1.5.350) citraṃ kirmīrakalmāṣaśabalaitāśca karbure
children.translated_text:
## Tawny (6), Variegated (6) ##
(1.5.349) <s>Kaḍāra</s>, <s>kapila</s>, <s>piṅga</s>, <s>piśaṅga</s>, <s>kadru</s>, <s>piṅgala</s> [mean tawny].
(1.5.350) <s>Citra</s>, <s>kirmīra</s>, <s>kalmāṣa</s>, <s>śabala</s>, <s>etā</s> [are synonyms for] variegated (<s>karbura</s>).

children.text:
## Colors as words are masculine, as adjectives follow nouns ##
(1.5.351) guṇe śuklādayaḥ puṃsi guṇiliṅgāstu tadvati
children.translated_text:
## Colors as words are masculine; as adjectives, they follow the noun ##
(1.5.351) When denoting a quality [i.e., color as abstract noun], <s>śukla</s> and the rest are masculine; when [modifying] something possessing that quality, they follow the gender of the qualified noun.
<s>Śabdavarga</s> (Section on Speech).

children.text:
## Talk or speech or language (13) ##
(1.6.352) brāhmī tu bhāratī bhāṣā gīrvāgvāṇī sarasvatī
(1.6.353) vyāhāra uktirlapitaṃ bhāṣitaṃ vacanaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Talk or speech or language (13) ##
(1.6.352) <s>Brāhmī</s>, <s>Bhāratī</s>, <s>bhāṣā</s>, <s>gīr</s>, <s>vāk</s>, <s>vāṇī</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>,
(1.6.353) <s>vyāhāra</s>, <s>ukti</s>, <s>lapita</s>, <s>bhāṣita</s>, <s>vacana</s>, <s>vacas</s> [are synonyms for speech/language].

children.text:
## Corrupted (or changed) speech (2), word (1), Sentence (1) ##
(1.6.354) apabhraṃśo 'paśabdaḥ syācchāstre śabdastu vācakaḥ
(1.6.355) tiṅ subantacayo vākyaṃ kriyā vā kārakānvitā
children.translated_text:
## Corrupted (or changed) speech (2), Word (1), Sentence (1) ##
(1.6.354) <s>Apabhraṃśa</s> and <s>apaśabda</s> [mean] corrupted speech. In grammar, <s>śabda</s> is a word (signifier).
(1.6.355) A sentence (<s>vākya</s>) is a collection of <s>tiṅ</s> (verb-endings) and <s>subanta</s> (noun-endings) — or [it is defined as] an action (<s>kriyā</s>) joined with case-relations (<s>kāraka</s>).

children.text:
## Vedas (scriptures) (4), Prescribed way of life (dharme) (1) ##
(1.6.356) śrutiḥ strī veda āmnāyastrayī dharmastu tadvidhiḥ
children.translated_text:
## Vedas (scriptures) (4), Prescribed way of life (dharma) (1) ##
(1.6.356) <s>Śruti</s> (feminine), <s>Veda</s>, <s>āmnāya</s>, <s>trayī</s> [are synonyms for scripture]. <s>Dharma</s> means its (<s>Veda</s>'s) prescribed code.

children.text:
## Three vedas (listed) (1), Subsidiary vedas (vedanga) (1), Om (2) ##
(1.6.357) striyāmṛk sāmayajuṣī iti vedāstrayastrayī
(1.6.358) śikṣetyādi śruteraṅgamoṅkārapraṇavau samau
children.translated_text:
## Three Vedas (listed) (1), Subsidiary Vedas (Vedāṅga) (1), Om (2) ##
(1.6.357) <s>Ṛk</s>, <s>Sāman</s>, and <s>Yajus</s> (feminine) — these three <s>Vedas</s> are the <s>trayī</s>.
(1.6.358) <s>Śikṣā</s> and the rest are the limbs of <s>śruti</s>. <s>Oṃkāra</s> and <s>praṇava</s> are synonymous.

children.text:
## History (2), Vedic accents (1), Logic (1), Ethics (1) ##
(1.6.359) itihāsaḥ purāvṛttamudāttādyāstrayaḥ svarāḥ
(1.6.360) ānvīkṣikī daṇḍanītistarkavidyārthaśāstrayoḥ
children.translated_text:
## History (2), Vedic accents (1), Logic (1), Ethics (1) ##
(1.6.359) <s>Itihāsa</s> and <s>purāvṛtta</s> [mean history]. <s>Udātta</s> and the rest — the three [types of] accents (<s>svara</s>).
(1.6.360) <s>Ānvīkṣikī</s> [means logic]; <s>daṇḍanīti</s> [means] political science. <s>Tarkavidyā</s> and <s>arthaśāstra</s> [are synonyms for the two respectively].

children.text:
## Tale (1), Epic story (1), Story (2), Riddle (2) ##
(1.6.361) ākhyāyikopalabdhārthā purāṇaṃ pañcalakṣaṇam
(1.6.362) prabandhakalpanā kathā pravahlikā prahelikā
children.translated_text:
## Tale (1), Epic story (1), Story (2), Riddle (2) ##
(1.6.361) <s>Ākhyāyikā</s> [means] a tale with established meaning. <s>Purāṇa</s> has five characteristics.
(1.6.362) <s>Kathā</s> [means] a story that is an imaginative composition. <s>Pravahlikā</s> and <s>prahelikā</s> [mean] riddle.

children.text:
## Social code (Dharma) (1), Compendium (2) ##
(1.6.363) smṛtistu dharmasaṃhitā samāhṛtistu saṃgrahaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Social code (Dharma) (1), Compendium (2) ##
(1.6.363) <s>Smṛti</s> is a collection of <s>dharma</s> (code of conduct). <s>Samāhṛti</s> and <s>saṃgraha</s> [mean] compendium.

children.text:
## Poetic challenge line for completion (1), Rumor (2) ##
(1.6.364) samasyā tu samāsārthā kiṃvadantī janaśrutiḥ
children.translated_text:
## Poetic challenge line for completion (1), Rumor (2) ##
(1.6.364) <s>Samasyā</s> is a verse requiring completion. <s>Kiṃvadantī</s> and <s>janaśruti</s> [mean] rumor.

children.text:
## News (4), Name (6), Call or summons (3), Collective call (1) ##
(1.6.365) vārtā pravṛttirvṛttānta udantaḥ syādathāhvayaḥ
(1.6.366) ākhyāhve abhidhānaṃ ca nāmadheyaṃ ca nāma ca
(1.6.367) hūtirākāraṇāhvānaṃ saṃhūtirbahubhiḥ kṛtā
children.translated_text:
## News (4), Name (6), Call or summons (3), Collective call (1) ##
(1.6.365) <s>Vārtā</s>, <s>pravṛtti</s>, <s>vṛttānta</s>, and <s>udanta</s> [mean news]. Now, <s>āhvaya</s>,
(1.6.366) <s>ākhyā</s>, <s>āhva</s>, <s>abhidhāna</s>, <s>nāmadheya</s>, and <s>nāman</s> [mean name].
(1.6.367) <s>Hūti</s>, <s>ākāraṇa</s>, and <s>āhvāna</s> [mean summons]. <s>Saṃhūti</s> is a summons made by many.

children.text:
## Dispute or debate (2), Preface or introduction (2) ##
(1.6.368) vivādo vyavahāraḥ syādupanyāsastu vāṅmukham
children.translated_text:
## Dispute or debate (2), Preface or introduction (2) ##
(1.6.368) <s>Vivāda</s> and <s>vyavahāra</s> [mean dispute/legal proceeding]. <s>Upanyāsa</s> and <s>vāṅmukha</s> [mean introduction].

children.text:
## Illustration or example (2), Oath (2), Question (3), Answer (2) ##
(1.6.369) upoddhāta udāhāraḥ śapanaṃ śapathaḥ pumān
(1.6.370) praśno 'nuyogaḥ pṛcchā ca prativākyottare same
children.translated_text:
## Illustration or example (2), Oath (2), Question (3), Answer (2) ##
(1.6.369) <s>Upoddhāta</s> and <s>udāhāra</s> [mean illustration/example]. <s>Śapana</s> and <s>śapatha</s> (masculine) [mean oath].
(1.6.370) <s>Praśna</s>, <s>anuyoga</s>, and <s>pṛcchā</s> [mean question]. <s>Prativākya</s> and <s>uttara</s> are synonymous [meaning answer].

children.text:
## Groundless demand (2), False accusation (2), Rapture or roar (1)##
(1.6.371) mithyābhiyogo 'bhyākhyānamatha mithyābhiśaṃsanam
(1.6.372) abhiśāpaḥ praṇādastu śabdaḥ syādanurāgajaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Groundless demand (2), False accusation (2), Rapture or roar (1) ##
(1.6.371) <s>Mithyābhiyoga</s> and <s>abhyākhyāna</s> [mean groundless demand/false claim]. Now, <s>mithyābhiśaṃsana</s>
(1.6.372) and <s>abhiśāpa</s> [mean false accusation]. <s>Praṇāda</s> means a sound born of rapture.

children.text:
## Fame (3), Praise (4), Repetition (1), Shouting (2) ##
(1.6.373) yaśaḥ kīrtiḥ samajñā ca stavaḥ stotraṃ stutirnutiḥ
(1.6.374) āmreḍitaṃ dvistriruktamuccairghuṣṭaṃ tu ghoṣaṇā
children.translated_text:
## Fame (3), Praise (4), Repetition (1), Shouting (2) ##
(1.6.373) <s>Yaśas</s>, <s>kīrti</s>, and <s>samajñā</s> [mean fame]. <s>Stava</s>, <s>stotra</s>, <s>stuti</s>, and <s>nuti</s> [mean praise].
(1.6.374) <s>Āmreḍita</s> [means] saying twice or thrice (repetition). <s>Ghuṣṭa</s> (used with 'uccais') and <s>ghoṣaṇā</s> [mean] loud proclamation.

children.text:
## Trembling (of speech in stress) (1), Censure, blame or contempt (10) ##
(1.6.375) kākuḥ striyāṃ vikāro yaḥ śokabhītyādibhirdhvaneḥ
(1.6.376) avarṇākṣepanirvādaparīvādāpavādavat.
(1.6.377) upakrośo jugupsā ca kutsā nindā ca garhaṇe
children.translated_text:
## Trembling (of speech in stress) (1), Censure, blame or contempt (10) ##
(1.6.375) <s>Kāku</s> (feminine) is the alteration of sound [i.e., voice] due to grief, fear, and the like.
(1.6.376-377) <s>Avarṇa</s>, <s>ākṣepa</s>, <s>nirvāda</s>, <s>parīvāda</s>, <s>apavāda</s>, <s>upakrośa</s>, <s>jugupsā</s>, <s>kutsā</s>, <s>nindā</s>, and <s>garhaṇa</s> [are ten synonyms for censure/blame].

children.text:
## Harsh speech (2), Reproach (1), Admonition or gossip (1) ##
(1.6.378) pāruṣyamativādaḥ syād bhartsanaṃ tvapakāragīḥ
(1.6.379) yaḥ saninda upālambhastatra syātparibhāṣaṇam
children.translated_text:
## Harsh speech (2), Reproach (1), Admonition or gossip (1) ##
(1.6.378) <s>Pāruṣya</s> and <s>ativāda</s> [mean harsh speech]. <s>Bhartsana</s> means speech of reproach.
(1.6.379) A censorious admonition (<s>upālambha</s>) [is called] <s>paribhāṣaṇa</s>.

children.text:
## Accusation (of adultery) (1), Conversation (2), Rambling (speech) (1) ##
(1.6.380) tatra tvākṣāraṇā yaḥ syādākrośo maithunaṃ prati
(1.6.381) syādābhāṣaṇamālāpaḥ pralāpo 'narthakaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Accusation (of adultery) (1), Conversation (2), Rambling (speech) (1) ##
(1.6.380) <s>Ākṣāraṇā</s> therein is the abuse (<s>ākrośa</s>) pertaining to sexual misconduct.
(1.6.381) <s>Ābhāṣaṇa</s> and <s>ālāpa</s> [mean conversation]. <s>Pralāpa</s> is meaningless speech.

children.text:
## repetitious speech (2), Lamentation (2) ##
(1.6.382) anulāpo muhurbhāṣā vilāpaḥ paridevanam
children.translated_text:
## Repetitious speech (2), Lamentation (2) ##
(1.6.382) <s>Anulāpa</s> is repeated speech (<s>muhurbhāṣā</s>). <s>Vilāpa</s> and <s>paridevanā</s> [mean lamentation].

children.text:
## Quarrel (2), Familiar or confidential conversation (1) ##
(1.6.383) vipralāpo virodhoktiḥ saṃlāpo bhāṣaṇaṃ mithaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Quarrel (2), Familiar or confidential conversation (1) ##
(1.6.383) <s>Vipralāpa</s> and <s>virodhokti</s> [mean quarrel/contradictory speech]. <s>Saṃlāpa</s> means mutual conversation.

children.text:
## Good speech (2), Denial or excuse (2), Objection (3), Cursing (3) ##(1.6.384) supralāpaḥ suvacanamapalāpastu nihnavaḥ
(1.6.385) codyamākṣepābhiyogau śāpākrośau dureṣaṇā
children.translated_text:
## Good speech (2), Denial or excuse (2), Objection (3), Cursing (3) ##
(1.6.384) <s>Supralāpa</s> and <s>suvacana</s> [mean good speech]. <s>Apalāpa</s> and <s>nihnava</s> [mean denial/concealment].
(1.6.385) <s>Codya</s>, <s>ākṣepa</s>, and <s>abhiyoga</s> [mean objection]. <s>Śāpa</s>, <s>ākrośa</s>, and <s>dureṣaṇā</s> [mean cursing].

children.text:
## Sweet-talk (3), Message (2) ##
(1.6.386) astrī cāṭu caṭu ślāghā premṇā mithyāvikatthanam
(1.6.387) sandeśavāgvācikaṃ syādvāgbhedāstu triṣūttare
children.translated_text:
## Sweet-talk (3), Message (2) ##
(1.6.386) <s>Cāṭu</s>, <s>caṭu</s> (not feminine), and <s>ślāghā</s> [mean sweet-talk, i.e.,] false boasting out of affection.
(1.6.387) <s>Sandeśavāk</s> and <s>vācika</s> [mean message]. The following types of speech take all three genders.

children.text: ## Following adjectives of speech take appropriate genders ##
