children.translated_text: ## Following adjectives of speech take appropriate genders ##

children.text:
## Inauspicious (1), Auspicious (1), Very sweet (1), Proper or coherent (2) ##
(1.6.388) ruśatī vāgakalyāṇī syātkalyā tu śubhātmikā
(1.6.389) atyarthamadhuraṃ sāntvaṃ saṃgataṃ hṛdayaṅgamam
children.translated_text:
## Inauspicious (1), Auspicious (1), Very sweet (1), Proper or coherent (2) ##
(1.6.388) <s>Ruśatī</s> is inauspicious speech. <s>Kalyā</s> is that which is auspicious.
(1.6.389) <s>Sāntva</s> means exceedingly sweet [speech]. <s>Saṃgata</s> and <s>hṛdayaṃgama</s> [mean coherent/touching speech].

children.text:
## Harsh (2), Obscene or crude (2), Pleasing and true (1), Contradictory (2)##
(1.6.390) niṣṭhuraṃ paruṣaṃ grāmyamaślīlaṃ sūnṛtaṃ priye
(1.6.391) satye 'tha saṃkulakliṣṭe parasparaparāhate
children.translated_text:
## Harsh (2), Obscene or crude (2), Pleasing and true (1), Contradictory (2) ##
(1.6.390) <s>Niṣṭhura</s> and <s>paruṣa</s> [mean harsh]. <s>Grāmya</s> and <s>aślīla</s> [mean obscene]. <s>Sūnṛta</s> is [speech that is both] pleasing and
(1.6.391) true. <s>Saṃkula</s> and <s>kliṣṭa</s> [mean] mutually contradictory (<s>parasparaparāhata</s>).

children.text:
## Slurred (1), Fast (1), Sputtered (1), Meaningless (1) ##
(1.6.392) luptavarṇapadaṃ grastaṃ nirastaṃ tvaritoditam
(1.6.393) jambūkṛtaṃ saniṣṭīvamabaddhaṃ syādanarthakam
children.translated_text:
## Slurred (1), Fast (1), Sputtered (1), Meaningless (1) ##
(1.6.392) <s>Grasta</s> [means speech with] dropped letters and words. <s>Nirasta</s> is [speech] uttered hurriedly.
(1.6.393) <s>Jambūkṛta</s> is [speech] with spitting. <s>Abaddha</s> means meaningless.

children.text:
## Inappropriate (2), Oxymoron (1), Sarcastic (2), Loving (1) ##
(1.6.394) anakṣaramavācyaṃ syādāhataṃ tu mṛṣārthakam
(1.6.395) solluṭhanaṃ tu sotprāsaṃ maṇitaṃ ratikūjitam
children.translated_text:
## Inappropriate (2), Oxymoron (1), Sarcastic (2), Loving (1) ##
(1.6.394) <s>Anakṣara</s> and <s>avācya</s> [mean inappropriate speech]. <s>Āhata</s> means [speech] with false meaning.
(1.6.395) <s>Solluṭhana</s> and <s>sotprāsa</s> [mean sarcastic speech]. <s>Maṇita</s> is [speech as] the cooing of love.

children.text:
## Plain, pleasant, clear (5), Unclear or garbled (2), False (1) ##
(1.6.396) śrāvyaṃ hṛdyaṃ manohāri vispaṣṭaṃ prakaṭoditam
(1.6.397) atha mliṣṭamavispaṣṭaṃ vitathaṃ tvanṛtaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Plain, pleasant, clear (5), Unclear or garbled (2), False (1) ##
(1.6.396) <s>Śrāvya</s>, <s>hṛdya</s>, <s>manohāri</s>, <s>vispaṣṭa</s>, and <s>prakaṭodita</s> [mean pleasant/clear speech].
(1.6.397) Now, <s>mliṣṭa</s> and <s>avispaṣṭa</s> [mean unclear]. <s>Vitatha</s> and <s>anṛta</s> [mean false] speech.

children.text:
## True (4)##
(1.6.398) satyaṃ tathyamṛtaṃ samyagamūni triṣu tadvati
children.translated_text:
## True (4) ##
(1.6.398) <s>Satya</s>, <s>tathya</s>, <s>ṛta</s>, <s>samyak</s> — these [mean true]; in all three genders when qualifying something possessing that quality.

children.text:
## Sound (17), (Sound of) clothes or leaves (1) ##
(1.6.399) śabde ninādaninadadhvanidhvānaravasvanāḥ
(1.6.400) svānanirghoṣanirhrādanādanisvānanisvanāḥ
(1.6.401) āravārāvasaṃrāvavirāvā atha marmaraḥ
children.translated_text:
## Sound (17), (Sound of) clothes or leaves (1) ##
(1.6.399-401) <s>Nināda</s>, <s>ninada</s>, <s>dhvani</s>, <s>dhvāna</s>, <s>rava</s>, <s>svana</s>, <s>svāna</s>, <s>nirghoṣa</s>, <s>nirhrāda</s>, <s>nāda</s>, <s>nisvāna</s>, <s>nisvana</s>, <s>ārava</s>, <s>ārāva</s>, <s>saṃrāva</s>, <s>virāva</s> [are 17 synonyms for sound]. Now, <s>marmara</s> [is the sound of] clothes or leaves.

children.text:
## (Sound of) ornaments (1), (sound of) string instruments (5), Same but louder (2) ##
(1.6.402) svanite vastraparṇānāṃ bhūṣaṇānāṃ tu śiñjitam
(1.6.403) nikvāṇo nikvaṇaḥ kvāṇaḥ kvaṇaḥ kvaṇanamityapi
(1.6.404) vīṇāyāḥ kvaṇite prādeḥ prakvāṇaprakvaṇādayaḥ
children.translated_text:
## (Sound of) ornaments (1), (Sound of) string instruments (5), Same but louder (2) ##
(1.6.402) <s>Śiñjita</s> is the sound of ornaments.
(1.6.403-404) <s>Nikvāṇa</s>, <s>nikvaṇa</s>, <s>kvāṇa</s>, <s>kvaṇa</s>, and <s>kvaṇana</s> are [the sounds] of string instruments. When of the <s>vīṇā</s> specifically: <s>prakvāṇa</s>, <s>prakvaṇa</s>, etc. [with the prefix <s>pra</s>].

children.text:
## Uproar (2), Uproar by birds (1), Echo (2), Singing (2) ##
(1.6.405) kolāhalaḥ kalakalastiraścāṃ vāśitaṃ rutam
(1.6.406) strī pratiśrutpratidhvāne gītaṃ gānamime same
children.translated_text:
## Uproar (2), Uproar by birds (1), Echo (2), Singing (2) ##
(1.6.405) <s>Kolāhala</s> and <s>kalakala</s> [mean uproar]. <s>Vāśita</s> and <s>ruta</s> are the sounds of animals.
(1.6.406) <s>Pratiśrut</s> and <s>pratidhvāni</s> (feminine) [mean echo]. <s>Gīta</s> and <s>gāna</s> are synonymous [meaning singing].
<s>Nāṭyavarga</s> (Section on Drama).

children.text: ## The seven notes. These are respectively natural sounds of: ##
children.translated_text: ## The seven notes. These are respectively natural sounds of: ##

children.text: ## Elephants, Cows, Goats, Peacocks, Curlews (krauncha), Horses, Cuckoos ##
children.translated_text: ## Elephants, Cows, Goats, Peacocks, Curlews (<s>krauñca</s>), Horses, Cuckoos ##

children.text: ## In usual notation, these are: BDECFAG ##
children.translated_text: ## In usual notation, these are: B D E C F A G ##

children.text:
## Minute tone (1), Pleasing soft tone (1), Medium pitch (1), High pitch (1) ##
(1.7.407) niṣādarṣabhagāndhāraṣaḍjamadhyamadhaivatāḥ
(1.7.408) pañcamaścetyamī sapta tantrīkaṇṭhotthitāḥ svarāḥ
(1.7.409) kākalī tu kale sūkṣme dhvanī tu madhurāsphuṭe
(1.7.410) kalo mandrastu gambhīre tāro 'tyuccaistrayastriṣu
children.translated_text:
## Minute tone (1), Pleasing soft tone (1), Medium pitch (1), High pitch (1) ##
(1.7.407-408) <s>Niṣāda</s>, <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Gāndhāra</s>, <s>Ṣaḍja</s>, <s>Madhyama</s>, <s>Dhaivata</s>, and <s>Pañcama</s> — these are the seven <s>svaras</s> (notes) produced from strings or the throat.
(1.7.409) <s>Kākalī</s> is a minute, subtle tone. <s>Dhvanī</s> is a sweet but indistinct [tone].
(1.7.410) <s>Kala</s> and <s>mandra</s> [mean] deep-pitched. <s>Tāra</s> [means] very high-pitched — these three take all three genders.

children.text:
## In the stomach form 22 low tones (Shruti). They become medium or high pitched if made in throat or head.##
(1.7.411) nṛṇāmurasi madhyastho dvāviṃśatividho dhvaniḥ
(1.7.412) sa mandraḥ kaṇṭhamadhyasthastāraḥ śirasi gīyate
children.translated_text:
## In the stomach form 22 low tones (Śruti). They become medium or high pitched if made in throat or head. ##
(1.7.411) Sound of twenty-two kinds, produced in the middle region [i.e., the chest] of humans —
(1.7.412) that is <s>mandra</s> (low). Produced from the throat it is <s>madhyama</s> (middle); that sung from the head is <s>tāra</s> (high).

children.text:
## Harmony (1), Lute (veena) (3), Seven stringed lute (1) ##
(1.7.413) samanvitalayastvekatālo vīṇā tu vallakī
(1.7.414) tripañcī sā tu tantrībhiḥ saptabhiḥ parivādinī
children.translated_text:
## Harmony (1), Lute (vīṇā) (3), Seven-stringed lute (1) ##
(1.7.413) <s>Ekatāla</s> [means] having rhythm (<s>laya</s>) in unison. <s>Vīṇā</s> and <s>vallakī</s> [are names for the lute].
(1.7.414) <s>Tripañcī</s> [is another name]. That [vīṇā] with seven strings is [called] <s>parivādinī</s>.

children.text:
## String instrument (1), Drum instrument (1), Wind instrument (1), Bell or gong (1) ##
(1.7.415) tataṃ vīṇādikaṃ vādyamānaddhaṃ murajādikam
(1.7.416) vaṃśādikaṃ tu suṣiraṃ kāṃsyatālādikaṃ ghanam
children.translated_text:
## String instrument (1), Drum instrument (1), Wind instrument (1), Bell or gong (1) ##
(1.7.415) <s>Tata</s> [means] stringed instruments such as the <s>vīṇā</s>. <s>Ānaddha</s> [means] covered-skin instruments such as the <s>muraja</s>.
(1.7.416) <s>Suṣira</s> [means] hollow/wind instruments such as the flute. <s>Ghana</s> [means] solid instruments like cymbals and gongs.

children.text:
## Any of these four instruments (2), Twofaced drum (2), Its three types ##
(1.7.417) caturvidhamidaṃ vādyaṃ vāditrātodyanāmakam
(1.7.418) mṛdaṅgā murajā bhedāstvaṅkyāliṅgyordhvakāstrayaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Any of these four instruments (2), Two-faced drum (2), Its three types ##
(1.7.417) This fourfold [classification of] musical instruments is also called <s>vāditra</s> and <s>ātodya</s>.
(1.7.418) <s>Mṛdaṅga</s> and <s>muraja</s> [are two-faced drums]; their three types are <s>aṅkya</s> (placed on the lap), <s>āliṅgya</s> (embraced), and <s>ūrdhvaka</s> (vertical).

children.text:
## Large drum (2), Kettle drum (2), Large kettle drum (2), Bow (for playing string instrument) (1) ##
(1.7.419) syād yaśaḥpaṭaho ḍhakkā bherī strī dundubhiḥ pumān
(1.7.420) ānakaḥ paṭaho 'strī syāt koṇo vīṇādi vādanam
children.translated_text:
## Large drum (2 synonyms), Kettle drum (2 synonyms), Large kettle drum (2 synonyms), Bow for playing string instrument (1 synonym) ##
(1.7.419) <s>Yaśaḥpaṭaha</s> and <s>ḍhakkā</s> [mean a large drum]; <s>bherī</s> (feminine) and <s>dundubhi</s> (masculine) [mean kettle drum].
(1.7.420) <s>Ānaka</s> and <s>paṭaha</s> (not feminine) [mean a large kettle drum]; <s>koṇa</s> [is] the bow for playing <s>vīṇā</s> and other [stringed instruments].

children.text:
## Parts of the lute: Neck (1), The bowl (2) ##
(1.7.421) vīṇādaṇḍaḥ pravālaḥ syāt kakubhastu prasevakaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Parts of the lute: Neck (1 synonym), The bowl (2 synonyms) ##
(1.7.421) The neck of the <s>vīṇā</s> (lute) is <s>pravāla</s>; the bowl is <s>kakubha</s> or <s>prasevaka</s>.

children.text:
Six names of other special drums, (Female) dancer (2) ## The body (1), String attachment (1) ##
(1.7.422) kolambakastu kāyo 'syā upanāho nibandhanam
children.translated_text:
## The body (1 synonym), String attachment (1 synonym) ##
(1.7.422) <s>Kolambaka</s> is its body; <s>upanāha</s> is the binding [of strings]; <s>nibandhana</s> [is also the string attachment].

children.text:
186
(1.7.423) vādyaprabhedā ḍamarumaḍḍuḍiṇḍimajharjharāḥ
(1.7.424) mardalaḥ paṇavo 'nye ca nartakīlāsike same
children.translated_text:
## Six names of other special drums, (Female) dancer (2 synonyms) ##
(1.7.423) Types of percussion instruments: <s>ḍamaru</s>, <s>maḍḍu</s>, <s>ḍiṇḍima</s>, <s>jharjhara</s>,
(1.7.424) <s>mardala</s>, <s>paṇava</s>, and others; <s>nartakī</s> and <s>lāsikā</s> are equivalent [both mean female dancer].

children.text:
## Dancing speeds low, medium, high, Beating time(1), Musical pause or rest (1)##
(1.7.425) vilambitaṃ drutaṃ madhyaṃ tattvamogho ghanaṃ kramāt
(1.7.426) tālaḥ kālakriyāmānaṃ layaḥ sāmyamamathāstriyām
children.translated_text:
## Dancing speeds: low, medium, high; Beating time (1 synonym), Musical pause or rest (1 synonym) ##
(1.7.425) <s>Vilambita</s> (slow), <s>druta</s> (fast), <s>madhya</s> (medium) [are the three tempos]; <s>tattva</s>, <s>ogha</s>, <s>ghana</s> [are their corresponding densities], in order.
(1.7.426) <s>Tāla</s> is the measure of time-keeping; <s>laya</s> is evenness (not feminine) [i.e., musical pause or rest].

children.text:
## Dance (6), The musical arts (dance, song, instrument) (1) ##
(1.7.427) tāṇḍavaṃ naṭanaṃ nāṭyaṃ lāsyaṃ nṛtyaṃ ca nartane
(1.7.428) tauryatrikaṃ nṛtyagītavādyaṃ nāṭyamidaṃ trayam
children.translated_text:
## Dance (6 synonyms), The musical arts (dance, song, instrument) (1 synonym) ##
(1.7.427) <s>Tāṇḍava</s>, <s>naṭana</s>, <s>nāṭya</s>, <s>lāsya</s>, <s>nṛtya</s> [are synonyms for dance/dancing].
(1.7.428) <s>Tauryatrika</s> [means] the triad of dance, song, and instrumental music; this [triad] is [also called] <s>nāṭya</s>.

children.text:
## Female impersonator dancer in drama (3), Courtesan (1) ##
(1.7.429) bhrakuṃsaśca bhrukuṃsaśca bhrūkuṃsaśceti nartakaḥ
(1.7.430) strīveṣadhārī puruṣo nāṭyoktau gaṇikāñjukā
children.translated_text:
## Female impersonator dancer in drama (3 synonyms), Courtesan (1 synonym) ##
(1.7.429) <s>Bhrakuṃsa</s>, <s>bhrukuṃsa</s>, and <s>bhrūkuṃsa</s> — a dancer
(1.7.430) who is a man wearing women's dress; in dramatic usage, <s>gaṇikā</s> [is called] <s>añjukā</s>.

children.text:
## Husband of sister (1), Learned man (1), Father (1), Prince (2)##
(1.7.431) bhaginīpatirāvutto bhāvo vidvānathāvukaḥ
(1.7.432) janako yuvarājastu kumāro bhartṛdārakaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Husband of sister (1 synonym), Learned man (1 synonym), Father (1 synonym), Prince (2 synonyms) ##
(1.7.431) A sister's husband is <s>āvutta</s>; <s>bhāva</s> [means] a learned man; then <s>āvuka</s>
(1.7.432) [means] father; <s>yuvarāja</s> and <s>kumāra</s> are [both names for] the son of the king (prince) [or] <s>bhartṛdāraka</s>.

children.text:
## King (2), Princess (1), Queen (1), Other wives of a king (1) ##
(1.7.433) rājā bhaṭṭārako devastatsutā bhartṛdārikā
(1.7.434) devī kṛtābhiṣekāyāmitarāsu tu bhaṭṭinī
children.translated_text:
## King (2 synonyms), Princess (1 synonym), Queen (1 synonym), Other wives of a king (1 synonym) ##
(1.7.433) <s>Rājan</s> [is also called] <s>bhaṭṭāraka</s> and <s>deva</s>; his daughter is <s>bhartṛdārikā</s> (princess).
(1.7.434) <s>Devī</s> [means] the consecrated queen; for the other [wives], <s>bhaṭṭinī</s> [is used].

children.text:
## Interjection for a forbidden act (1), King's brother-in-law (1) ##
(1.7.435) abrahmaṇyamavadhyoktau rājaśyālastu rāṣṭriyaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Interjection for a forbidden act (1 synonym), King's brother-in-law (1 synonym) ##
(1.7.435) <s>Abrahmaṇya</s> [is the exclamation] at the mention of a forbidden act; the king's brother-in-law is <s>rāṣṭriya</s>.

children.text:
## Mother (1), Young lass (2), Venerable man (1), Catastrophe or end of drama (2) ##
(1.7.436) ambā mātātha bālā syādvāsūrāryastu māriṣaḥ
(1.7.437) attikā bhaginī jyeṣṭhā niṣṭhā nirvahaṇe same
## Vocatives for different female servants (1) each, Gesture (2), Expressive gesture (2) ##
(1.7.438) haṇḍe hañje halāhvāne nīcāṃ ceṭīṃ sakhīṃ prati
(1.7.439) aṅgahāro 'ṅgavikṣepo vyañjakābhinayau samau
children.translated_text:
## Mother (1 synonym), Young lass (2 synonyms), Venerable man (1 synonym), Catastrophe or end of drama (2 synonyms) ##
(1.7.436) <s>Ambā</s> [means] mother; then <s>bālā</s> and <s>vāsūra</s> [mean a young girl]; <s>ārya</s> and <s>māriṣa</s> [mean a venerable man].
(1.7.437) <s>Attikā</s> [means] elder sister; <s>niṣṭhā</s> and <s>nirvahaṇa</s> are equivalent [meaning the conclusion/catastrophe of a drama].
## Vocatives for different female servants (1 each), Gesture (2 synonyms), Expressive gesture (2 synonyms) ##
(1.7.438) <s>Haṇḍe</s>, <s>hañje</s>, <s>halā</s> [are forms of address] toward a low maidservant and a female friend [respectively].
(1.7.439) <s>Aṅgahāra</s> (bodily movement) and <s>aṅgavikṣepa</s> [are synonyms for gesture]; <s>vyañjaka</s> and <s>abhinaya</s> are equivalent [meaning expressive acting].

children.text:
## Acting by body or expression (1), Eight types of emotions (rasa) listed ##
(1.7.440) nirvṛtte tvaṅgasattvābhyāṃ dve triṣvāṅgikasāttvike
(1.7.441) śṛṅgāravīrakaruṇādbhutahāsyabhayānakāḥ
children.translated_text:
## Acting by body or expression (1 synonym), Eight types of emotions (rasa) listed ##
(1.7.440) When produced by body and inner feeling respectively, both [take the adjective] <s>āṅgika</s> and <s>sāttvika</s> in all three genders.
(1.7.441) <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), <s>vīra</s> (heroic), <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic), <s>adbhuta</s> (marvelous), <s>hāsya</s> (comic), <s>bhayānaka</s> (fearful),

children.text:
## Love emotion (3), Heroism (2), Tenderness (7), Merriment (3), Disgust(2) ##
(1.7.442) bībhatsaraudrau ca rasāḥ śṛṅgāraḥ śucirujjvalaḥ
(1.7.443) utsāhavardhano vīraḥ kāruṇyaṃ karuṇā ghṛṇā
(1.7.444) kṛpā dayānukampā syādanukrośo 'pyatho hasaḥ
(1.7.445) hāso hāsyaṃ ca bībhatsaṃ vikṛtaṃ triṣvidaṃ dvayam
children.translated_text:
## Love emotion (3 synonyms), Heroism (2 synonyms), Tenderness (7 synonyms), Merriment (3 synonyms), Disgust (2 synonyms) ##
(1.7.442) <s>bībhatsa</s> (disgusting), and <s>raudra</s> (furious) — these are the [eight] <s>rasas</s>. <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> [is also called] <s>śuci</s> and <s>ujjvala</s>.
(1.7.443) <s>Utsāhavardhana</s> [is a synonym for] <s>vīra</s> (heroic); <s>kāruṇya</s>, <s>karuṇā</s>, <s>ghṛṇā</s>,
(1.7.444) <s>kṛpā</s>, <s>dayā</s>, <s>anukampā</s>, and <s>anukrośa</s> [are synonyms for compassion/tenderness]; then <s>hasa</s>,
(1.7.445) <s>hāsa</s>, and <s>hāsya</s> [mean laughter/merriment]; <s>bībhatsa</s> and <s>vikṛta</s> [mean disgust] — this [latter pair used] in all three genders.

children.text:
## Wonderment (4), Terror (9), Anger or horror (2), Fear (6) ##
(1.7.446) vismayo 'dbhutamāścaryaṃ citramapyatha bhairavam
(1.7.447) dāruṇaṃ bhīṣaṇaṃ bhīṣmaṃ ghoraṃ bhīmaṃ bhayānakam
(1.7.448) bhayaṅkaraṃ pratibhayaṃ raudraṃ tūgramamī triṣu
(1.7.449) caturdaśa darastrāso bhītirbhīḥ sādhvasaṃ bhayam
children.translated_text:
## Wonderment (4 synonyms), Terror (9 synonyms), Anger or horror (2 synonyms), Fear (6 synonyms) ##
(1.7.446) <s>Vismaya</s>, <s>adbhuta</s>, <s>āścarya</s>, and <s>citra</s> [mean wonderment]; then <s>bhairava</s>,
(1.7.447) <s>dāruṇa</s>, <s>bhīṣaṇa</s>, <s>bhīṣma</s>, <s>ghora</s>, <s>bhīma</s>, <s>bhayānaka</s>,
(1.7.448) <s>bhayaṅkara</s>, <s>pratibhaya</s> [all mean terrible/terrifying]; <s>raudra</s> means fierce (<s>ugra</s>) — these [are used] in all three genders.
(1.7.449) [There are] fourteen [synonyms for fear]; <s>dara</s>, <s>trāsa</s>, <s>bhīti</s>, <s>bhī</s>, <s>sādhvasa</s>, and <s>bhaya</s> [are six of them].

children.text:
## Mental sentiment or attitude (1), Expression of it (1) ##
(1.7.450) vikāro mānaso bhāvo 'nubhāvo bhāvabodhakaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Mental sentiment or attitude (1 synonym), Expression of it (1 synonym) ##
(1.7.450) A mental transformation is <s>bhāva</s> (emotional state); <s>anubhāva</s> is that which manifests [or communicates] the <s>bhāva</s>.

children.text:
## Pride (5), Arrogance (6), Disrespect (9) ##
(1.7.451) garvo 'bhimāno 'haṅkāro mānaścittasamunnatiḥ
(1.7.452) darpo 'valoko 'vaṣṭambhaścittodrekaḥ smayo madaḥ
(1.7.453) anādaraḥ paribhavaḥ parībhāvastiraskriyā
(1.7.454) rīḍhāvamānanāvajñāvahelanamasūrkṣaṇam
children.translated_text:
## Pride (5 synonyms), Arrogance (6 synonyms), Disrespect (9 synonyms) ##
(1.7.451) <s>Garva</s>, <s>abhimāna</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, <s>māna</s>, and <s>cittasamunnati</s> (mental elevation) [are synonyms for pride].
(1.7.452) <s>Darpa</s>, <s>avaloka</s>, <s>avaṣṭambha</s>, <s>cittodreka</s>, <s>smaya</s>, and <s>mada</s> [are synonyms for arrogance].
(1.7.453) <s>Anādara</s>, <s>paribhava</s>, <s>parībhāva</s>, <s>tiraskriyā</s>,
(1.7.454) <s>rīḍhā</s>, <s>avamānanā</s>, <s>avajñā</s>, <s>avahelana</s>, and <s>asūrkṣaṇa</s> [are synonyms for disrespect/contempt].

children.text:
## Modesty or shame (5), Bashfulness (1) ##
(1.7.455) mandākṣaṃ hrīstrapā vrīḍā lajjā sāpatrapānyataḥ
children.translated_text:
## Modesty or shame (5 synonyms), Bashfulness (1 synonym) ##
(1.7.455) <s>Mandākṣa</s>, <s>hrī</s>, <s>trapā</s>, <s>vrīḍā</s>, and <s>lajjā</s> [are synonyms for modesty/shame]; <s>sāpatrapa</s> [means bashfulness, which is] different.

children.text:
## Patience, tolerance (2), Greed (for other's property) (1) ##
(1.7.456) kṣāntistitikṣābhidhyā tu parasya viṣaye spṛhā
children.translated_text:
## Patience, tolerance (2 synonyms), Greed for other's property (1 synonym) ##
(1.7.456) <s>Kṣānti</s> and <s>titikṣā</s> [mean patience/tolerance]; <s>abhidhyā</s> is desire for another's property.

children.text:
## Jealousy or envy (2), Nitpicking (1), Enmity (3), Grief (3) ##
(1.7.457) akṣāntirīrṣyāsūyā tu doṣāropo guṇeṣvapi
(1.7.458) vairaṃ virodho vidveṣo manyuśokau tu śuk striyām
children.translated_text:
## Jealousy or envy (2 synonyms), Nitpicking (1 synonym), Enmity (3 synonyms), Grief (3 synonyms) ##
(1.7.457) <s>Akṣānti</s> and <s>īrṣyā</s> [mean jealousy]; <s>asūyā</s> is the attribution of faults even in virtues.
(1.7.458) <s>Vaira</s>, <s>virodha</s>, and <s>vidveṣa</s> [mean enmity]; <s>manyu</s> and <s>śoka</s> [mean grief]; also <s>śuc</s> (feminine).

children.text:
## Repentance (3), Wrath or rage (7) ##
(1.7.459) paścāttāpo 'nutāpaśca vipratīsāra ityapi
(1.7.460) kopakrodhāmarṣaroṣapratighā ruṭ kṛdhau striyau
children.translated_text:
## Repentance (3 synonyms), Wrath or rage (7 synonyms) ##
(1.7.459) <s>Paścāttāpa</s>, <s>anutāpa</s>, and <s>vipratīsāra</s> [mean repentance].
(1.7.460) <s>Kopa</s>, <s>krodha</s>, <s>amarṣa</s>, <s>roṣa</s>, <s>pratigha</s>, <s>ruṭ</s>, and <s>kṛdh</s> — the last two [are] feminine [and all mean wrath/rage].

children.text:
## Character or good conduct (1), Insanity (2) ##
(1.7.461) śucau tu carite śīlamunmādaścittavibhramaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Character or good conduct (1 synonym), Insanity (2 synonyms) ##
(1.7.461) In the sense of pure conduct, <s>śīla</s> [means character]; <s>unmāda</s> and <s>cittavibhrama</s> [mean insanity].

children.text:
## Affection or kindness (3), Desire or wish (12), Lust (1) ##
(1.7.462) premā nā priyatā hārdaṃ premasneho 'tha dohadam
(1.7.463) icchā kāṅkṣā spṛhehā tṛḍ vāñchā lipsā manorathaḥ
(1.7.464) kāmo 'bhilāṣastarṣaśca so 'tyarthaṃ lālasā dvayoḥ
children.translated_text:
## Affection or kindness (3 synonyms), Desire or wish (12 synonyms), Lust (1 synonym) ##
(1.7.462) <s>Preman</s> (not feminine), <s>priyatā</s>, <s>hārda</s>, <s>premasneha</s> [mean affection]; then <s>dohada</s>,
(1.7.463) <s>icchā</s>, <s>kāṅkṣā</s>, <s>spṛhā</s>, <s>īhā</s>, <s>tṛṣ</s>, <s>vāñchā</s>, <s>lipsā</s>, <s>manoratha</s>,
(1.7.464) <s>kāma</s>, <s>abhilāṣa</s>, and <s>tarṣa</s> [are synonyms for desire]; when excessive, <s>lālasā</s> [is used] — in both [masculine and feminine].

children.text:
## Moral reflection (1), Mental decease (1) Recollection (3) Anxiety (2) ##
(1.7.465) upādhirnā dharmacintā puṃsyādhirmānasī vyathā
(1.7.466) syāccintā smṛtirādhyānamutkaṇṭhotkalike same
children.translated_text:
## Moral reflection (1 synonym), Mental distress (1 synonym), Recollection (3 synonyms), Anxiety (2 synonyms) ##
(1.7.465) <s>Upādhi</s> (not feminine) [means] moral reflection (<s>dharmacintā</s>); <s>ādhi</s> (masculine) [means] mental distress.
(1.7.466) <s>Cintā</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, and <s>ādhyāna</s> [mean reflection/remembrance]; <s>utkaṇṭhā</s> and <s>utkali</s> are equivalent [meaning anxiety/longing].

children.text:
## Perseverance or enthusiasm (2), Fortitude (1) ##
(1.7.467) utsāho 'dhyavasāyaḥ syāt sa vīryamatiśaktibhāk
children.translated_text:
## Perseverance or enthusiasm (2 synonyms), Fortitude (1 synonym) ##
(1.7.467) <s>Utsāha</s> and <s>adhyavasāya</s> [mean perseverance/enthusiasm]; when endowed with extraordinary power, that [is called] <s>vīrya</s> (fortitude).

children.text:
## Fraud or deceit (9), Carelessness or error (2) ##
(1.7.468) kapaṭo 'strī vyājadambhopadhayaś chadmakaitave
(1.7.469) kusṛtirnikṛtiḥ śāṭhyaṃ pramādo 'navadhānatā
children.translated_text:
## Fraud or deceit (9 synonyms), Carelessness or error (2 synonyms) ##
(1.7.468) <s>Kapaṭa</s> (not feminine), <s>vyāja</s>, <s>dambha</s>, <s>upadhi</s>, <s>chadman</s>, <s>kaitava</s>,
(1.7.469) <s>kusṛti</s>, <s>nikṛti</s>, and <s>śāṭhya</s> [are synonyms for deceit]; <s>pramāda</s> and <s>anavadhānatā</s> [mean carelessness].

children.text:
## Eagerness or curiosity (4), Women's affectionate actions (six listed) (1) ##
(1.7.470) kautūhalaṃ kautukaṃ ca kutukaṃ ca kutūhalam
(1.7.471) strīṇāṃ vilāsabibbokavibhramā lalitaṃ tathā
(1.7.472) helā līletyamī hāvāḥkriyāḥ śṛṅgārabhāvajāḥ
children.translated_text:
## Eagerness or curiosity (4 synonyms), Women's affectionate actions (six listed) ##
(1.7.470) <s>Kautūhala</s>, <s>kautuka</s>, <s>kutuka</s>, and <s>kutūhala</s> [mean curiosity/eagerness].
(1.7.471) Among women: <s>vilāsa</s>, <s>bibboka</s>, <s>vibhrama</s>, <s>lalita</s>, likewise
(1.7.472) <s>helā</s>, <s>līlā</s> — these are <s>hāvas</s> (amorous gestures); actions born of the erotic sentiment.

children.text:
## Sport or amusement (6), Concealment or disguise (3) ##
(1.7.473) dravakeliparīhāsāḥ krīḍā līlā ca narma ca
(1.7.474) vyājo 'padeśo lakṣyaṃ ca krīḍā khelā ca kūrdanam
children.translated_text:
## Sport or amusement (6 synonyms), Concealment or disguise (3 synonyms) ##
(1.7.473) <s>Drava</s>, <s>keli</s>, <s>parīhāsa</s>, <s>krīḍā</s>, <s>līlā</s>, and <s>narman</s> [are synonyms for sport/play].
(1.7.474) <s>Vyāja</s>, <s>apadeśa</s>, and <s>lakṣya</s> [mean pretext/disguise]; <s>krīḍā</s>, <s>khelā</s>, and <s>kūrdana</s> [mean sport/jumping].

children.text:
## Sweat (3), Unconsciousness (2), camouflage (2), Excitement or hurry (2) ##
(1.7.475) gharmo nidāghaḥ svedaḥ syātpralayo naṣṭaceṣṭatā
(1.7.476) avahitthākāraguptiḥ samau saṃvegasaṃbhramau
children.translated_text:
## Sweat (3 synonyms), Unconsciousness (2 synonyms), Camouflage (2 synonyms), Excitement or hurry (2 synonyms) ##
(1.7.475) <s>Gharma</s>, <s>nidāgha</s>, and <s>sveda</s> [mean sweat]; <s>pralaya</s> and <s>naṣṭaceṣṭatā</s> [mean loss of consciousness].
(1.7.476) <s>Avahitthā</s> and <s>ākāragupti</s> [mean concealment of feelings]; <s>saṃvega</s> and <s>saṃbhrama</s> are equivalent [meaning excitement/haste].

children.text:
## Three laughs: loud articulated (1), smile (1), laugh (1), Thrill (goosepimples) (2) ##
(1.7.477) syādācchuritakaṃ hāsaḥ sotprāsaḥ sa manāk smitam
(1.7.478) madhyamaḥ syādvihasitaṃ romāñco romaharṣaṇam

## Weeping (3), Yawning (2), Dishonest talk (2), Deviation or failure (2) ##
(1.7.479) kranditaṃ ruditam kruṣṭaṃ jṛmbhastu triṣu jṛmbhaṇam
(1.7.480) vipralambho visaṃvādo riṅgaṇaṃ skhalanaṃ same
children.translated_text:
## Weeping (3 synonyms), Yawning (2 synonyms), Dishonest talk (2 synonyms), Deviation or failure (2 synonyms) ##
(1.7.479) <s>Krandita</s>, <s>rudita</s>, and <s>kruṣṭa</s> [mean weeping]; <s>jṛmbha</s> (in all three genders) and <s>jṛmbhaṇa</s> [mean yawning].
(1.7.480) <s>Vipralambha</s> and <s>visaṃvāda</s> [mean deception/dishonest talk]; <s>riṅgaṇa</s> and <s>skhalana</s> are equivalent [meaning stumbling/failure].

children.text:
## Sleep (5), Sleepiness or lassitude (2), Frown (3)##
(1.7.481) syānnidrā śayanaṃ svāpaḥ svapnaḥ saṃveśa ityapi
(1.7.482) tandrī pramīlā bhrakuṭirbhrukuṭirbhrūkuṭiḥ striyām
children.translated_text:
## Sleep (5 synonyms), Sleepiness or lassitude (2 synonyms), Frown (3 synonyms) ##
(1.7.481) <s>Nidrā</s>, <s>śayana</s>, <s>svāpa</s>, <s>svapna</s>, and <s>saṃveśa</s> [are synonyms for sleep].
(1.7.482) <s>Tandrī</s> and <s>pramīlā</s> [mean drowsiness]; <s>bhrakuṭi</s>, <s>bhrukuṭi</s>, and <s>bhrūkuṭi</s> (feminine) [mean frown].

children.text:
## (Angry) staring (1), Natural state or nature (5), trembling (2), Elation or festival (5) ##
(1.7.483) adṛṣṭiḥ syādasaumye 'kṣṇi saṃsiddhiprakṛtī tvime
(1.7.484) svarūpaṃ ca svabhāvaśca nisargaścātha vepathuḥ
(1.7.485) kampo 'tha kṣaṇa uddharṣo maha uddhava utsavaḥ
children.translated_text:
## (Angry) staring (1 synonym), Natural state or nature (5 synonyms), Trembling (2 synonyms), Elation or festival (5 synonyms) ##
(1.7.483) <s>Adṛṣṭi</s> [means] an unkind gaze; <s>saṃsiddhi</s> and <s>prakṛti</s> — these two [mean natural state],
(1.7.484) and <s>svarūpa</s>, <s>svabhāva</s>, and <s>nisarga</s> [also mean nature]; then <s>vepathu</s>
(1.7.485) and <s>kampa</s> [mean trembling]; then <s>kṣaṇa</s>, <s>uddharṣa</s>, <s>maha</s>, <s>uddhava</s>, and <s>utsava</s> [mean elation/festival].
Chapter on the Underworld and Serpents (<s>Pātālabhogi-varga</s>).

children.text: ## Nether world (5), Hole or empty space (11) ##
children.translated_text: ## Nether world (5 synonyms), Hole or empty space (11 synonyms) ##

children.text:
## The word ##sushhiraM## has a variant ##shushhiraM##. Similar for ##sushhiH## also ##
(1.8.486) adhobhuvanapātālaṃ balisadma rasātalam
(1.8.487) nāgaloko 'tha kuharaṃ suṣiraṃ vivaraṃ bilam
(1.8.488) chidraṃ nirvyathanaṃ rokaṃ randhraṃ śvabhraṃ vapā suṣiḥ
children.translated_text:
## (The word <s>suṣira</s> has a variant <s>śuṣira</s>; similarly <s>suṣi</s>) ##
(1.8.486) <s>Adhobhuvana</s>, <s>pātāla</s>, <s>balisadman</s> (abode of <s>Bali</s>), <s>rasātala</s>,
(1.8.487) and <s>nāgaloka</s> (world of serpents) [are synonyms for the nether world]; then <s>kuhara</s>, <s>suṣira</s>, <s>vivara</s>, <s>bila</s>,
(1.8.488) <s>chidra</s>, <s>nirvyathana</s>, <s>roka</s>, <s>randhra</s>, <s>śvabhra</s>, <s>vapā</s>, and <s>suṣi</s> [are synonyms for hole/cavity].

children.text:
## Hole in the ground (2), Darkness (5), Complete darkness (1), Partial darkness (1) ##
(1.8.489) gartāvaṭau bhuvi śvabhre sarandhre suṣiraṃ triṣu
(1.8.490) andhakāro 'striyāṃ dhvāntaṃ tamisraṃ timiraṃ tamaḥ
(1.8.491) dhvānte gāḍhe 'ndhatamasaṃ kṣīṇe 'vatamasaṃ tamaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Hole in the ground (2 synonyms), Darkness (5 synonyms), Complete darkness (1 synonym), Partial darkness (1 synonym) ##
(1.8.489) <s>Garta</s> and <s>avaṭa</s> [mean a pit in the ground]; <s>suṣira</s> [is used] in all three genders when [meaning] having a hole.
(1.8.490) <s>Andhakāra</s> (not feminine), <s>dhvānta</s>, <s>tamisra</s>, <s>timira</s>, and <s>tamas</s> [are synonyms for darkness].
(1.8.491) When darkness is dense: <s>andhatamasa</s>; when diminished: <s>avatamasa</s>.

children.text:
## Universal darkness (1), Snake (2), King of snakes (2), A type of snake (2), Python or large snake (3) ##
(1.8.492) viṣvaksaṃtamasaṃ nāgāḥ kādraveyāstadīśvare
(1.8.493) śeṣo 'nanto vāsukistu sarparājo 'tha gonase
(1.8.494) tilitsaḥ syādajagare śayurvāhasa ityubhau
children.translated_text:
## Universal darkness (1 synonym), Snake (2 synonyms), King of snakes (2 synonyms), A type of snake (2 synonyms), Python or large snake (3 synonyms) ##
(1.8.492) <s>Viṣvaksaṃtamasa</s> [means all-pervading darkness]; <s>nāgas</s> are <s>kādraveyas</s> (sons of <s>Kadrū</s>); their lords:
(1.8.493) <s>Śeṣa</s> [called also] <s>Ananta</s>; and <s>Vāsuki</s> is the king of serpents; then <s>gonasa</s>,
(1.8.494) <s>tilitsa</s> [are types of snakes]; for the python (<s>ajagara</s>): <s>śayu</s> and <s>vāhasa</s> — both [are synonyms].

children.text:
## Water snake (2), A type of nonpoisonous snake (2), A variegated snake (2), Shedded snake (2) ##
(1.8.495) alagardo jalavyālaḥ samau rājilaḍuṇḍumau
(1.8.496) māludhāno mātulāhirnirmukto muktakañcukaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Water snake (2 synonyms), A type of non-poisonous snake (2 synonyms), A variegated snake (2 synonyms), Shed snake (2 synonyms) ##
(1.8.495) <s>Alagarda</s> and <s>jalavyāla</s> are equivalent [meaning water snake]; <s>rājila</s> and <s>ḍuṇḍuma</s> [are types of snakes].
(1.8.496) <s>Māludhāna</s> and <s>mātulāhi</s> [are types of snakes]; <s>nirmukta</s> and <s>muktakañcuka</s> [mean a snake that has shed its skin].

children.text:
## Snake or serpent (33) ##
(1.8.497) sarpaḥ pṛdākurbhujago bhujaṅgo 'hirbhujaṅgamaḥ
(1.8.498) āśīviṣo viṣadharaścakrī vyālaḥ sarīsṛpaḥ
(1.8.499) kuṇḍalī gūḍhapāccakṣuḥśravāḥ kākodaraḥ phaṇī
(1.8.500) darvīkaro dīrghapṛṣṭho dandaśūko bileśayaḥ
(1.8.501) uragaḥ pannago bhogī jihmagaḥ pavanāśanaḥ
(1.8.502) lelihāno dvirasano gokarṇaḥ kañcukī tathā
(1.8.503) kumbhīnasaḥ phaṇadharo harirbhogadharastathā
children.translated_text:
## Snake or serpent (33 synonyms) ##
(1.8.497) <s>Sarpa</s>, <s>pṛdāku</s>, <s>bhujaga</s>, <s>bhujaṅga</s>, <s>ahi</s>, <s>bhujaṅgama</s>,
(1.8.498) <s>āśīviṣa</s> (fang-venomed), <s>viṣadhara</s> (venom-bearer), <s>cakrin</s> (coiled), <s>vyāla</s>, <s>sarīsṛpa</s> (creeping),
(1.8.499) <s>kuṇḍalin</s> (coiled one), <s>gūḍhapāt</s> (hidden-footed), <s>cakṣuḥśravas</s> (ear-eyed), <s>kākodara</s>, <s>phaṇin</s> (hooded),
(1.8.500) <s>darvīkara</s> (ladle-handed), <s>dīrghapṛṣṭha</s> (long-backed), <s>dandaśūka</s> (biter), <s>bileśaya</s> (dwelling in holes),
(1.8.501) <s>uraga</s> (chest-goer), <s>pannaga</s>, <s>bhogin</s> (coiled), <s>jihmaga</s> (crooked-goer), <s>pavanāśana</s> (wind-eater),
(1.8.502) <s>lelihāna</s> (licker), <s>dvirasana</s> (two-tongued), <s>gokarṇa</s>, <s>kañcukin</s> (having a sheath), likewise
(1.8.503) <s>kumbhīnasa</s>, <s>phaṇadhara</s> (hood-bearer), <s>hari</s>, and <s>bhogadhara</s> (coil-bearer) [are all synonyms for snake].

children.text:
## Body of a snake (1), Fang (2), Pertaining to a snake (1), Hood of a snake(2) ##
(1.8.504) aheḥ śarīraṃ bhogaḥ syādāśīrapyahidaṃṣṭrikā
(1.8.505) triṣvāheyaṃ viṣāsthyādi sphaṭāyāṃ tu phaṇā dvayoḥ
children.translated_text:
## Body of a snake (1 synonym), Fang (2 synonyms), Pertaining to a snake (1 synonym), Hood of a snake (2 synonyms) ##
(1.8.504) The body of a snake is [called] <s>bhoga</s> (coil); <s>āśīra</s> and <s>ahidaṃṣṭrikā</s> [mean fang].
(1.8.505) <s>Āheya</s> [means] pertaining to a snake [used] in all three genders — for venom, bones, etc.; for the expanded hood: <s>sphaṭā</s> and <s>phaṇā</s> — both.

children.text:
## Snake's venom (3), List of nine specific venoms ##
(1.8.506) samau kañcukanirmokau kṣveḍastu garalaṃ viṣam
(1.8.507) puṃsi klībe ca kākolakālakūṭahalāhalāḥ
(1.8.508) saurāṣṭrikaḥ śauklikeyo brahmaputraḥ pradīpanaḥ
(1.8.509) dārado vatsanābhaśca viṣabhedā amī nava
children.translated_text:
## Snake's venom (3 synonyms), List of nine specific venoms ##
(1.8.506) <s>Kañcuka</s> and <s>nirmoka</s> are equivalent [meaning shed skin]; <s>kṣveḍa</s>, <s>garala</s>, and <s>viṣa</s> [mean venom/poison].
(1.8.507) [These are] masculine and neuter: <s>kākola</s>, <s>kālakūṭa</s>, <s>halāhala</s>,
(1.8.508) <s>saurāṣṭrika</s>, <s>śauklikeya</s>, <s>brahmaputra</s>, <s>pradīpana</s>,
(1.8.509) <s>dārada</s>, and <s>vatsanābha</s> — these nine are the varieties of poison.

children.text:
## Poison expert (2), Snake catcher (2) ##
(1.8.510) viṣavaidyo jāṅguliko vyālagrāhyahituṇḍikaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Poison expert (2 synonyms), Snake catcher (2 synonyms) ##
(1.8.510) <s>Viṣavaidya</s> and <s>jāṅgulika</s> [mean a poison-doctor]; <s>vyālagrāhin</s> and <s>ahituṇḍika</s> [mean a snake-catcher].
Chapter on Hell (<s>Narakavarga</s>).

children.text:
## Hell (4), Six specific hells listed, (Hell-bound) souls (1), River in hell (1), Misery (in hell) (1) ##
(1.9.511) syānnārakastu narako nirayo durgatiḥ striyām
(1.9.512) tadbhedāstapanāvīcimahārauravarauravāḥ
(1.9.513) saṃghātaḥ kālasūtraṃ cetyādyāḥ sattvāstu nārakāḥ
(1.9.514) pretā vaitaraṇī sindhuḥ syādalakṣmīstu nirrtiḥ
children.translated_text:
## Hell (4), Six specific hells listed, (Hell-bound) souls (1), River in hell (1), Misery (in hell) (1) ##
(1.9.511) '<s>Nāraka</s>' (hellish), '<s>naraka</s>' (hell), '<s>niraya</s>' (the condemned state), '<s>durgati</s>' (evil destiny) — [the last is] feminine.
(1.9.512) Its divisions are: <s>Tapana</s> (the Scorching), <s>Avīci</s> (the Waveless), <s>Mahāraurava</s> (the Great Screaming), <s>Raurava</s> (the Screaming),
(1.9.513) <s>Saṃghāta</s> (the Crushing), and <s>Kālasūtra</s> (the Black Thread) — these are the chief [hells]. The beings [there] are called '<s>nārakāḥ</s>' (hell-denizens).
(1.9.514) '<s>Pretas</s>' (departed spirits) [dwell in hell]. '<s>Vaitaraṇī</s>' is the river [in hell]. '<s>Alakṣmī</s>' (misfortune) is also [called] '<s>nirṛti</s>'.

children.text:
## Condemnation (to hell) (2), Agony (3) ##
(1.9.515) viṣṭirājūḥ kāraṇā tu yātanā tīvravedanā
children.translated_text:
## Condemnation (to hell) (2), Agony (3) ##
(1.9.515) '<s>Viṣṭi</s>' and '<s>ājū</s>' [mean condemnation]. '<s>Kāraṇā</s>' (punishment), '<s>yātanā</s>' (torment), and '<s>tīvravedanā</s>' (acute suffering) [are synonyms for agony].

children.text:
## Pain or suffering of various types (9) ##
(1.9.516) pīḍā bādhā vyathā duḥkhamāmanasyaṃ prasūtijam
(1.9.517) syātkaṣṭaṃ kṛcchramābhīlaṃ triṣveṣāṃ bhedyagāmi yat

children.translated_text: End of the Water Section}

children.text:
## Sea or ocean (15), Specific oceans (two listed) ##
(1.10.518) samudro 'bdhirakūpāraḥ pārāvāraḥ saritpatiḥ
(1.10.519) udanvānudadhiḥ sindhuḥ sarasvānsāgaro 'rṇavaḥ
(1.10.520) ratnākaro jalanidhiryādaḥpatirapāmpatiḥ
(1.10.521) tasya prabhedāḥ kṣīrodo lavaṇodastathāpare
children.translated_text:
## Sea or ocean (15), Specific oceans (two listed) ##
(1.10.518) '<s>Samudra</s>' (ocean), '<s>abdhi</s>' (receptacle of waters), '<s>akūpāra</s>' (boundless), '<s>pārāvāra</s>' (having a far shore), '<s>saritpati</s>' (lord of rivers),
(1.10.519) '<s>udanvān</s>' (abounding in water), '<s>udadhi</s>' (water-receptacle), '<s>sindhu</s>' (sea), '<s>sarasvān</s>' (possessing currents), '<s>sāgara</s>' (ocean), '<s>arṇava</s>' (flood),
(1.10.520) '<s>ratnākara</s>' (mine of gems), '<s>jalanidhi</s>' (water-treasury), '<s>yādaḥpati</s>' (lord of aquatic creatures), '<s>apāmpati</s>' (lord of waters) —
(1.10.521) its divisions are: <s>Kṣīroda</s> (the Milky Ocean) and <s>Lavaṇoda</s> (the Salt Ocean), and others.

children.text:
## Water (27), watery (2) ##
(1.10.522) āpaḥ strī bhūmni vārvāri salilaṃ kamalaṃ jalaṃ
(1.10.523) payaḥ kīlālamamṛtaṃ jīvanaṃ bhuvanaṃ vanam
(1.10.524) kabandhamudakaṃ pāthaḥ puṣkaraṃ sarvatomukham
(1.10.525) ambhorṇastoyapānīyanīrakṣīro 'mbuśambaram
(1.10.526) meghapuṣpaṃ ghanarasastriṣu dve āpyamammayam
children.translated_text:
## Water (27), watery (2) ##
(1.10.522) '<s>Āpaḥ</s>' (waters) — feminine, [used] in the plural; '<s>vār</s>,' '<s>vāri</s>,' '<s>salila</s>,' '<s>kamala</s>,' '<s>jala</s>'
(1.10.523) '<s>payas</s>,' '<s>kīlāla</s>,' '<s>amṛta</s>,' '<s>jīvana</s>' (life-giving), '<s>bhuvana</s>,' '<s>vana</s>,'
(1.10.524) '<s>kabandha</s>,' '<s>udaka</s>,' '<s>pāthas</s>,' '<s>puṣkara</s>,' '<s>sarvatomukha</s>' (flowing in all directions),
(1.10.525) '<s>ambhas</s>,' '<s>arṇas</s>,' '<s>toya</s>,' '<s>pānīya</s>,' '<s>nīra</s>,' '<s>kṣīra</s>,' '<s>ambu</s>,' '<s>śambara</s>,'
(1.10.526) '<s>meghapuṣpa</s>' (cloud-flower), '<s>ghanarasas</s>' (cloud-essence) — [used] in all three genders; [and] '<s>āpya</s>' and '<s>ammaya</s>' [mean] 'watery.'

children.text:
## Wave (4), Big wave (2), Whirlpool (1), Droplet (4) ##
(1.10.527) bhaṅgastaraṅga ūrmirvā striyāṃ vīcirathormiṣu
(1.10.528) mahatsūllolakallolau syādāvarto 'mbhasāṃ bhramaḥ
(1.10.529) pṛṣanti bindupṛṣatāḥ pumāṃso vipruṣaḥ striyām
children.translated_text:
## Wave (4), Big wave (2), Whirlpool (1), Droplet (4) ##
(1.10.527) '<s>Bhaṅga</s>' (wave), '<s>taraṅga</s>' (wave), '<s>ūrmi</s>' — [the last is] optionally feminine; '<s>vīci</s>' — [used] in [the context of] great waves;
(1.10.528) '<s>ullola</s>' and '<s>kallola</s>' [mean] 'great wave'; '<s>āvarta</s>' (whirlpool) is the spinning of waters.
(1.10.529) '<s>Pṛṣat</s>,' '<s>bindu</s>,' '<s>pṛṣata</s>' — [all] masculine; '<s>vipruṣ</s>' — feminine [mean 'droplet'].

children.text:
## Circular motion in a water drain (4), Bank or shore (5) ##
(1.10.530) cakrāṇi puṭabhedāḥ syurbhramāśca jalanirgamāḥ
(1.10.531) kūlaṃ rodhaśca tīraṃ ca pratīraṃ ca taṭaṃ triṣu
children.translated_text:
## Circular motion in a water drain (4), Bank or shore (5) ##
(1.10.530) '<s>Cakrāṇi</s>' (circles), '<s>puṭabhedāḥ</s>' (cavity-openings) — these are '<s>bhramāḥ</s>' (swirls), [referring to] water-drains.
(1.10.531) '<s>Kūla</s>' (bank), '<s>rodhas</s>' (embankment), '<s>tīra</s>' (shore), '<s>pratīra</s>' (opposite bank), and '<s>taṭa</s>' (slope) — [all used] in all three genders.

children.text: ## Two banks listed, The channel or bed of a river (1) ##(1.10.532) pārāvāre parārvācī tīre pātraṃ tadantaram
children.translated_text:
## Two banks listed, The channel or bed of a river (1) ##
(1.10.532) '<s>Pāra</s>' and '<s>avāra</s>' are the far and near banks. '<s>Pātra</s>' is the bed; '<s>tadantara</s>' [means] 'the space between' [the banks].

children.text:
## Island (2), Islet in the river bank (1), Sandy beach (2) ##
(1.10.533) dvīpo 'striyāmantarīpaṃ yadantarvāriṇastaṭam
(1.10.534) toyotthitaṃ tatpulinaṃ saikataṃ sikatāmayam
children.translated_text:
## Island (2), Islet in the river bank (1), Sandy beach (2) ##
(1.10.533) '<s>Dvīpa</s>' (island) — not feminine. '<s>Antarīpa</s>' is a sandbank within the water's edge.
(1.10.534) '<s>Pulina</s>' (sandy shore) is [that which is] raised from the water. '<s>Saikata</s>' (sandy) means made of sand.

children.text:
## Mud or clay (5), Overflow (2), Ditches (for water) made in dry beds (2) ##
(1.10.535) niṣadvarastu jambālaḥ paṅko 'strī śādakardamau
(1.10.536) jalocchvāsāḥ parīvāhāḥ kūpakāstu vidārakāḥ
children.translated_text:
## Mud or clay (5), Overflow (2), Ditches (for water) made in dry beds (2) ##
(1.10.535) '<s>Niṣadvaras</s>,' '<s>jambāla</s>,' '<s>paṅka</s>' (mud) — not feminine; '<s>śāda</s>' and '<s>kardama</s>' (clay) [are synonyms].
(1.10.536) '<s>Jalocchvāsāḥ</s>' (water-overflows) are '<s>parīvāhāḥ</s>' (drainage channels). '<s>Kūpakāḥ</s>' (wells) are '<s>vidārakāḥ</s>' (ditches cut in dry beds).

children.text:
## Navigable (1), Boat (3), Raft or small boat (3), Stream of water (1) ##
(1.10.537) nāvyaṃ triliṅgaṃ nautārye striyāṃ naustaraṇistariḥ
(1.10.538) uḍupaṃ tu plavaḥ kolaḥ sroto 'mbusaraṇaṃ svataḥ
children.translated_text:
## Navigable (1), Boat (3), Raft or small boat (3), Stream of water (1) ##
(1.10.537) '<s>Nāvya</s>' (navigable) — [used] in all three genders, [refers to] what is fit for a boat. '<s>Nau</s>' (boat), '<s>taraṇi</s>,' '<s>tari</s>' — feminine.
(1.10.538) '<s>Uḍupa</s>' (raft), '<s>plava</s>' (float), '<s>kola</s>' (small boat) [are synonyms]. '<s>Srotas</s>' (stream) is the natural flow of water.

children.text:
## Toll (for crossing river) (2), Wooden water carrier (1), Merchants on waterways (2), Helmsman (2) ##
(1.10.539) ātarastarapaṇyaṃ syād droṇī kāṣṭāmbuvāhinī
(1.10.540) sāṃyātrikaḥ potavaṇik karṇadhārastu nāvikaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Toll (for crossing river) (2), Wooden water carrier (1), Merchants on waterways (2), Helmsman (2) ##
(1.10.539) '<s>Ātara</s>' (toll) and '<s>tarapaṇya</s>' (ferry-fee) [are synonyms]. '<s>Droṇī</s>' is a wooden water-carrier.
(1.10.540) '<s>Sāṃyātrika</s>' (fellow-traveler) and '<s>potavaṇik</s>' (boat-merchant) [are synonyms]. '<s>Karṇadhāra</s>' (helmsman) is '<s>nāvika</s>' (boatman).

children.text:
## Steersman or rower (2), Mast (2), Oar (2), Rudder (2) ##
(1.10.541) niyāmakāḥ potavāhāḥ kūpako guṇavṛkṣakaḥ
(1.10.542) naukādaṇḍaḥ kṣepaṇī syādaritraṃ kenipātakaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Steersman or rower (2), Mast (2), Oar (2), Rudder (2) ##
(1.10.541) '<s>Niyāmakāḥ</s>' (steersmen) are '<s>potavāhāḥ</s>' (boat-propellers). '<s>Kūpaka</s>' (mast) is '<s>guṇavṛkṣaka</s>' (rope-tree).
(1.10.542) '<s>Naukādaṇḍa</s>' (boat-pole) and '<s>kṣepaṇī</s>' (oar) [are synonyms]. '<s>Aritra</s>' (rudder) is '<s>kenipātaka</s>'.

children.text:
## Scraper or shovel (2), Bucket (2), Half of a boat (1), Alit (1) ##
(1.10.543) abhriḥ strī kāṣṭakuddālaḥ sekapātraṃ tu secanam
(1.10.544) klībe 'rdhanāvaṃ nāvo 'rdhe 'tītanauke 'tinu triṣu
children.translated_text:
## Scraper or shovel (2), Bucket (2), Half of a boat (1), Alit (1) ##
(1.10.543) '<s>Abhri</s>' (scraper) — feminine — is a wooden spade. '<s>Sekapātra</s>' (sprinkling-vessel) is '<s>secana</s>' (bucket).
(1.10.544) '<s>Ardhanāva</s>' (half-boat) — neuter — [refers to] half of a boat. '<s>Atinu</s>' [means] 'having crossed the boat' — [used] in all three genders.

children.text:
## Clear or transparent (2), Turbid (3), Deep (3), Shallow (1) ##
(1.10.545) triṣvāgādhātprasanno 'cchaḥ kaluṣo 'naccha āvilaḥ
(1.10.546) nimnaṃ gabhīraṃ gambhīramuttānaṃ tadviparyaye
children.translated_text:
## Clear or transparent (2), Turbid (3), Deep (3), Shallow (1) ##
(1.10.545) [Used] in all three genders, from the bottomless: '<s>prasanna</s>' (clear) and '<s>accha</s>' (transparent) [are synonyms]. '<s>Kaluṣa</s>' (turbid), '<s>anaccha</s>' (unclear), '<s>āvila</s>' (muddy) [are synonyms].
(1.10.546) '<s>Nimna</s>' (low), '<s>gabhīra</s>' (deep), '<s>gambhīra</s>' (profound) [are synonyms]. '<s>Uttāna</s>' (shallow) is the opposite of those.

children.text:
## Bottomless or very deep (2), Fisherman (3), (Fishing) net (2), (Hemp) rope (2) ##
(1.10.547) agādhamatalasparśe kaivarte dāśadhīvarau
(1.10.548) ānāyaḥ puṃsi jālaṃ syācchaṇasūtraṃ pavitrakam
children.translated_text:
## Bottomless or very deep (2), Fisherman (3), (Fishing) net (2), (Hemp) rope (2) ##
(1.10.547) '<s>Agādha</s>' and '<s>atalasparśa</s>' [mean] 'bottomless.' '<s>Kaivarta</s>,' '<s>dāśa</s>,' '<s>dhīvara</s>' [mean] 'fisherman.'
(1.10.548) '<s>Ānāya</s>' — masculine — and '<s>jāla</s>' [mean] 'net.' '<s>Śaṇasūtra</s>' (hemp-rope) is '<s>pavitrakam</s>'.

children.text:
## Fish storage (2), Fishing (2), Fish (8), Specific (flat) fish (2) ##
(1.10.549) matsyādhānī kuveṇī syād baḍiśaṃ matsyavedhanam
(1.10.550) pṛthuromā jhaṣo matsyo mīno vaisāriṇo 'ṇḍajaḥ
(1.10.551) visāraḥ śakulī cātha gaḍakaḥ śakulārbhakaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Fish storage (2), Fishing (2), Fish (8), Specific (flat) fish (2) ##
(1.10.549) '<s>Matsyādhānī</s>' (fish-basket) is '<s>kuveṇī</s>.' '<s>Baḍiśa</s>' (fish-hook) is '<s>matsyavedhana</s>' (fish-piercer).
(1.10.550) '<s>Pṛthuromā</s>' (broad-scaled), '<s>jhaṣa</s>,' '<s>matsya</s>,' '<s>mīna</s>,' '<s>vaisāriṇa</s>,' '<s>aṇḍaja</s>' (egg-born) [all mean 'fish'].
(1.10.551) '<s>Visāra</s>' and '<s>śakulī</s>' [are specific flat fish]; and then '<s>gaḍaka</s>' is a small <s>śakula</s>.

children.text:
## Porpoise (2), Specific small fish (2), Type of carp (2), Type of white fish (2) ##
(1.10.552) sahasradaṃṣṭraḥ pāṭhīna ulūpī śiśukaḥ samau
(1.10.553) nalamīnaścilicimaḥ proṣṭhī tu śapharī dvayoḥ
children.translated_text:
## Porpoise (2), Specific small fish (2), Type of carp (2), Type of white fish (2) ##
(1.10.552) '<s>Sahasradaṃṣṭra</s>' (thousand-toothed) is the <s>pāṭhīna</s> (sheatfish). '<s>Ulūpī</s>' and '<s>śiśuka</s>' (porpoise) are synonymous.
(1.10.553) '<s>Nalamīna</s>' (reed-fish) is '<s>cilicima</s>.' '<s>Proṣṭhī</s>' is '<s>śapharī</s>' — [both apply] to either [type].

children.text:
## Tiny fish (1), List of specific seven fishes, Aquatic creatures (2) ##
(1.10.554) kṣudrāṇḍamatsyasaṃghātaḥ potādhānamatho jhaṣāḥ
(1.10.555) rohito madguraḥ śālo rājīvaḥ śakulastimiḥ
(1.10.556) timiṅgalādayaścātha yādāṃsi jalajantavaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Tiny fish (1), List of specific seven fishes, Aquatic creatures (2) ##
(1.10.554) '<s>Potādhāna</s>' is a mass of tiny eggs and fish. And then the fishes [are]:
(1.10.555) <s>Rohita</s>, <s>madgura</s> (catfish), <s>śāla</s>, <s>rājīva</s> (striped), <s>śakula</s>, <s>timi</s> (whale),
(1.10.556) <s>timiṅgala</s> (whale-swallower) and others. And '<s>yādāṃsi</s>' and '<s>jalajantavaḥ</s>' (water-born creatures) [are synonyms for aquatic creatures].

children.text:
## List of four aquatic creatures, Crab (2), Turtle or tortoise (3) ##
(1.10.557) tadbhedāḥ śiśumārodraśaṅkavo makarādayaḥ
(1.10.558) syātkulīraḥ karkaṭakaḥ kūrme kamaṭhakacchapau
children.translated_text:
## List of four aquatic creatures, Crab (2), Turtle or tortoise (3) ##
(1.10.557) Their divisions are: <s>śiśumāra</s> (Gangetic dolphin), <s>udra</s> (otter), <s>śaṅku</s> (swordfish), <s>makara</s> (sea-monster), and others.
(1.10.558) '<s>Kulīra</s>' is '<s>karkaṭaka</s>' (crab). For tortoise: '<s>kamaṭha</s>' and '<s>kacchapa</s>' [are synonyms].

children.text:
## Shark (2), Crocodile (2), Worm (3), Crocodile in Ganges (2) ##
(1.10.559) grāho 'vahāro nakrastu kumbhīro 'tha mahīlatā
(1.10.560) gaṇḍūpadaḥ kiñculako nihākā godhikā same
children.translated_text:
## Shark (2), Crocodile (2), Worm (3), Crocodile in Ganges (2) ##
(1.10.559) '<s>Grāha</s>' (seizer) is '<s>avahāra</s>.' '<s>Nakra</s>' (crocodile) is '<s>kumbhīra</s>.' And '<s>mahīlatā</s>' (earth-creeper),
(1.10.560) '<s>gaṇḍūpada</s>,' '<s>kiñculaka</s>' [mean 'worm']. '<s>Nihākā</s>' and '<s>godhikā</s>' (iguana) are synonymous.

children.text:
## Leech (3), Pearl oyster (2), Conch (2) ##
(1.10.561) raktapā tu jalaukāyāṃ striyāṃ bhūmni jalaukasaḥ
(1.10.562) muktāsphoṭaḥ striyāṃ śuktiḥ śaṅkhaḥ syātkamburastriyau
children.translated_text:
## Leech (3), Pearl oyster (2), Conch (2) ##
(1.10.561) '<s>Raktapā</s>' (blood-drinker) [means 'leech']; for '<s>jalaukā</s>' (leech) — feminine [and] used in the plural: '<s>jalaukasaḥ</s>' (water-dwellers).
(1.10.562) '<s>Muktāsphoṭa</s>' (pearl-splitter) — feminine — is '<s>śukti</s>' (oyster). '<s>Śaṅkha</s>' (conch) is '<s>kambura</s>' — [the latter] feminine.

children.text:
## Small shell (2), Bivalve shell (2), Frog (6) ##
(1.10.563) kṣudraśaṅkhāḥ śaṅkhanakhāḥ śambūkā jalaśuktayaḥ
(1.10.564) bheke maṇḍūkavarṣābhūśālūraplavadardurāḥ
children.translated_text:
## Small shell (2), Bivalve shell (2), Frog (6) ##
(1.10.563) '<s>Kṣudraśaṅkhāḥ</s>' (small conchs) are '<s>śaṅkhanakhāḥ</s>' (conch-nails). '<s>Śambūkāḥ</s>' (snails) are '<s>jalaśuktayaḥ</s>' (water-oysters).
(1.10.564) For frog: '<s>bheka</s>,' '<s>maṇḍūka</s>,' '<s>varṣābhū</s>' (rain-born), '<s>śālūra</s>,' '<s>plava</s>' (leaper), '<s>dardura</s>'.

children.text:
## Small worm (2), Female frog (2), Female turtle (2) ##
(1.10.565) śilī gaṇḍūpadī bhekī varṣābhvī kamaṭhī ḍuliḥ
children.translated_text:
## Small worm (2), Female frog (2), Female turtle (2) ##
(1.10.565) '<s>Śilī</s>' is '<s>gaṇḍūpadī</s>' (female worm). '<s>Bhekī</s>' is '<s>varṣābhvī</s>' (female frog). '<s>Kamaṭhī</s>' is '<s>ḍuli</s>' (female turtle).

children.text:
## Female sheat fish (1), Cocle (2), Lake or pond (2), Deep lake (1) ##
(1.10.566) madgurasya priyā śṛṅgī durnāmā dīrghakośikā
(1.10.567) jalāśayā jalādhārāstatrāgādhajalo hradaḥ
children.translated_text:
## Female sheat fish (1), Cocle (2), Lake or pond (2), Deep lake (1) ##
(1.10.566) The female of the <s>madgura</s> (catfish) is '<s>śṛṅgī</s>.' '<s>Durnāmā</s>' (ill-named) is '<s>dīrghakośikā</s>' (long-sheathed) [i.e., a cockle].
(1.10.567) '<s>Jalāśaya</s>' (water-reservoir) and '<s>jalādhāra</s>' (water-container) [mean 'lake']. Among those, one with bottomless water is a '<s>hrada</s>' (deep lake).

children.text:
## Trough near a well (2), Well (4) ##
(1.10.568) āhāvastu nipānaṃ syādupakūpajalāśaye
(1.10.569) puṃsyevāndhuḥ prahiḥ kūpa udapānṃ tu puṃsi vā
children.translated_text:
## Trough near a well (2), Well (4) ##
(1.10.568) '<s>Āhāva</s>' (trough) is '<s>nipāna</s>,' referring to a water-reservoir near a well.
(1.10.569) '<s>Andhu</s>' — masculine only, '<s>prahi</s>,' '<s>kūpa</s>,' '<s>udapāna</s>' — [the last is] optionally masculine [all mean 'well'].

children.text:
## Wooden contraption for extracting water from well (1), Facing of well ##
(1.10.570) nemistrikāsya vīnāho mukhabandhanamasya yat
children.translated_text:
## Wooden contraption for extracting water from well (1), Facing of well ##
(1.10.570) '<s>Nemi</s>' is the pulley-frame [of a well]. '<s>Vīnāha</s>' is the facing that serves as its mouth-binding.

children.text:
## Square or large pond (2), Natural pond (2) ##
(1.10.571) puṣkariṇyāṃ tu khātaṃ syādakhātaṃ devakhātakam
children.translated_text:
## Square or large pond (2), Natural pond (2) ##
(1.10.571) '<s>Puṣkariṇī</s>' (lotus-pond) — '<s>khāta</s>' (excavated) [refers to an artificial pond]; '<s>akhāta</s>' (unexcavated) is a '<s>devakhātaka</s>' (natural, divinely-made pond).

children.text:
## Deep pond or tank (5), Basin (2), Large circular reservoir (2) ##
(1.10.572) padmākarastaḍāgo 'strī kāsāraḥ sarasī saraḥ
(1.10.573) veśantaḥ palvalaṃ cālpasaro vāpī tu dīrghikā
children.translated_text:
## Deep pond or tank (5), Basin (2), Large circular reservoir (2) ##
(1.10.572) '<s>Padmākara</s>' (lotus-mine), '<s>taḍāga</s>' — not feminine, '<s>kāsāra</s>,' '<s>sarasī</s>,' '<s>saras</s>' [all mean 'lake/pond'].
(1.10.573) '<s>Veśanta</s>' and '<s>palvala</s>' [mean] 'small lake.' '<s>Vāpī</s>' is '<s>dīrghikā</s>' (long reservoir).

children.text:
## Moat or ditch (2), Dike or dam (1), Watering basin around a tree (3), River (16) ##
(1.10.574) kheyaṃ tu parikhādhārastvambhasāṃ yatra dhāraṇam
(1.10.575) syādālavālamāvālamāvāpo 'tha nadī sarit
(1.10.576) taraṅgiṇī śaivalinī taṭinī hrādinī dhunī
(1.10.577) srotasvinī dvīpavatī sravantī nimnagāpagā
(1.10.578) kūlaṅkaṣā nirjhariṇī rodhovakrā sarasvatī
children.translated_text:
## Moat or ditch (2), Dike or dam (1), Watering basin around a tree (3), River (16) ##
(1.10.574) '<s>Kheya</s>' is a moat or ditch. '<s>Ādhāra</s>' (container) is that in which waters are held.
(1.10.575) '<s>Ālavāla</s>,' '<s>āvāla</s>,' '<s>āvāpa</s>' [mean] 'watering-basin around a tree.' Then, '<s>nadī</s>' (river) and '<s>sarit</s>' (stream),
(1.10.576) '<s>taraṅgiṇī</s>' (wave-bearing), '<s>śaivalinī</s>' (moss-covered), '<s>taṭinī</s>' (banked), '<s>hrādinī</s>' (roaring), '<s>dhunī</s>' (rushing),
(1.10.577) '<s>srotasvinī</s>' (stream-bearing), '<s>dvīpavatī</s>' (island-having), '<s>sravantī</s>' (flowing), '<s>nimnagā</s>' (flowing downward), '<s>apagā</s>' (water-going),
(1.10.578) '<s>kūlaṅkaṣā</s>' (bank-eroding), '<s>nirjhariṇī</s>' (cascading), '<s>rodhovakrā</s>' (dam-bending), '<s>sarasvatī</s>' (full of pools) — [all are synonyms for river].

children.text:
## River Ganges (8) ##
(1.10.579) gaṅgā viṣṇupadī jahnutanayā suranimnagā
(1.10.580) bhāgīrathī tripathagā trisrotā bhīṣmasūrapi
children.translated_text:
## River Ganges (8) ##
(1.10.579) '<s>Gaṅgā</s>,' '<s>Viṣṇupadī</s>' (born from <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s foot), '<s>Jahnutanayā</s>' (daughter of <s>Jahnu</s>), '<s>Suranimnagā</s>' (celestial river),
(1.10.580) '<s>Bhāgīrathī</s>' (brought by <s>Bhagīratha</s>), '<s>Tripathagā</s>' (flowing in three paths), '<s>Trisrotā</s>' (three-streamed), and '<s>Bhīṣmasū</s>' (mother of <s>Bhīṣma</s>) also.

children.text:
## River Yamuna (4), River Narmada (4) ##
(1.10.581) kālindī sūryatanayā yamunā śamanasvasā
(1.10.582) revā tu narmadā somodbhavā mekalakanyakā
children.translated_text:
## River Yamuna (4), River Narmada (4) ##
(1.10.581) '<s>Kālindī</s>,' '<s>Sūryatanayā</s>' (daughter of <s>Sūrya</s>), '<s>Yamunā</s>,' '<s>Śamanasvasā</s>' (sister of <s>Yama</s>).
(1.10.582) '<s>Revā</s>' is '<s>Narmadā</s>,' '<s>Somodbhavā</s>' (born from <s>Soma</s>), '<s>Mekalakanyakā</s>' (daughter of the <s>Mekala</s> mountain).

children.text:
## River created at the time of Gauri's marriage (2), River brought down by ##kaartaviiryaarjuna##(2) ##
(1.10.583) karatoyā sadānīrā bāhudā saitavāhinī
children.translated_text:
## River created at the time of Gauri's marriage (2), River brought down by Kārtavīryārjuna (2) ##
(1.10.583) '<s>Karatoyā</s>' is '<s>Sadānīrā</s>' (always watery). '<s>Bāhudā</s>' is '<s>Saitavāhinī</s>' (cold-flowing).

children.text:
## River Shatardu (2), River Vipasha (2), River Shona (2), Canal (1) ##
(1.10.584) śatadrustu śutudriḥ syādvipāśā tu vipāṭ striyām
(1.10.585) śoṇo hiraṇyavāhaḥ syātkulyālpā kṛtrimā sarit
children.translated_text:
## River Shatadru (2), River Vipasha (2), River Shona (2), Canal (1) ##
(1.10.584) '<s>Śatadru</s>' is '<s>Śutudri</s>.' '<s>Vipāśā</s>' is '<s>Vipāṭ</s>' — feminine.
(1.10.585) '<s>Śoṇa</s>' is '<s>Hiraṇyavāha</s>' (gold-bearing). '<s>Kulyā</s>' is a small, man-made river (canal).

children.text:
## List of five rivers, additional list includes:## kaushikii, gaNDakii, charmaNvatii,godaa, veNii ## etc.##
## Mouth of a river (1), Channel or water-course (1) ##
(1.10.586) śarāvatī vetravatī candrabhāgā sarasvatī
(1.10.587) kāverī sarito 'nyāśca sambhedaḥ sindhusaṅgamaḥ
(1.10.588) dvayoḥ praṇālī payasaḥ padavyāṃ triṣu tūttarau
children.translated_text:
## List of five rivers, additional list includes Kauśikī, Gaṇḍakī, Carmaṇvatī, Godā, Veṇī, etc. ##
## Mouth of a river (1), Channel or water-course (1) ##
(1.10.586) <s>Śarāvatī</s>, <s>Vetravatī</s>, <s>Candrabhāgā</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>,
(1.10.587) <s>Kāverī</s> — and other rivers. '<s>Saṃbheda</s>' (confluence) is the joining of rivers.
(1.10.588) '<s>Praṇālī</s>' is a water channel — [used] for the two [genders]; but '<s>uttara</s>' is [used] in all three genders.

children.text:
## Things born in a river ##devikaa## or ##sarayuu##: sample construction ##
(1.10.589) devikāyāṃ sarayvāṃ ca bhave dāvikasāravau
children.translated_text:
## Things born in a river Devikā or Sarayū: sample construction ##
(1.10.589) [That which] is born in the <s>Devikā</s> and the <s>Sarayū</s> [rivers is called] '<s>dāvika</s>' and '<s>sārava</s>' respectively.

children.text:
## Night-blooming lotus: White (2), Red (2) ##
(1.10.590) saugandhikaṃ tu kalhāraṃ hallakaṃ raktasandhyakam
children.translated_text:
## Night-blooming lotus: White (2), Red (2) ##
(1.10.590) '<s>Saugandhika</s>' (fragrant) is '<s>kalhāra</s>' (white night-lotus). '<s>Hallaka</s>' is '<s>raktasandhyaka</s>' (red twilight-lotus).

children.text:
## Water lily (2), Blue (2), White (2), Root (of) lily (1), Pistia Stratiotes (2) ##
(1.10.591) syādutpalaṃ kuvalayamatha nīlāmbujanma ca
(1.10.592) indīvaraṃ ca nīle 'sminsite kumudakairave
(1.10.593) śālūkameṣāṃ kandaḥ syādvāriparṇī tu kumbhikā
children.translated_text:
## Water lily (2), Blue (2), White (2), Root (of) lily (1), Pistia Stratiotes (2) ##
(1.10.591) '<s>Utpala</s>' (water lily) is '<s>kuvalaya</s>.' And then '<s>nīlāmbujanma</s>' (blue water-born),
(1.10.592) '<s>indīvara</s>' — these [mean] 'blue [lotus].' For the white [one]: '<s>kumuda</s>' and '<s>kairava</s>' [are the names].
(1.10.593) '<s>Śālūka</s>' is the root of these [lotuses]. '<s>Vāriparṇī</s>' (water-leafed) is '<s>kumbhikā</s>' (water lettuce).

children.text:
## Aquatic plant, moss (3), Full of lilies (2), Full of lotuses (3) ##
(1.10.594) jalanīlī tu śaivālaṃ śaivalo 'tha kumudvatī
(1.10.595) kumudinyāṃ nalinyāṃ tu visinīpadminīmukhāḥ
children.translated_text:
## Aquatic plant, moss (3), Full of lilies (2), Full of lotuses (3) ##
(1.10.594) '<s>Jalanīlī</s>' (water-blue) is '<s>śaivāla</s>' (moss); '<s>śaivala</s>' [is a variant]. And then '<s>kumudvatī</s>,'
(1.10.595) '<s>kumudinyām</s>' [mean 'full of lilies']; but '<s>nalinī</s>,' '<s>visinī</s>,' '<s>padminī</s>' and the like [mean 'full of lotuses'].

children.text:
## Lotus (16) ##
(1.10.596) vā puṃsi padmaṃ nalinamaravindaṃ mahotpalam
(1.10.597) sahasrapatraṃ kamalaṃ śatapatraṃ kuśeśayam
(1.10.598) paṅkeruhaṃ tāmarasaṃ sārasaṃ sarasīruham
(1.10.599) bisaprasūnarājīvapuṣkarāmbhoruhāṇi ca
children.translated_text:
## Lotus (16) ##
(1.10.596) Optionally masculine: '<s>padma</s>,' '<s>nalina</s>,' '<s>aravinda</s>,' '<s>mahotpala</s>' (great water-lily),
(1.10.597) '<s>sahasrapatra</s>' (thousand-petaled), '<s>kamala</s>,' '<s>śatapatra</s>' (hundred-petaled), '<s>kuśeśaya</s>' (resting in the waters),
(1.10.598) '<s>paṅkeruha</s>' (mud-born), '<s>tāmarasa</s>' (copper-red), '<s>sārasa</s>' (of the lake), '<s>sarasīruha</s>' (lake-grown),
(1.10.599) '<s>bisaprasūna</s>' (fiber-flower), '<s>rājīva</s>' (striped), '<s>puṣkara</s>,' '<s>ambhoruha</s>' (water-born) — [all are synonyms for lotus].

children.text:
## Lotus: white (2), red (3), Stalk of water lily (3) ##
(1.10.600) puṇḍarīkaṃ sitāmbhojamatha raktasaroruhe
(1.10.601) raktotpalaṃ kokanadaṃ nālo nālamathāstriyām
children.translated_text:
## Lotus: white (2), red (3), Stalk of water lily (3) ##
(1.10.600) '<s>Puṇḍarīka</s>' and '<s>sitāmbhoja</s>' (white water-born) [mean 'white lotus']. And for the red lotus:
(1.10.601) '<s>raktotpala</s>' (red water-lily), '<s>kokanada</s>' [are synonyms]. '<s>Nāla</s>' and '<s>nāla</s>' [mean 'stalk'] — the latter not feminine.

children.text: ## Lotus fibre (2), Collection of water lilies (1) ##
children.translated_text: ## Lotus fibre (2), Collection of water lilies (1) ##

children.text:
## The words ##khaNDA## or ##shhaNDa## mean an assemblage in general. ##
(1.10.602) mṛṇālaṃ bisamabjādikadambe khaṇḍamastriyām
children.translated_text:
## The words khaṇḍa or ṣaṇḍa mean an assemblage in general. ##
(1.10.602) '<s>Mṛṇāla</s>' (lotus fiber) is '<s>bisa</s>.' A collection of lotuses and the like is '<s>kadamba</s>'; '<s>khaṇḍa</s>' — not feminine [means 'a cluster'].

children.text:
## Parts of water lily: root (2), filament (2), new leaf (2), Lotus seed (2) ##
(1.10.603) karahāṭaḥ śiphākandaḥ kiñjalkaḥ kesaro 'striyām
(1.10.604) saṃvartikā navadalaṃ bījakośo varāṭakaḥ
children.translated_text: Parts of a water lily: <s>karahāṭaḥ</s> and <s>śiphākandaḥ</s> are synonyms for root; <s>kiñjalkaḥ</s> and <s>kesaraḥ</s> (not feminine) are synonyms for filament; <s>saṃvartikā</s> and <s>navadalam</s> are synonyms for new leaf; <s>bījakośaḥ</s> and <s>varāṭakaḥ</s> are synonyms for lotus seed-pod.
End of the section (<s>kāṇḍasamāptiḥ</s>).

children.text:
## All the 10 sections of the first part with main and related words are thus finished. ##
(1.11.605) uktaṃ svarvyomadikkāladhīśabdādi sanāṭyakam
(1.11.606) pātālabhoginarakaṃ vāri caiṣāṃ ca saṅgatam
(1.11.607) ityamarasiṃhakṛtau nāmaliṅgānuśāsane
(1.11.608) svarādikāṇḍaḥ prathamaḥ sāṅga eva samarthitaḥ
children.translated_text: All the ten sections of the first part, with main and related words, are thus finished. The topics of heaven, sky, directions, time, mind, speech and so forth together with drama, the netherworld, serpents, hell, water, and their associated terms have been stated. Thus in the <s>Nāmaliṅgānuśāsana</s> composed by <s>Amarasiṃha</s>, the first part called <s>Svarādikāṇḍa</s> (beginning with heaven) is fully established with all its sub-sections.
<s>Amarakośa</s>, also known as <s>Nāmaliṅgānuśāsana</s>, Part 2.
In the <s>Amarakośa</s>, the second part is the <s>Bhūmyādikāṇḍa</s> (the section beginning with Earth).
Division of sections (<s>vargabhedāḥ</s>):
The sections here are arranged by: earth (<s>pṛthvī</s>), city (<s>pura</s>), mountain (<s>kṣmābhṛt</s>), forest (<s>vana</s>), herbs (<s>oṣadhi</s>), animals (<s>mṛga</s>) and others,
humans (<s>nṛ</s>), <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and <s>Śūdras</s> — these are stated here with all their main and subsidiary terms.
Section on Earth (<s>bhūmivargaḥ</s>).
Synonyms for the Earth (fem.): <s>bhūḥ</s>, <s>bhūmiḥ</s>, <s>acalā</s>, <s>anantā</s>, <s>rasā</s>, <s>viśvambharā</s>, <s>sthirā</s>,

children.text: (2.1.4) dharā dharitrī dharaṇiḥ kṣoṇirjyā kāśyapī kṣitiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>dharā</s>, <s>dharitrī</s>, <s>dharaṇiḥ</s>, <s>kṣoṇiḥ</s>, <s>jyā</s>, <s>kāśyapī</s>, <s>kṣitiḥ</s>,
<s>sarvaṃsahā</s>, <s>vasumatī</s>, <s>vasudhā</s>, <s>urvī</s>, <s>vasundharā</s>,

children.text: (2.1.6) gotrā kuḥ pṛthivī pṛthvī kṣmāvanirmedinī mahī
children.translated_text: <s>gotrā</s>, <s>kuḥ</s>, <s>pṛthivī</s>, <s>pṛthvī</s>, <s>kṣmā</s>, <s>avaniḥ</s>, <s>medinī</s>, <s>mahī</s>,

children.text: (2.1.7) vipulā gahvarī dhātrī gaurilā kumbhinī kṣamā
children.translated_text: <s>vipulā</s>, <s>gahvarī</s>, <s>dhātrī</s>, <s>gauḥ</s>, <s>ilā</s>, <s>kumbhinī</s>, <s>kṣamā</s>,
<s>bhūtadhātrī</s>, <s>ratnagarbhā</s>, <s>jagatī</s>, <s>sāgarāmbarā</s> — all these are synonyms for the Earth.

children.text: (2.1.9) mṛnmṛttikā praśastā tu mṛtsā mṛtsnā ca mṛttikā
children.translated_text: <s>Mṛt</s> and <s>mṛttikā</s> mean soil. The superior kind is called <s>mṛtsā</s>, <s>mṛtsnā</s>, and also <s>mṛttikā</s> (clay).

children.text:
(2.1.10) urvarā sarvasasyāḍhyā syādūṣaḥ kṣāramṛttikā
(2.1.11) ūṣavānūṣaro dvāvapyanyaliṅgau sthalaṃ sthalī
children.translated_text: <s>Urvarā</s> means land rich in all crops. <s>Ūṣaḥ</s> (masc.) means saline soil (<s>kṣāramṛttikā</s>). <s>Ūṣavān</s> and <s>ūṣaraḥ</s> — both can be of any gender. <s>Sthalam</s> (neut.) and <s>sthalī</s> (fem.) mean dry ground.
<s>Maruḥ</s> and <s>dhanvā</s> are synonyms for desert, both equal. <s>Khila</s> and <s>aprahata</s> are synonyms for uncultivated land, both equal (and in dual).

children.text: (2.1.13) triṣvatho jagatī loko viṣṭapaṃ bhuvanaṃ jagat
children.translated_text: <s>Jagatī</s>, <s>lokaḥ</s>, <s>viṣṭapam</s>, <s>bhuvanam</s>, <s>jagat</s> — these are synonyms for the world. They are used in all three genders.
This world is called <s>Bhāratam varṣam</s> (the land of <s>Bhārata</s>), which lies south of the river <s>Śarāvatī</s>.
A <s>deśa</s> (country/region): that which is to the east and south is called <s>prācya</s> (eastern); that to the west and north is called <s>udīcya</s> (northern).
A border region is called <s>pratyanta</s> or <s>mlecchadeśa</s> (land of the barbarians). The central region is called <s>madhyadeśa</s> or <s>madhyama</s>.
<s>Āryāvarta</s> (the abode of the noble) is the sacred land (<s>puṇyabhūmi</s>) between the <s>Vindhya</s> and <s>Himālaya</s> mountains.
<s>Nīvṛt</s> means a settled habitation. <s>Janapada</s> and <s>deśaviṣaya</s> are synonyms for a district or province. <s>Upavartanam</s> means a suburb or outskirts.
A place abounding in reeds is called <s>naḍvān</s> or <s>naḍvala</s> — these are used in all three genders.
A place abounding in lotuses is called <s>kumudvān</s>; a place abounding in cane-reeds is called <s>vetasvān</s>.
<s>Śādvalaḥ</s> means a place green with grass. <s>Paṅkilaḥ</s> means a place full of mud (<s>jambāla</s>).
A marshy place, mostly water, is called <s>anūpam</s> (neut.). <s>Kacchaḥ</s> (masc.) is also of that nature.
<s>Śarkarā</s> (fem.) means gravel. <s>Śarkarilaḥ</s> and <s>śārkaraḥ</s> mean a gravelly place.
These same formations apply to a region with sand (<s>sikatāvat</s>), and so on, to be inferred similarly.
A country nourished by river-water is called <s>nadīmātṛka</s>; one nourished by rain-water is called <s>devamātṛka</s>,
respectively, in that order.
In a well-governed country, one says <s>rājanvān</s>; in other contexts, <s>rājavān</s>.
<s>Goṣṭham</s> and <s>gosthānakam</s> mean a cow-pen. <s>Gauṣṭhīnam</s> means what formerly was a cow-pen.
<s>Parisaraḥ</s> means the surrounding border-land. <s>Setuḥ</s> means a dam or bridge — feminine as <s>āl</s>, and masculine.
<s>Vāmalūraḥ</s> and <s>nākuḥ</s> are synonyms. <s>Valmīkam</s> (anthill) is both masculine and neuter.
<s>Ayanam</s>, <s>vartma</s>, <s>mārga</s>, <s>adhvan</s>, <s>panthānaḥ</s>, <s>padavī</s>, <s>sṛtiḥ</s>,
<s>saraṇiḥ</s>, <s>paddhatiḥ</s>, <s>padyā</s>, <s>vartanī</s>, <s>ekapadī</s> — all these are synonyms for a road or path.
<s>Atipanthāḥ</s>, <s>supanthāḥ</s>, and <s>satpathaḥ</s> are synonyms for a well-maintained, good road.

children.text: (2.1.34) vyadhvo duradhvo vipathaḥ kadadhvā kāpathaḥ samāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vyadhvaḥ</s>, <s>duradhvaḥ</s>, <s>vipathaḥ</s>, <s>kadadhvā</s>, and <s>kāpathaḥ</s> are synonyms for a bad road — all equal in meaning.
<s>Apanthāḥ</s> means a pathless place; <s>apatham</s> is its equal. <s>Śṛṅgāṭakam</s> and <s>catuṣpatham</s> mean a crossroads.
<s>Prāntaram</s> means a long, desolate road. <s>Kāntāram</s> means a road that is difficult to traverse.
<s>Gavyūtiḥ</s> (fem.) is a measure of two <s>krośas</s>. <s>Nalvaḥ</s> is four hundred <s>kiṣku</s> (cubits).
<s>Ghaṇṭāpathaḥ</s> and <s>saṃsaraṇam</s> are synonyms for a royal highway. <s>Upaniṣkaram</s> means the area just outside a city gate.
<s>Dyāvāpṛthivyau</s>, <s>rodasyau</s>, <s>dyāvābhūmī</s>, and <s>rodasī</s> — these (in dual) mean heaven and earth together.

children.text: (2.1.40) divaspṛthivyau gañjā tu rumā syāllavaṇākaraḥ | iti bhūmivargaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Divaspṛthivyau</s> also means heaven and earth. <s>Gañjā</s> means a treasure-house. <s>Rumā</s> means a salt-mine (<s>lavaṇākara</s>). Thus ends the section on Earth (<s>bhūmivargaḥ</s>).
Section on Cities (<s>puravargaḥ</s>).

children.text: (2.2.41) pūḥ strī purīnagaryau vā pattanaṃ puṭabhedanam | atha puravargaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Pūḥ</s> (fem.), <s>purī</s>, <s>nagarī</s> (optionally fem.), <s>pattanam</s>, <s>puṭabhedanam</s> — these are synonyms for a city. Now begins the section on cities.
<s>Sthānīyam</s> means a provincial town. <s>Nigamaḥ</s> is another kind. A city that is subordinate to the capital (<s>mūlanagara</s>)
is called <s>śākhānagaram</s> (a branch-city). <s>Veśaḥ</s> means a quarter inhabited by courtesans (<s>veśyā</s>).
<s>Āpaṇaḥ</s> means a shop or marketplace in the sense of a place of sitting. <s>Vipaṇiḥ</s> and <s>paṇyavīthikā</s> mean a market-street.
<s>Rathyā</s>, <s>pratolī</s>, and <s>viśikhā</s> are synonyms for a broad street. <s>Cayaḥ</s> and <s>vapram</s> (not feminine) mean a rampart or embankment.

children.text: (2.2.46) prākāro varaṇaḥ sālaḥ prācīnaṃ prātanto vṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Prākāraḥ</s>, <s>varaṇaḥ</s>, <s>sālaḥ</s> are synonyms for a surrounding wall. <s>Prācīnam</s>, <s>prātantaḥ</s>, and <s>vṛtiḥ</s> mean a fence or enclosure.
<s>Bhittiḥ</s> (fem.) and <s>kuḍyam</s> mean a wall. <s>Eḍūkam</s> means a structure with bones deposited inside it.
<s>Gṛham</s>, <s>geham</s>, <s>udavasitam</s>, <s>veśma</s>, <s>sadma</s>, <s>niketanam</s>,
<s>niśāntam</s>, <s>pastya</s>, <s>sadanam</s>, <s>bhavanam</s>, <s>agāram</s>, <s>mandiram</s>,
<s>gṛhāḥ</s> (masc. plural only), <s>nikāyyaḥ</s>, <s>nilayaḥ</s>, <s>ālayaḥ</s> — all these are synonyms for a house or dwelling.

children.text: (2.2.51) vāsaḥ kuṭī dvayoḥ śālā sabhā saṃjavanaṃ tvidam
children.translated_text: <s>Vāsaḥ</s> and <s>kuṭī</s> are used in both genders. <s>Śālā</s> means a hall. <s>Sabhā</s> and <s>saṃjavanam</s> — this (latter) is the same (as sabhā, an assembly hall).
<s>Catuḥśālam</s> means a four-sided hall. For sages, a <s>parṇaśālā</s> (leaf-hut) or <s>uṭaja</s> (not feminine) is used.
<s>Caityam</s> and <s>āyatanam</s> are synonyms for a temple or sacred enclosure. A horse-stable is called <s>mandurā</s> (<s>vājiśālā</s>).
<s>Āveśanam</s> means a craftsmen's workshop (<s>śilpiśālā</s>). <s>Prapā</s> means a water-dispensing shed (<s>pānīyaśālikā</s>).
<s>Maṭhaḥ</s> means a residence for students and the like. <s>Gañjā</s> means a liquor-house (<s>madirāgṛham</s>).
<s>Garbhāgāram</s> means an inner chamber or bedroom (<s>vāsagṛham</s>). <s>Ariṣṭam</s> means a lying-in chamber (<s>sūtikāgṛham</s>).
<s>Kuṭṭimaḥ</s> (not feminine) means a paved or plastered floor (<s>nibaddhā bhūḥ</s>). <s>Candraśālā</s> means an upper room or rooftop pavilion (<s>śirogṛham</s>).
<s>Vātāyanam</s> and <s>gavākṣaḥ</s> are synonyms for a window. <s>Maṇḍapaḥ</s> (not feminine) means an open pavilion or public shelter (<s>janāśrayaḥ</s>).
<s>Harmya</s> and the like mean the residences of the wealthy. <s>Prāsādaḥ</s> means the palace of gods and kings.
<s>Saudhaḥ</s> (not feminine) means a royal residence (<s>rājasadanam</s>). <s>Upakāryā</s> and <s>upakārikā</s> are synonyms for a subsidiary building.
<s>Svastikaḥ</s>, <s>sarvatobhadraḥ</s>, <s>nandyāvarta</s> and others,
as well as <s>vicchandakaḥ</s> — these are varieties or designs of royal mansions.
<s>Stryagāram</s> means the women's quarters. For kings, <s>antaḥpuram</s> and <s>avarodhanam</s> mean the inner palace (harem).
<s>Śuddhāntaḥ</s> and <s>avarodhaḥ</s> also mean the inner apartments. <s>Aṭṭaḥ</s> means a watchtower. <s>Kṣaumam</s> (not feminine) means a linen cloth.
<s>Praghāṇa</s>, <s>praghaṇa</s>, and <s>alinda</s> are synonyms for the outer porch or vestibule at the outer gate.
<s>Gṛhāvagrahaṇī</s> means the threshold. <s>Dehalī</s> also means a threshold. <s>Aṅgaṇam</s>, <s>catvaram</s>, and <s>ajiram</s> are synonyms for a courtyard.
A stone placed underneath the wooden door-frame is called <s>nāsā</s>; the timber placed above it is also specified.
<s>Pracchannam</s> means a concealed inner door. <s>Pakṣadvāram</s> or <s>pakṣakam</s> means a side-door or wicket.
<s>Valīka</s> and <s>nīdhram</s> mean the edge of a roof-panel. Then <s>paṭalam</s> and <s>chadiḥ</s> mean the roof or covering.
<s>Gopānasī</s> and <s>valabhī</s> mean the curved beam used for roofing.
For the eave-bracket (<s>kapotapālikā</s>), <s>viṭaṅkam</s> is used, which is both masculine and neuter.
<s>Dvāḥ</s> (fem.) and <s>dvāram</s> mean a door. <s>Pratīhāraḥ</s> means a door-keeper. <s>Hitardhi</s> means a raised platform or <s>vedikā</s>.
<s>Toraṇaḥ</s> (not feminine) means an outer gateway or arch. <s>Gopuram</s> means a city gate-tower.
<s>Kūṭam</s> means the ornamental top of a city gate — the elephant-tusk-shaped projection on it. Then, in all three genders:
<s>Kapāṭam</s> and <s>araram</s> are synonyms for a door-panel. <s>Viṣkambhaḥ</s> means a bolt. <s>Argalam</s> can be either neuter or feminine.
<s>Ārohaṇam</s> and <s>sopānam</s> mean a staircase. <s>Niśreṇī</s> means a ladder (<s>adhirohiṇī</s>).
<s>Saṃmārjanī</s> and <s>śodhanī</s> mean a broom. <s>Saṃkaraḥ</s> and <s>avakaraḥ</s> mean sweepings or rubbish.
<s>Mukham</s> means an outlet or opening when referring to something thrown out. <s>Niḥsaraṇam</s> means an exit. <s>Saṃniveśaḥ</s> means a settlement or layout. <s>Nikarṣaṇam</s> means a drainage.
<s>Saṃvasathaḥ</s> and <s>grāmaḥ</s> are synonyms for a village. <s>Veśmabhūḥ</s> and <s>vāstuḥ</s> (not feminine) mean a house-site or plot.
The outskirts of a village are called <s>upaśalyam</s>. <s>Sīmā</s> and <s>sīme</s> — both are feminine, meaning a boundary.

children.text: (2.2.81) ghoṣa ābhīrapallī syātpakkaṇaḥ śabarālayaḥ | iti puravargaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Ghoṣaḥ</s> means a settlement of cowherds (<s>Ābhīra</s>). <s>Pakkaṇaḥ</s> means a settlement of forest-dwellers (<s>Śabara</s>). Thus ends the section on cities (<s>puravargaḥ</s>).
Section on Mountains (<s>śailavargaḥ</s>).
Synonyms for mountain: <s>mahīdhraḥ</s>, <s>śikharin</s>, <s>kṣmābhṛt</s>, <s>ahāryaḥ</s>, <s>dharaḥ</s>, <s>parvataḥ</s>. Now begins the section on mountains.
<s>Adriḥ</s>, <s>gotraḥ</s>, <s>giriḥ</s>, <s>grāvā</s>, <s>acalaḥ</s>, <s>śailaḥ</s>, <s>śiloccayaḥ</s> — these are also synonyms for mountain.
<s>Lokālokaḥ</s> and <s>Cakravālaḥ</s> are names of the boundary mountain encircling the world. <s>Trikūṭaḥ</s> and <s>Trikakut</s> are synonyms for the three-peaked mountain.
<s>Astaḥ</s> is the western mountain (the setting mountain). <s>Udayaḥ</s> is the eastern mountain (the rising mountain).
<s>Himavān</s>, <s>Niṣadhaḥ</s>, <s>Vindhyaḥ</s>, <s>Mālyavān</s>, <s>Pāriyātrikaḥ</s>,
<s>Gandhamādanaḥ</s> and others such as <s>Hemakūṭa</s> — these are names of specific mountains (<s>naga</s>).
<s>Pāṣāṇaḥ</s>, <s>prastaraḥ</s>, <s>grāvā</s>, <s>upalaḥ</s>, <s>aśmā</s> (masc.) mean stone or rock. <s>Śilā</s> (fem.) and <s>dṛṣat</s> (fem.) also mean stone.
<s>Kūṭaḥ</s> (not feminine), <s>śikharam</s>, and <s>śṛṅgam</s> mean a peak or summit. <s>Prapātaḥ</s> means a precipice. <s>Ataṭaḥ</s> and <s>bhṛguḥ</s> mean a cliff or steep slope.
<s>Kaṭakaḥ</s> (not feminine) and <s>nitambaḥ</s> mean the slope or hip of a mountain. <s>Snuḥ</s>, <s>prasthaḥ</s>, and <s>sānuḥ</s> (not feminine) mean a plateau or tableland.
<s>Utsaḥ</s> and <s>prasravaṇam</s> mean a spring. <s>Vāripravāhaḥ</s>, <s>nirjharaḥ</s>, and <s>jharaḥ</s> mean a waterfall or mountain stream.

children.text: (2.3.92) darī tu kandaro vā strī devakhātabile guhā
children.translated_text: <s>Darī</s> (fem.) and <s>kandaraḥ</s> (masc. or fem.) mean a cave. <s>Devakhāta</s>, <s>bila</s>, and <s>guhā</s> also mean a cave or cavern.
<s>Gahvaram</s> means a deep recess or ravine. <s>Gaṇḍaśailāḥ</s> are large boulders that have fallen from a mountain.
<s>Dantakāḥ</s> are rocky projections that extend outward and sideways from a mountain.
<s>Khaniḥ</s> (fem.) and <s>ākaraḥ</s> mean a mine. <s>Pādāḥ</s> means the foothills or outlying mountains (<s>pratyantaparvatāḥ</s>).
<s>Upatyakā</s> means the land near the base of a mountain. <s>Adhityakā</s> means the land above, on the mountain's upper surface.
<s>Dhātuḥ</s> means mineral ores such as <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) found in mountains. <s>Gairikam</s> specifically means red ochre.

children.text: (2.3.98) nikuñjakuñjau vā klībe latādipihitodare | iti śailavargaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Nikuñjaḥ</s> and <s>kuñjaḥ</s> (optionally neuter) mean a bower or arbour concealed by creepers. Thus ends the section on mountains (<s>śailavargaḥ</s>).
Section on Forests and Herbs (<s>vanauṣadhivargaḥ</s>).

children.text: (2.4.99) aṭavyaraṇyaṃ vipinaṃ gahanaṃ kānanaṃ vanam | atha vanauṣadhivargaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Aṭavī</s>, <s>araṇyam</s>, <s>vipinam</s>, <s>gahanam</s>, <s>kānanam</s>, <s>vanam</s> — these are synonyms for a forest. Now begins the section on forests and herbs.
<s>Mahāraṇyam</s> means a great wilderness. <s>Araṇyānī</s> is a feminine form for forest. <s>Niṣkuṭāḥ</s> means gardens attached to houses (<s>gṛhārāma</s>).
<s>Ārāmaḥ</s> and <s>upavanam</s> mean a pleasure garden — an artificially made forest.
A garden at the residence of a minister or courtesan is called <s>vṛkṣavāṭikā</s> (a tree-garden or grove).
<s>Ākrīḍaḥ</s> (masc.) and <s>udyānam</s> mean a royal pleasure-park — a public garden belonging to the king.
This same, when designated for the women of the inner palace, is called <s>pramadavanam</s> (the pleasure-grove of the queen's quarters).
<s>Vīthī</s>, <s>āliḥ</s>, <s>āvaliḥ</s>, <s>paṅktiḥ</s>, <s>śreṇī</s>, <s>lekhā</s> — these are synonyms for a row or line. <s>Rājayaḥ</s> also means rows (of trees).
<s>Vanyā</s> means a grove or collection of forest-trees. <s>Aṅkuraḥ</s> means a fresh sprout or newly emerged shoot.
Synonyms for a tree: <s>vṛkṣaḥ</s>, <s>mahīruhaḥ</s>, <s>śākhī</s>, <s>viṭapī</s>, <s>pādapaḥ</s>, <s>taruḥ</s>,
<s>anokahaḥ</s>, <s>kuṭaḥ</s>, <s>śālaḥ</s>, <s>palāśī</s>, <s>druḥ</s>, <s>drumaḥ</s>, <s>āgamāḥ</s> — all are synonyms for tree.
<s>Vānaspatyaḥ</s> is a tree that bears fruit from flowers. <s>Vanaspatiḥ</s> is a tree that bears fruit without flowers.
<s>Oṣadhyaḥ</s> (herbs) are plants that perish after their fruit ripens. A plant that is never barren (always fruit-bearing) is called <s>phalegrahī</s>.
<s>Vandhyaḥ</s> and <s>aphalaḥ</s> mean barren (fruitless). <s>Avakeśī</s> also means barren. <s>Phalavān</s>, <s>phalinaḥ</s>, and <s>phalī</s> mean fruit-bearing.
<s>Praphulla</s>, <s>utphulla</s>, <s>saṃphulla</s>, <s>vyākośa</s>, <s>vikaca</s>, <s>sphuṭa</s>,
and <s>phulla</s> — all these mean 'in full bloom' (<s>vikasite</s>). <s>Avandhya</s> and the like are used in all three genders.
<s>Sthāṇuḥ</s> (masc. or fem.) means a stump or dead tree-trunk. <s>Dhruvaḥ</s> and <s>śaṅkuḥ</s> are synonyms. <s>Kṣupaḥ</s> means a shrub with short branches and spreading roots.
<s>Stamba</s> and <s>gulma</s> mean a bush without a trunk. <s>Vallī</s>, <s>vratatī</s>, and <s>latā</s> mean a creeper or vine.
<s>Latā</s>, <s>pratāninī</s>, <s>vīrut</s>, and <s>gulminī</s> are synonyms. <s>Ulapa</s> also means a type of creeping plant.
<s>Ucchrāyaḥ</s>, <s>utsedhaḥ</s>, and <s>ucchrayaḥ</s> are synonyms for the height of a tree and the like — the upward growth (<s>āroha</s>).
<s>Prakāṇḍaḥ</s> (not feminine) and <s>skandhaḥ</s> mean the trunk of a tree — the portion from the root to the branches.
<s>Śākhā</s> and <s>latā</s> are synonyms for a branch; <s>skandhaśākhā</s> and <s>śālā</s> mean a main branch. <s>Śiphā</s> and <s>jaṭā</s> mean aerial roots.
<s>Śākhāśiphāvarohaḥ</s> means a hanging aerial root descending from the branches — a creeper that grows downward from the branches to the ground.

children.text: (2.4.121) śirograṃ śikharaṃ vā nā mūlaṃ budhno 'ṅghrināmakaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śiras</s>, <s>agra</s>, and <s>śikharam</s> (masc. or neut.) mean the top or crown of a tree. <s>Mūlam</s>, <s>budhnaḥ</s>, and <s>aṅghriḥ</s> mean the root or base.

children.text: (2.4.122) sāro majjā nari tvakstrī valkaṃ valkalamastriyām
children.translated_text: <s>Sāraḥ</s> and <s>majjā</s> (fem.) mean the heartwood or pith. <s>Tvak</s> (fem.) means the bark. <s>Valkam</s> and <s>valkalam</s> (not feminine) also mean bark.
<s>Kāṣṭham</s> means wood. <s>Dāru</s> also means timber. <s>Indhanam</s> means fuel, as do <s>idhma</s>, <s>edhaḥ</s>, and <s>samit</s> (fem.).

children.text: (2.4.124) niṣkuhaḥ koṭaraṃ vā nā vallarirmañjariḥ striyau
children.translated_text: <s>Niṣkuhaḥ</s> and <s>koṭaram</s> (masc. or neut.) mean a hollow in a tree. <s>Vallarī</s> and <s>mañjarī</s> (both fem.) mean a flower-cluster or blossom-spray.

children.text: (2.4.125) patraṃ palāśaṃ chadanaṃ dalaṃ parṇaṃ chadaḥ pumān
children.translated_text: <s>Patram</s>, <s>palāśam</s>, <s>chadanam</s>, <s>dalam</s>, <s>parṇam</s> — these mean a leaf. <s>Chadaḥ</s> (masc.) also means a leaf.
