<s>Pallavaḥ</s> (not feminine) and <s>kisalayam</s> mean a tender young shoot or sprout. <s>Vistāraḥ</s> and <s>viṭapaḥ</s> (not feminine) mean the spreading canopy of a tree.
<s>Phalam</s> means fruit of trees and the like. <s>Sasyam</s> means crop or harvest. <s>Vṛntam</s> means the stalk connecting the fruit to the branch (<s>prasavabandhanam</s>).

children.text: (2.4.128) āme phale śalāṭuḥ syācchuṣke vānamubhe triṣu
children.translated_text: An unripe fruit is called <s>śalāṭuḥ</s>. A dried fruit is called <s>vānam</s>. Both are used in all three genders.

children.text: (2.4.129) kṣārako jālakaṃ klībe kalikā korakaḥ pumān
children.translated_text: <s>Kṣārakaḥ</s> means an alkali plant. <s>Jālakam</s> (neut.) means a bud-covering or calyx. <s>Kalikā</s> (fem.) and <s>korakaḥ</s> (masc.) mean a bud.
<s>Gucchakaḥ</s> and <s>stabakaḥ</s> mean a bunch or cluster of flowers. <s>Kuṅmalaḥ</s> and <s>mukulaḥ</s> (not feminine) mean a bud about to open.

children.text: (2.4.131) striyaḥ sumanasaḥ puṣpaṃ prasūnaṃ kusumaṃ sumam
children.translated_text: <s>Sumanasaḥ</s> (fem. plural), <s>puṣpam</s>, <s>prasūnam</s>, <s>kusumam</s>, <s>sumam</s> — these are synonyms for a flower.
<s>Makarandaḥ</s> means flower-nectar (<s>puṣparasaḥ</s>). <s>Parāgaḥ</s> means pollen — the dust of flowers (<s>sumanorajaḥ</s>).
All the terms minus the last two syllables designate the fruit as well. <s>Harītakī</s> and the like are feminine.

<s>Āśvattham</s> (from the <s>Aśvattha</s> tree), <s>vaiṇavam</s> (from bamboo), <s>plākṣam</s> (from the <s>Plakṣa</s> tree), <s>naiyagrodham</s> (from the banyan), <s>aiṅgudam</s> — these refer to the respective fruits.

children.text: (2.4.135) bārhataṃ ca phale jambvā jambūḥ strī jambu jāmbavam
children.translated_text: <s>Bārhatam</s> refers to the fruit of the <s>Bṛhatī</s> plant. <s>Jambūḥ</s> (fem.) is the rose-apple tree. <s>Jambu</s> and <s>jāmbavam</s> refer to its fruit.
(2.4.136) Among flowers, <s>jātī</s> and others retain their own gender; <s>vrīhi</s> (rice) and others [retain their gender] when denoting fruit.
(2.4.137) <s>vidārī</s> and others are [used] also for roots; <s>pāṭalā</s> is neuter also when denoting a flower.
(2.4.138) <s>Bodhidruma</s> (the tree of enlightenment), <s>Caladala</s> (trembling-leaved), <s>Pippala</s>, <s>Kuñjarāśana</s> (elephant-food),
(2.4.139) [are synonyms] for the <s>aśvattha</s> (sacred fig) tree. Then for the <s>kapittha</s> (wood-apple) tree: <s>Dadhittha</s>, <s>Grāhi</s>, <s>Manmatha</s>,
(2.4.140) and also <s>Dadhiphala</s> (curd-fruit), <s>Puṣpaphala</s> (flower-fruit), <s>Dantaśaṭha</s> [are synonyms for kapittha].
(2.4.141) <s>Udumbara</s> (cluster fig): <s>Jantuphala</s> (insect-fruit), <s>Yajñāṅga</s> (part of sacrifice), <s>Hemadugdhaka</s> (golden-milked).
(2.4.142) For <s>kovidāra</s> (Bauhinia): <s>Camarika</s>, <s>Kuddāla</s>, <s>Yugapatraka</s> (paired-leaf).
(2.4.143) <s>Saptaparṇa</s> (seven-leaved): <s>Viśālatvak</s> (broad-barked), <s>Śārada</s> (autumnal), <s>Viṣamacchada</s> (odd-leaved).
(2.4.144) For <s>āragvadha</s> (Cassia fistula): <s>Rājavṛkṣa</s> (king-tree), <s>Śampāka</s>, <s>Caturaṅgula</s> (four-fingers),
(2.4.145) <s>Ārevata</s>, <s>Vyādhighāta</s> (disease-destroyer), <s>Kṛtamāla</s> (wreath-maker), <s>Suvarṇaka</s> (golden).
(2.4.146) For <s>jambīra</s> (citron): <s>Dantaśaṭha</s>, <s>Jambha</s>, <s>Jambhīra</s>, <s>Jambhala</s>.
(2.4.147) <s>Varuṇa</s>: <s>Varaṇa</s>, <s>Setu</s>, <s>Tiktaśāka</s> (bitter vegetable), <s>Kumāraka</s> (youthful).
(2.4.148) For <s>puṃnāga</s> (Calophyllum): <s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>Tuṅga</s> (tall), <s>Kesara</s> (stamen), <s>Devavallabha</s> (beloved of gods).
(2.4.149) For <s>pāribhadra</s>: <s>Nimbataru</s> (neem tree), <s>Mandāra</s>, <s>Pārijātaka</s> (coral tree).
(2.4.150) For <s>tiniśa</s>: <s>Syandana</s> (flowing), <s>Nemī</s>, <s>Rathadru</s> (chariot-wood), <s>Atimuktaka</s> (fully liberated).
(2.4.151) <s>Vañjula</s> and <s>Citrakṛt</s> (picture-maker) [are synonyms for the Asoka tree]; then [separately] <s>Pītanaka</s> and <s>Pītana</s> are a pair [of synonyms].
(2.4.152) For <s>āmrātaka</s> (hog plum); then for <s>madhūka</s> (mahua): <s>Guḍapuṣpa</s> (molasses-flower) and <s>Madhudruma</s> (honey tree).
(2.4.153) <s>Vānaprastha</s> (forest-dwelling) and <s>Madhuṣṭhīla</s> [are synonyms for madhūka]; the aquatic variety of this is <s>Madhūlaka</s>.
(2.4.154) <s>Pīlu</s>: <s>Guḍaphala</s> (molasses-fruit), <s>Sraṃsī</s> (drooping); but when it grows on mountains,
(2.4.155) <s>Akṣoṭa</s> and <s>Kandarāla</s> are a pair [for the walnut]; for <s>aṅkoṭa</s>: <s>Nikocaka</s>.
(2.4.156) For <s>palāśa</s> (flame of the forest): <s>Kiṃśuka</s>, <s>Parṇa</s> (leaf), <s>Vātapota</s>. Then for <s>vetasa</s> (cane/rattan):
(2.4.157) <s>Rathābhra</s>, <s>Puṣpavidura</s>, <s>Śītavānīra</s>, <s>Vañjula</s> [are synonyms for vetasa].
(2.4.158) <s>Parivyādha</s> and <s>Vidula</s> are a pair [of synonyms]; and <s>Nādeyī</s> [is a synonym] for the water-cane (<s>ambuvetasa</s>).
(2.4.159) For <s>śobhāñjana</s> (drumstick tree): <s>Śigru</s>, <s>Tīkṣṇagandha</s> (sharp-smelling), <s>Kākṣīva</s>, <s>Mocaka</s>.
(2.4.160) The red variety of this is <s>Madhuśigru</s> (sweet drumstick); <s>Ariṣṭa</s> and <s>Phenila</s> (foamy) are synonyms [for the soapnut tree].
(2.4.161) For <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple): <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>, <s>Śailūṣa</s>, and also <s>Mālūra</s>, <s>Śrīphala</s> (auspicious fruit).
(2.4.162) <s>Plakṣa</s> (white fig): <s>Jaṭī</s> (matted) and <s>Parkaṭī</s>; the <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan) is <s>Bahupād</s> (many-footed), <s>Vaṭa</s>.
(2.4.163) <s>Gālava</s>, <s>Śābara</s>, <s>Lodhra</s>, <s>Tirīṭa</s>, <s>Tilva</s>, <s>Mārjana</s> (cleanser) [are synonyms for the lodhra tree].
(2.4.164) <s>Āmra</s> (mango): <s>Cūta</s>, <s>Rasāla</s> (juicy); that which is especially fragrant is <s>Sahakāra</s>, <s>Atisaurabha</s> (very fragrant).
(2.4.165) <s>Kumbholūkhala</s> is neuter; <s>Kauśika</s>, <s>Guggulu</s> (bdellium), <s>Pura</s> [are synonyms for guggulu].
(2.4.166) <s>Śelu</s>: <s>Śleṣmātaka</s> (phlegm-producing), <s>Śīta</s> (cool), <s>Uddāla</s>, <s>Bahuvāraka</s> (many-shielded).
(2.4.167) <s>Rājādana</s> (king's food): <s>Priyāla</s>, <s>Sannakadru</s>, <s>Dhanuṣpaṭa</s> (bow-cloth) [are synonyms].
(2.4.168) <s>Gambhārī</s>: <s>Sarvatobhadrā</s> (auspicious on all sides), <s>Kāśmarī</s>, <s>Madhuparṇikā</s> (honey-leaved),
(2.4.169) <s>Śrīparṇī</s> (glorious-leaved), <s>Bhadraparṇī</s> (auspicious-leaved); <s>Kāśmarya</s> also [is a synonym]. Then for [the next] two:
(2.4.170) <s>Karkandhū</s>, <s>Badarī</s>, <s>Koli</s> [are synonyms for the jujube]; <s>Kola</s>, <s>Kuvala</s>, and <s>Phenila</s> (foamy) [are synonyms for the fruit].
(2.4.171) <s>Sauvīra</s>, <s>Badara</s>, <s>Ghoṇṭā</s> also [are synonyms]; then <s>Svādukaṇṭaka</s> (sweet-thorned),
(2.4.172) <s>Vikaṅkata</s>, <s>Suvā</s>, <s>Vṛkṣa</s>, <s>Granthila</s> (knotty), and <s>Vyāghrapād</s> (tiger-footed) also [are synonyms for a thorny tree].
(2.4.173) <s>Airāvata</s>, <s>Nāgaraṅga</s> (serpent-colored); <s>Nādeyī</s>, <s>Bhūmijambukā</s> (ground-jambū) [are synonyms for a citrus variety].
(2.4.174) <s>Tinduka</s> (persimmon): <s>Sphūrjaka</s>, <s>Kālaskandha</s> (dark-trunked) [are synonyms] for the <s>śitisāraka</s> (dark-hearted tree).
(2.4.175) <s>Kākendu</s>, <s>Kulaka</s>, <s>Kākatinduka</s> [are synonyms] for <s>kākapīluka</s> (crow-fruit).
(2.4.176) <s>Golīḍha</s>, <s>Jhāṭala</s>, <s>Ghaṇṭāpāṭali</s>; <s>Mokṣamuṣkaka</s> [are synonyms for the same tree].
(2.4.177) <s>Tilaka</s>: <s>Kṣuraka</s> (razor-like), <s>Śrīmān</s> (glorious); <s>Picula</s> and <s>Jhāvuka</s> are a pair [of synonyms for another tree].
(2.4.178) <s>Śrīparṇikā</s>, <s>Kumudikā</s> (lotus-like), <s>Kumbhī</s> (pot-shaped); <s>Kaiṭarya</s> and <s>Kaṭphala</s> [are synonyms].
(2.4.179) <s>Kramuka</s> (areca/betel-nut): its other name is <s>Paṭṭikā</s>; <s>Paṭṭī</s>, <s>Lākṣāprasādana</s> (lac-producing).

children.text: (2.4.180) tūdastu yūpaḥ kramuko brahmaṇyo brahmadāru ca
children.translated_text: (2.4.180) <s>Tūda</s>: <s>Yūpa</s> (sacrificial post), <s>Kramuka</s>, <s>Brahmaṇya</s> (devoted to Brahman), <s>Brahmadāru</s> (Brahman's wood).
(2.4.181) <s>Tūla</s> (cotton) also [is a synonym]; <s>Nīpa</s>, <s>Priyaka</s>, <s>Kadamba</s> [are synonyms]; <s>Haripriya</s> (dear to <s>Hari</s>) [is another].
(2.4.182) <s>Vīravṛkṣa</s> (hero-tree), <s>Aruṣkara</s>; <s>Agnimukhi</s> (fire-faced), <s>Bhallātakī</s> (marking-nut) [are used] in all three genders.
(2.4.183) For <s>gardabhāṇḍa</s> (donkey-fruit): <s>Kandarāla</s>, <s>Kapītana</s>, <s>Supārśvaka</s> (pleasant-sided).
(2.4.184) <s>Plakṣa</s> also [refers to this]; <s>Tintiḍī</s>, <s>Ciñcā</s>, <s>Amlikā</s> [are synonyms for the tamarind]; then for <s>pītasāraka</s> (yellow-hearted wood):
(2.4.185) <s>Sarja</s>, <s>Kāsana</s>, <s>Bandhūkapuṣpa</s> (Bandhūka-flowered), <s>Priyaka</s>, <s>Jīvaka</s> [are synonyms].
(2.4.186) For <s>sāla</s> (sal tree): <s>Sarja</s>, <s>Kārśya</s>, <s>Aśvakarṇaka</s> (horse-eared); <s>Sasyasambara</s> [is another synonym].
(2.4.187) <s>Nadīsarja</s> (river-sarja), <s>Vīrataru</s> (hero-tree), <s>Indradru</s> (Indra's tree); <s>Kakubha</s>, <s>Arjuna</s> [are synonyms for the Arjuna tree].
(2.4.188) <s>Rājādana</s> (king's food), <s>Phalādhyakṣa</s> (superintendent of fruits) [are synonyms for this tree]; then for <s>kṣīrikā</s> (milky tree), the next two [verses apply]:
(2.4.189) <s>Iṅgudī</s>: <s>Tāpasataru</s> (ascetic's tree). For <s>bhūrja</s> (birch): <s>Carmi</s> (having bark) and <s>Mṛdutvac</s> (soft-barked).
(2.4.190) <s>Picchilā</s> (slimy), <s>Pūraṇī</s> (filling), <s>Mocā</s> (liberating), <s>Sthirāyuḥ</s> (long-lived); <s>Śālmali</s> (silk-cotton tree) [is used] in both [genders].
(2.4.191) <s>Picchā</s> refers to the gum of the <s>śālmalī</s>; <s>Rocana</s> (shining), <s>Kūṭaśālmali</s> (false silk-cotton) [are synonyms for a variety].
(2.4.192) <s>Cirabilvā</s>, <s>Naktamāla</s> (night-garland), <s>Karaja</s> [are synonyms] for <s>karañja</s> (Pongamia).
(2.4.193) <s>Prakīrya</s>, <s>Pūtikaraja</s> (foul-karaja), <s>Pūtika</s> (stinking), <s>Kalimāraka</s> (sin-destroyer) [are synonyms for a variety of karañja].
(2.4.194) [These are] varieties of <s>karañja</s>; <s>Ṣaḍgrantha</s> (six-knotted), <s>Markaṭī</s> (monkey-plant), <s>Aṅgāravallī</s> (ember-creeper) [are further synonyms].
(2.4.195) <s>Rohī</s>, <s>Rohitaka</s>, <s>Plīhaśatru</s> (enemy of spleen-disease), <s>Dāḍimapuṣpaka</s> (pomegranate-flowered) [are synonyms for the rohitaka tree].
(2.4.196) <s>Gāyatrī</s>, <s>Bālatanaya</s> (son of strength); <s>Khadira</s> (catechu): <s>Dantadhāvana</s> (tooth-cleanser).
(2.4.197) <s>Arimeda</s> [is a synonym] for the <s>viṭkhadira</s> (false catechu); <s>Kadara</s> [is a synonym] for the white <s>khadira</s>.
(2.4.198) <s>Somavalka</s> (soma-barked) also [is a synonym]; then <s>Vyāghrapuccha</s> (tiger-tail) and <s>Gandharvahastaka</s> (Gandharva's hand) [are synonyms for another plant].
(2.4.199) <s>Eraṇḍa</s> (castor): <s>Urubūka</s>, <s>Rucaka</s> (bright), <s>Citraka</s> (spotted) also [refer to] it.
(2.4.200) <s>Cañcu</s>, <s>Pañcāṅgula</s> (five-fingered), <s>Maṇḍa</s>, <s>Vardhamāna</s> (increasing), <s>Vyaḍambaka</s> [are also synonyms for castor].

children.text: (2.4.201) alpā śamī śamīraḥ syācchamī saktuphalā śivā
children.translated_text: (2.4.201) The small [variety] is <s>śamī</s>; <s>Śamīra</s> [refers to] the [large] <s>Śamī</s> (Prosopis): <s>Saktuphalā</s> (flour-fruited), <s>Śivā</s> (auspicious).
(2.4.202) <s>Piṇḍītaka</s>, <s>Marubaka</s>, <s>Śvasana</s> (breathing), <s>Karahāṭaka</s> [are synonyms for a type of basil].
(2.4.203) <s>Śalya</s> (thorn) also [is a synonym] for the <s>madana</s> (thorn-apple); <s>Śakrapādapa</s> (Indra's tree), <s>Pāribhadraka</s> [are synonyms for the coral tree].

children.text: (2.4.204) bhadradāru drukilimaṃ pītadāru ca dāru ca
children.translated_text: (2.4.204) <s>Bhadradāru</s> (auspicious wood), <s>Drukilima</s>, <s>Pītadāru</s> (yellow wood), and <s>Dāru</s> (wood),
(2.4.205) <s>Pūtikāṣṭha</s> (fragrant wood)—these seven are [synonyms] for <s>devadāru</s> (deodar cedar); then for [the next] two [verses]:
(2.4.206) <s>Pāṭali</s>: <s>Pāṭalā</s>, <s>Amoghā</s> (unfailing), <s>Kācasthālī</s>, <s>Phaleruhā</s> (fruit-growing).
(2.4.207) <s>Kṛṣṇavṛntā</s> (black-stemmed), <s>Kuberākṣī</s> (Kubera-eyed); <s>Śyāmā</s> (dark) is also called <s>Mahilāhvayā</s> (named after a woman).

children.text: (2.4.208) latā govandanī gundrā priyaṅguḥ phalinī phalī
children.translated_text: (2.4.208) <s>Latā</s> (creeper), <s>Govandanī</s>, <s>Gundrā</s>; <s>Priyaṅgu</s> (beauty-berry): <s>Phalinī</s> (fruit-bearing), <s>Phalī</s>.
(2.4.209) <s>Viṣvaksenā</s> (of Viṣvaksena), <s>Gandhaphalī</s> (fragrant-fruited), <s>Kārambhā</s>, <s>Priyaka</s>—she [is also called by these names].
(2.4.210) <s>Maṇḍūkaparṇa</s> (frog-leaved), <s>Patrorṇa</s> (leaf-wooled), <s>Naṭa</s>, <s>Kaṭvaṅga</s>, <s>Ṭuṇṭuka</s>,
(2.4.211) <s>Syonāka</s>, <s>Śukanāsa</s> (parrot-nosed), <s>Arkṣa</s>, <s>Dīrghavṛnta</s> (long-stalked), <s>Kuṭannaṭa</s> [are synonyms for the same tree].

children.text: (2.4.212) amṛtā ca vayaḥsthā ca triliṅgastu bibhītakaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.4.212) <s>Amṛtā</s> (immortal) and <s>Vayaḥsthā</s> (age-sustaining) [are synonyms]; <s>Bibhītaka</s> (beleric myrobalan) is [used] in all three genders.
(2.4.213) <s>Nākṣa</s>, <s>Tuṣa</s> (husk), <s>Karṣaphala</s> (ploughing-fruit), <s>Bhūtāvāsa</s> (abode of spirits), <s>Kalidruma</s> (tree of strife) [are synonyms for bibhītaka].
(2.4.214) <s>Abhayā</s> (fearless), <s>Avyathā</s> (painless), <s>Pathyā</s> (wholesome), <s>Kāyasthā</s> (body-dweller), <s>Pūtanā</s>, <s>Amṛtā</s> (immortal),
(2.4.215) <s>Karītakī</s>, <s>Haimavatī</s> (from the Himalayas), <s>Cetakī</s>, <s>Śreyasī</s> (auspicious), <s>Śivā</s> (beneficent) [are synonyms for <s>harītakī</s>, the chebulic myrobalan].
(2.4.216) <s>Pītadru</s> (yellow tree), <s>Sarala</s> (pine), <s>Pūtikāṣṭha</s> (fragrant wood) also [are synonyms]; then <s>Drumotpala</s> (tree-lotus),
(2.4.217) <s>Karṇikāra</s>, <s>Parivyādha</s> [are synonyms for the same tree]. <s>Lakuca</s>, <s>Likuca</s>, <s>Ḍahu</s>,
(2.4.218) <s>Panasa</s> (jackfruit), <s>Kaṇṭakiphala</s> (thorny-fruited) [are synonyms]. <s>Nicula</s>, <s>Hijjala</s>, <s>Ambuja</s> (water-born) [are synonyms for the water-palm].
(2.4.219) <s>Kākodumbarikā</s> (crow-fig), <s>Phalgu</s>; <s>Malayū</s>, <s>Jaghanephalā</s> (hip-fruited) [are synonyms for a fig variety].
(2.4.220) <s>Ariṣṭa</s> (soapnut): <s>Sarvatobhadra</s> (auspicious on all sides), <s>Hiṅgu</s>, <s>Niryāsa</s> (resin), <s>Mālaka</s>,
(2.4.221) <s>Picumanda</s> also [are synonyms] for the <s>nimba</s> (neem tree); then <s>Picchilā</s> (slimy) [refers to] <s>aguru</s> (eaglewood), <s>Śiṃśapā</s> (dalbergia),
(2.4.222) <s>Kapilā</s> (tawny), <s>Bhasmagarbhā</s> (ash-womb)—she [is śiṃśapā]. <s>Śirīṣa</s> (silk tree): <s>Kapītana</s>,
(2.4.223) <s>Bhaṇḍila</s> also [is a synonym]; then <s>Cāmpeya</s>, <s>Campaka</s>, <s>Hemapuṣpaka</s> (golden-flowered) [are synonyms for the champaka tree].
(2.4.224) The bud of this [campaka] is <s>Gandhaphalī</s> (fragrant-fruited); then for the <s>kesara</s> (filament) [tree]:
(2.4.225) <s>Bakula</s>, <s>Vañjula</s>; for the <s>aśoka</s> tree: <s>Karaka</s> and <s>Dāḍima</s> (pomegranate) are equal [synonyms].
(2.4.226) <s>Cāmpeya</s>, <s>Kesara</s>, <s>Nāgakesara</s> (serpent-stamen), <s>Kāñcanāhvaya</s> (called golden) [are synonyms for Mesua ferrea].
(2.4.227) <s>Jayā</s> (victorious), <s>Jayantī</s>, <s>Tarkārī</s>, <s>Nādeyī</s> (riverine), <s>Vaijayantikā</s> (triumphant) [are synonyms].
(2.4.228) <s>Śrīparṇa</s> (glorious-leaved): <s>Agnimantha</s> (fire-churner) [is a synonym]; <s>Kaṇikā</s>, <s>Gaṇikārikā</s> [are also synonyms].
(2.4.229) <s>Jaya</s> (victorious); then <s>Kuṭaja</s>: <s>Śakra</s> (Indra's), <s>Vatsaka</s>, <s>Girimallikā</s> (mountain jasmine).
(2.4.230) The fruit of this very [kuṭaja] is [called] <s>Kaliṅga</s>, <s>Indrayava</s> (Indra's barley), <s>Bhadrayava</s> (auspicious barley).
(2.4.231) <s>Kṛṣṇapāka</s> (black-ripening), <s>Phalāvigna</s>, <s>Suṣeṇa</s> [are synonyms] for <s>karamardaka</s> (Christ's thorn).
(2.4.232) <s>Kālaskandha</s> (dark-trunked): <s>Tamāla</s> (bay leaf tree), <s>Tāpiccha</s> also. Then for <s>sinduka</s>:
(2.4.233) <s>Sinduvāra</s> and <s>Indrasurasa</s> (Indra's basil) [are synonyms]; also <s>Nirguṇḍī</s> and <s>Indrāṇikā</s>.

children.text: (2.4.234) veṇī garā garī devatāḍo jīmūta ityapi
children.translated_text: (2.4.234) <s>Veṇī</s> (braided), <s>Garā</s>, <s>Garī</s>, <s>Devatāḍa</s> (god-striking), <s>Jīmūta</s> (cloud) also [are synonyms for the same].

children.text: (2.4.235) śrīhastinī tu bhūruṇḍī tṛṇaśūnyaṃ tu mallikā
children.translated_text: (2.4.235) <s>Śrīhastinī</s> (auspicious elephant-plant): <s>Bhūruṇḍī</s>; <s>Tṛṇaśūnya</s> (grass-devoid) refers to <s>mallikā</s> (jasmine),
(2.4.236) <s>Bhūpadī</s> (earth-footed), <s>Śītabhīru</s> (cold-fearing) also [are synonyms for jasmine]; that same [jasmine], when wild, is <s>Āsphoṭā</s>.

children.text: (2.4.237) śephālikā tu suvahā nirguṇḍī nīlikā ca sā
children.translated_text: (2.4.237) <s>Śephālikā</s>: <s>Suvahā</s> (easy to carry), <s>Nirguṇḍī</s>, <s>Nīlikā</s> (bluish) also [refer to] her.
(2.4.238) The white variety is <s>Śvetasurasā</s> (white basil), <s>Bhūtaveśī</s>; then <s>Māgadhī</s> (from Magadha),
(2.4.239) <s>Gaṇikā</s> (courtesan), <s>Yūthikā</s> (cluster-jasmine), <s>Ambaṣṭhā</s>; the yellow [variety] is <s>Hemapuṣpikā</s> (golden-flowered).
(2.4.240) <s>Atimukta</s> (fully liberated): <s>Puṇḍraka</s> [is a synonym]; <s>Vāsantī</s> (vernal), <s>Mādhavī</s> (of spring) are [synonyms for] a creeper.
(2.4.241) <s>Sumanā</s> (fragrant), <s>Mālatī</s>, <s>Jāti</s> (jasmine), <s>Saptalā</s>, <s>Navamālikā</s> (new-garland) [are synonyms].
(2.4.242) The intermediate [variety] is <s>kunda</s> (jasmine); <s>Raktaka</s> (red): <s>Bandhūka</s>, <s>Bandhujīvaka</s> (kinsman-life).
(2.4.243) <s>Sahā</s> (enduring), <s>Kumārī</s> (maiden), <s>Taraṇi</s> (crossing); <s>Amlāna</s> (unfading) is <s>Mahāsahā</s> (greatly enduring).
(2.4.244) Among these, the red one is <s>Kurabaka</s>; among those, the yellow one is <s>Kurakaṇṭaka</s> (thorn of Kura).

children.text: (2.4.245) nīlī jhiṇṭī dvayorbāṇā dāsī cārtagalaśca sā
children.translated_text: (2.4.245) <s>Nīlī</s> (indigo), <s>Jhiṇṭī</s> [are synonyms] for both; <s>Bāṇā</s> (arrow), <s>Dāsī</s> (servant), and <s>Ārtagala</s> [refer to] her.
(2.4.246) <s>Saireyaka</s>: <s>Jhiṇṭī</s> [is a synonym]; when it is red, <s>Kurabaka</s> [is the name].
(2.4.247) The yellow <s>Kuraṇṭaka</s> [is called] <s>Jhiṇṭī</s>; when [it is used] for both, <s>Sahacarī</s> [applies].
(2.4.248) <s>Oṇḍrapuṣpa</s> (Oṇḍra-flower), <s>Japāpuṣpa</s> (hibiscus flower), <s>Vajrapuṣpa</s> (diamond-flower) [refer to] sesame flower.
(2.4.249) <s>Pratihāsa</s> (counter-laughter), <s>Śataprāsa</s> (hundred-speared), <s>Caṇḍāta</s>, <s>Hayamāraka</s> (horse-killer) [are synonyms for the oleander].
(2.4.250) For <s>karavīra</s> (oleander); for <s>karīra</s> (caper): <s>Krakara</s> and <s>Granthilā</s> (knotty) are both [synonyms].
(2.4.251) <s>Unmatta</s> (maddening), <s>Kitava</s> (gambler), <s>Dhūrta</s> (cunning), <s>Dhattūra</s> (thorn-apple), <s>Kanakāhvaya</s> (called golden) [are synonyms for Datura].
(2.4.252) <s>Mātula</s> (maternal uncle), <s>Madana</s> (intoxicating) also [are synonyms]; its fruit is <s>Mātulaputraka</s> (uncle's son).
(2.4.253) <s>Phalapūra</s> (fruit-filling), <s>Bījapūra</s> (seed-filling), <s>Rucaka</s> (pleasing) [are synonyms] for <s>mātuluṅga</s> (citron).
(2.4.254) <s>Samīraṇa</s> (wind), <s>Marubaka</s>, <s>Prasthapuṣpa</s> (plateau-flower), <s>Phaṇijjaka</s> (hooded) [are synonyms for marjoram].
(2.4.255) <s>Jambīra</s> also [is a synonym]; then for <s>parṇāsa</s>: <s>Kaṭhiñjara</s> and <s>Kuṭheraka</s> [are synonyms].
(2.4.256) The white [variety] is <s>Arjaka</s>; here <s>Pāṭhī</s> [refers to] <s>Citraka</s> (Plumbago): <s>Vahnisaṃjñaka</s> (called fire).
(2.4.257) <s>Arkāhva</s> (called Arka), <s>Vasuka</s>, <s>Āsphoṭa</s>, <s>Gaṇarūpa</s> (troop-formed), <s>Vikīraṇa</s> (scattering) [are synonyms for the sun-plant].
(2.4.258) <s>Mandāra</s> also, <s>Arkaparṇa</s> (Arka-leaved); the white variety is <s>Alarka</s> and <s>Pratāpasa</s> (radiant).
(2.4.259) <s>Śivamallī</s>, <s>Pāśupata</s> (of Śiva), <s>Ekāṣṭhīla</s> (single-stoned), <s>Buka</s>, <s>Vasu</s> (wealth) [are synonyms for a type of plant].
(2.4.260) <s>Vandā</s> (parasite), <s>Vṛkṣādanī</s> (tree-eater), <s>Vṛkṣaruhā</s> (tree-grower), <s>Jīvantikā</s> (life-sustaining) also [are synonyms for a parasitic plant].
(2.4.261) <s>Vatsādanī</s> (calf-eater), <s>Chinnaruhā</s> (growing when cut), <s>Guḍūcī</s> (Tinospora), <s>Tantrikā</s> (stringy), <s>Amṛtā</s> (immortal).
(2.4.262) <s>Jīvantikā</s> (life-sustaining), <s>Somavallī</s> (Soma-creeper), <s>Viśalyā</s> (thorn-removing), <s>Madhuparṇī</s> (honey-leaved) also [are synonyms].

children.text: (2.4.263) mūrvā devī madhurasā moraṭā tejanī sravā
children.translated_text: (2.4.263) <s>Mūrvā</s>: <s>Devī</s> (divine), <s>Madhurasā</s> (sweet-juiced), <s>Moraṭā</s>, <s>Tejanī</s> (radiant), <s>Sravā</s> (flowing).
(2.4.264) <s>Madhūlikā</s> (honey-like), <s>Madhuśreṇī</s> (honey-row), <s>Gokarṇī</s> (cow-eared), <s>Pīluparṇī</s> (Pīlu-leaved) also [are synonyms for mūrvā].
(2.4.265) <s>Pāṭā</s>: <s>Ambaṣṭā</s>, <s>Viddhakarnṇī</s> (pierced-eared), <s>Sthāpanī</s> (stabilizing), <s>Śreyasī</s> (beneficial), <s>Rasā</s> (juicy).
(2.4.266) <s>Ekāṣṭīlā</s> (single-stoned), <s>Pāpacelī</s> (sin-removing), <s>Prācīnā</s> (eastern), <s>Vanatiktikā</s> (forest-bitter) [are also synonyms for pāṭā].
(2.4.267) <s>Kaṭu</s> (pungent), <s>Kaṭambharā</s>; <s>Śoka</s>-<s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Kaṭurohiṇī</s> (pungent Rohiṇī) [are synonyms for the same plant].
(2.4.268) <s>Matsyapittā</s> (fish-bile), <s>Kṛṣṇabhedī</s> (dark-piercing), <s>Cakrāṅgī</s> (wheel-bodied), <s>Śakulādanī</s> (fish-eating) [are also synonyms].
(2.4.269) <s>Ātmaguptā</s> (self-concealed), <s>Jahā</s>, <s>Vyaṇḍā</s>, <s>Kaṇḍūrā</s> (itchy), <s>Prāvṛṣāyaṇī</s> (rainy-season plant),
(2.4.270) <s>Ṛṣyaproktā</s> (spoken of by sages), <s>Śūkaśimbi</s> (bristle-pod), <s>Kapikacchu</s> (monkey-scratch), <s>Markaṭī</s> (monkey-plant) [are synonyms for velvet bean].
(2.4.271) <s>Citropacitrā</s> (variegated), <s>Nyagrodhī</s> (downward-growing), <s>Dravantī</s> (flowing), <s>Śambarī</s>, <s>Vṛśā</s> (strong) [are synonyms].
(2.4.272) <s>Pratyakśreṇī</s> (facing-row), <s>Sutaśreṇī</s> (son-row), <s>Raṇḍā</s> (widow), <s>Mūṣikaparṇī</s> (mouse-leaved) also [are synonyms for the same plant].
(2.4.273) <s>Apāmārga</s> (chaff-flower): <s>Śaikharika</s>, <s>Dhāmārgava</s>, <s>Mayūraka</s> (peacock-like),
(2.4.274) <s>Pratyakparṇī</s> (forward-leaved), <s>Keśaparṇī</s> (hair-leaved), <s>Kiṇihī</s>, <s>Kharamañjarī</s> (rough-clustered) [are also synonyms for apāmārga].
(2.4.275) <s>Hañjikā</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> (of Brahmins), <s>Padmā</s> (lotus-like), <s>Bhargī</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇayaṣṭikā</s> (Brahmin's staff) [are synonyms].
(2.4.276) <s>Aṅgāravallī</s> (ember-creeper), <s>Bāleya</s>, <s>Śāka</s> (vegetable), <s>Barbara</s>, <s>Vardhaka</s> (increasing) [are synonyms].
(2.4.277) <s>Mañjiṣṭhā</s> (madder): <s>Vikasā</s> (expanding), <s>Jiṅgī</s>, <s>Samaṅgā</s>, <s>Kālameṣikā</s> (dark-ram plant).
(2.4.278) <s>Maṇḍūkaparṇī</s> (frog-leaved): <s>Maṇḍīrī</s>, <s>Bhaṇḍī</s>, <s>Yojanavallī</s> (league-creeper) also [are synonyms].
(2.4.279) <s>Yāsa</s>, <s>Yavāsa</s>, <s>Duḥsparśa</s> (hard to touch), <s>Dhanvayāsa</s> (desert yāsa), <s>Kunāśaka</s> [are synonyms for a thorny plant].
(2.4.280) <s>Rodanī</s> (weeping), <s>Kacchurā</s>, <s>Anantā</s> (endless), <s>Samudrāntā</s> (ocean-ending), <s>Durālabhā</s> (hard to obtain) [are synonyms].
(2.4.281) <s>Pṛśniparṇī</s> (spotted-leaved), <s>Pṛthakparṇī</s> (separate-leaved), <s>Citraparṇī</s> (variegated-leaved), <s>Aṅghrivallikā</s> (foot-creeper) [are synonyms].
(2.4.282) <s>Kroṣṭuvinnā</s> (jackal's excrement), <s>Siṃhapucchī</s> (lion's tail), <s>Kalaśī</s> (pot-shaped), <s>Dhāvanī</s> (washing), <s>Guhā</s> (cave) [are also synonyms].
(2.4.283) <s>Nidigdhikā</s> (scorching), <s>Spṛśī</s> (touching), <s>Vyāghrī</s> (tigress), <s>Bṛhatī</s> (great), <s>Kaṇṭakārikā</s> (thorny) [are synonyms for the thorny nightshade].
(2.4.284) <s>Pracodanī</s> (impelling), <s>Kulī</s>, <s>Kṣudrā</s> (small), <s>Duḥsparśā</s> (hard to touch), <s>Rāṣṭrikā</s> also [are synonyms for a small variety].
(2.4.285) <s>Nīlī</s> (indigo): <s>Kālā</s> (dark), <s>Klītakikā</s>, <s>Grāmīṇā</s> (rural), <s>Madhuparṇikā</s> (honey-leaved).

children.text: (2.4.286) rañjanī śrīphalī tutthā droṇī dolā ca nīlinī
children.translated_text: (2.4.286) <s>Rañjanī</s> (dyeing), <s>Śrīphalī</s> (auspicious-fruited), <s>Tutthā</s>, <s>Droṇī</s> (trough), <s>Dolā</s> (swinging), <s>Nīlinī</s> (bluish) [are also synonyms for indigo].
(2.4.287) <s>Avalguja</s>: <s>Somarājī</s> (Soma's queen), <s>Suvalli</s> (good creeper), <s>Somavallikā</s> (Soma's creeper).
(2.4.288) <s>Kālameṣī</s> (dark-ram), <s>Kṛṣṇaphalī</s> (black-fruited), <s>Bākucī</s>, <s>Pūtiphalī</s> (stinking-fruited) also [are synonyms for avalguja].

children.text: (2.4.292) cavyaṃ tu cavikā kākaciñcīguñje tu kṛṣṇalā
(2.4.296) śṛngī mahauṣadhaṃ cātha kṣīrāvī dugdhikā same
(2.4.307) miśreyāpyatha sīhuṇḍo vajraḥ snukstrī snuhī guḍā
(2.4.311) mṛdvīkā gostanī drākṣā svādvī madhuraseti ca
(2.4.316) vidārī kṣīraśuklekṣugandhā kroṣṭī tu yā sitā
(2.4.326) nakuleṣṭā bhujaṃgākṣī chatrākī suvahā ca sā
(2.4.329) bhāradvājī tu sā vanyā śṛṅgī tu ṛṣabho vṛśaḥ
(2.4.342) śaileyaṃ tālaparṇī tu daityā gandhakuṭī murā
(2.4.343) gandhinī gajabhakṣyā tu suvahā surabhī rasā
(2.4.362) marunmālā tu piśunā spṛkkā devī latā laghuḥ
(2.4.371) juṅgo bramhī tu matsyākṣī vayaḥsthā somavallarī
(2.4.376) elāparṇī tu suvahā rāsnā yuktarasā ca sā
(2.4.401) avākpuṣpī kāravī ca saraṇā tu prasāriṇī
(2.4.422) ikṣugandhā poṭagalaḥ puṃsi bhūmni tu balvajāḥ
(2.4.428) astrī kuśaṃ kutho darbhaḥ pavitramatha kattṛṇam 980
(2.4.434) ghoṇṭā tu pūgaḥ kramuko guvākaḥ khapuro 'sya tu
(2.4.436) kharjūraḥ ketakī tālī kharjurī ca tṛṇadrumāḥ iti vanauṣadhivargaḥ
(2.4.437) siṃho mṛgendraḥ pañcāsyo haryakṣaḥ kesarī hariḥ
(2.4.441) varāhaḥ sūkaro ghṛṣṭiḥ kolaḥ potrī kiriḥ kiṭiḥ
children.translated_text: (2.4.441) <s>Varāha</s>, <s>sūkara</s>, <s>ghṛṣṭi</s>, <s>kola</s>, <s>potrī</s>, <s>kiri</s>, and <s>kiṭi</s> [are synonyms for a boar].

children.text: (2.4.442) daṃṣṭrī ghoṇī stabdharomā kroḍo bhūdāra ityapi
children.translated_text: (2.4.442) <s>Daṃṣṭrī</s>, <s>ghoṇī</s>, <s>stabdharomā</s>, <s>kroḍa</s>, and <s>bhūdāra</s> are also [synonyms for a boar].
(2.4.443) <s>Kapi</s>, <s>plavaṅga</s>, <s>plavaga</s>, <s>śākhāmṛga</s>, and <s>valīmukha</s>,

children.text: (2.4.444) markaṭo vānaraḥ kīśo vanaukā atha bhalluke
children.translated_text: (2.4.444) <s>markaṭa</s>, <s>vānara</s>, <s>kīśa</s>, and <s>vanauka</s> [are synonyms for a monkey]. Now, for a bear:
(2.4.445) <s>ṛkṣa</s>, <s>acchabhalla</s>, and <s>bhallūka</s> [are synonyms for a bear]. For a rhinoceros: <s>khaḍga</s> and <s>khaḍgin</s>.
(2.4.446) <s>Lulāya</s> [is a synonym for a rhinoceros]. <s>Mahiṣa</s> (buffalo), <s>vāha</s>, <s>dviṣat</s>, <s>kāsara</s>, and <s>sairibha</s> [are synonyms for a buffalo].
(2.4.447) In the feminine, <s>śivā</s>. <s>Bhūrimāya</s>, <s>gomāyu</s>, <s>mṛgadhūrtaka</s>,
(2.4.448) <s>śṛgāla</s>, <s>vañcaka</s>, <s>kroṣṭu</s>, <s>pheru</s>, <s>pherava</s>, and <s>jambuka</s> [are synonyms for a jackal].
(2.4.449) <s>Otur</s>, <s>biḍāla</s>, <s>mārjāra</s>, <s>vṛṣadaṃśaka</s>, and <s>ākhubhuk</s> [are synonyms for a cat].
(2.4.450) The three — <s>gaudhera</s>, <s>gaudhāra</s>, and <s>godheya</s> — [are synonyms for] the offspring of a monitor lizard (<s>godhikā</s>).
(2.4.451) <s>Śvāvit</s> and <s>śalya</s> [are synonyms for a porcupine]; for its quill: <s>śalalī</s>, <s>śalala</s>, and <s>śala</s>.
(2.4.452) <s>Vātapramīr</s> and <s>vātamṛga</s> [are synonyms for an antelope]. <s>Koka</s> is a wolf. <s>Tīhāmṛga</s> and <s>vṛka</s> [are also synonyms for a wolf].
(2.4.453) For a deer: <s>kuraṅga</s>, <s>vātāyu</s>, <s>hariṇa</s>, and <s>ajinayoni</s> [are synonyms].
(2.4.454) <s>Aiṇeya</s> is the hide of a female deer (<s>eṇī</s>); <s>aiṇa</s> is used for both [genders] in all three [grammatical genders].
(2.4.455) <s>Kadalī</s>, <s>kandalī</s>, <s>cīna</s>, <s>camūru</s>, and <s>priyaka</s>,
(2.4.456) and <s>samūru</s> — these are [types of] deer [called] <s>hariṇa</s>; they are sources of deer-skin (<s>ajinayoni</s>).
(2.4.457) <s>Kṛṣṇasāra</s>, <s>ruru</s>, <s>nyaṅku</s>, <s>raṅku</s>, <s>śambara</s>, and <s>rauhiṣa</s>,
(2.4.458) <s>gokarṇa</s>, <s>pṛṣata</s>, <s>aiṇa</s>, <s>ṛśya</s>, <s>rohita</s>, and <s>camara</s> are [types of] deer.

children.text: (2.4.459) gandharvaḥ śarabho rāmaḥ sṛmaro gavayaḥ śaśaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.4.459) <s>Gandharva</s>, <s>śarabha</s>, <s>rāma</s>, <s>sṛmara</s>, <s>gavaya</s>, and <s>śaśa</s> (hare).
(2.4.460) These and others, beginning with the lord of beasts (<s>mṛgendra</s>) and beginning with cattle (<s>go</s>), are the species of animals (<s>paśujāti</s>).

children.text: (2.4.461) adhogantā tu khanako vṛkaḥ pundhvaja unduraḥ
children.translated_text: (2.4.461) One that goes underground is a burrower (<s>khanaka</s>). <s>Vṛka</s> and <s>pundhvaja</s> [are synonyms for] a rat (<s>undura</s>).
(2.4.462) <s>Unduru</s>, <s>mūṣaka</s>, and also <s>ākhu</s> [are synonyms for a rat]. <s>Girikā</s> is a young mouse (<s>bālamūṣikā</s>).
(2.4.463) <s>Cucundarī</s> and <s>gandhamūṣī</s> [are synonyms for a musk-rat]; <s>dīrghadehī</s> is a [long-bodied] mouse (<s>mūṣikā</s>).
(2.4.464) <s>Saraṭa</s> and <s>kṛkalāsa</s> [are synonyms for a chameleon]. <s>Musalī</s> is a house-lizard (<s>gṛhagodhikā</s>).
(2.4.465) <s>Lūtā</s> (feminine) [means a spider]; <s>tantuvāya</s>, <s>ūrṇanābha</s>, and <s>markaṭaka</s> are synonyms.
(2.4.466) <s>Nīlaṅgu</s> is a worm (<s>kṛmi</s>). <s>Karṇajalaukā</s> and <s>śatapadī</s> are both [synonyms for a centipede].
(2.4.467) <s>Vṛścika</s> (scorpion) and <s>śūkakīṭa</s> are synonyms. <s>Ali</s> and <s>druṇa</s> are also [synonyms] for a scorpion.
(2.4.468) <s>Pārāvata</s>, <s>kalarava</s>, and <s>kapota</s> [are synonyms for a pigeon]. Now, <s>śaśādana</s> (hawk):
(2.4.469) <s>Patrī</s> and <s>śyena</s> [are synonyms for a hawk]. <s>Ulūka</s> (owl) has synonyms <s>vāyasārāti</s> and <s>pecaka</s>.
(2.4.470) <s>Divāndha</s> (day-blind), <s>kauśika</s>, <s>ghūka</s>, <s>divābhīta</s> (afraid of day), and <s>niśāṭana</s> (night-wanderer) [are synonyms for an owl].
(2.4.471) <s>Vyāghrāṭa</s> is a synonym for <s>bharadvāja</s> (skylark). <s>Khañjarīṭa</s> is a synonym for <s>khañjana</s> (wagtail).
(2.4.472) <s>Lohapṛṣṭha</s> (iron-backed) is a synonym for <s>kaṅka</s> (heron). Now, <s>cāṣa</s> and <s>kikīdivi</s> [are synonyms for the blue jay],
(2.4.473) <s>kaliṅga</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, and <s>dhūmyāṭa</s> [are also synonyms]. Now, <s>śatapatraka</s> (woodpecker),
(2.4.474) <s>dārvāghāṭa</s> [is its synonym]. Now, <s>sāraṅga</s>, <s>stokaka</s>, and <s>cātaka</s> are synonyms [for the rain-bird].
(2.4.475) <s>Kṛkavāku</s>, <s>tāmracūḍa</s> (copper-crested), <s>kukkuṭa</s>, and <s>caraṇāyudha</s> (spur-footed) [are synonyms for a cock].

children.text: (2.4.476) caṭakaḥ kalaviṅkaḥ syāttasya strī caṭakā tayoḥ
children.translated_text: (2.4.476) <s>Caṭaka</s> and <s>kalaviṅka</s> [are synonyms for a sparrow]. Its feminine form is <s>caṭakā</s>. Of the pair:
(2.4.477) when the male is meant, it is <s>cāṭakaira</s>; when the female is meant, it is just <s>caṭakā</s>.
(2.4.478) <s>Karkareṭu</s> and <s>kareṭu</s> are synonyms. <s>Kṛkaṇa</s> and <s>krakara</s> are synonyms [for a type of partridge].
(2.4.479) <s>Vanapriya</s> (forest-lover), <s>parabhṛta</s> (reared by another), <s>kokila</s>, and <s>pika</s> are also [synonyms for a cuckoo].
(2.4.480) For a crow: <s>karaṭa</s>, <s>ariṣṭa</s>, <s>balipuṣṭa</s> (fed by offerings), and <s>sakṛtpraja</s> (having one brood),
(2.4.481) <s>dhvāṅkṣa</s>, <s>ātmaghoṣa</s> (self-sounding), <s>parabhṛt</s>, <s>balibhuj</s> (offering-eater), and <s>vāyasa</s> are also [synonyms for a crow].

children.text: (2.4.482) sa eva ca cirañjīvī caikadṛṣṭiśca maukuliḥ
children.translated_text: (2.4.482) And he is also [called] <s>cirañjīvī</s> (long-lived) and <s>ekadṛṣṭi</s> (one-eyed), and <s>maukuli</s>.
(2.4.483) <s>Droṇakāka</s> is the same as <s>kākola</s>. <s>Dātyūha</s> and <s>kālakaṇṭhaka</s> (dark-throated) [are synonyms for the gallinule].
(2.4.484) <s>Ātāpicilla</s> [is a type of bird]. <s>Dākṣāyya</s> and <s>gṛdhra</s> [are synonyms for a vulture]. <s>Kīra</s> and <s>śuka</s> are synonyms [for a parrot].
(2.4.485) <s>Kruṅkrauñca</s> [is a synonym for a heron]. Now, <s>baka</s> and <s>kahva</s> [are synonyms for a crane]. <s>Puṣkarāhva</s> is a synonym for <s>sārasa</s> (crane).
(2.4.486) <s>Koka</s>, <s>cakra</s>, and <s>cakravāka</s> (ruddy goose), also called <s>rathāṅgāhvaya</s> (wheel-named).
(2.4.487) <s>Kādamba</s> and <s>kalahaṃsa</s> [are synonyms for a goose]. <s>Utkrośa</s> and <s>kurara</s> are synonyms [for an osprey].
(2.4.488) <s>Haṃsas</s> (swans) have white wings (<s>śvetagarut</s>), circular markings (<s>cakrāṅga</s>), and dwell on [Lake] <s>Mānasa</s>.
(2.4.489) <s>Rājahaṃsas</s> (royal swans) are those that are white with red beaks and feet.
(2.4.490) Those with dull-colored [beaks and feet] and jasmine-white [bodies] are <s>mallikākṣa</s>; <s>dhārtarāṣṭras</s> are those [white] with non-white [markings].
(2.4.491) <s>Śarāri</s>, <s>rāṭi</s>, and <s>rāḍi</s> [are synonyms]; <s>balākā</s> and <s>bisakaṇṭhikā</s> [are synonyms for a female crane].
(2.4.492) The female of a swan (<s>haṃsa</s>) is <s>varaṭā</s>; that of a crane (<s>sārasa</s>) is <s>lakṣmaṇā</s>.
(2.4.493) <s>Jatukā</s> and <s>jinapatrā</s> are synonyms. <s>Paroṣṇī</s> and <s>tailapāyikā</s> [are synonyms for a bat].
(2.4.494) <s>Varvaṇā</s> is a fly (<s>makṣikā</s>). <s>Nīlā</s> [is a blue fly]. <s>Saraghā</s> is a honey-bee (<s>madhumakṣikā</s>).
(2.4.495) <s>Pataṅgikā</s> and <s>puttikā</s> [are synonyms for a white ant]. <s>Daṃśa</s> is a horse-fly (<s>vanamakṣikā</s>).
(2.4.496) <s>Daṃśī</s> is a small species of the same. <s>Gandholī</s> and <s>varaṭā</s> [apply to] both.

children.text: (2.4.497) bhṛṅgārī jhīrukā cīrī jhillikā ca samā imāḥ
children.translated_text: (2.4.497) <s>Bhṛṅgārī</s>, <s>jhīrukā</s>, <s>cīrī</s>, and <s>jhillikā</s> are synonyms [for a cricket].
(2.4.498) <s>Pataṅga</s> and <s>śalabha</s> are synonyms [for a moth/grasshopper]. <s>Khadhyota</s> and <s>jyotiriṅgaṇa</s> [are synonyms for a firefly].
(2.4.499) <s>Madhuvrata</s>, <s>madhukara</s>, <s>madhuliṭ</s>, and <s>madhupa</s>,
(2.4.500) <s>dvirepha</s>, <s>puṣpaliḍ</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, <s>ṣaṭpada</s>, and <s>bhramarālaya</s> [are synonyms for a bee].
(2.4.501) <s>Mayūra</s>, <s>barhiṇa</s>, <s>barhī</s>, <s>nīlakaṇṭha</s> (blue-necked), and <s>bhujaṃgabhuk</s> (snake-eater),
(2.4.502) <s>śikhāvala</s>, <s>śikhī</s>, <s>kekī</s>, and <s>meghanādānulāsī</s> (one who dances at the sound of clouds) [are synonyms for a peacock].
(2.4.503) <s>Kekā</s> is the cry of a peacock. <s>Candraka</s> and <s>mecaka</s> are synonyms [for the eye-spots on a peacock's tail].

children.text: (2.4.504) śikhā cūḍā śikhaṇḍas tu picchabarhe napuṃsake
children.translated_text: (2.4.504) <s>Śikhā</s> and <s>cūḍā</s> [mean the crest]. <s>Śikhaṇḍa</s> [means the tail-fan]; <s>piccha</s> and <s>barha</s> are neuter [synonyms for a peacock feather].
(2.4.505) For a bird: <s>vihaṅga</s>, <s>vihaga</s>, <s>vihaṅgama</s>, and <s>vihāyasa</s>,
(2.4.506) <s>śakunti</s>, <s>pakṣin</s>, <s>śakuni</s>, <s>śakunta</s>, <s>śakuna</s>, and <s>dvija</s> (twice-born),
(2.4.507) <s>patatri</s>, <s>patri</s>, <s>pataga</s>, <s>patat</s>, <s>patraratha</s>, and <s>aṇḍaja</s> (egg-born),
(2.4.508) <s>nagauka</s>, <s>vāji</s>, <s>vikira</s>, <s>viviṣkira</s>, and <s>patatraya</s>,
(2.4.509) <s>nīḍodbhava</s> (nest-born), <s>garutmat</s>, <s>pitsant</s>, and <s>nabhasaṃgama</s> (sky-traveller) [are all synonyms for a bird].

children.text: (2.4.510) teṣāṃ viśeṣā hārīto madguḥ kāraṇḍavaḥ plavaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.4.510) Their specific varieties are: <s>hārīta</s>, <s>madgu</s> (cormorant), <s>kāraṇḍava</s> (a type of duck), <s>plava</s>,
(2.4.511) <s>tittiri</s> (partridge), <s>kukkubha</s>, <s>lāva</s> (quail), <s>jīvañjīva</s>, and <s>koraka</s>,
(2.4.512) <s>koyaṣṭika</s>, <s>ṭiṭṭibhaka</s> (lapwing), <s>vartaka</s>, <s>vartikā</s>, and others.
(2.4.513) <s>Garut</s>, <s>pakṣa</s>, and <s>chada</s> [mean a wing]. <s>Patra</s> and <s>patatra</s> [mean a feather]; <s>tanūruha</s> [means body-hair/plumage].
(2.4.514) <s>Pakṣati</s> (feminine) [means the wing-joint]. <s>Pakṣamūla</s> [means the base of the wing]. <s>Cañcu</s> and <s>stroṭi</s> are both feminine [meaning beak].
(2.4.515) <s>Praḍīna</s> (flying forth), <s>uḍḍīna</s> (flying up), and <s>saṃḍīna</s> (flying together) — these are the actions of bird-flight.
(2.4.516) <s>Peśī</s> and <s>kośa</s> [mean an egg-shell]. When without these two, it is <s>aṇḍa</s> (egg). <s>Kulāya</s> and <s>nīḍa</s> (nest) are not feminine.

children.text: (2.4.517) potaḥ pāko 'rbhako ḍimbhaḥ pṛthukaḥ śāvakaḥ śiśuḥ
children.translated_text: (2.4.517) <s>Pota</s>, <s>pāka</s>, <s>arbhaka</s>, <s>ḍimbha</s>, <s>pṛthuka</s>, <s>śāvaka</s>, and <s>śiśu</s> [are synonyms for a young one/chick].

children.text: (2.4.518) strīpuṃsau mithunaṃ dvandvaṃ yugmaṃ tu yugulaṃ yugam
children.translated_text: (2.4.518) A male and female [together form] <s>mithuna</s> (pair) and <s>dvandva</s> (couple). <s>Yugma</s>, <s>yugula</s>, and <s>yuga</s> [also mean a pair].
(2.4.519) For a group: <s>nivaha</s>, <s>vyūha</s>, <s>sandoha</s>, <s>visara</s>, and <s>vraja</s>,
(2.4.520) <s>stoma</s>, <s>ogha</s>, <s>nikara</s>, <s>trāta</s>, <s>vāra</s>, <s>saṃghāta</s>, and <s>saṃcaya</s>,
(2.4.521) <s>samudāya</s>, <s>samudaya</s>, <s>samavāya</s>, and <s>gaṇa</s> [are all synonyms for a group/collection].
(2.4.522) In the feminine: <s>saṃhati</s>. <s>Vṛnda</s>, <s>nikuramba</s>, and <s>kadambaka</s> [are synonyms for a cluster].
(2.4.523) Varieties of groups: <s>varga</s> is [a group] of equals; <s>saṃgha</s> and <s>sārtha</s> are of living beings.
(2.4.524) <s>Kula</s> is [a group] of the same species. <s>Yūtha</s> is [a herd] of animals, [used in] masculine and neuter.
(2.4.525) <s>Samāja</s> is of animals; of others it is <s>samāja</s>. Now, of those sharing the same characteristics:
(2.4.526) it is <s>nikāya</s>. <s>Puñja</s> and <s>rāśi</s> [mean a heap]; <s>utkara</s> and <s>kūṭa</s> are not feminine.
(2.4.527) <s>Kāpota</s>, <s>śauka</s>, <s>māyūra</s>, <s>taittira</s>, and so forth [are names] for the flock of that [species].

children.text: (2.4.528) gṛhāsaktāḥ pakṣimṛgāśchekāste gṛhyakāśca te | iti siṃhādivargaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.4.528) Birds and animals attached to a household are domesticated (<s>cheka</s>); they are also called <s>gṛhyaka</s>. Thus ends the section on lions and other animals (<s>siṃhādivarga</s>).

children.text: (2.5.529) manuṣyā mānuṣā martyā manujā mānavā narāḥ | atha manuṣyavargaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.5.529) <s>Manuṣya</s>, <s>mānuṣa</s>, <s>martya</s>, <s>manuja</s>, <s>mānava</s>, and <s>nara</s> [are synonyms for a human being]. Now begins the section on human beings (<s>manuṣyavarga</s>).

children.text: (2.5.530) syuḥ pumāṃsaḥ pañcajanāḥ puruṣāḥ pūruṣā naraḥ
children.translated_text: (2.5.530) <s>Pumāṃs</s>, <s>pañcajana</s>, <s>puruṣa</s>, <s>pūruṣa</s>, and <s>nara</s> [are synonyms for a man].

children.text: (2.5.531) strī yoṣidabalā yoṣā nārī sīmantinī vadhūḥ
children.translated_text: (2.5.531) <s>Strī</s>, <s>yoṣit</s>, <s>abalā</s>, <s>yoṣā</s>, <s>nārī</s>, <s>sīmantinī</s>, and <s>vadhū</s> [are synonyms for a woman],
(2.5.532) <s>pratīpadarśinī</s>, <s>vāmā</s>, <s>vanitā</s>, and <s>mahilā</s> likewise.
(2.5.533) Specific [terms for women]: <s>aṅganā</s>, <s>bhīru</s> (the timid one), <s>kāminī</s> (the desirable one), and <s>vāmalocanā</s> (the beautiful-eyed one),

children.text: (2.5.534) pramadā māninī kāntā lalanā ca nitambinī
children.translated_text: (2.5.534) <s>pramadā</s>, <s>māninī</s> (the proud one), <s>kāntā</s> (the beloved), <s>lalanā</s>, and <s>nitambinī</s> (the broad-hipped one),

children.text: (2.5.535) sundarī ramaṇī rāmā kopanā saiva bhāminī
children.translated_text: (2.5.535) <s>sundarī</s> (the beautiful one), <s>ramaṇī</s> (the delightful one), <s>rāmā</s>, <s>kopanā</s> (the angry one) — she is also <s>bhāminī</s>,
(2.5.536) <s>varārohā</s> (of fine hips), <s>mattakāśinī</s> (of intoxicating appearance), <s>uttamā</s> (the excellent one), and <s>varavarṇinī</s> (of finest complexion).
(2.5.537) She who has been consecrated is the chief queen (<s>mahiṣī</s>); the other wives of the king are <s>bhoginī</s>.
(2.5.538) <s>Patnī</s> (wife), <s>pāṇigṛhītī</s> (one whose hand is taken), <s>dvitīyā</s> (the second [half]), and <s>sahadharmiṇī</s> (partner in duty) [are synonyms].

children.text: (2.5.539) bhāryā jāyātha puṃbhūmni dārāḥ syāttu kuṭumbinī
children.translated_text: (2.5.539) <s>Bhāryā</s> and <s>jāyā</s> [are synonyms for wife]. Now, in the masculine plural: <s>dāra</s> [means wives]. <s>Kuṭumbinī</s> [means a housewife].

children.text: (2.5.540) purandhrī sucaritrā tu satī sādhvī pativratā
children.translated_text: (2.5.540) <s>Purandhrī</s> [means a virtuous wife]. One of good conduct is <s>satī</s>, <s>sādhvī</s>, and <s>pativratā</s> (devoted to her husband).
(2.5.541) One whose husband has taken a co-wife is <s>sāpatnikā</s>; <s>adhyūḍhā</s> and <s>adhivinnā</s> [are synonyms]. Now, <s>svayaṃvarā</s> (one who chooses her own husband),
(2.5.542) and <s>patiṃvarā</s> [are synonyms]. A marriageable maiden is <s>varyā</s>. Now, <s>kulastrī</s> and <s>kulapālikā</s> [mean a woman of noble family].
(2.5.543) <s>Kanyā</s> and <s>kumārī</s> [mean a maiden]. <s>Gaurī</s> is one who is naked [i.e., prepubescent] — one who has not yet had her menses (<s>anāgatārtavā</s>).
(2.5.544) One who is in the middle [stage] and has seen her menses (<s>dṛṣṭarajā</s>) — <s>taruṇī</s> and <s>yuvati</s> are synonyms.
(2.5.545) <s>Snuṣā</s>, <s>janī</s>, and <s>vadhū</s> are synonyms [for a daughter-in-law]. <s>Ciriṇṭī</s> means <s>suvāsinī</s> (an auspicious married woman).

children.text: (2.5.546) icchāvatī kāmukā syād vṛṣasyantī tu kāmukī
children.translated_text: (2.5.546) One who is desirous is <s>kāmukā</s>; one who is lustful is <s>vṛṣasyantī</s>, that is, <s>kāmukī</s>.

children.text: (2.5.547) kāntārthinī tu yā yāti saṃketaṃ sābhisārikā
children.translated_text: (2.5.547) One who goes to a secret rendezvous seeking her lover is an <s>abhisārikā</s>.
(2.5.548) <s>Puṃścalī</s>, <s>dharṣiṇī</s>, <s>bandhakī</s>, <s>asatī</s> (unchaste woman), <s>kulaṭā</s>, and <s>itvarī</s>,

children.text: (2.5.549) svairiṇī pāṃsulā ca syādaśiśvī śiśunā vinā
children.translated_text: (2.5.549) <s>svairiṇī</s> (a wanton woman), and <s>pāṃsulā</s> are synonyms. <s>Aśiśvī</s> means one without a child.
(2.5.550) <s>Avīrā</s> means one without a husband or son. <s>Viśvastā</s> and <s>avidhavā</s> are synonyms [for a woman whose husband is alive].
(2.5.551) <s>Āli</s> and <s>sakhī</s> [mean a female friend]; <s>vayasyā</s> [means a friend of the same age]. Now, <s>pativatnī</s> and <s>sabhartṛkā</s> [mean a woman who has a husband].

children.text: (2.5.552) vṛddhā paliknī prājñī tu prajñā prājñā tu dhīmatī
children.translated_text: (2.5.552) An old woman is <s>vṛddhā</s> and <s>paliknī</s> (grey-haired). <s>Prājñī</s> is a wise woman; <s>prajñā</s> means wisdom, and <s>prājñā</s> means one possessed of wisdom (<s>dhīmatī</s>).

children.text: (2.5.553) śūdrī śūdrasya bhāryā syācchūdrā tajjātireva ca
children.translated_text: (2.5.553) <s>Śūdrī</s> is the wife of a <s>Śūdra</s>; <s>śūdrā</s> is [a woman] of that caste itself.
(2.5.554) <s>Ābhīrī</s> means a woman of the <s>Ābhīra</s> caste (a great <s>Śūdra</s> woman); the word is the same for both caste and spousal relation.
(2.5.555) <s>Āryāṇī</s> is one who is herself noble (<s>āryā</s>). <s>Kṣatriyā</s> and <s>kṣatriyāṇī</s> [are used similarly].
(2.5.556) <s>Upādhyāyā</s> and <s>upādhyāyī</s> [mean a female teacher in her own right]. <s>Ācāryā</s> is also [used] independently.

children.text: (2.5.557) ācāryānī tu puṃyoge syādaryī kṣatriyī tathā
children.translated_text: (2.5.557) <s>Ācāryānī</s> [means the wife of an <s>ācārya</s>], used in spousal connection. <s>Āryī</s> and <s>kṣatriyī</s> are similarly [spousal forms].
(2.5.558) <s>Upādhyāyānī</s> and <s>upādhyāyī</s> [are spousal forms]. <s>Poṭā</s> means one having characteristics of both male and female.
(2.5.559) <s>Vīrapatnī</s> and <s>vīrabhāryā</s> [mean the wife of a hero]. The mother of a hero is <s>vīrasū</s>.

children.text: (2.5.560) jātāpatyā prajātā ca prasūtā ca prasūtikā
children.translated_text: (2.5.560) <s>Jātāpatyā</s>, <s>prajātā</s>, <s>prasūtā</s>, and <s>prasūtikā</s> [are synonyms for a woman who has given birth].
(2.5.561) <s>Nagnikā</s> and <s>koṭavī</s> are [terms for] a naked woman. <s>Dūtī</s> and <s>saṃcārikā</s> are synonyms [for a female messenger].
(2.5.562) <s>Kātyāyanī</s> is a woman who is middle-aged (<s>ardhavṛddhā</s>), wears ochre robes (<s>kāṣāyavasanā</s>), and is without a husband (<s>adhavā</s>).
(2.5.563) <s>Sairandhrī</s> is a woman dwelling in another's house, self-dependent, and skilled in crafts (<s>śilpakārikā</s>).
(2.5.564) <s>Asikni</s> is a young woman (<s>avṛddhā</s>) who is a maidservant (<s>preṣyā</s>) and moves within the inner chambers (<s>antaḥpuracāriṇī</s>).

children.text: (2.5.565) vārastrī gaṇikā veśyā rūpājīvātha sā janaiḥ
children.translated_text: (2.5.565) <s>Vārastrī</s>, <s>gaṇikā</s>, <s>veśyā</s>, and <s>rūpājīvā</s> (one who lives by her beauty) [are synonyms for a courtesan]. Now, she who by people
(2.5.566) is honored is the chief courtesan (<s>vāramukhyā</s>). <s>Kuṭṭanī</s> and <s>śambhalī</s> are synonyms [for a procuress].
(2.5.567) <s>Vipraśnikā</s> means a fortune-teller (<s>īkṣaṇikā</s>) and astrologer (<s>daivajñā</s>). Now, a menstruating woman (<s>rajasvalā</s>):
(2.5.568) <s>strīdharmiṇī</s> (having the female condition), <s>avirātreyī</s>, <s>malinī</s> (impure), and <s>puṣpavatī</s> (having her flower) [are synonyms].
(2.5.569) <s>Ṛtumatī</s> (in season) and <s>udakyā</s> are also [synonyms]. <s>Rajas</s>, <s>puṣpa</s>, and <s>ārtava</s> [are synonyms for menstrual blood].
(2.5.570) <s>Śraddhālu</s> and <s>dohadavatī</s> [mean a pregnant woman with cravings]. <s>Niṣkalā</s> means one who has ceased menstruating (<s>vigatārtavā</s>).
(2.5.571) <s>Āpannasattvā</s>, <s>gurviṇī</s>, <s>antarvatnī</s>, and <s>garbhiṇī</s> [are synonyms for a pregnant woman].
(2.5.572) The collective [noun] from <s>gaṇikā</s> is <s>gāṇikya</s>; from <s>garbhiṇī</s> it is <s>gārbhiṇa</s>; from <s>yuvati</s> it is <s>yauvata</s>; [and] <s>gaṇa</s> [means a group].
(2.5.573) <s>Punarbhū</s>, <s>didhiṣū</s>, and <s>ūḍhā</s> [are synonyms for a remarried woman]. Her husband is <s>dviḥ</s> (i.e., <s>didhiṣu</s>) [one who has married a remarried woman].

children.text: (2.5.574) sa tu dvijo 'gredidhiṣūḥ saiva yasya kuṭumbinī
children.translated_text: (2.5.574) But a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [who marries such a woman] is called <s>agredidhiṣu</s>; she of whom he is the householder [is also so designated].
(2.5.575) <s>Kānīna</s> means a son born of an unmarried girl. Now, the son of a fortunate woman (<s>subhagā</s>):
(2.5.576) is <s>saubhāgineya</s>. <s>Pārastraiṇeya</s> is the son of another man's wife.
(2.5.577) <s>Paitṛṣvaseya</s> and <s>paitṛṣvasrīya</s> are [synonyms for] the son of a paternal aunt (<s>pitṛsvasṛ</s>).
(2.5.578) The son of a maternal aunt (<s>mātṛsvasṛ</s>) is likewise [designated]. <s>Vaimātreya</s> is one born of a step-mother (<s>vimātṛja</s>).
(2.5.579) Now, <s>bāndhakinya</s> and <s>bandhula</s> are [synonyms for] the son of an unchaste woman (<s>asatīsuta</s>).

children.text: (2.5.580) kaulaṭeraḥ kaulateyo bhikṣukī tu satī yadi
children.translated_text: (2.5.580) <s>Kaulaṭera</s> and <s>kaulateya</s> [are synonyms for such a son]. But if the unchaste woman is a mendicant (<s>bhikṣukī</s>) who is virtuous (<s>satī</s>),
(2.5.581) then her son is <s>kaulaṭineya</s>; he is also [called] <s>kaulateya</s>.

children.text: (2.5.582) ātmajastanayaḥ sūnuḥ sutaḥ putraḥ striyāṃ tvamī
children.translated_text: (2.5.582) <s>Ātmaja</s>, <s>tanaya</s>, <s>sūnu</s>, <s>suta</s>, and <s>putra</s> [are synonyms for a son]. In the feminine, all of these
(2.5.583) denote a daughter (<s>duhitṛ</s>). <s>Apatya</s> and <s>toka</s> are the same for both [son and daughter].
(2.5.584) For one's own-born: <s>aurasa</s> and <s>rasya</s>. <s>Tāta</s>, <s>janaka</s>, and <s>pitṛ</s> [are synonyms for father].
(2.5.585) <s>Janayitrī</s>, <s>prasū</s>, <s>mātṛ</s>, and <s>jananī</s> [are synonyms for mother]. <s>Bhaginī</s> and <s>svasṛ</s> [are synonyms for sister].

children.text: (2.5.586) nanāndā tu svasā patyurnaptrī pautrī sutātmajā
children.translated_text: (2.5.586) <s>Nanāndā</s> is the husband's sister. <s>Naptrī</s> and <s>pautrī</s> [are synonyms for] a son's daughter (<s>sutātmajā</s>).
(2.5.587) The wives of a group of brothers are <s>yātaras</s> (sisters-in-law) to each other.
(2.5.588) <s>Prajāvatī</s> [means one who has offspring]. The wife of a brother is <s>bhrātṛjāyā</s>. The wife of a maternal uncle (<s>mātula</s>) is <s>mātulānī</s>, that is, <s>mātulī</s>.

children.text: (2.5.589) patipatnyoḥ prasūḥ śvaśrūḥ śvaśurastu pitā tayoḥ
children.translated_text: (2.5.589) The mother of [both] husband and wife is the mother-in-law (<s>śvaśrū</s>); the father of either is the father-in-law (<s>śvaśura</s>).
(2.5.590) The father's brother is <s>pitṛvya</s>; the mother's brother is <s>mātula</s> (maternal uncle).
(2.5.591) <s>Śyāla</s> — brothers of the wife; <s>svāmin</s> — husband; <s>devṛ</s> and <s>devara</s> — husband's brother; masculine
(2.5.592) <s>Svasrīya</s>, <s>bhāgineya</s> — sister's son; <s>jāmātṛ</s> — son-in-law, the husband of one's daughter
(2.5.593) <s>Pitāmaha</s> — father's father (paternal grandfather); his father is <s>prapitāmaha</s> (great-grandfather)
(2.5.594) Likewise from the mother's side, <s>mātāmaha</s> etc.; <s>sapiṇḍa</s> and <s>sanābhi</s> — those sharing the same lineage; synonyms
(2.5.595) <s>Samānodara</s>, <s>sodarya</s>, <s>sagarbhya</s>, <s>sahaja</s> — born of the same womb; synonyms
(2.5.596) <s>Sagotra</s>, <s>bāndhava</s>, <s>jñāti</s>, <s>bandhu</s>, <s>sva</s>, <s>svajana</s> — kinsman, relative; synonyms
(2.5.597) <s>Jñāteya</s> — the state of being a kinsman; <s>bandhutā</s> — relationship; these denote respectively the abstract quality and the collective group
(2.5.598) <s>Dhava</s>, <s>priya</s>, <s>pati</s>, <s>bhartṛ</s> — husband; <s>jāra</s> and <s>upapati</s> — paramour, illicit lover; synonyms

children.text: (2.5.599) amṛte jārajaḥ kuṇḍo mṛte bhartari golakaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.5.599) Born of a paramour while the husband is alive: <s>kuṇḍa</s>; born after the husband's death: <s>golaka</s>
(2.5.600) <s>Bhrātrīya</s>, <s>bhrātṛja</s> — brother's son (nephew); <s>bhrātṛ</s> and <s>bhaginī</s> — brother and sister; together they are called <s>bhrātarau</s> (the sibling pair)
(2.5.601) <s>Mātāpitarau</s>, <s>pitarau</s> — mother and father (parents); <s>mātarapitarau</s> — parents; <s>prasū</s> and <s>janayitṛ</s> — the one who gives birth and the one who begets

children.text: (2.5.602) śvaśrūśvaśurau śvaśurau putrau putraśca duhitā ca
children.translated_text: (2.5.602) <s>Śvaśrū</s> and <s>śvaśura</s> — mother-in-law and father-in-law (collectively <s>śvaśurau</s>); <s>putra</s> and <s>duhitṛ</s> — son and daughter (collectively <s>putrau</s>)

children.text: (2.5.603) daṃpatī jaṃpatī jāyāpatī bhāryāpatī ca tau
children.translated_text: (2.5.603) <s>Daṃpatī</s>, <s>jaṃpatī</s>, <s>jāyāpatī</s>, <s>bhāryāpatī</s> — husband and wife (the married couple); synonyms
(2.5.604) <s>Garbhāśaya</s> — the womb; <s>jarāyu</s> — the placenta/membrane; <s>ulba</s> — the caul; <s>kalala</s> — the embryo in its earliest stage; not feminine

children.text: (2.5.605) sūtimāso vaijanano garbho bhrūṇa imau samau
children.translated_text: (2.5.605) <s>Sūtimāsa</s>, <s>vaijanana</s> — the month of delivery; <s>garbha</s> and <s>bhrūṇa</s> — embryo, fetus; these two are synonyms
(2.5.606) <s>Tṛtīyāprakṛti</s> — the third nature; <s>śaṇḍha</s>, <s>klība</s>, <s>paṇḍa</s> — eunuch, impotent person; used in the neuter gender

children.text: (2.5.607) śiśutvaṃ śaiśavaṃ bālyaṃ tāruṇyaṃ yauvanaṃ same
children.translated_text: (2.5.607) <s>Śiśutva</s>, <s>śaiśava</s> — infancy; <s>bālya</s> — childhood; <s>tāruṇya</s>, <s>yauvana</s> — youth; synonyms in pairs
(2.5.608) <s>Sthāvira</s> — old age; <s>vṛddhatva</s> — the state of being old; <s>vārdhaka</s> — applied also to a group of the aged

children.text: (2.5.609) palitaṃ jarasā śauklyaṃ keśādau visrasā jarā
children.translated_text: (2.5.609) <s>Palita</s> — greyness of hair due to old age; <s>jarā</s> — old age, decay, with withering
(2.5.610) <s>Uttānaśayā</s> — an infant lying on its back; <s>ḍimbhā</s> — a babe; <s>stanapā</s>, <s>stanandhayī</s> — one who suckles, a suckling infant
(2.5.611) <s>Bāla</s> — a boy; <s>māṇavaka</s> — a lad; <s>vayastha</s>, <s>taruṇa</s>, <s>yuvā</s> — one in the prime of youth; synonyms

children.text: (2.5.612) pravayāḥ sthaviro vṛddho jīno jīrṇo jarannapi
children.translated_text: (2.5.612) <s>Pravayās</s>, <s>sthavira</s>, <s>vṛddha</s> — aged, old; <s>jīna</s>, <s>jīrṇa</s>, <s>jarat</s> — decrepit, worn out; also synonyms
(2.5.613) <s>Varṣīyān</s> — elder; <s>daśamī</s>, <s>jyāyān</s> — senior; <s>pūrvaja</s>, <s>agriya</s>, <s>agraja</s> — the firstborn, elder
(2.5.614) For the younger-born: <s>kaniṣṭha</s>, <s>yavīya</s>, <s>avara</s>, <s>anuja</s> — the youngest, the junior
(2.5.615) <s>Amāṃsa</s>, <s>durbala</s>, <s>chāta</s> — lean, weak, emaciated; <s>balavān</s>, <s>māṃsala</s>, <s>aṃsala</s> — strong, muscular, robust
(2.5.616) <s>Tundila</s>, <s>tundibha</s>, <s>tundī</s>, <s>bṛhatkukṣi</s>, <s>picaṇḍila</s> — pot-bellied, big-bellied; synonyms
(2.5.617) <s>Avaṭīṭa</s>, <s>avanāṭa</s>, <s>avabhraṭa</s> — one with a flat or depressed nose; having a snub nose

children.text: (2.5.618) keśavaḥ keśikaḥ keśī valino valibhaḥ samau
children.translated_text: (2.5.618) <s>Keśava</s>, <s>keśika</s>, <s>keśin</s> — long-haired, having beautiful hair; <s>valin</s>, <s>valibha</s> — wrinkled; synonyms
(2.5.619) <s>Vikalāṅga</s> — one with a deformed limb; <s>apogaṇḍa</s> — beardless youth; <s>kharva</s>, <s>hrasva</s>, <s>vāmana</s> — short, dwarfish; synonyms
(2.5.620) <s>Kharaṇās</s>, <s>kharaṇasa</s> — one with a rough nose; <s>vigra</s> — one who has lost the nose
(2.5.621) <s>Khuraṇās</s>, <s>khuraṇasa</s> — one with a nose like a hoof; <s>prajñu</s> — one with protruding knees
(2.5.622) <s>Ūrdhvajñu</s>, <s>ūrdhvajānu</s> — one with knees pointing upward; <s>saṃjñu</s>, <s>saṃhatajānuka</s> — one with knees pressed together

children.text: (2.5.623) syādeḍe badhiraḥ kubje gaḍulaḥ kukare kuṇiḥ
children.translated_text: (2.5.623) <s>Eḍa</s> — deaf; <s>badhira</s> — deaf; <s>kubja</s> — hunchback; <s>gaḍula</s> — hunchbacked; <s>kukara</s>, <s>kuṇi</s> — having a crooked arm
(2.5.624) <s>Pṛśni</s> — having little body hair; <s>śroṇa</s> — lame; <s>paṅgu</s> — crippled; <s>muṇḍa</s> — shaven-headed, applied to one whose head is shaved
(2.5.625) <s>Valira</s> — squint-eyed; <s>kekara</s> — cross-eyed; <s>khoḍa</s>, <s>khañja</s> — lame, limping; used in all three genders; <s>jarāvara</s> — aged, worn by old age
(2.5.626) <s>Jaḍula</s> — having a mole; <s>kālaka</s> — a dark spot; <s>piplu</s> — a freckle; <s>tilaka</s>, <s>tilakālaka</s> — a mole, a beauty mark
(2.5.627) <s>Anāmaya</s>, <s>ārogya</s> — health, freedom from disease; <s>cikitsā</s> — medical treatment; <s>rukpratikriyā</s> — remedy for illness
(2.5.628) <s>Bheṣaja</s>, <s>auṣadha</s>, <s>bhaiṣajya</s> — medicine, remedy; <s>agada</s> — antidote; <s>jāyuti</s> — also a synonym for medicine
(2.5.629) Feminine: <s>ruj</s>, <s>rujā</s> — pain; <s>upatāpa</s>, <s>roga</s>, <s>vyādhi</s>, <s>gada</s>, <s>āmaya</s> — disease, illness, ailment; synonyms

children.text: (2.5.630) kṣayaḥ śoṣaśca yakṣmā ca pratiśyāyastu pīnasaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.5.630) <s>Kṣaya</s>, <s>śoṣa</s>, <s>yakṣman</s> — consumption, wasting disease; <s>pratiśyāya</s>, <s>pīnasa</s> — cold, nasal catarrh

children.text: (2.5.631) strī kṣutkṣutaṃ kṣavaḥ puṃsi kāsastu kṣavathuḥ pumān
children.translated_text: (2.5.631) Feminine: <s>kṣut</s> — hunger; <s>kṣuta</s>, <s>kṣava</s> — sneeze; masculine; <s>kāsa</s>, <s>kṣavathu</s> — cough, sneezing; masculine
(2.5.632) <s>Śopha</s>, <s>śvayathu</s>, <s>śotha</s> — swelling, edema; <s>pādasphoṭa</s>, <s>vipādikā</s> — cracking of the feet

children.text: (2.5.633) kilāsasidhme kacchvāṃ tu pāma pāmā vicarcikā
children.translated_text: (2.5.633) <s>Kilāsa</s>, <s>sidhma</s> — types of skin disease, leucoderma; <s>kacchū</s> — scabies; <s>pāman</s>, <s>pāmā</s>, <s>vicarcikā</s> — eczema, scab

children.text: (2.5.634) kaṇḍūḥ kharjūśca kaṇḍūyā visphoṭaḥ piṭakaḥ striyām
children.translated_text: (2.5.634) <s>Kaṇḍū</s>, <s>kharjū</s> — itch; <s>kaṇḍūyā</s> — itching; <s>visphoṭa</s>, <s>piṭaka</s> — blister, pustule; feminine
(2.5.635) <s>Vraṇa</s> — wound, ulcer; not feminine; <s>īrma</s>, <s>maru</s> — wound on the arm; neuter; <s>nāḍīvraṇa</s> — a fistula; masculine
(2.5.636) <s>Koṭha</s> — urticaria; <s>maṇḍalaka</s> — ringworm; <s>kuṣṭha</s> — leprosy; <s>śvitra</s> — vitiligo; <s>durnāmaka</s>, <s>arśas</s> — hemorrhoids, piles
(2.5.637) <s>Ānāha</s>, <s>nibandha</s> — constipation, intestinal obstruction; <s>grahaṇīruk</s> — sprue, chronic diarrhea; <s>pravāhikā</s> — dysentery

children.text: (2.5.638) pracchardikā vamiśca strī pumāṃstu vamathuḥ samāḥ
children.translated_text: (2.5.638) <s>Pracchardikā</s>, <s>vami</s> — vomiting; feminine; <s>vamathu</s> — vomiting; masculine; these are synonyms
(2.5.639) Types of disease: <s>vidradhi</s> — abscess; feminine; <s>jvara</s> — fever; <s>meha</s> — urinary disorder; <s>bhagandhara</s> — fistula-in-ano
(2.5.640) <s>Ślīpada</s>, <s>pādavalmīka</s> — elephantiasis (swelling of the legs); <s>keśaghna</s>, <s>indraluptaka</s> — alopecia, hair loss
(2.5.641) <s>Aśmarī</s> — urinary calculus (kidney stone); <s>mūtrakṛcchra</s> — dysuria (difficulty in urination); the former two refer to seminal disorders; used in all three genders
(2.5.642) <s>Rogahārin</s> — disease-remover; <s>agadaṃkāra</s> — medicine-maker; <s>bhiṣaj</s>, <s>vaidya</s> — physician, doctor; synonyms for a healer

children.text: (2.5.643) vārto nirāmayaḥ kalya ullāgho nirgato gadāt
children.translated_text: (2.5.643) <s>Vārta</s>, <s>nirāmaya</s>, <s>kalya</s> — healthy, well; <s>ullāgha</s> — recovered; one who has emerged from disease
(2.5.644) <s>Glāna</s>, <s>glāsnu</s> — languishing, feeble; <s>āmayāvin</s> — afflicted with disease; <s>vikṛta</s>, <s>vyādhita</s>, <s>apaṭu</s> — diseased, unhealthy, indisposed
(2.5.645) <s>Ātura</s>, <s>abhyamita</s>, <s>abhyānta</s> — sick, afflicted; <s>pāmanaka</s>, <s>kacchura</s> — one suffering from skin disease; synonyms
(2.5.646) <s>Dadruṇa</s> — one suffering from ringworm (<s>dadru</s>); <s>arśasa</s> — one afflicted with piles (<s>arśas</s>)
(2.5.647) <s>Vātakin</s> — one suffering from wind-disorder (<s>vātaroga</s>); <s>sātisāra</s>, <s>atisārakin</s> — one afflicted with diarrhea
(2.5.648) <s>Kullacillapilla</s> — these apply to one with watering eyes (<s>klinnākṣa</s>); also applied when the eye is moist
(2.5.649) <s>Unmatta</s> — mad, insane; <s>unmādavat</s> — one possessed by madness; <s>śleṣmala</s>, <s>śleṣmaṇa</s>, <s>kaphin</s> — one afflicted with phlegm
(2.5.650) <s>Nyubja</s> — bent, stooped; <s>bhugna</s> — curved; <s>rujā</s> — pain; <s>vṛddhanābhi</s> — one with a protruding navel (hernia); <s>tundila</s>, <s>tundibha</s> — pot-bellied

(2.5.651) <s>Vilāsin</s> — one with leucoderma; <s>sidhmala</s> — afflicted with white spots; <s>andha</s>, <s>adṛś</s> — blind; <s>mūrcchālu</s> — prone to fainting; <s>mūrta</s>, <s>mūrcchita</s> — fainted, unconscious
(2.5.652) <s>Śukra</s>, <s>tejas</s>, <s>retas</s> — semen, vital fluid; <s>bīja</s>, <s>vīrya</s>, <s>indriya</s> — seed, potency, virile power; also synonyms

children.text: (2.5.653) māyuḥ pittaṃ kaphaḥ śleṣmā striyāṃ tu tvagasṛgdharā
children.translated_text: (2.5.653) <s>Māyu</s> — bile; <s>pitta</s> — bile (one of the three humors); <s>kapha</s>, <s>śleṣman</s> — phlegm; feminine: <s>tvak</s> — skin; <s>asṛk</s> — blood; <s>dharā</s> — that which holds
(2.5.654) <s>Piśita</s>, <s>tarasa</s>, <s>māṃsa</s>, <s>palala</s>, <s>kravya</s>, <s>āmiṣa</s> — flesh, meat; synonyms
(2.5.655) When heated and dried: <s>vallūra</s> — dried meat, jerky; used in all three genders
(2.5.656) For blood: <s>asṛj</s>, <s>lohita</s>, <s>asra</s>, <s>rakta</s>, <s>kṣataja</s>, <s>śoṇita</s> — blood; synonyms
(2.5.657) <s>Bukka</s> — the heart (as choicest flesh); <s>hṛdaya</s>, <s>hṛd</s> — the heart; <s>medas</s> — fat; <s>vapā</s>, <s>vasā</s> — suet, adipose tissue

children.text: (2.5.658) paścādgrīvāśirā manyā nāḍī tu dhamaniḥ śirā
children.translated_text: (2.5.658) At the back of the neck, the artery is called <s>manyā</s>; <s>nāḍī</s>, <s>dhamanī</s>, <s>śirā</s> — vein, artery, blood vessel

children.text: (2.5.659) tilakaṃ kloma mastiṣkaṃ gordaṃ kiṭṭaṃ malo 'striyām
children.translated_text: (2.5.659) <s>Tilaka</s> — the lungs; <s>kloman</s> — the right lung; <s>mastiṣka</s> — the brain; <s>gorda</s> — a gland; <s>kiṭṭa</s>, <s>mala</s> — waste, impurity; not feminine
(2.5.660) <s>Antra</s> — intestine; <s>purītat</s> — the intestinal contents; <s>gulma</s> — abdominal tumor, spleen enlargement; <s>plīhan</s> — the spleen; masculine; then <s>vasnasā</s> —

children.text: (2.5.661) snāyuḥ striyāṃ kālakhaṇḍayakṛtī tu same ime
children.translated_text: (2.5.661) <s>Snāyu</s> — sinew, tendon; feminine; <s>kālakhaṇḍa</s>, <s>yakṛt</s> — the liver; these two are synonyms
(2.5.662) <s>Sṛṇikā</s>, <s>syandanī</s>, <s>lālā</s> — saliva, drool; <s>dūṣikā</s> — the discharge from the eyes, eye-mucus
(2.5.663) Nasal discharge: <s>siṃghāṇa</s> — nasal mucus; <s>piñjūṣa</s> — ear-wax, the impurity of the ears
(2.5.664) <s>Mūtra</s>, <s>prasrāva</s> — urine; <s>uccāra</s>, <s>avaskara</s> — excrement; <s>śamala</s>, <s>śakṛt</s> — feces
(2.5.665) <s>Purīṣa</s>, <s>gūtha</s>, <s>varcaska</s> — excrement, stool; not feminine; <s>viṣṭhā</s>, <s>viś</s> — feces; feminine
(2.5.666) <s>Karpara</s>, <s>kapāla</s> — skull, cranium; not feminine; <s>kīkasa</s>, <s>kulya</s>, <s>asthi</s> — bone; synonyms
(2.5.667) <s>Kaṃkāla</s> — skeleton (the bones of the body); <s>kaśerukā</s> — vertebra (the bone of the spine)

children.text: (2.5.668) śirosthani karoṭiḥ strī pārśvāsthani tu parśukā
children.translated_text: (2.5.668) <s>Karoṭi</s> — the cranium (bone of the head); feminine; <s>parśukā</s> — a rib (bone of the side)
(2.5.669) <s>Aṅga</s>, <s>pratīka</s>, <s>avayava</s>, <s>apaghana</s> — limb, body part; then <s>kalevara</s> —

children.text: (2.5.670) gātraṃ vapuḥ saṃhananaṃ śarīraṃ varṣma vigrahaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.5.670) <s>Gātra</s>, <s>vapus</s>, <s>saṃhanana</s>, <s>śarīra</s>, <s>varṣman</s>, <s>vigraha</s> — body, frame, physique; synonyms
(2.5.671) <s>Kāya</s>, <s>deha</s> — body; neuter and masculine; <s>mūrti</s>, <s>tanu</s>, <s>tanū</s> — body, form; feminine
(2.5.672) <s>Pādāgra</s>, <s>prapada</s> — the forepart of the foot, toes; <s>pāda</s>, <s>pad</s>, <s>aṅghri</s>, <s>caraṇa</s> — foot; not feminine
(2.5.673) At that joint: <s>ghuṭikā</s> — the ankle bone; <s>gulpha</s> — the ankle; masculine; <s>pārṣṇi</s> — the heel; below them
(2.5.674) <s>Jaṅghā</s> — the shin, lower leg; <s>prasṛtā</s> — extended; <s>jānu</s> — the knee; <s>ūru</s>, <s>parvāṣṭhīvat</s> — the thigh, kneecap; not feminine
(2.5.675) <s>Sakthi</s> — thigh; neuter; <s>ūru</s> — thigh; masculine; the joint of that is <s>vaṅkṣaṇa</s> — the groin; masculine
(2.5.676) <s>Guda</s> — the anus; <s>apāna</s> — the lower abdomen; <s>pāyu</s> — the rectum; feminine; <s>basti</s> — the bladder; below the navel, for both (male and female)

children.text: (2.5.677) kaṭo nā śroṇiphalakaṃ kaṭiḥ śroṇiḥ kakudmatī
children.translated_text: (2.5.677) <s>Kaṭa</s> — the hip; feminine; <s>śroṇiphalaka</s> — the hip bone; <s>kaṭi</s>, <s>śroṇi</s> — the waist, hip; <s>kakudmatī</s> — having a hump

children.text: (2.5.678) paścānnitambaḥ strīkaṭyāḥ klībe tu jaghanaṃ puraḥ
children.translated_text: (2.5.678) Behind: <s>nitamba</s> — the buttock, posterior of the hip; feminine of <s>kaṭi</s>; neuter: <s>jaghana</s> — the front of the hip/pubic region
(2.5.679) <s>Kūpaka</s> — the two dimples on the buttocks; when both are absent: <s>kakundara</s>
(2.5.680) Feminine: <s>sphic</s> — the buttocks; <s>kaṭiprotha</s> — the hip prominence; <s>upastha</s> — the genitalia (of both male and female, to be described)
(2.5.681) <s>Bhaga</s>, <s>yoni</s> — the female genitalia; for both (genders); <s>śiśna</s>, <s>meḍhra</s>, <s>mehana</s>, <s>śephas</s> — the penis
(2.5.682) <s>Muṣka</s>, <s>aṇḍakośa</s>, <s>vṛṣaṇa</s> — the scrotum, testicles; <s>trika</s> — the region below the spine at the back
(2.5.683) <s>Picaṇḍa</s>, <s>kukṣi</s> — the belly, abdomen; <s>jaṭhara</s>, <s>udara</s> — the stomach, belly; <s>tunda</s> — the paunch; <s>stana</s>, <s>kuca</s> — the breast

children.text: (2.5.684) cūcukaṃ tu kucāgraṃ syānna nā kroḍaṃ bhujāntaram
children.translated_text: (2.5.684) <s>Cūcuka</s> — the nipple, the tip of the breast; neuter/feminine; <s>kroḍa</s> — the chest between the arms, the bosom

children.text: (2.5.685) uro vatsaṃ ca vakṣaśca pṛṣṭhaṃ tu caramaṃ tanoḥ
children.translated_text: (2.5.685) <s>Uras</s>, <s>vatsa</s>, <s>vakṣas</s> — the chest, breast; <s>pṛṣṭha</s> — the back, the rear of the body
(2.5.686) <s>Skandha</s> — the shoulder; <s>bhujaśiras</s>, <s>aṃsa</s> — the shoulder-top; not feminine; the joints of these are <s>jatruṇī</s> — the collarbones
(2.5.687) At the base of the arms, both: <s>kakṣa</s> — the armpit; <s>pārśva</s> — the side of the body; not feminine; below them

children.text: (2.5.688) madhyamaṃ cāvalagnaṃ ca madhyo 'strī dvau parau dvayoḥ
children.translated_text: (2.5.688) <s>Madhyama</s>, <s>avalagna</s> — the waist, middle part; <s>madhya</s> — the middle; not feminine; the latter two apply to both
(2.5.689) <s>Bhuja</s>, <s>bāhu</s> — the arm; <s>praveṣṭa</s> — the forearm; <s>dos</s> — the arm; <s>kaphoṇi</s>, <s>kūrpara</s> — the elbow
(2.5.690) Above that is <s>pragaṇḍa</s> — the upper arm; below it is <s>prakoṣṭha</s> — the forearm
(2.5.691) From the wrist to the little finger: the outer part of the hand is <s>karabha</s> — the metacarpus
(2.5.692) <s>Pañcaśākha</s> — the five-branched; <s>śaya</s>, <s>pāṇi</s> — the hand; <s>tarjanī</s>, <s>pradeśinī</s> — the index finger
(2.5.693) <s>Aṅguli</s>, <s>karaśākhā</s> — the fingers (branches of the hand); masculine: <s>aṅguṣṭha</s> — the thumb; <s>pradeśinī</s> — the index finger

children.text: (2.5.694) madhyamānāmikā cāpi kaniṣṭhā ceti tāḥ kramāt
children.translated_text: (2.5.694) <s>Madhyamā</s> — the middle finger; <s>anāmikā</s> — the ring finger (the unnamed one); and <s>kaniṣṭhā</s> — the little finger; these in order
(2.5.695) <s>Punarbhava</s> — that which grows again; <s>kararuha</s> — that which grows on the hand; <s>nakha</s> — fingernail; not feminine; <s>nakhara</s> — claw; not feminine
(2.5.696) <s>Prādeśa</s>, <s>tāla</s>, <s>gokarna</s> — spans measured from the index finger and extended thumb
(2.5.697) With the thumb and little finger extended: <s>vitasti</s> — a span of twelve finger-breadths
(2.5.698) On the hand: <s>capeṭa</s>, <s>pratala</s>, <s>prahasta</s> — a slap, an open-palm strike; with fingers spread
(2.5.699) The two palms joined together: <s>saṃhatatala</s>, <s>pratala</s> — the left and right palms pressed together
(2.5.700) <s>Pāṇi</s> with fingers bent inward: <s>nikubja</s>; <s>prasṛti</s> — two handfuls; when both joined: <s>añjali</s> — the cupped hands; masculine

children.text: (2.5.701) prakoṣṭhe vistṛtakare hasto muṣṭyā tu baddhayā
children.translated_text: (2.5.701) From the forearm with hand extended: <s>hasta</s> — a cubit; with the fist closed,
(2.5.702) that is <s>ratni</s> — a cubit (with closed fist); <s>aratni</s> — the measure with a fist excluding the little finger
(2.5.703) <s>Vyāma</s> — a fathom; the span of both arms with hands extended sideways
(2.5.704) With arms stretched upward with hands: in human measurement, <s>pauruṣa</s> — a man's height; used in all three genders
(2.5.705) <s>Kaṇṭha</s>, <s>gala</s> — the throat; then for the neck: <s>grīvā</s>, <s>śirodhi</s>, <s>kandharā</s> — the neck; also synonyms
(2.5.706) <s>Kambugrīvā</s> — a conch-like neck (with three lines); <s>avaṭu</s> — the hollow of the throat; <s>ghāṭā</s>, <s>kṛkāṭikā</s> — the nape, back of the neck
(2.5.707) <s>Vaktra</s>, <s>āsya</s>, <s>vadana</s>, <s>tuṇḍa</s>, <s>ānana</s>, <s>lapana</s>, <s>mukha</s> — the face, mouth; synonyms

children.text: (2.5.708) klībe ghrāṇaṃ gandhavahā ghoṇā nāsā ca nāsikā
children.translated_text: (2.5.708) Neuter: <s>ghrāṇa</s> — the nose; <s>gandhavahā</s>, <s>ghoṇā</s>, <s>nāsā</s>, <s>nāsikā</s> — the nose; synonyms
(2.5.709) <s>Oṣṭha</s>, <s>adhara</s> — the lips; also called <s>radanacchada</s> — tooth-covers; <s>daśanavāsas</s> — garment of the teeth
(2.5.710) Below: <s>cibuka</s> — the chin; <s>gaṇḍa</s>, <s>kapola</s> — the cheeks; beyond that: <s>hanu</s> — the jaw

children.text: (2.5.711) radanā daśanā dantā radāstālu tu kākudam
children.translated_text: (2.5.711) <s>Radana</s>, <s>daśana</s>, <s>danta</s>, <s>rada</s> — teeth; <s>tālu</s>, <s>kākuda</s> — the palate
(2.5.712) <s>Rasajñā</s>, <s>rasanā</s>, <s>jihvā</s> — the tongue (knower of taste); at the corners of the lips: <s>sṛkkiṇī</s> — the corners of the mouth
(2.5.713) <s>Lalāṭa</s>, <s>alika</s> — the forehead; <s>godhi</s> — the upper forehead; above the eyes: <s>bhrū</s> — the eyebrows; feminine, dual
(2.5.714) <s>Kūrca</s> — the space between the eyebrows; not feminine; <s>tārakā</s> — the pupil of the eye; <s>kanīnikā</s> — the pupil
(2.5.715) <s>Locana</s>, <s>nayana</s>, <s>netra</s>, <s>īkṣaṇa</s>, <s>cakṣus</s>, <s>akṣi</s> — the eye; synonyms

children.text: (2.5.716) dṛgdṛṣṭī cāsru netrāmbu rodanaṃ cāsramaśru ca
children.translated_text: (2.5.716) <s>Dṛś</s>, <s>dṛṣṭi</s> — sight, vision; <s>asru</s>, <s>netrāmbu</s>, <s>rodana</s>, <s>asra</s>, <s>aśru</s> — tears; synonyms
(2.5.717) <s>Apāṅga</s> — the outer corner of the eye; <s>kaṭākṣa</s> — a sidelong glance, a glance from the corner of the eye

children.text: (2.5.718) karṇaśabdagrahau śrotraṃ śrutiḥ strī śravaṇaṃ śravaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.5.718) <s>Karṇa</s> — the ear (that which grasps sound); <s>śrotra</s>, <s>śruti</s>, <s>śravaṇa</s>, <s>śravas</s> — the ear, hearing; feminine for <s>śruti</s>

children.text: (2.5.719) uttamāṅgaṃ śiraḥ śīrṣaṃ mūrdhā nā mastako 'striyām
children.translated_text: (2.5.719) <s>Uttamāṅga</s> — the highest limb; <s>śiras</s>, <s>śīrṣa</s> — the head; <s>mūrdhan</s> — the crown of the head; feminine; <s>mastaka</s> — the head; not feminine

children.text: (2.5.720) cikuraḥ kuntalo vālaḥ kacaḥ keśaḥ śiroruhaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.5.720) <s>Cikura</s>, <s>kuntala</s>, <s>vāla</s>, <s>kaca</s>, <s>keśa</s>, <s>śiroruha</s> — hair of the head; synonyms
(2.5.721) A mass of those: <s>kaiśika</s>, <s>kaiśya</s> — head of hair; <s>alaka</s> — curls; <s>cūrṇakuntala</s> — curly locks
(2.5.722) Those on the forehead: <s>bhramaraka</s> — curls on the forehead; <s>kākapakṣa</s> — a side-lock (crow's wing); <s>śikhaṇḍaka</s> — a crest of hair
(2.5.723) <s>Kabarī</s> — a braid, hair-arrangement; <s>keśaveśa</s> — a hairstyle; then <s>dhammilla</s> — a chignon, hair tied together

children.text: (2.5.724) śikhā cūḍā keśapāśī vratinastu saṭā jaṭā
children.translated_text: (2.5.724) <s>Śikhā</s>, <s>cūḍā</s> — a topknot; <s>keśapāśin</s> — having a mass of hair; for an ascetic: <s>saṭā</s>, <s>jaṭā</s> — matted locks
(2.5.725) <s>Veṇī</s>, <s>praveṇī</s> — a braid, plait; <s>śīrṣaṇya</s>, <s>śirasya</s> — relating to the head; for clean, beautiful hair
(2.5.726) <s>Pāśa</s>, <s>pakṣa</s>, <s>hasta</s> — these mean 'bundle' or 'collection' when used after <s>kaca</s> (hair); the latter meanings are from their other senses

children.text: (2.5.727) tanūruhaṃ roma loma tadvṛddhau śmaśru pummukhe
children.translated_text: (2.5.727) <s>Tanūruha</s>, <s>roman</s>, <s>loman</s> — body hair; when grown fully on the face: <s>śmaśru</s> — beard, facial hair; masculine on the face
(2.5.728) <s>Ākalpa</s>, <s>veṣa</s> — attire, costume; <s>nepathya</s> — theatrical costume, dress; <s>pratikarman</s>, <s>prasādhana</s> — toilette, grooming
(2.5.729) These ten are used in all three genders; <s>alaṃkartṛ</s> — one who adorns; <s>alaṃkariṣṇu</s> — fond of adorning; <s>maṇḍita</s> — adorned
(2.5.730) <s>Prasādhita</s>, <s>alaṃkṛta</s>, <s>bhūṣita</s>, <s>pariṣkṛta</s> — adorned, decorated, embellished; synonyms
(2.5.731) <s>Vibhrāj</s>, <s>bhrājiṣṇu</s>, <s>rociṣṇu</s> — shining, resplendent; <s>bhūṣaṇa</s> — adornment; <s>alaṃkriyā</s> — the act of ornamentation
(2.5.732) <s>Alaṃkāra</s>, <s>ābharaṇa</s>, <s>pariṣkāra</s>, <s>vibhūṣaṇa</s> — ornament, jewellery, decoration; synonyms
(2.5.733) <s>Maṇḍana</s> — adornment; also; <s>mukuṭa</s>, <s>kirīṭa</s> — a crown, diadem; masculine and neuter
(2.5.734) <s>Cūḍāmaṇi</s> — a crest-jewel, head ornament; <s>śiroratna</s> — a head-gem; <s>tarala</s> — the central gem in a necklace
(2.5.735) <s>Vālapāśyā</s> — a hair-ribbon; <s>pāritathyā</s> — a headband; <s>patrapāśyā</s> — a leaf-ornament; <s>lalāṭikā</s> — a forehead ornament

children.text: (2.5.746) strīkaṭyāṃ mekhalā kāñcī saptakī raśanā tathā
(2.5.747) klībe sārasanaṃ cātha puṃskaṭyāṃ śṛṅkhalaṃ triṣu
(2.5.751) vālkaṃ kṣaumādi phālaṃ tu kārpāsaṃ bādaraṃ ca tat
(2.5.756) kṣaumaṃ dukūlaṃ syāddve tu nivītaṃ prāvṛtaṃ triṣu
(2.5.773) snānaṃ carcā tu cārcikyaṃ sthāsako 'tha prabodhanam
(2.5.776) dvitīyaṃ ca turīyaṃ ca na striyāmatha kuṅkumam
(2.5.779) lākṣā rākṣā jatu klībe yāvo 'lakto drumāmayaḥ
(2.5.797) mālyaṃ mālāsrajau mūrdhni keśamadhye tu garbhakaḥ
(2.5.807) darpaṇe mukurādarśau vyajanaṃ tālavṛntakam | iti manuṣyavargaḥ
(2.6.817) dhīro manīṣī jñaḥ prājñaḥ saṃkhyāvānpaṇḍitaḥ kaviḥ
(2.6.826) yaṣṭā ca yajamānaśca sa somavati dīkṣitaḥ
(2.6.828) sa gīrpatīṣṭayā sthapatiḥ somapīthī tu somapāḥ
(2.6.856) āmikṣā sā śṛtoṣṇe yā kṣīre syāddadhiyogataḥ
(2.6.860) dhruvopabhṛjjuhūrnā tu sruvo bhedāḥ srucaḥ striyaḥ
(2.6.864) sāṃnāyyaṃ haviragnau tu hutaṃ triṣu vaṣaṭ kṛtam
(2.6.866) triṣvatha kratukarmeṣṭaṃ pūrtaṃ khātādi karma yat

children.translated_text: (2.6.884) <s>Prācetasa</s> and <s>Ādikavi</s> (the first poet) [are synonyms for <s>Vālmīki</s>]; he is also called <s>Maitrāvaruṇi</s> (son of <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>),
(2.6.885) and <s>Vālmīka</s>; then <s>Gādheya</s> (son of <s>Gādhi</s>) [means] <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, also called <s>Kauśika</s>,
(2.6.886) <s>Vyāsa</s> [is also called] <s>Dvaipāyana</s>, <s>Pārāśarya</s> (son of <s>Parāśara</s>), and <s>Satyavatīsuta</s> (son of <s>Satyavatī</s>),
(2.6.887) <s>Ānupūrvī</s> (feminine) [means] orderly sequence; <s>āvṛt</s>, <s>paripāṭhī</s>, and <s>anukrama</s> [are synonyms],
(2.6.888) <s>paryāya</s> is also [a synonym]; <s>atipāta</s> means omission; <s>paryaya</s> and <s>upātyaya</s> [are its synonyms],
(2.6.889) <s>Niyama</s> (observance) and <s>vrata</s> (vow) [are synonyms], not feminine; <s>puṇyaka</s> [refers to meritorious acts] such as <s>upavāsa</s> (fasting) and the like,
(2.6.890) <s>aupavasta</s> means fasting (<s>upavāsa</s>); <s>viveka</s> [means] discrimination, the state of being separate (<s>pṛthagātmatā</s>),
(2.6.891) <s>brahmavarcasa</s> means the splendor arising from study and religious observance; then <s>añjali</s> [means the joined palms],
(2.6.892) in recitation [it is called] <s>brahmāñjali</s>; in recitation, the drops [of saliva from chanting] are called <s>brahmabindus</s>,
(2.6.893) in meditation, yoga posture [is called] <s>brahmāsana</s>; in ritual procedure (<s>kalpa</s>), <s>vidhi</s> and <s>krama</s> [are synonyms for prescribed method],
(2.6.894) the primary [prescribed rule] is called <s>kalpa</s>; <s>anukalpa</s> is the secondary, inferior alternative,
(2.6.895) the formal initiation of Vedic study preceded by <s>saṃskāra</s> (purificatory rites) is called <s>upākaraṇa</s>,
(2.6.896) <s>pādagrahaṇa</s> (grasping the feet) and <s>abhivādana</s> (respectful salutation) are synonyms [used when greeting] an equal,
(2.6.897) <s>bhikṣu</s> (mendicant), <s>parivrāṭ</s> (wandering ascetic), <s>karmandī</s>, <s>pārāśarya</s>, and <s>maskarī</s> [are synonyms for a renunciant],

(2.6.898) <s>tapasvī</s> (practitioner of austerities) and <s>tāpasa</s> [are synonyms]; <s>pārikāṅkṣī</s> (one who awaits), <s>vācaṃyama</s> (one who controls speech) and <s>muni</s> (sage) [are synonyms],
(2.6.899) one who endures the hardship of austerities is called <s>dānta</s> (self-restrained); <s>varṇin</s> and <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student) [are synonyms],

(2.6.900) <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer) and <s>satyavacas</s> (truth-speaker) [are synonyms]; <s>snātaka</s> (one who has completed Vedic study) and <s>āpluta</s> (one who has bathed) and <s>vratin</s> (observer of vows) [are synonyms],
(2.6.901) those who have conquered the aggregate of senses are called <s>yatins</s> and <s>yatayas</s> (ascetics),
(2.6.902) one who by the force of his vow sleeps on the bare ground is called <s>sthaṇḍilaśāyyin</s> (one who sleeps on open ground),
(2.6.903) also <s>sthāṇḍila</s>; then <s>viraja</s> and <s>tamasa</s> [mean] those who have transcended both [<s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>],

(2.6.904) <s>pavitra</s> (pure), <s>prayata</s> (ritually prepared), and <s>pūta</s> (purified) [are synonyms]; <s>pāṣaṇḍas</s> [are] those who wear all [kinds of religious] marks (<s>sarvaliṅgin</s>),

children.text: (2.6.905) pālāśo daṇḍa āṣāḍho vrate rāmbhastu vaiṇavaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.6.905) a staff made of <s>palāśa</s> (Butea frondosa) [is used in certain vows]; <s>āṣāḍha</s> [is a staff used] in [another] vow; <s>rāmbha</s> [is one made] of bamboo (<s>vaiṇava</s>),
(2.6.906) <s>kamaṇḍalu</s> (water-pot, not feminine) and <s>kuṇḍī</s> [are synonyms]; the seat of ascetics is called <s>bṛṣī</s> (a cushion of grass),

children.text: (2.6.907) ajinaṃ carma kṛttiḥ strī bhaikṣaṃ bhikṣākadambakam
children.translated_text: (2.6.907) <s>ajina</s> (skin), <s>carma</s> (hide), and <s>kṛtti</s> (feminine, skin) [are synonyms]; <s>bhaikṣa</s> [means] a collection of alms (<s>bhikṣākadambaka</s>),

children.text: (2.6.908) svādhyāyaḥ syājjapaḥ sutyābhiṣavaḥ savanaṃ ca sā
children.translated_text: (2.6.908) <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study) means <s>japa</s> (recitation); <s>sutya</s>, <s>abhiṣava</s>, and <s>savana</s> (pressing of Soma) [are synonyms], and that [<s>sutya</s>] is feminine,
(2.6.909) that which destroys all sins, to be recited, is called <s>aghamarṣaṇa</s> [and is used] in all three [genders],
(2.6.910) <s>darśa</s> (new-moon sacrifice) and <s>paurṇamāsa</s> (full-moon sacrifice) are the two sacrifices performed separately at the end of each fortnight,
(2.6.911) that obligatory action which requires bodily means [for its performance] is called <s>yama</s> (restraint),
(2.6.912) <s>niyama</s> (observance) is that obligatory action which requires an external means [for its accomplishment],
