children.text: (2.6.913) kṣauram tu bhadrākaraṇaṃ muṇḍanaṃ vapanaṃ triṣu
children.translated_text: (2.6.913) <s>kṣaura</s> means tonsure; <s>bhadrākaraṇa</s>, <s>muṇḍana</s>, and <s>vapana</s> [are synonyms, used] in all three [genders],

children.text: (2.6.914) kakṣāpaṭī ca kaupīnaṃ śāṭī ca strīti lakṣyataḥ
children.translated_text: (2.6.914) <s>kakṣāpaṭī</s> and <s>kaupīna</s> (loincloth) [are synonyms]; <s>śāṭī</s> [is a garment], marked as feminine,
(2.6.915) <s>upavīta</s> (sacred thread) and <s>brahmasūtra</s> [are synonyms]; when the right hand is raised [the thread is worn in the normal manner],
(2.6.916) <s>prācīnāvīta</s> [is when the thread is worn] on the other [left shoulder]; <s>nivīta</s> is [when it is] hanging around the neck,
(2.6.917) at the tips of the fingers is the <s>daiva-tīrtha</s> (sacred part for gods); at the base of the little fingers is the <s>kāya-tīrtha</s> (sacred part for beings),
(2.6.918) between the thumb and [fore]finger is the <s>pitrya-tīrtha</s> (sacred part for ancestors); at the base of the thumb is the <s>brāhma-tīrtha</s> (sacred part for <s>Brahmā</s>),
(2.6.919) <s>brahmabhūya</s>, <s>brahmatva</s>, and <s>brahmasāyujya</s> (union with <s>Brahman</s>) [are synonyms],
(2.6.920) <s>devabhūya</s> and similar [forms mean identity with a deity]; <s>kṛcchra</s> [includes penances] such as <s>sāntapana</s> and the like,

(2.6.921) <s>saṃnyāsa</s> [means renunciation]; in [the context of] fasting unto death, [it is] masculine; <s>prāya</s> [is its synonym]; then <s>vīrahā</s> [means one who kills a hero, i.e., one who commits suicide by fasting],
(2.6.922) one whose sacred fire has been extinguished is called <s>naṣṭāgni</s>; <s>kuhanā</s> [means] the feigning of a false mode of life out of greed,
(2.6.923) <s>vrātya</s> is one devoid of <s>saṃskāras</s> (purificatory rites); <s>asvādhyāya</s> [means one who does not study]; <s>nirākṛti</s> [means one who is rejected],

(2.6.924) <s>dharmadhvajin</s> (one who makes a show of virtue) and <s>liṅgavṛttin</s> (one who lives by religious marks) [are synonyms]; <s>avakīrṇin</s> [means] one who has violated his vow (<s>kṣatavrata</s>),
(2.6.925) one in whose sleep [the sun] sets, [and] one in whose sleep [the sun] rises,
(2.6.926) are called respectively <s>aṃśumān</s>, <s>abhiniṣmukta</s>, and <s>abhyudita</s>,
(2.6.927) <s>parivettar</s> (one who marries before the elder brother) is the younger brother who marries while the elder remains unwed,
(2.6.928) <s>parivitti</s> is that [elder brother whose younger brother marries first]; <s>vivāha</s> and <s>upayama</s> [are synonyms for marriage],
(2.6.929) likewise <s>pariṇaya</s>, <s>udvāha</s>, <s>upayāma</s>, and <s>pāṇipīḍana</s> (clasping of hands) [are synonyms for marriage],
(2.6.930) <s>vyavāya</s>, <s>grāmyadharma</s>, <s>maithuna</s>, <s>nidhuvana</s>, and <s>rata</s> [are synonyms for sexual union],
(2.6.931) the three aims (<s>trivarga</s>) are <s>dharma</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>artha</s>; the four aims (<s>caturvarga</s>) include <s>mokṣa</s> as well,

children.text: (2.6.932) sabalaistaiścaturbhadraṃ janyāḥ snigdhāḥ varasya ye | iti brahmavargaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.6.932) together with their supports, the four constitute <s>caturbhadra</s> (the four blessings); the affectionate kinsmen of the bridegroom are called <s>janya</s>. Thus ends the <s>Brahmavarga</s> (section on Brahmins).

children.text: (2.7.933) mūrdhābhiṣikto rājanyo bāhujaḥ kṣatriyo virāṭ | atha kṣatriyavargaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.7.933) One anointed on the head is called <s>rājanya</s> (royal), <s>bāhuja</s> (arm-born), <s>kṣatriya</s> (warrior), and <s>virāṭ</s>. Now begins the <s>Kṣatriyavarga</s> (section on warriors).
(2.7.934) <s>rājā</s> (king), <s>rāṭ</s>, <s>pārthiva</s>, <s>kṣmābhṛt</s> (earth-bearer), <s>nṛpa</s>, <s>bhūpa</s> (protector of the earth), and <s>mahīkṣit</s> (lord of the earth) [are synonyms],
(2.7.935) a king before whom all neighboring rulers bow is called <s>adhīśvara</s> (overlord),

(2.7.936) <s>cakravartin</s> (universal sovereign) and <s>sārvabhauma</s> (lord of the whole earth) [are synonyms]; another king [ruling a smaller territory] is <s>maṇḍaleśvara</s> (lord of a province),
(2.7.937) one who has performed the <s>Rājasūya</s> sacrifice and who is lord of a circle [of vassal kings],

children.text: (2.7.938) śāsti yaścājñayā rājñaḥ sa samrāḍatha rājakam
children.translated_text: (2.7.938) and who rules by the command of the [supreme] king — he is called <s>samrāṭ</s> (emperor); then <s>rājaka</s> [means a petty king],
(2.7.939) <s>rājanyaka</s> [also means a petty king]; in the context of groups of kings and <s>kṣatriyas</s>, [these terms are used] respectively,
(2.7.940) <s>mantrin</s> (counselor), <s>dhīsaciva</s> (wise minister), and <s>amātya</s> (minister) [are synonyms]; others are <s>karmasacivas</s> (executive ministers),
(2.7.941) <s>mahāmātras</s> [mean] chief officials; <s>purodhā</s> and <s>purohita</s> (royal chaplain) [are synonyms],
(2.7.942) for the judge of legal disputes, <s>prāḍvivāka</s> and <s>akṣadarśaka</s> [are synonyms],
(2.7.943) <s>pratīhāra</s> (chamberlain), <s>dvārapāla</s>, <s>dvāstha</s>, and <s>dvāsthitadarśaka</s> [are synonyms for doorkeeper],
(2.7.944) <s>rakṣivarga</s> (the guard corps) [includes] <s>anīkastha</s> (one stationed in the army); <s>adhyakṣa</s> (superintendent) and <s>adhikṛta</s> (officer) are synonyms,
(2.7.945) <s>sthāyuka</s> [means] an officer appointed over a village; <s>gopa</s> [is an officer] over many villages,
(2.7.946) <s>bhaurika</s> [means] superintendent of gold; <s>rūpyādhyakṣa</s> (superintendent of silver) is also called <s>naiṣkika</s>,
(2.7.947) the person appointed over the inner apartments (<s>antaḥpura</s>) is called <s>antarvaṃśika</s>,
(2.7.948) <s>sauvidallas</s>, <s>kañcukins</s> (armored attendants), <s>sthāpatyas</s>, and <s>sauvidas</s> — these [are synonyms for chamberlains],
(2.7.949) <s>śaṇḍha</s> (eunuch) and <s>varṣavara</s> are synonyms; <s>sevaka</s> (servant), <s>arthī</s> (supplicant), and <s>anujīvin</s> (dependent) [are synonyms],
(2.7.950) the king whose territory is adjacent is the enemy (<s>śatru</s>); beyond that is the friend (<s>mitra</s>),
(2.7.951) the <s>udāsīna</s> (neutral king) is farther away; the <s>pārṣṇigrāha</s> (rearward enemy) is behind,
(2.7.952) for an enemy: <s>vairin</s>, <s>sapatna</s>, <s>ari</s>, <s>dviṣat</s>, <s>dveṣaṇa</s>, and <s>durhṛd</s> [are synonyms],
(2.7.953) <s>dviṭ</s>, <s>vipakṣa</s>, <s>ahita</s>, <s>amitra</s>, <s>dasyu</s>, <s>śātrava</s>, and <s>śatru</s> [are further synonyms],
(2.7.954) <s>abhighātin</s>, <s>parārāti</s>, <s>pratyarthin</s>, and <s>paripanthin</s> [are also synonyms for enemy],

children.text: (2.7.955) vayasyaḥ snigdhaḥ savayā atha mitraṃ sakhā suhṛt
children.translated_text: (2.7.955) <s>vayasya</s> (companion), <s>snigdha</s> (affectionate one), and <s>savayā</s> (one of the same age) [are synonyms]; then <s>mitra</s> (friend), <s>sakhā</s>, and <s>suhṛt</s> [are synonyms],
(2.7.956) <s>sakhya</s> (friendship) [is defined as] that arising from [taking] seven steps together (<s>sāptapadīna</s>); <s>anurodha</s> [means] compliance (<s>anuvartana</s>),
(2.7.957) <s>praṇidhi</s> (spy), disguised according to his appropriate class, [is also called] <s>apasarpa</s>, <s>cara</s>, and <s>spaśa</s>,
(2.7.958) also <s>cāra</s> and <s>gūḍhapuruṣa</s> (secret agent); <s>āpta</s> (trusted one) and <s>pratyayita</s> (reliable one) are synonyms,
(2.7.959) <s>sāṃvatsara</s> (astrologer), <s>jyautiṣika</s> (astronomer), <s>daivajña</s> (diviner), and <s>gaṇaka</s> (calculator) [are synonyms],
(2.7.960) also <s>mauhūrtika</s>, <s>mauhūrtajñānin</s> (one who knows auspicious moments), and <s>kārtāntika</s> [are synonyms],
(2.7.961) <s>tāntrika</s> [means] one who knows established doctrines; <s>satrin</s> (one who performs a <s>sattra</s> sacrifice) and <s>gṛhapati</s> (householder) are synonyms,
(2.7.962) <s>lipikāra</s> (scribe), <s>akṣaracañcu</s> (skilled in letters), and <s>akṣaracuñcu</s> [are synonyms for] a writer,
(2.7.963) the arrangement of written letters is called <s>lipi</s> or <s>libhi</s>, both feminine,
(2.7.964) a carrier of messages is called <s>dūta</s> (messenger); <s>dūtya</s> [refers to] the state and act of being a messenger,
(2.7.965) <s>adhvanīna</s>, <s>adhvaga</s>, <s>adhvanya</s>, <s>pāntha</s>, and <s>pathika</s> [are synonyms for] a traveler,
(2.7.966) the lord (<s>svāmin</s>), minister (<s>amātya</s>), ally (<s>suhṛt</s>), treasury (<s>kośa</s>), territory (<s>rāṣṭra</s>), fort (<s>durga</s>), and army (<s>bala</s>),
(2.7.967) are the constituents of a kingdom (<s>rājyāṅgas</s>) [also called] <s>prakṛtis</s>; the guilds (<s>śreṇīs</s>) of the citizens [are also recognized],
(2.7.968) <s>sandhi</s> (alliance), <s>vigraha</s> (war), <s>yāna</s> (marching), <s>āsana</s> (encamping), <s>dvaida</s> (double policy), and <s>āśraya</s> (seeking refuge),
(2.7.969) [these are] the six strategies (<s>ṣaḍguṇas</s>); the three powers (<s>śaktis</s>) arise from authority (<s>prabhāva</s>), energy (<s>utsāha</s>), and counsel (<s>mantra</s>),

children.text: (2.7.970) kṣayaḥ sthānaṃ ca vṛddhiśca trivargo nītivedinām
children.translated_text: (2.7.970) decline (<s>kṣaya</s>), stability (<s>sthāna</s>), and prosperity (<s>vṛddhi</s>) are the three conditions (<s>trivarga</s>) known to those versed in statecraft,
(2.7.971) that glory (<s>pratāpa</s>) and might (<s>prabhāva</s>) which constitutes power (<s>tejas</s>) arises from treasury and military force,
(2.7.972) <s>bheda</s> (dissension), <s>daṇḍa</s> (punishment), <s>sāma</s> (conciliation), and <s>dāna</s> (gift) — these are the four means of statecraft (<s>upāyacatuṣṭaya</s>),

children.text: (2.7.973) sāhasaṃ tu samo (damo) daṇḍaḥ sāma sāntvamatho samau
children.translated_text: (2.7.973) <s>sāhasa</s> [means] forceful punishment (<s>daṇḍa</s>); <s>sāma</s> and <s>sāntva</s> (gentle persuasion) are synonyms,
(2.7.974) <s>bheda</s> and <s>upajāpa</s> (secret instigation) [are synonyms]; <s>upadhā</s> [means] testing [of ministers] by means of <s>dharma</s> and other [criteria],
(2.7.975) [a king who is] diminished, not fully possessed of the five [elements], who is within the range of the third [degree of power],
(2.7.976) <s>vivikta</s> (secluded), <s>vijana</s> (unpeopled), <s>channa</s> (concealed), and <s>niḥśalāka</s> (without a pass) [are synonyms]; likewise <s>rahas</s> (secrecy),
(2.7.977) <s>rahas</s> and <s>upāṃśu</s> (whispered) [are synonyms] when not [used as] a gender marker; <s>rahasya</s> (secret) [is the adjective used] in all three genders,
(2.7.978) <s>visrambha</s> (confidence) and <s>viśvāsa</s> (trust) are synonyms; <s>bhreṣa</s> and <s>bhraṃśa</s> [mean] falling away from what is proper,
(2.7.979) <s>abhreṣa</s>, <s>nyāya</s>, and <s>kalpa</s> [are synonyms for propriety]; <s>deśarūpa</s> and <s>samañjasa</s> (fitting) [are synonyms],
(2.7.980) <s>yukta</s> (appropriate), <s>aupayika</s> (expedient), <s>labhya</s> (attainable), <s>bhajamāna</s>, and <s>abhinītavat</s> [are synonyms for what is proper],

children.text: (2.7.981) nyāyyaṃ ca triṣu ṣaṭ saṃpradhāraṇā tu samarthanam
children.translated_text: (2.7.981) also <s>nyāyya</s> [means proper], in all three genders; <s>saṃpradhāraṇā</s> means deliberation (<s>samarthana</s>),

children.text: (2.7.982) avavādastu nirdeśo nideśaḥ śāsanaṃ ca saḥ
children.translated_text: (2.7.982) <s>avavāda</s> means instruction (<s>nirdeśa</s>); <s>nideśa</s> and <s>śāsana</s> (command) are its synonyms,

children.text: (2.7.983) śiṣṭiścājñā ca saṃsthā tu maryādā dhāraṇā sthitiḥ
children.translated_text: (2.7.983) also <s>śiṣṭi</s> and <s>ājñā</s> (command); <s>saṃsthā</s> means regulation; <s>maryādā</s> (boundary), <s>dhāraṇā</s> (maintenance), and <s>sthiti</s> (stability) [are synonyms],
(2.7.984) <s>sudharaṇā</s> and <s>sudhārā</s> (feminine), <s>susthiti</s> (good order), <s>sudaśā</s> (good condition), and <s>unnati</s> (prosperity) [are synonyms],
(2.7.985) <s>āgas</s> (offense), <s>aparādha</s> (crime), and <s>mantu</s> [are synonyms]; <s>uddāna</s> (confinement) and <s>bandhana</s> (imprisonment) are synonyms,

children.text: (2.7.986) dvipādyo dviguṇo daṇḍo bhāgadheyaḥ karo baliḥ
children.translated_text: (2.7.986) a fine doubled is called <s>dviguṇa-daṇḍa</s>; <s>bhāgadheya</s> (share), <s>kara</s> (tax), and <s>bali</s> (tribute) [are synonyms for tax],
(2.7.987) a toll payable at ferries and the like is called <s>śulka</s> (not feminine); <s>prābhṛta</s> means a present (<s>pradeśana</s>),
(2.7.988) <s>upāyana</s> (gift), <s>upagrāhya</s>, <s>upahāra</s> (offering), and <s>upadā</s> [are synonyms],

children.text: (2.7.989) yautakādi tu yaddeyaṃ sudāyo haraṇaṃ ca tat
children.translated_text: (2.7.989) <s>yautaka</s> and the like [refer to] what is given [at marriage]; <s>sudāya</s> and <s>haraṇa</s> (taking) are also [synonyms],
(2.7.990) <s>tatkāla</s> (that time) means the present moment (<s>tadātva</s>); the future time is called <s>āyati</s>,
(2.7.991) <s>sāndṛṣṭika</s> [means] an immediately visible result; <s>udarka</s> [means] a future result,
(2.7.992) <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen [danger]) [arises from] fire, water, and the like; <s>dṛṣṭa</s> (seen [danger]) arises from one's own or the enemy's forces,
(2.7.993) for kings, a great fear is that which arises from their own faction,
(2.7.994) <s>prakriyā</s> means authority (<s>adhikāra</s>); <s>cāmara</s> (yak-tail fan) [is also called] <s>prakīrṇaka</s>,
(2.7.995) the royal seat is called <s>bhadrāsana</s> (auspicious throne) and <s>siṃhāsana</s> (lion-throne),

children.text: (2.7.996) haimaṃ chatraṃ tvātapatraṃ rājñastu nṛpalakṣma tat
children.translated_text: (2.7.996) a golden umbrella is called <s>ātapatra</s> (sunshade); for a king it is the royal insignia (<s>nṛpalakṣman</s>),
(2.7.997) <s>bhadrakumbha</s> (auspicious pot) and <s>pūrṇakumbha</s> (full pot) [are synonyms]; <s>bhṛṅgāra</s> (golden pitcher) [is also called] <s>kanakālukā</s>,
(2.7.998) <s>niveśa</s> and <s>śibira</s> (camp) [are synonyms, neuter]; <s>sajjana</s> means protection (<s>uparakṣaṇa</s>),
(2.7.999) elephants, horses, chariots, and foot-soldiers are the four limbs of an army (<s>senāṅga</s>),
(2.7.1000) <s>dantin</s> (tusked one), <s>dantāvala</s>, <s>hastin</s> (one with a trunk), <s>dvirada</s> (two-tusked), <s>anekapa</s> (much-drinking), and <s>dvipa</s> [are synonyms for elephant],

children.text: (2.7.1001) mataṅgajo gajo nāgaḥ kuñjaro vāraṇaḥ karī
children.translated_text: (2.7.1001) <s>mataṅgaja</s>, <s>gaja</s>, <s>nāga</s>, <s>kuñjara</s>, <s>vāraṇa</s>, and <s>karin</s> [are further synonyms for elephant],
(2.7.1002) <s>ibha</s>, <s>stamberabha</s>, and <s>padmin</s> [are also synonyms]; the leader of a herd is called <s>yūthapa</s> (herd-lord),
(2.7.1003) <s>madotkaṭa</s> (wild with rut) and <s>madakala</s> (intoxicated with rut) [describe a rutting elephant]; <s>kalabha</s> [means] a young elephant (<s>kariśāvaka</s>),

(2.7.1004) <s>prabhinna</s> (with temples split open), <s>garjita</s> (trumpeting), and <s>matta</s> (intoxicated) [describe an elephant in rut]; <s>udvānta</s> and <s>nirmada</s> [describe one whose rut has subsided],

children.text: (2.7.1005) hāstikaṃ gajatā vṛnde kariṇī dhenukā vaśā
children.translated_text: (2.7.1005) <s>hāstika</s> [means] the state of being an elephant; in a herd, [a female elephant is called] <s>kariṇī</s>, <s>dhenukā</s>, and <s>vaśā</s>,

children.text: (2.7.1006) gaṇḍaḥ kaṭo mado dānaṃ vamathuḥ karaśīkaraḥ
children.translated_text: (2.7.1006) <s>gaṇḍa</s> (temple), <s>kaṭa</s> [are parts of the elephant's head]; <s>mada</s> and <s>dāna</s> [mean] the rut-fluid; <s>vamathu</s> and <s>karaśīkara</s> [mean] the spray from the trunk,

children.text: (2.7.1007) kumbhau tu piṇḍau śirasastayormadhye viduḥ pumān
children.translated_text: (2.7.1007) the <s>kumbhas</s> (frontal globes) are the two protuberances on the head; the space between them is known as masculine,
(2.7.1008) <s>avagraha</s> [means] the forehead; <s>īṣikā</s> means the ridge above the eye (<s>akṣikūṭaka</s>),
(2.7.1009) the outer corner region is called <s>niryāṇa</s>; the base of the ear is called <s>cūlikā</s>,
(2.7.1010) below the frontal globe is <s>vāhittham</s>; <s>pratimāna</s> is [the part] below that,
(2.7.1011) <s>āsana</s> [means] the region of the shoulders; <s>padmaka</s> and <s>bindujālaka</s> [refer to the spotted markings on the elephant],
(2.7.1012) <s>pārśvabhāga</s> and <s>pakṣabhāga</s> [mean] the flank; <s>dantabhāga</s> is the part in front,
(2.7.1013) the two [regions] before and behind, starting from the legs, are called <s>gātra</s> and <s>avara</s> respectively,
(2.7.1014) <s>totra</s> (goad), <s>veṇuka</s> [are implements]; <s>ālāna</s> [means] a tethering post; in chains,
(2.7.1015) <s>anduka</s> and <s>nigaḍa</s> (fetter, not feminine) [are synonyms]; <s>aṅkuśa</s> (elephant goad, not feminine) [is also called] <s>sṛṇi</s> (feminine),

children.text: (2.7.1016) dūṣyā (cūṣā) kakṣyā varatrā syātkalpanā sajjanā same
children.translated_text: (2.7.1016) <s>dūṣyā</s> (<s>cūṣā</s>), <s>kakṣyā</s> (girth-strap), and <s>varatrā</s> [are synonyms]; <s>kalpanā</s> and <s>sajjanā</s> (harnessing) are synonyms,
(2.7.1017) <s>praveṇī</s> [means] the covering cloth; <s>varṇa</s> and <s>paristoma</s> [are coverings]; <s>kutha</s> [is used] in both [genders],

children.text: (2.7.1018) vītaṃ tvasāraṃ hastyaśvaṃ vārī tu gajabandhanī
children.translated_text: (2.7.1018) <s>vīta</s> means a worthless elephant or horse; <s>vārī</s> is a female elephant's tethering rope,
(2.7.1019) for a horse: <s>ghoṭaka</s>, <s>vīti</s> (<s>pīti</s>), <s>turaga</s>, <s>turaṅga</s>, <s>aśva</s>, and <s>turaṅgama</s> [are synonyms],
(2.7.1020) <s>vājin</s>, <s>vāha</s>, <s>arvan</s>, <s>gandharva</s>, <s>haya</s>, <s>saindhava</s>, and <s>sapti</s> [are further synonyms for horse],
(2.7.1021) <s>ājāneya</s> (well-born) and <s>kulīna</s> (of noble breed) [are synonyms]; <s>vinīta</s> (well-trained) and <s>sādhuvāhin</s> (good carrier) [are synonyms],
(2.7.1022) <s>vanāyuja</s> [horses are] from forests; <s>pārasīka</s> [horses are] from Persia; <s>kāmboja</s> and <s>bāhlika</s> [horses are named after their lands of origin],
(2.7.1023) <s>yayu</s> [is a name for] a horse; <s>aśvamedhīya</s> [means] fit for the horse-sacrifice; <s>javana</s> [means] one surpassing in speed,

children.text: (2.7.1024) pṛṣṭhyaḥ sthaurī sitaḥ karko rathyo voḍhā rathasya yaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.7.1024) <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> (a riding horse), <s>sthaurin</s>, <s>sita</s>, and <s>karka</s> [are synonyms]; <s>rathya</s> [means] one who draws a chariot (<s>voḍhā rathasya</s>),

children.text: (2.7.1025) bālaḥ kiśoro vāmyaśvā vaḍavā vāḍavaṃ gaṇe
children.translated_text: (2.7.1025) <s>bāla</s> (young) and <s>kiśora</s> (colt) [are synonyms]; <s>vāmī</s> [means] a female horse; <s>vaḍavā</s> (mare) [is also used]; <s>vāḍava</s> [refers to] a herd [of horses],
(2.7.1026) <s>āśvīna</s> (in all three genders) [means] the distance covered by a horse in a single day,

children.text: (2.7.1027) kaśyaṃ tu madhyamaśvānāṃ heṣā hreṣā ca nisvanaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.7.1027) <s>kaśya</s> [pertains to] middling horses; <s>heṣā</s> and <s>hreṣā</s> [mean] neighing, [which is] their sound,
(2.7.1028) <s>nigāla</s> [means] the region of the throat; in a group [the collective term is] <s>aśvīya</s>, like <s>āśvavat</s>
(2.7.1029) <s>Āskanditam</s> (galloping), <s>dhauritakam</s> (trotting), <s>recitam</s> (ambling), <s>valgitam</s> (cantering), and <s>plutam</s> (leaping)

children.text: (2.7.1030) gatayo 'mūḥ pañca dhārā ghoṇā tu prothamastriyām
children.translated_text: (2.7.1030) — these are the five gaits. <s>Dhārā</s> and <s>ghoṇā</s> mean the nostril of a horse; <s>protha</s> is not feminine.

children.text: (2.7.1031) kavikā tu khalīno 'strī śaphaṃ klībe khuraḥ pumān
children.translated_text: (2.7.1031) <s>Kavikā</s> means the bit; <s>khalīna</s> (bit) is not feminine. <s>Śapha</s> (hoof) is neuter; <s>khura</s> (hoof) is masculine.
(2.7.1032) <s>Puccha</s> (tail) is not feminine; <s>lūma</s> and <s>lāṅgūla</s> (tail) are synonyms. <s>Vālahasta</s> and <s>vāladhi</s> also mean tail.
(2.7.1033) In all three genders: <s>upāvṛtta</s> and <s>luṭhita</s> (rolling on the ground) refer to rolling repeatedly on the ground.

children.text: (2.7.1034) yāne cakriṇi yuddhārthe śatāṅgaḥ syandano rathaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.7.1034) A wheeled vehicle used for battle: <s>śatāṅga</s>, <s>syandana</s>, and <s>ratha</s> (chariot) are synonyms.
(2.7.1035) That is called <s>puṣparatha</s> (pleasure chariot) — a wheeled vehicle not intended for battle.

children.text: (2.7.1036) karṇīrathaḥ pravahaṇaṃ ḍayanaṃ ca samaṃ trayam
children.translated_text: (2.7.1036) <s>Karṇīratha</s> (cart), <s>pravahaṇa</s> (transport vehicle), and <s>ḍayana</s> — these three are synonymous.
(2.7.1037) <s>Anas</s> (cart) is neuter; <s>śakaṭa</s> (cart) is not feminine. <s>Gantrī</s> and <s>kambalivāhyaka</s> (blanket-covered conveyance) are synonyms.
(2.7.1038) <s>Śibikā</s> (palanquin) is a carried conveyance. <s>Dolā</s> (swing) and <s>preṅkhā</s> and the like are feminine.
(2.7.1039) Both <s>dvaipa</s> and <s>vaiyāghra</s> refer to a chariot covered with leopard skin.
(2.7.1040) A chariot covered with a white blanket is called <s>pāṇḍukambalī</s>.
(2.7.1041) For a chariot covered with blankets and the like, terms such as <s>kāmbala</s> and <s>vāstra</s> are used.
(2.7.1042) In all three genders, <s>dvaipa</s> and the like; <s>rathyā</s> (road for chariots) is used for a chariot route; <s>rathakaḍyā</s> for a chariot track.
(2.7.1043) <s>Dhūḥ</s> (chariot pole) is feminine or neuter; <s>yānamukha</s> (front of the vehicle) is also used. <s>Rathāṅga</s> (chariot part) and <s>apaskara</s> (chariot accessory) are synonyms.

children.text: (2.7.1044) cakraṃ rathāṅgaṃ tasyānte nemiḥ strī syātpradhiḥ pumān
children.translated_text: (2.7.1044) <s>Cakra</s> (wheel) and <s>rathāṅga</s> are synonyms. At its rim, <s>nemi</s> (felly) is feminine; <s>pradhi</s> (rim) is masculine.
(2.7.1045) <s>Piṇḍikā</s> (nave) and <s>nābhi</s> (hub) are synonyms. For the axle-pin at the end of the axle, both terms <s>aṇi</s> are used.
(2.7.1046) <s>Rathagupti</s> (chariot guard) and <s>varūtha</s> (fender) are not feminine. <s>Kūbara</s> (chariot pole) and <s>yugandhara</s> (yoke-bearer) are synonyms.
(2.7.1047) <s>Anukarṣī</s> (rear axle): the wooden piece below. <s>Prāsaṅga</s> is not feminine. <s>Yuga</s> (yoke) and the like — <s>yuga</s> is also used.

children.text: (2.7.1048) sarvaṃ syādvāhanaṃ yānaṃ yugyaṃ patraṃ ca dhoraṇam
children.translated_text: (2.7.1048) <s>Vāhana</s> (mount), <s>yāna</s> (vehicle), <s>yugya</s> (yoked animal), <s>patra</s> (conveyance), and <s>dhoraṇa</s> (riding animal) all mean a vehicle or mount.
(2.7.1049) A relay of vehicles is called <s>vainītaka</s>; it is not feminine.
(2.7.1050) <s>Ādhoraṇa</s> (elephant rider), <s>hastipaka</s> (elephant keeper), <s>hastyāroha</s> (elephant rider), and <s>niṣādin</s> (mounted warrior) are synonyms.

children.text: (2.7.1051) niyantā prājitā yantā sūtaḥ kṣattā ca sārathiḥ
children.translated_text: (2.7.1051) <s>Niyantā</s> (driver), <s>prājitā</s> (charioteer), <s>yantā</s> (controller), <s>sūta</s> (charioteer), <s>kṣattā</s> (driver), and <s>sārathi</s> (charioteer) are synonyms.
(2.7.1052) <s>Savyeṣṭha</s> (one who stands on the left) and <s>dakṣiṇastha</s> (one who stands on the right) — these are designations for chariot attendants.
(2.7.1053) <s>Rathin</s> (chariot warrior) and <s>syandanāroha</s> (chariot rider) are synonyms. <s>Aśvāroha</s> (horseman) and <s>sādin</s> (cavalryman) are synonyms.
(2.7.1054) <s>Bhaṭa</s> (soldier), <s>yodha</s> (warrior), and <s>yoddhā</s> (fighter) are synonyms. Those who guard the army are <s>sainika</s> (soldiers).

children.text: (2.7.1055) senāyāṃ samavetā ye sainyāste sainikāśca te
children.translated_text: (2.7.1055) Those who are assembled in the army are called <s>sainya</s> (troops), and they are also <s>sainika</s> (soldiers).
(2.7.1056) Those who are strong with a thousand — <s>sāhasra</s> and <s>sahasrin</s> (commanding a thousand) are their names.
(2.7.1057) <s>Paridhistha</s> (one stationed around) and <s>paricara</s> (attendant) are synonyms. <s>Senānī</s> (general) and <s>vāhinīpati</s> (commander of forces) are synonyms.
(2.7.1058) <s>Kañcuka</s> (coat of mail) and <s>vārabāṇa</s> (arrow-ward) are not feminine. That which is tied in the middle by those wearing armor
(2.7.1059) is called <s>sārasana</s> (waist-guard). <s>Adhikāṅga</s> means an extra body-piece. Then <s>śīrṣaka</s> (helmet)

children.text: (2.7.1060) śīrṣaṇyaṃ ca śirastre 'tha tanutraṃ varma daṃśanam
children.translated_text: (2.7.1060) and <s>śīrṣaṇya</s> are synonyms for headgear. Then <s>tanutra</s> (body armor), <s>varma</s> (armor), and <s>daṃśana</s> (mail)
(2.7.1061) <s>uraśchada</s> (breastplate), <s>kaṅkaṭaka</s> (armor), <s>jāgara</s> (armor), and <s>kavaca</s> (cuirass) — not feminine —
(2.7.1062) <s>āmukta</s> (armored), <s>pratimukta</s> (armored), and <s>pinaddha</s> (girded) are like <s>āpinaddha</s> (bound in armor).
(2.7.1063) <s>Saṃnaddha</s> (armored), <s>varmita</s> (armored), <s>sajja</s> (equipped), <s>daṃśita</s> (mailed), and <s>vyūḍhakaṅkaṭa</s> (fully armored) are synonyms.
(2.7.1064) In all three genders, <s>āmukta</s> and the like apply to those wearing armor. <s>Kāvacika</s> is used for a group of armored warriors.
(2.7.1065) <s>Padāti</s> (foot soldier), <s>patti</s> (infantryman), <s>padaga</s> (one who goes on foot), <s>pādātika</s>, and <s>padāta</s> are synonyms.
(2.7.1066) <s>Padga</s> and <s>padika</s> are also used. Then <s>pādāta</s> (infantry) refers to a body of foot soldiers.
(2.7.1067) For those whose livelihood is weapons: <s>kāṇḍapṛṣṭha</s>, <s>āyudhīya</s>, and <s>āyudhika</s> (armed man) are synonymous.
(2.7.1068) <s>Kṛtahasta</s> (skilled hand) means one whose arrows are well-aimed; like <s>kṛtapuṅkha</s> (one whose arrows are well-feathered).
(2.7.1069) <s>Aparāddhapṛṣatka</s> (one who has missed the target) is one whose arrow has strayed from the mark.
(2.7.1070) <s>Dhanvī</s> (bowman), <s>dhanuṣmān</s> (archer), <s>dhānuṣka</s> (archer), <s>niṣaṅgī</s> (quiver-bearer) — not feminine — and <s>dhanurdhara</s> (bow-bearer) are synonyms.
(2.7.1071) <s>Kāṇḍavān</s> (arrow-bearer) and <s>kāṇḍīra</s> are synonyms. <s>Śāktīka</s> (spearman) and <s>śaktihetika</s> (spear-wielder) are synonyms.
(2.7.1072) <s>Yāṣṭīka</s> (staff-wielder) and <s>pāraśvathika</s> (axe-wielder) are those whose weapons are staffs and battle-axes respectively.
(2.7.1073) <s>Naistriṃśika</s> (swordsman) is one whose weapon is a sword. <s>Prāsika</s> (lance-wielder) and <s>kauntika</s> (spearman) are synonymous.
(2.7.1074) <s>Carmī</s> (shield-bearer) and <s>phalakapāṇi</s> (board-handed) are synonyms. <s>Patākī</s> (standard-bearer) and <s>vaijayantikaḥ</s> (victory-banner holder) are synonyms.
(2.7.1075) <s>Anuplava</s> (companion), <s>sahāya</s> (ally), <s>anucara</s> (follower), <s>anucara</s> (attendant), and <s>abhicara</s> (associate) are synonymous.
(2.7.1076) <s>Purogā</s> (one who goes before), <s>agresara</s> (forerunner), <s>praṣṭhā</s> (leader), <s>agrataḥsara</s> (going ahead), and <s>puraḥsara</s> (vanguard) are synonyms.
(2.7.1077) <s>Purogama</s> (going ahead) and <s>purogāmī</s> (one who goes forward) are synonyms. <s>Mandagāmī</s> (slow-goer) and <s>manthara</s> (sluggish) are synonyms.
(2.7.1078) <s>Jaṅghāla</s> (swift-footed) and <s>atijavas</s> (very fast) are synonymous. <s>Jaṅghākarika</s> (runner) and <s>jāṅghika</s> (one who goes on foot) are equal.

children.text: (2.7.1079) tarasvī tvarito vegī prajasvī javano javaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.7.1079) <s>Tarasvī</s> (energetic), <s>tvarita</s> (quick), <s>vegī</s> (speedy), <s>prajasvī</s> (vigorous), <s>javana</s> (swift), and <s>java</s> (speed) are synonyms.

children.text: (2.7.1080) jayyo yaḥ śakyate jetuṃ jeyo jetavyamātrake
children.translated_text: (2.7.1080) <s>Jayya</s> means one who can be conquered; <s>jeya</s> refers merely to what is to be conquered.

children.text: (2.7.1081) jaitrastu jetā yo gacchatyalaṃ vidviṣataḥ prati
children.translated_text: (2.7.1081) <s>Jaitra</s> (victorious) is one who is a conqueror, who marches effectively against enemies.
(2.7.1082) He is called <s>abhyamitra</s> (advancing against the enemy), also <s>abhyamitrīya</s> and <s>abhyamitrīṇa</s>.
(2.7.1083) <s>Ūrjasvala</s> and <s>ūrjasvī</s> (vigorous) refer to one endowed with exceeding strength.
(2.7.1084) <s>Svādu</s> (pleasant), <s>rasvā</s>, <s>anurasa</s>, <s>ila</s> are synonyms. <s>Rathika</s> (chariot warrior), <s>rathira</s>, and <s>rathī</s> are synonyms.
(2.7.1085) <s>Kāmagāmī</s> (going at will), <s>anukāmīna</s> — and <s>atyantīna</s> likewise means exceedingly.

children.text: (2.7.1086) śūro vīraśca vikrānto jetā jiṣṇuśca jitvaraḥ
children.translated_text: (2.7.1086) <s>Śūra</s> (hero), <s>vīra</s> (valiant), <s>vikrānta</s> (mighty), <s>jetā</s> (conqueror), <s>jiṣṇu</s> (victorious), and <s>jitvara</s> (triumphant) are synonyms.
(2.7.1087) <s>Sāṃyugīna</s> (skilled in battle) means one who excels in combat. <s>Śastrajīva</s> (one who lives by weapons) and the like are in all three genders.
(2.7.1088) <s>Dhvajinī</s> (bannered army), <s>vāhinī</s> (division), <s>senā</s> (army), <s>pṛtanā</s> (host), <s>anīkinī</s> (battalion), and <s>camū</s> (army) are synonyms.
(2.7.1089) <s>Varūthinī</s> (armored force), <s>bala</s> (force), <s>sainya</s> (army), <s>cakra</s> (army array), and <s>anīka</s> (battle line) — not feminine —
(2.7.1090) <s>Vyūha</s> (battle formation) means the arrangement of forces; by differentiation, formations such as <s>daṇḍa</s> (staff formation) and others are used in battle.
(2.7.1091) <s>Pratyāsāra</s> (rear guard), <s>vyūhapārṣṇi</s> (rear of the formation), and <s>pratigraha</s> (reserve force) at the army's rear are synonyms.
(2.7.1092) One elephant, one chariot, three horses, and five foot soldiers constitute a <s>patti</s> (the smallest unit).
(2.7.1093) With each component tripled progressively, the names are given in ascending order accordingly.
(2.7.1094) <s>Senāmukha</s> (army front), <s>gulma</s> (platoon), <s>gaṇa</s> (troop), <s>vāhinī</s> (division), <s>pṛtanā</s> (brigade), <s>camū</s> (corps),
(2.7.1095) <s>anīkinī</s> (battalion), <s>daśānīkinī</s> (ten battalions), and <s>akṣauhiṇī</s> (complete army). Then, in prosperity:
(2.7.1096) <s>Saṃpatti</s> (fortune), <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity), and <s>Lakṣmī</s> (wealth) are synonyms. In adversity: <s>vipatti</s> (misfortune), <s>vipad</s> (calamity), and <s>āpad</s> (disaster).
(2.7.1097) <s>Āyudha</s> (weapon) and <s>praharaṇa</s> (striking weapon) are synonyms. <s>Śastra</s> (edged weapon) and <s>astra</s> (missile weapon) — both not feminine —
(2.7.1098) <s>Dhanus</s> (bow), <s>cāpa</s> (bow), <s>dhanva</s> (bow), <s>śarāsana</s> (bow), <s>kodaṇḍa</s> (bow), and <s>kārmuka</s> (bow) are synonyms.
(2.7.1099) <s>Iṣvāsa</s> (archer) is also used. Then <s>Karṇa's</s> bow is called <s>Kālapṛṣṭha</s>.
(2.7.1100) <s>Arjuna's</s> (Kapidhvaja's) bow is called <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> or <s>Gāṇḍiva</s>; it is masculine or neuter.
(2.7.1101) Its tip is called <s>aṭanī</s> (bow-tip). <s>Godhā</s> (leather guard) refers to the leather guard protecting the finger from the bowstring.

children.text: (2.7.1102) lastakastu dhanurmadhyaṃ morvī jyā śiñjinī guṇaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.7.1102) <s>Lastaka</s> is the middle of the bow. <s>Morvī</s> (bowstring), <s>jyā</s> (string), <s>śiñjinī</s> (twanging string), and <s>guṇa</s> (string) are synonyms.
(2.7.1103) <s>Pratyālīḍha</s> and <s>ālīḍha</s> and the like constitute the five archery stances.

children.text: (2.7.1104) lakṣyaṃ lakṣaṃ śaravyaṃ ca śarābhyāsa upāsanam
children.translated_text: (2.7.1104) <s>Lakṣya</s> (target), <s>lakṣa</s> (mark), and <s>śaravya</s> (target) are synonyms. Archery practice is called <s>upāsana</s>.
(2.7.1105) <s>Pṛṣatka</s> (arrow), <s>bāṇa</s> (arrow), <s>viśikha</s> (arrow), <s>ajihma</s> (straight-flying), <s>ga</s> (going), <s>khaga</s> (sky-going), and <s>āśuga</s> (swift-going)
(2.7.1106) <s>kalamba</s> (arrow), <s>mārgaṇa</s> (arrow), and <s>śara</s> (arrow) are synonyms. <s>Patrī</s> (feathered arrow) and <s>ropa</s> (arrow); <s>iṣu</s> (arrow) is in two genders.
(2.7.1107) <s>Prakṣveḍana</s> (iron arrows) and <s>nārāca</s> (iron arrow) are synonyms. <s>Pakṣa</s> (feather) and <s>vāja</s> (fletching) — in all three genders for the latter terms.
(2.7.1108) <s>Nirasta</s> (discharged) refers to an arrow that has been shot. <s>Viṣākta</s> (poisoned), <s>digdha</s> (smeared), and <s>liptaka</s> (coated) refer to poisoned arrows.
(2.7.1109) <s>Tūṇa</s> (quiver), <s>upāsaṅga</s> (quiver), <s>tūṇīra</s> (quiver), and <s>niṣaṅga</s> (quiver) are synonyms. <s>Iṣudhi</s> (quiver) is in two genders.
(2.7.1110) <s>Tūṇī</s> is feminine for quiver. For the sword: <s>nistriṃśa</s> (sword), <s>candrahāsa</s> (scimitar), <s>asi</s> (sword), and <s>ṛṣṭi</s> (sword) are synonyms.
(2.7.1111) <s>Kaukṣeyaka</s> (girdle-sword), <s>maṇḍalāgra</s> (curved-tipped sword), and <s>karavāla</s> (sword) — like <s>kṛpāṇa</s> (blade).
(2.7.1112) <s>Tsaru</s> (hilt) refers to the handle of a sword and the like. <s>Mekhalā</s> (belt) is what fastens it.

children.text: (2.7.1113) phalako 'strī phalaṃ carma saṃgrāho muṣṭirasya yaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.7.1113) <s>Phalaka</s> (shield) is not feminine; <s>phala</s> (shield) and <s>carma</s> (leather shield) are synonyms. <s>Saṃgrāha</s> (grip) is its handle.
(2.7.1114) <s>Drughaṇa</s> (mallet), <s>mudgara</s> (hammer), and <s>ghana</s> (mace) are synonyms. <s>Īlī</s> (small sword) and <s>karavālikā</s> (dagger) are synonyms.
(2.7.1115) <s>Bhindipāla</s> (javelin) and <s>sṛga</s> (javelin) are synonymous. <s>Parigha</s> (iron bar) and <s>parighātin</s> (mace-wielder)
(2.7.1116) are in two genders. <s>Kuṭhāra</s> (axe), <s>svadhiti</s> (hatchet), <s>paraśu</s> (axe), and <s>paraśvadha</s> (battle-axe) are synonyms.
(2.7.1117) Also feminine forms: <s>asiputrī</s> (small sword), <s>churikā</s> (knife), and <s>asidhenukā</s> (dagger).

children.text: (2.7.1118) vā puṃsi śalyaṃ śaṅkurnā sarvalā tomaro 'striyām
children.translated_text: (2.7.1118) Optionally masculine: <s>śalya</s> (dart) and <s>śaṅku</s> (spike) are not feminine. <s>Sarvalā</s> and <s>tomara</s> (lance) — not feminine.
(2.7.1119) <s>Prāsa</s> (lance) and <s>kunta</s> (spear) are synonyms. <s>Koṇa</s> (point) and the feminine forms <s>pālī</s>, <s>aśri</s>, and <s>koṭi</s> (edge, point) are synonyms.
(2.7.1120) <s>Sarvābhisāra</s> (general muster), <s>sarvaugha</s> (complete assembly), — meaning the complete marshaling of all forces.
(2.7.1121) <s>Lohābhisāra</s> (review of arms) is the ceremony of lustration of weapons for kings who bear arms.
(2.7.1122) The marching of an army against the enemy is called <s>abhiṣeṇana</s> (military expedition).
(2.7.1123) <s>Yātrā</s> (march), <s>vrajyā</s> (expedition), <s>abhiniryāṇa</s> (sortie), <s>prasthāna</s> (departure), <s>gamana</s> (going), and <s>gama</s> (going) are synonyms.
(2.7.1124) <s>Āsāra</s> (onset), <s>prasaraṇa</s> (advance), <s>pracakra</s> (movement) — meaning movement or setting forth.
(2.7.1125) The advance against enemies by one who is fearless in battle — that is <s>abhikrama</s> (attack).
(2.7.1126) <s>Vaitālika</s> (bard who awakens) means one who rouses from sleep. <s>Cākrika</s> and <s>ghāṇṭika</s> (bell-ringer) have similar meaning.
(2.7.1127) <s>Māgadha</s> (panegyrist from Magadha) and <s>magadha</s> are synonyms. <s>Bandin</s> (eulogist) and <s>stutipāṭhaka</s> (reciter of praises) are synonyms.
(2.7.1128) <s>Saṃśaptaka</s> (sworn warriors) are those who by mutual oath do not retreat from battle.

children.text: (2.7.1129) reṇurdvayoḥ striyāṃ dhūliḥ pāṃsurnā na dvayo rajaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.7.1129) <s>Reṇu</s> (dust) is in two genders, feminine being <s>dhūli</s> (dust). <s>Pāṃsu</s> (dust) is not feminine; in two genders is <s>rajas</s> (dust).
(2.7.1130) In powder form: <s>kṣoda</s> (fine powder). <s>Samutpiñja</s> and <s>piñjala</s> mean greatly agitated.
(2.7.1131) <s>Patākā</s> (banner) and <s>vaijayantī</s> (victory flag) are synonyms. <s>Ketana</s> (flag) and <s>dhvaja</s> (banner) — not feminine.
(2.7.1132) That (banner) is a token of heroic aspiration. The battlefield is one that instills fear in those who approach.
(2.7.1133) 'I am first! I am first!' — this attitude is called <s>ahaṃpūrvikā</s> (competitive rivalry); it is feminine.
(2.7.1134) <s>Āhopuruṣikā</s> (boasting) is self-aggrandizement arising from pride.

children.text: (2.7.1135) ahamahamikā tu sā syāt parasparaṃ yo bhavatyahaṅkāraḥ
children.translated_text: (2.7.1135) <s>Ahamahamikā</s> (mutual rivalry) is the mutual ego-assertion between persons.

children.text: (2.7.1136) draviṇaṃ taraḥ sahobalaśauryāṇi sthāma śuṣmaṃ ca
children.translated_text: (2.7.1136) <s>Draviṇa</s> (wealth), <s>taras</s> (energy), <s>sahas</s> (might), <s>bala</s> (strength), <s>śaurya</s> (valor), <s>sthāma</s> (power), and <s>śuṣma</s> (vigor)
(2.7.1137) <s>Śakti</s> (power), <s>parākrama</s> (prowess), <s>prāṇa</s> (vital force), and <s>vikrama</s> (valor) — <s>atiśaktitā</s> means exceeding power.

children.text: (2.7.1138) vīrapāṇaṃ tu yatpānaṃ vṛtte bhāvini vā raṇe
children.translated_text: (2.7.1138) <s>Vīrapāna</s> (hero's drink) is the drinking that occurs during or after a battle.
(2.7.1139) <s>Yuddha</s> (battle), <s>āyodhana</s> (combat), <s>janya</s> (fight), <s>praghana</s> (onslaught), and <s>pravidāraṇa</s> (rending)
(2.7.1140) <s>mṛdha</s> (conflict), <s>āskandana</s> (assault), <s>saṃkhya</s> (battle), <s>samīka</s> (engagement), and <s>sāṃparāyika</s> (relating to the next world, i.e., deadly combat)
(2.7.1141) — not feminine — <s>samara</s> (war), <s>anīka</s> (battle array), <s>raṇa</s> (battle), <s>kalaha</s> (quarrel), and <s>vigraha</s> (conflict)
(2.7.1142) <s>saṃprahāra</s> (clash), <s>abhisaṃpāta</s> (encounter), <s>kali</s> (strife), <s>saṃsphoṭa</s> (collision), and <s>saṃyuga</s> (engagement)
(2.7.1143) <s>abhyāmarda</s> (crushing), <s>samāghāta</s> (clash), <s>saṃgrāma</s> (battle), <s>abhyāgama</s> (encounter), and <s>āhava</s> (war)
(2.7.1144) <s>samudāya</s> (assemblage) is feminine. <s>Saṃyat</s> (battle), <s>samiti</s> (encounter), <s>āji</s> (contest), <s>samid</s> (fight), and <s>yudh</s> (war) are synonyms.
(2.7.1145) <s>Niyuddha</s> (close combat) means hand-to-hand fighting. <s>Tumula</s> (tumultuous) refers to the confusion of battle.

children.text: (2.7.1146) kṣvedā tu siṃhanādaḥ syāt kariṇāṃ ghaṭanā ghaṭā
children.translated_text: (2.7.1146) <s>Kṣvedā</s> (battle cry) is the lion's roar. <s>Ghaṭanā</s> and <s>ghaṭā</s> (clash) refer to the engagement of elephants.
(2.7.1147) <s>Krandana</s> (war cry) is the clamor of warriors. <s>Bṛṃhita</s> (trumpeting) is the sound made by elephants.
(2.7.1148) <s>Visphāra</s> (twanging) is the sound of a bow. <s>Patāha</s> (war drum) and <s>ambara</s> (drum) are synonymous.

children.text: (2.7.1149) prasabhaṃ tu balātkāro haṭho 'tha skhalitaṃ chalam
children.translated_text: (2.7.1149) <s>Prasabha</s> (forcible) means violence. <s>Haṭha</s> (force) also means violence. Then <s>skhalita</s> (stumbling) and <s>chala</s> (deception).
(2.7.1150) <s>Ajanya</s> (portent), neuter: <s>utpāta</s> (omen) and <s>upasarga</s> (calamity) — these three are synonymous.

children.text: (2.7.1151) mū{chā}ṛ tu kaśmalaṃ moho.āpyavama{da}ṛs tu pīdanam
children.translated_text: (2.7.1151) <s>Mūrchā</s> (fainting) and <s>kaśmala</s> (bewilderment) and <s>moha</s> (delusion) are synonyms. <s>Avamarda</s> (crushing) means oppression.
(2.7.1152) <s>Abhyavaskandana</s> (overcoming) and <s>abhyāsādana</s> (approaching to attack) are synonyms. <s>Vijaya</s> (victory) and <s>jaya</s> (triumph) are synonyms.
(2.7.1153) <s>Vairaśuddhi</s> (satisfaction of enmity), <s>pratīkāra</s> (retaliation), and <s>vairaniryātana</s> (revenge) — she (vairaśuddhi) refers to these.
(2.7.1154) <s>Pradrāva</s> (flight), <s>uddrāva</s> (fleeing upward), <s>sandrāva</s> (fleeing together), <s>sandāva</s> (stampede), <s>vidrava</s> (scattering), and <s>drava</s> (rout) are synonyms.
(2.7.1155) <s>Apakrama</s> (retreat) and <s>apayāna</s> (withdrawal) are synonyms. <s>Bhaṅga</s> (breaking of ranks) in battle is <s>parājaya</s> (defeat).
(2.7.1156) <s>Parājita</s> (defeated) and <s>parābhūta</s> (overcome) are synonyms. In all three genders: <s>naṣṭa</s> (lost) and <s>tirohita</s> (vanished).
(2.7.1157) <s>Pramāpaṇa</s> (destroying), <s>nibarhaṇa</s> (slaying), <s>nikāraṇa</s> (killing), <s>viśāraṇa</s> (cutting down),
(2.7.1158) <s>pravāsana</s> (banishing), <s>parāsana</s> (driving away), <s>niṣūdana</s> (annihilating), <s>nihiṃsana</s> (injuring),
(2.7.1159) <s>nivāraṇa</s> (warding off), <s>saṃjñapana</s> (executing), <s>nigranthana</s> (binding), <s>apāsana</s> (removing),
(2.7.1160) <s>nistarhaṇa</s> (overcoming), <s>nihanana</s> (striking down), <s>kṣaṇana</s> (destroying), <s>parivarjana</s> (abandoning),
(2.7.1161) <s>nivārapaṇa</s> (preventing), <s>viśasana</s> (slaughtering), <s>māraṇa</s> (killing), and <s>pratighātana</s> (striking back)
(2.7.1162) <s>udvāsana</s> (banishing), <s>pramathana</s> (crushing), <s>krathana</s> (slaying), and <s>ujjāsana</s> (expelling)

(2.7.1163) <s>ālambha</s> (slaughter), <s>piñja</s> (killing), <s>viśara</s> (destruction), <s>ghāta</s> (killing), <s>unmātha</s> (uprooting), and <s>vadha</s> (slaying) — all are synonyms for killing.

(2.7.1164) <s>Pañcatā</s> (death, dissolution into five elements), <s>kāladharma</s> (the law of time, death), <s>diṣṭānta</s> (end of destiny), <s>pralaya</s> (dissolution), <s>atyaya</s> (passing away),

children.text: (2.7.1165) anto nāśo dvayor mṛtyur maraṇaṃ nidhano 'striyām
children.translated_text: (2.7.1165) <s>anta</s> (end) and <s>nāśa</s> (destruction) are in two genders. <s>Mṛtyu</s> (death) and <s>maraṇa</s> (dying) are synonyms. <s>Nidhana</s> (death) is not feminine.
(2.7.1166) <s>Parāsu</s> (dead), <s>prāptapañcatva</s> (one who has attained the five elements), <s>pareta</s> (departed), <s>preta</s> (deceased), and <s>saṃsthita</s> (passed away) are synonyms.

children.text: (2.7.1167) mṛtapramītau triṣvete, citā cityā citiḥ striyām
children.translated_text: (2.7.1167) <s>Mṛta</s> (dead) and <s>pramīta</s> (deceased) are in all three genders. <s>Citā</s> (funeral pyre), <s>cityā</s>, and <s>citi</s> are feminine.
(2.7.1168) <s>Kabandha</s> (headless trunk) is not feminine — it refers to a body with the head cut off.
(2.7.1169) <s>Śmaśāna</s> (cremation ground) and <s>pitṛvana</s> (grove of the ancestors) are synonyms. <s>Kuṇapa</s> (corpse) and <s>śava</s> (dead body) — not feminine.
(2.7.1170) <s>Pragraha</s> (capture) and <s>upagraha</s> (seizure) refer to imprisonment. <s>Kārā</s> (prison) refers to a place of confinement.

(2.7.1171) In the masculine: <s>bhū</s> (earth), <s>agni</s> (fire), <s>asava</s> (life breaths), and <s>prāṇa</s> (vital airs) are used thus. <s>Jīva</s> (life) and <s>asudhāraṇa</s> (sustaining of life breaths) are synonyms.

children.text: (2.7.1172) āyur jīvitakālo, nā jīvatur jīvanauṣadham | iti kṣatriyavargaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.7.1172) <s>Āyus</s> (life-span) is the time of life; <s>jīvatu</s> (life-giving), neuter, is a life-restoring medicine. Thus ends the <s>Kṣatriya</s> section.
The <s>Vaiśya</s> section.

children.text: (2.8.1173) ūravya ūruja aryā vaiśyā bhūmispṛśo viśaḥ | atha vaiśyavargaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1173) <s>Ūravya</s>, <s>ūruja</s>, <s>ārya</s>, <s>vaiśya</s>, <s>bhūmispṛś</s>, and <s>viś</s> [are synonyms for a member of the <s>Vaiśya</s> class]. Now [begins] the <s>Vaiśya</s> section.
(2.8.1174) <s>Ājīva</s> (livelihood), <s>jīvikā</s> (livelihood), feminine, and <s>vṛtti</s> (occupation), feminine, [are synonyms] for the means of living.

children.text: (2.8.1175) striyāṃ kṛṣiḥ pāśupālyaṃ vāṇijyaṃ ceti vṛttayaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1175) The occupations are: agriculture (<s>kṛṣi</s>), feminine; cattle-rearing (<s>pāśupālya</s>); and trade (<s>vāṇijya</s>).

(2.8.1176) Service (<s>sevā</s>) is a dog's livelihood. Falsehood (<s>anṛta</s>) [is one livelihood]. Gleaning (<s>kṛśi</s>), and living by gathering (<s>uñchaśila</s>), is <s>ṛta</s> (truthful livelihood).
(2.8.1177) Two [livelihoods] of the borrowed and the unborrowed are, respectively, <s>mṛta</s> (dead) and <s>amṛta</s> (immortal).
(2.8.1178) <s>Satyānṛta</s> (truth-and-falsehood) is the state of being a merchant. <s>Ṛṇa</s> (debt) is <s>pṛdañcana</s>.
(2.8.1179) <s>Uddhāra</s> (extraction) [means debt-recovery]; <s>ṛprayoga</s> (lending on interest), however, is <s>kusīda</s> (usury), the livelihood from interest (<s>vṛddhijīvikā</s>).
(2.8.1180) What is obtained by begging is <s>yācitaka</s> (borrowed). What is obtained by exchange is <s>āpamityaka</s> (bartered).
(2.8.1181) <s>Uttamarṇa</s> (creditor) and <s>adhamarṇa</s> (debtor) are two: the lender and the borrower, respectively.
(2.8.1182) <s>Kusīdika</s>, <s>vārdhūṣika</s>, <s>vṛddhyājīva</s>, and <s>vārdhuṣi</s> [are synonyms for a usurer].
(2.8.1183) <s>Kṣetrājīva</s> (one who lives by the field), <s>karṣaka</s> (ploughman), <s>kṛṣika</s>, and <s>kṛṣīvala</s> [are synonyms for a farmer].
(2.8.1184) A field is [called] <s>vraihīya</s> or <s>śāleya</s> when it is suitable for producing <s>vrīhi</s> (rice) or <s>śāli</s> (paddy).

children.text: (2.8.1185) yavyaṃ yavakyaṃ yaṣṭikyaṃ yavādibhavanaṃ hi yat
children.translated_text: (2.8.1185) <s>Yavya</s>, <s>yavakya</s>, <s>yaṣṭikya</s> [are terms for a field] that is suitable for growing barley (<s>yava</s>) and the like.
(2.8.1186) Like <s>tilya</s> and <s>tailīna</s> [for a sesame field]; <s>māṣa</s>, <s>umā</s>, <s>ṇubhaṅga</s>, and the like [show] variation of form.
(2.8.1187) <s>Maudgīna</s>, <s>kaudravīṇa</s>, and the like — [terms for fields] suitable for growing other grains.
(2.8.1188) For a vegetable field and the like: <s>śāka</s>, <s>śākata</s>, <s>śākaśākin</s>.

children.text: (2.8.1189) bījākṛtaṃ tūprakṛṣṭe sītyaṃ kṛṣṭaṃ ca halyavat
children.translated_text: (2.8.1189) <s>Bījākṛta</s> (unsown) [applies to] unploughed [land]; <s>sītya</s> and <s>kṛṣṭa</s> (ploughed) are like <s>halya</s> (ploughed with a plough).
(2.8.1190) <s>Triguṇākṛta</s>, <s>tṛtīyākṛta</s>, <s>trihalya</s>, <s>trisītya</s> — [all refer to land] ploughed three times.
(2.8.1191) But for [land] ploughed twice: <s>sarva</s>, <s>pūrva</s>, <s>śambākṛta</s> — also [used] in this [sense].
(2.8.1192) [Fields measured by] <s>droṇa</s>, <s>āḍhaka</s>, and the like [in terms of] sowing-capacity [are called] <s>drauṇika</s>, <s>āḍhakika</s>, and so on.
(2.8.1193) But a <s>kharī</s>-sowing [field] is <s>khārīka</s>. <s>Uttamarṇa</s> and so on [are used] in all three genders.
(2.8.1194) <s>Vapra</s> (raised bed) [is used] in masculine and neuter. <s>Kedāra</s> is a field; but its [derivative is]

children.text: (2.8.1195) kaidārakaṃ syāt kaidā{ya}ṛṃ kṣetraṃ kaidārikaṃ gaṇe
children.translated_text: (2.8.1195) <s>kaidāraka</s> or <s>kaidārya</s> — a field. <s>Kaidārika</s> [is used] in a collective sense.
(2.8.1196) <s>Loṣṭāni</s> [and] <s>leṣṭavaḥ</s> (clods of earth) are masculine. <s>Koṭiśa</s> is a clod-breaker.
(2.8.1197) <s>Prājana</s>, <s>todana</s>, <s>totra</s> [are synonyms for a goad]. <s>Khanitra</s> is [a tool] for digging.
(2.8.1198) <s>Dātra</s> and <s>lavitra</s> [are synonyms for a sickle]. <s>Ābandha</s>, <s>yotra</s>, <s>yoktra</s> [are synonyms for a yoke-strap]. And <s>phala</s> (ploughshare).

children.text: (2.8.1199) nirīṣaṃ kuṭakaṃ phālaḥ kṛṣako lāṃgalaṃ halam
children.translated_text: (2.8.1199) <s>Nirīṣa</s> and <s>kuṭaka</s> [are parts of the plough]. <s>Phāla</s>, <s>kṛṣaka</s>, <s>lāṅgala</s>, and <s>hala</s> [are synonyms for a plough].

children.text: (2.8.1200) godāraṇaṃ ca sīro 'tha śamyā strī yugakīlakaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1200) <s>Godāraṇa</s> and <s>sīra</s> [are also ploughs]. Then <s>śamyā</s>, feminine, is the yoke-pin.
(2.8.1201) <s>Īṣā</s> is the plough-shaft. <s>Sītā</s> is the furrow made by the plough.

children.text: (2.8.1202) puṃsi medhiḥ khale dāru nyastaṃ yat paśubandhane
children.translated_text: (2.8.1202) <s>Medhi</s>, masculine, is the post fixed on the threshing-floor for tying cattle.
(2.8.1203) <s>Āśu</s> is early-ripening rice. <s>Pāṭala</s> [is a type]. <s>Śitaśūka</s> and <s>yava</s> (barley) are synonyms.

children.text: (2.8.1204) tokmas tu tatra harite kalāyas tu satīnakaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1204) <s>Tokma</s> is the green [sprout] thereof. <s>Kalāya</s> is <s>satīnaka</s> (a type of pea).
(2.8.1205) <s>Hareṇu</s> and <s>reṇuka</s> [are synonyms for a type of grain]. <s>Koradūṣa</s> is <s>kodrava</s> (millet).
(2.8.1206) <s>Maṅgalyaka</s> is <s>masūra</s> (lentil). Then <s>makuṣṭhaka</s> and <s>mayuṣṭhaka</s> [are synonyms].
(2.8.1207) For <s>vanamudga</s> (wild mung-bean); for <s>sarṣapa</s> (mustard), the two [synonyms are] <s>tantubha</s> and <s>kadambaka</s>.

children.text: (2.8.1208) siddhārthas tveṣa dhavalo godhūmaḥ sumanaḥ samau
children.translated_text: (2.8.1208) <s>Siddhārtha</s> is white mustard. <s>Godhūma</s> (wheat) and <s>sumanas</s> are synonyms.

children.text: (2.8.1209) syād yāvakas tu kulmāṣaś caṇako harimanthakaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1209) <s>Yāvaka</s> is <s>kulmāṣa</s> (parched barley). <s>Caṇaka</s> (chickpea) is <s>harimanthaka</s>.

children.text: (2.8.1210) dvau tile tilapejaś ca tilapiñjaś ca niṣphale
children.translated_text: (2.8.1210) Two [terms] for sesame: <s>tilapeja</s> and <s>tilapiñja</s> — when huskless.
(2.8.1211) <s>Kṣava</s> produces sneezing. <s>Rājikā</s>, <s>kṛṣṇikā</s>, and <s>asurī</s> [are synonyms for black mustard].

children.text: (2.8.1212) striyau kaṅgupriyaṅgū dve atasī syādumā kṣumā
children.translated_text: (2.8.1212) <s>Kaṅgu</s> and <s>priyaṅgu</s> (Italian millet) are two, feminine. <s>Atasī</s> is <s>umā</s> or <s>kṣumā</s> (flax).

children.text: (2.8.1213) mātulānī tu bhaṅgāyāṃ vrīhi bhedas tvaṇuḥ pumān
children.translated_text: (2.8.1213) <s>Mātulānī</s> is [used] for hemp (<s>bhaṅgā</s>). A variety of rice is <s>aṇu</s>, masculine.
(2.8.1214) <s>Kiṃśāru</s> is the awn of grain. <s>Kaṇiśa</s> is the ear of grain.

children.text: (2.8.1215) dhānyaṃ vrīhiḥ stambakariḥ stambo gucchas tṛṇādinaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1215) <s>Dhānya</s> (grain) is <s>vrīhi</s> (rice). <s>Stambakari</s> [is a type]. <s>Stamba</s> is a cluster of grass and the like.

children.text: (2.8.1216) nāḍī nālaṃ ca kāṇḍo 'sya palālostrī sa niṣphalaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1216) <s>Nāḍī</s> and <s>nāla</s> [are synonyms for a stalk]. <s>Kāṇḍa</s> is its [stem]. <s>Palāla</s>, feminine, is the straw — that which is without grain.

children.text: (2.8.1217) kaḍaṅgaro busaṃ klībe dhānyatvaci tuṣaḥ pumān
children.translated_text: (2.8.1217) <s>Kaḍaṅgara</s> is <s>busa</s>, neuter, [meaning chaff]. <s>Tuṣa</s> (husk), masculine, is the grain-covering.
(2.8.1218) <s>Śūka</s> (awn), not feminine, has a smooth or sharp tip. <s>Śamī</s> and <s>śimbā</s>, in the remaining three [genders, are synonyms for a pod].
(2.8.1219) <s>Ṛddha</s> and <s>āvasita</s> [mean] ripened grain. <s>Pūta</s> means winnowed or sifted.
(2.8.1220) <s>Māṣa</s> (black gram) and the like are <s>śamīdhānya</s> (pod-grains). <s>Yava</s> (barley) and the like are <s>śūkadhānya</s> (awned grains).

children.text: (2.8.1221) śālayaḥ kalamādyāś ca ṣaṣṭikādyāś ca puṃsyamī
children.translated_text: (2.8.1221) <s>Śāli</s> (paddy), <s>kalama</s>, and the like; and <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> (sixty-day rice) and the like — these are masculine.
(2.8.1222) <s>Tṛṇadhānya</s> (grass-grains) are <s>nīvāra</s> (wild rice). <s>Gavedhur</s> and <s>gavedhukā</s> [are synonyms], feminine.
(2.8.1223) <s>Ayogra</s> is a pestle (<s>musala</s>), not feminine. <s>Udūkhala</s> and <s>ulūkhala</s> [are synonyms for a mortar].
(2.8.1224) <s>Prasphoṭana</s> is a winnowing basket (<s>śūrpa</s>), not feminine. <s>Cālanī</s> [is a sieve]. <s>Titau</s>, masculine.
(2.8.1225) <s>Syūta</s> and <s>praseva</s> [are synonyms for a large basket]. <s>Kaṇḍola</s> and <s>piṭa</s> [mean a basket]. <s>Kaṭa</s> and <s>kiliñjaka</s> [are synonyms for a mat].
(2.8.1226) Are synonymous. For a kitchen: <s>rasavatī</s>, <s>pākasthāna</s>, and <s>mahānasa</s>.
(2.8.1227) <s>Paurogava</s> is the superintendent thereof. <s>Sūpakāras</s> (cooks) are <s>ballavas</s>.
(2.8.1228) <s>Ārālikā</s>, <s>āndhasikāḥ</s>, <s>sūdā</s>, <s>audanikā</s>, <s>guṇāḥ</s> [are synonyms for cooks].
(2.8.1229) <s>Āpūpika</s> and <s>kāndavika</s> [are synonyms for] a maker of sweetmeats. These [are used] in all three genders.
(2.8.1230) <s>Aśmanta</s>, <s>uddhāna</s>, <s>adhiśrayaṇī</s>, <s>cullī</s>, <s>antikā</s> [are synonyms for a cooking-hearth].
(2.8.1231) <s>Aṅgāradhānikā</s> is a charcoal-pan; also <s>āṅgāraśakaṭī</s>; also <s>hasantī</s>.
(2.8.1232) Also <s>hasanyā</s>. Then <s>aṅgāra</s> (ember), <s>alāta</s>, and <s>ulmuka</s> [are synonyms for a firebrand] — not feminine.

children.text: (2.8.1233) klībe 'mbarīpaṃ bhrāṣṭro nā kandur vā svedanī striyām
children.translated_text: (2.8.1233) <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, neuter, is a frying-pan. <s>Bhrāṣṭra</s>, masculine. <s>Kandu</s> or <s>svedanī</s>, feminine.
(2.8.1234) <s>Aliñjara</s> is a <s>maṇika</s> (pot). <s>Karālu</s> is a <s>galantikā</s> (water-pot).

children.text: (2.8.1235) piṭharaḥ sthālyukhā kuṇḍaṃ kalaśas tu triṣu dvayoḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1235) <s>Piṭhara</s>, <s>sthālī</s>, <s>ukhā</s>, <s>kuṇḍa</s> [are types of pots]. <s>Kalaśa</s> [is used] in all three genders for the first two.
(2.8.1236) <s>Ghaṭa</s> (jar), <s>kuṭa</s>, <s>nipāva</s>, feminine. <s>Śarāva</s> is <s>vardhamānaka</s> (an earthen dish).
(2.8.1237) <s>Ṛjīṣa</s> is a cake-pan. <s>Kaṃsa</s>, not feminine, is a drinking-vessel.

children.text: (2.8.1238) kutūḥ kṛtteḥ snehapātraṃ saivālpā kutupaḥ pumān
children.translated_text: (2.8.1238) <s>Kutu</s> from <s>kṛtti</s> (hide) is a vessel for oil. When small, <s>kutupa</s>, masculine.
(2.8.1239) <s>Sarva</s> and <s>āvapana</s> [mean] a vessel. <s>Bhāṇḍa</s> is a vessel, and <s>bhājana</s> is a container.

children.text: (2.8.1240) da{vi}ṛḥ kambiḥ khajākā ca syāt taddūr dāruhastakaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1240) <s>Darvī</s> and <s>kambi</s> [are synonyms for a ladle]. <s>Khajākā</s> is a wooden handle (lit. that which is a wooden-handled [spoon]).

children.text: (2.8.1241) astrī śākaṃ haritakaṃ śigrurasya tu nāḍikā
children.translated_text: (2.8.1241) <s>Śāka</s> (vegetable), not feminine, is <s>haritaka</s> (greens). <s>Śigru</s> is [the drumstick tree]; its <s>nāḍikā</s> [is the pod].

children.text: (2.8.1242) kalambaś ca kadambaś ca veṣavāra upaskaraḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1242) <s>Kalamba</s> and <s>kadamba</s> [are types of vegetables]. <s>Veṣavāra</s> is a preparation. <s>Upaskara</s> [is a condiment].

children.text: (2.8.1243) tintiḍīkaṃ ca cukraṃ ca vṛkṣāmlamatha vellajam
children.translated_text: (2.8.1243) <s>Tintiḍīka</s> and <s>cukra</s> [are synonyms for tamarind]. <s>Vṛkṣāmla</s> [is also tamarind]. Then <s>vellaja</s> (a sour substance).
(2.8.1244) <s>Marīca</s> (pepper) is <s>kolaka</s>, <s>kṛṣṇa</s> (black), <s>bhūṣaṇa</s>, <s>dharmapattana</s>.

children.text: (2.8.1245) jīrako jaraṇo 'jāji kaṇāḥ kṛṣṇe tu jīrake
children.translated_text: (2.8.1245) <s>Jīraka</s> (cumin) is <s>jaraṇa</s>, <s>ajāji</s>. <s>Kaṇā</s> [is the term] for black cumin.
(2.8.1246) <s>Suṣavī</s>, <s>kāravī</s>, <s>pṛthvī</s>, <s>pṛthu</s>, <s>kālopakuñjikā</s> [are synonyms for caraway].
(2.8.1247) <s>Ārdraka</s> is <s>śṛṅgabera</s> (ginger). Then <s>chatrā</s> is <s>vitunnaka</s> (coriander plant).
(2.8.1248) <s>Kustumbaru</s> is <s>dhānyāka</s> (coriander seeds). Then <s>śuṇṭhī</s> is <s>mahauṣadha</s> (dried ginger, the great medicine).
(2.8.1249) <s>Viśva</s>, feminine and neuter, is <s>nāgara</s> (dried ginger), <s>viśvabheṣaja</s> (the universal remedy).
(2.8.1250) <s>Āranālaka</s>, <s>sauvīraka</s>, <s>kulmāṣa</s>, <s>abhiśuta</s> [are types of fermented gruel].
(2.8.1251) <s>Avantisoma</s>, <s>dhānyāmla</s>, <s>kuñjala</s> [are also synonyms] for <s>kāñjika</s> (fermented rice-water).
(2.8.1252) <s>Sahasravedhi</s>, <s>jatuka</s>, <s>balhīka</s>, <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), <s>rāmaṭha</s> [are synonyms].

children.text: (2.8.1253) tatpatrī kāravī pṛthvī bāṣpikā kabarī pṛthuḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1253) Its leaf is <s>kāravī</s>, <s>pṛthvī</s>, <s>bāṣpikā</s>, <s>kabarī</s>, <s>pṛthu</s>.
(2.8.1254) Known as <s>niśā</s>, <s>kāñcanī</s>, <s>pītā</s> (yellow), <s>haridrā</s> (turmeric), and <s>varavarṇinī</s> (of excellent color).

children.text: (2.8.1255) sāmudraṃ yat tu lavaṇamakṣīvaṃ vaśiraṃ ca tat
children.translated_text: (2.8.1255) That salt which is sea-born (<s>sāmudra</s>) is <s>akṣīva</s> and <s>vaśira</s>.
(2.8.1256) <s>Saindhava</s>, not feminine, [means] cool and auspicious. <s>Māṇimantha</s> [is used] for that born in <s>Sindhu</s> (rock salt).

children.text: (2.8.1257) raumakaṃ vasukaṃ pākyaṃ biḍaṃ ca kṛtake dvayam
children.translated_text: (2.8.1257) <s>Raumaka</s> and <s>vasuka</s> [are types of salt]. <s>Pākya</s> and <s>biḍa</s> — [these] two [are terms] for artificial [salt].
(2.8.1258) For <s>sauvarcala</s> (black salt): <s>akṣarucaka</s>. <s>Tilaka</s> is there [used] for the dark [variety].
(2.8.1259) <s>Matsyaṇḍī</s> and <s>phāṇita</s> [are synonyms for molasses]. <s>Khaṇḍa</s> is a type of sugar. <s>Śarkarā</s> and <s>sitā</s> [are synonyms for sugar].
(2.8.1260) <s>Kūrcikā</s> is a milk-preparation. <s>Rasālā</s> is [a preparation] that has been cleaned/seasoned.
(2.8.1261) <s>Temana</s> is <s>niṣṭhāna</s> (a finishing preparation). <s>Vāsitā</s>, of three genders, [refers to] a slaughtered [animal].

children.text: (2.8.1262) śūlākṛtaṃ bhaṭitraṃ ca śūlyamukhyaṃ tu paiṭharam
children.translated_text: (2.8.1262) <s>Śūlākṛta</s> and <s>bhaṭitra</s> [mean] skewered [meat]. <s>Śūlya</s> and <s>mukhya</s> are <s>paiṭhara</s>.
(2.8.1263) <s>Praṇīta</s>, <s>upasaṃpanna</s>, and <s>prayasta</s> [are synonyms for] well-prepared.

children.text: (2.8.1264) syātpicchilaṃ tu vijilaṃ saṃmṛṣṭaṃ śodhitaṃ same
children.translated_text: (2.8.1264) <s>Picchila</s> is <s>vijila</s> (slimy). <s>Saṃmṛṣṭa</s> and <s>śodhita</s> are synonymous [meaning cleansed].
(2.8.1265) <s>Cikkaṇa</s>, <s>masṛṇa</s>, <s>snigdha</s> (smooth, oily) are synonymous. <s>Bhāvita</s> and <s>vāsita</s> (perfumed, seasoned) are synonymous.
(2.8.1266) <s>Āpakka</s> is <s>pauli</s> (half-cooked). <s>Abhyūṣa</s> [is a spicy preparation]. <s>Lāja</s> (parched grains) are masculine, on the ground also <s>akṣata</s> (unhusked).
(2.8.1267) <s>Pṛthaka</s> is <s>cipiṭaka</s> (flattened rice). <s>Dhānā</s>, feminine, is parched barley.
(2.8.1268) <s>Pūpa</s>, <s>apūpa</s>, and <s>piṣṭaka</s> [are synonyms for a cake]. <s>Karambha</s> is [a preparation of] curd and barley-meal.
(2.8.1269) <s>Bhissā</s>, feminine, is <s>bhakta</s> (cooked rice). <s>Andha</s>, <s>anna</s> (food), <s>odana</s>, not feminine — that is <s>dīdivi</s>.
(2.8.1270) <s>Bhissaṭā</s> and <s>dagdhikā</s> [are types of food]. <s>Sarvarasāgra</s> [means supreme in all flavors]. <s>Maṇḍa</s>, not feminine [is the cream or scum of boiled rice].
(2.8.1271) <s>Māsara</s>, <s>ācamana</s>, and <s>srāva</s> [are terms for] the watery part (<s>maṇḍa</s>) arising from cooked rice.

children.text: (2.8.1272) yavāgūruṣṇikā śrāṇā vilepī taralā ca sā
children.translated_text: (2.8.1272) <s>Yavāgū</s> (rice-gruel) is <s>uṣṇikā</s>. <s>Śrāṇā</s>, <s>vilepī</s>, and <s>taralā</s> are synonymous [for thin gruel].
(2.8.1273) <s>Mrakṣaṇa</s> and <s>abhyañjana</s> [mean anointing]. <s>Taila</s> (oil). <s>Kṛsara</s> is rice cooked with sesame (<s>tilaudana</s>).
(2.8.1274) <s>Gavya</s>, in all three genders, [means] everything belonging to cows. <s>Goviḍ</s> is cow-dung (<s>gomaya</s>), feminine.

children.text: (2.8.1275) tattu śuṣkaṃ karīṣo 'strī dugdhaṃ kṣīraṃ payassamam
children.translated_text: (2.8.1275) But that which is dry is <s>karīṣa</s>, not feminine. <s>Dugdha</s>, <s>kṣīra</s>, and <s>payas</s> (milk) are synonymous.
(2.8.1276) <s>Payasya</s> is <s>ājya</s> (ghee), <s>dadhi</s> (curd), and the like. <s>Trapsya</s> is curd. <s>Dhaneta</s> is another [term].
(2.8.1277) <s>Ghṛta</s>, <s>ājya</s>, <s>havis</s>, <s>sarpis</s> [are synonyms for ghee]. <s>Navanīta</s> is freshly churned [butter].
(2.8.1278) But that <s>haiyaṅgavīna</s> is ghee that is produced from yesterday's milking.
(2.8.1279) <s>Daṇḍāhata</s> and <s>kālaśeya</s> [are types of dairy products]. <s>Ariṣṭa</s> too is a cow-product.
(2.8.1280) <s>Takra</s> (buttermilk) is that which has water. <s>Mathita</s> (churned) has a quarter part water, half water, or is without water.
(2.8.1281) <s>Maṇḍa</s> is the cream of curd. <s>Mastu</s> [is whey]. <s>Pīyūṣa</s> is fresh milk (colostrum).

children.text: (2.8.1282) aśanāyā bubhukṣā kṣud grāsastu kavalaḥ pumān
children.translated_text: (2.8.1282) <s>Aśanāyā</s>, <s>bubhukṣā</s>, and <s>kṣud</s> [are synonyms for hunger]. <s>Grāsa</s> is <s>kavala</s> (a morsel), masculine.

children.text: (2.8.1283) sapītiḥ strī tulyapānaṃ sagdhiḥ strī sahabhojanam
children.translated_text: (2.8.1283) <s>Sapīti</s>, feminine, is drinking together. <s>Sagdhi</s>, feminine, is eating together.

children.text: (2.8.1284) udanyā tu pipāsā tṛṭ tarpo jagdhistu bhojanam
children.translated_text: (2.8.1284) <s>Udanyā</s> is <s>pipāsā</s> (thirst) [and] <s>tṛṭ</s>. <s>Tarpa</s> [is satisfaction]. <s>Jagdhi</s> is eating (<s>bhojana</s>).

children.text: (2.8.1285) jemanaṃ leha āhāro nighāso nyāda ityapi
children.translated_text: (2.8.1285) <s>Jemana</s>, <s>leha</s>, <s>āhāra</s>, <s>nighāsa</s>, <s>nyāda</s> [are synonyms for food/eating].
(2.8.1286) <s>Sauhitya</s>, <s>tarpaṇa</s>, <s>tṛpti</s> [are synonyms for satisfaction]. <s>Phelā</s> is the remnant of eaten [food].
(2.8.1287) <s>Kāma</s>, <s>prakāma</s>, <s>paryāpta</s>, <s>nikāma</s>, <s>iṣṭa</s>, <s>yathepsita</s> [are synonyms for "as desired" or "satisfactorily"].
(2.8.1288) <s>Gopa</s>, <s>gopāla</s>, <s>gosaṃkhya</s>, <s>godhuk</s>, <s>ābhīra</s>, <s>vallava</s> [are synonyms for a cowherd].
(2.8.1289) <s>Gomahiṣyādika</s> is a tether for cattle and the like. The two [terms] for a lord of cattle are:

children.text: (2.8.1290) gomān gomī gokulaṃ tu godhanaṃ syātgavāṃ vraje
children.translated_text: (2.8.1290) <s>Gomān</s> and <s>gomī</s> [mean a cattle-owner]. <s>Gokula</s> is <s>godhana</s> (cattle-wealth). For a herd of cows:
(2.8.1291) <s>Āśitam</s> and <s>gavīna</s>, in three genders — [referring to] a place where cows have grazed before.

children.text: (2.8.1292) ukṣā bhadro balīvarda ṛṣabho vṛṣabho vṛṣaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1292) <s>Ukṣan</s>, <s>bhadra</s>, <s>balīvarda</s>, <s>ṛṣabha</s>, <s>vṛṣabha</s>, <s>vṛṣa</s> [are synonyms for a bull].
(2.8.1293) <s>Anaḍvān</s> and <s>saurabheya</s> [are also bull-names]. <s>Gaur</s>. The collective of bulls is <s>aukṣaka</s>.
(2.8.1294) <s>Gavyā</s> and <s>gotrā</s> [are herds of cows]. For the calves and milch-cows: <s>vātsaka</s> and <s>dhainuka</s>.
(2.8.1295) A large bull is <s>mahokṣa</s>. An aged bull is <s>jaradgava</s>.

children.text: (2.8.1296) utpanna ukṣā jātokṣaḥ sadyo jātastu tarṇakaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1296) A newly born bull is <s>jātokṣa</s>. One just born is <s>tarṇaka</s>.
(2.8.1297) One that produces dung is <s>śakṛtkari</s>, applicable to a calf. <s>Damya</s> and <s>vatsatara</s> are synonymous [for a young bull to be tamed].
(2.8.1298) <s>Ārṣabhya</s> is one fit for castration. <s>Ṣaṇḍa</s>, <s>gopati</s>, <s>iṭcara</s> [are names for a castrated bull].

children.text: (2.8.1299) skandhadeśe svasya vahaḥ sāsnā tu galakambalaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1299) [A bull that] carries [loads] on its shoulder region is <s>svavaḥ</s>. <s>Sāsnā</s> is the dewlap.
(2.8.1300) <s>Nastita</s> is one led by a nose-rope (<s>nasyota</s>). <s>Praṣṭhavāḍ</s> is one that goes beside the yoke.
(2.8.1301) Those that draw yokes and the like are <s>yugya</s>, <s>prāsaṃgya</s>, and <s>śākaṭa</s>.
(2.8.1302) It ploughs with that; one who drives that ploughing [animal] — these are <s>hālika</s> and <s>sairika</s> [ploughmen].
(2.8.1303) <s>Dhurya</s>, <s>dhaureya</s>, and <s>dhurīṇa</s> [are synonyms for a yoke-bearer]. <s>Sadhuraṃdhara</s> [also means a yoke-bearer].
(2.8.1304) <s>Ekadhurīṇa</s> and <s>ekadhura</s> [and] <s>ekadhurāvaha</s> [are synonyms for one that bears a single yoke].

children.text: (2.8.1305) sa tu sarvadhurīṇaḥ syādyo vai sarvadhurāvahaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1305) But one who is <s>sarvadhurīṇa</s> (bearing all yokes) is one who indeed bears all yokes (<s>sarvadhurāvaha</s>).

children.text: (2.8.1306) māheyī saurabheyī gaurusrā mātā ca śṛṅgiṇī
children.translated_text: (2.8.1306) <s>Māheyī</s>, <s>saurabheyī</s> — a cow (<s>gaur</s>); <s>usrā</s>, mother, and <s>śṛṅgiṇī</s> (the horned one) [are synonyms].
(2.8.1307) <s>Arjunī</s>, <s>aghnī</s>, <s>rohiṇī</s> [are names of cows]. The best among cows is <s>naucikī</s>.
(2.8.1308) Names based on color and other distinctions would be <s>śabalī</s> (speckled), <s>dhavalā</s> (white), and so on.
(2.8.1309) <s>Dvihāyanī</s> is a two-year-old cow. A one-year-old is <s>ekahāyanī</s>.
(2.8.1310) A four-year-old is <s>caturhāṇī</s>. Likewise a three-year-old is <s>trihāyaṇī</s>.
(2.8.1311) <s>Vaśā</s> is a barren [cow]. <s>Vandhyā</s> and <s>avatokā</s> [also mean barren]. <s>Sravadgarbhā</s> [is one that miscarries]. Then <s>sandhinī</s> [is a cow that has conceived again].
(2.8.1312) <s>Ākrāntā</s> [is a cow] mounted by a bull. <s>Vehad</s> [is a cow] that harms the fetus.
(2.8.1313) <s>Kālyopasaryā</s> [is a cow] to be approached for milking [in the morning]. <s>Praṣṭhauhī</s> is a cow pregnant with her first calf.
(2.8.1314) <s>Acaṇḍī</s> (gentle cow) is called <s>sukarā</s>; one that bears many calves is <s>bahusūti</s> or <s>pareṣṭukā</s>
(2.8.1315) One that calved long ago is <s>baṣkayaṇī</s>; a cow that has recently calved is <s>navasūtikā</s>
(2.8.1316) <s>Suvratā</s> is one easy to milk; <s>pīnodhnī</s> or <s>pīvarastanī</s> means having a full udder
(2.8.1317) <s>Droṇakṣīrā</s> or <s>droṇadugdhā</s> is a cow yielding a <s>droṇa</s> measure of milk; <s>dhenuṣyā</s> means one tied in the <s>bandhaka</s> (stall)
(2.8.1318) <s>Samāṃsamīnā</s> is that very same [cow] that calves every year
(2.8.1319) <s>Ūdhas</s> (udder) is neuter, [also called] <s>āpīna</s>; <s>śivaka</s> and <s>kīlaka</s> (teats) are synonyms

children.text: (2.8.1320) na pumsi dāma sandānaṃ paśurajjustu dāmanī
children.translated_text: (2.8.1320) <s>Dāma</s> or <s>sandāna</s> (tether) is not masculine; an animal rope is <s>dāmanī</s>
(2.8.1321) <s>Vaiśākha</s>, <s>mantha</s>, <s>manthāna</s>, and <s>manthāna</s> denote a churning stick
(2.8.1322) <s>Kuṭhara</s> and <s>daṇḍaviṣkambha</s> [also mean churning stick]; <s>manthanī</s> and <s>gargarī</s> (churning vessel) are synonyms
(2.8.1323) For camel: <s>kramelaka</s>, <s>maya</s>, and <s>mahāṅga</s>; <s>karabha</s> means a young camel
(2.8.1324) <s>Karabhāḥ</s> are [also] called <s>śṛṅkhalakāḥ</s> (those with wooden foot-fetters)
(2.8.1325) A she-goat is <s>ajā</s> or <s>chāgī</s>; <s>śubha</s>, <s>chāga</s>, <s>basta</s>, and <s>chagalaka</s> denote a he-goat
(2.8.1326) <s>Meḍhra</s>, <s>urabhra</s>, <s>uraṇa</s>, <s>ūrṇāyu</s>, <s>meṣa</s>, and <s>vṛṣṇi</s> denote a ram or sheep
(2.8.1327) A herd of camels, sheep, or goats is respectively <s>auṣṭraka</s>, <s>aurabhrika</s>, and <s>ājaka</s>
(2.8.1328) <s>Cakrīvān</s> and <s>vāleya</s> [are synonyms]; <s>rāsabha</s>, <s>gardabha</s>, and <s>khara</s> denote a donkey
(2.8.1329) <s>Vaideha</s>, <s>sārthavāha</s>, <s>naigama</s>, <s>vāṇij</s>, and <s>vaṇik</s> denote a merchant
(2.8.1330) One who lives by trade is <s>āpaṇika</s>; he is also called <s>krayavikrayika</s> (buyer and seller)
(2.8.1331) A seller is <s>vikrayika</s>; <s>krāyika</s> and <s>krayika</s> (buyer) are synonyms

children.text: (2.8.1332) vāṇijyaṃ tu vaṇijyā syān mūlyaṃ vasno 'pyavakrayaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1332) <s>Vāṇijya</s> or <s>vaṇijyā</s> means trade; <s>mūlya</s> and <s>vasna</s> mean price, also <s>avakraya</s>
(2.8.1333) <s>Nīvī</s> and <s>paripaṇa</s> mean principal capital; <s>lābha</s> means profit, the surplus is <s>phala</s> (gain)
(2.8.1334) <s>Paridāna</s> and <s>parīvarta</s> mean exchange; <s>naimeya</s> and <s>niyama</s> also [mean the same]
(2.8.1335) <s>Upanidhi</s> (deposit) is masculine, [also called] <s>nyāsa</s>; <s>pratidāna</s> means returning it
(2.8.1336) <s>Prasārita</s> means displayed for sale, <s>krayya</s> [means buyable]; <s>kreya</s> and <s>kretavya</s> mean merely 'to be bought'
(2.8.1337) <s>Vikreya</s> and <s>paṇitavya</s> mean 'to be sold'; <s>paṇya</s>, <s>krayya</s>, etc. are used in all three genders
(2.8.1338) <s>Satyāpana</s> is neuter, <s>satyaṅkāra</s> [is masculine]; <s>satyākṛti</s> is feminine — [all mean] ratification of a sale

children.text: (2.8.1339) vipaṇo vikrayaḥ saṃkhyāḥ saṃkhyeye hyādaśa triṣu
children.translated_text: (2.8.1339) <s>Vipaṇa</s> means sale; <s>saṃkhyā</s> means number; [terms] up to ten are used in all three genders for countable [things]
(2.8.1340) <s>Viṃśati</s> (twenty) and higher are always singular; all [numerals] apply both to countable things and to [abstract] numbers

children.text: (2.8.1341) saṃkhyārthe dvibahutve stas tāsu cānavateḥ striyaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1341) In the sense of number, dual and plural forms exist; in those [numerals] below a hundred, the feminine [form is used]
(2.8.1342) From <s>paṅkti</s> (ten), <s>śata</s> (hundred), <s>sahasra</s> (thousand), etc., each is successively ten times greater
(2.8.1343) <s>Yautava</s>, <s>druvaya</s>, and <s>pāyya</s> — these three terms relate to measurement
(2.8.1344) <s>Māna</s> (measure) [is expressed] by <s>tulā</s> (balance), <s>aṅguli</s> (finger-breadth), and <s>prastha</s> (volume measure); five <s>guñjā</s> seeds make one <s>māṣaka</s>
(2.8.1345) Sixteen of those make one <s>akṣa</s> or <s>karṣa</s> (not feminine); a <s>pala</s> equals four <s>karṣas</s>
(2.8.1346) <s>Suvarṇa</s> and <s>bista</s> denote one <s>akṣa</s>-weight of gold; <s>kurubista</s> means one <s>pala</s>-weight of that [gold]
(2.8.1347) <s>Tulā</s> (feminine) equals one hundred <s>palas</s>; a <s>bhāra</s> equals twenty <s>tulās</s>

children.text: (2.8.1348) ācito daśa bhārāḥ syuḥ śākaṭo bhāra ācitaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1348) An <s>ācita</s> equals ten <s>bhāras</s>; a <s>śākaṭa</s> (cartload) is one <s>bhāra</s> [equivalent to] one <s>ācita</s>

children.text: (2.8.1349) kārṣāpaṇaḥ kārṣikaḥ syāt kārṣike tāmrike paṇaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1349) A <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> is [also] called <s>kārṣika</s>; <s>paṇa</s> refers to a <s>kārṣika</s> of copper
(2.8.1350) <s>Āḍhaka</s> and <s>droṇa</s> (not feminine), <s>khārī</s>, <s>vāha</s>, and <s>nikuñcaka</s> [are volume measures]
(2.8.1351) <s>Kuḍava</s>, <s>prastha</s>, and so forth are terms denoting measurement, [each] separate
(2.8.1352) <s>Pāda</s> means a quarter portion; <s>aṃśa</s> and <s>bhāga</s> mean a share or portion

children.text: (2.8.1353) dravyaṃ vittaṃ svāpateyaṃ rikthamṛkthaṃ dhanaṃ vasu
children.translated_text: (2.8.1353) <s>Dravya</s>, <s>vitta</s>, <s>svāpateya</s>, <s>riktham</s>, <s>ṛktham</s>, <s>dhana</s>, and <s>vasu</s> denote wealth
(2.8.1354) <s>Hiraṇya</s>, <s>draviṇa</s>, <s>dyumna</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>rai</s>, and <s>vibhava</s> also [denote wealth]
(2.8.1355) <s>Kośa</s> and <s>hiraṇya</s> also [refer to] gold and silver, wrought or unwrought

children.text: (2.8.1356) tābhyāṃ yadanyat tatkupyaṃ rūpyaṃ tad dvayamāhatam
children.translated_text: (2.8.1356) Whatever is other than those two is <s>kupya</s> (base metal); <s>rūpya</s> (silver) is that pair when stamped
(2.8.1357) <s>Gārutmata</s>, <s>marakata</s>, <s>aśmagarbha</s>, and <s>harinmaṇi</s> denote emerald
(2.8.1358) <s>Śoṇaratna</s> and <s>lohitaka</s> mean ruby, [also] <s>padmarāga</s>; then <s>mauktika</s> [means pearl]
(2.8.1359) <s>Muktā</s> also [means pearl]; then <s>vidruma</s> is masculine, <s>pravāla</s> (coral) is also neuter
(2.8.1360) <s>Ratna</s> and <s>maṇi</s> are used in both [masculine and neuter] genders, for the class including gems, pearls, and the like
(2.8.1361) <s>Svarṇa</s>, <s>suvarṇa</s>, <s>kanaka</s>, <s>hiraṇya</s>, <s>hema</s>, and <s>kāṭaka</s> [denote gold]
(2.8.1362) <s>Tapanīya</s>, <s>śātakumbha</s>, <s>gāṅgeya</s>, <s>bharma</s>, and <s>karvura</s> [also denote gold]
(2.8.1363) <s>Cāmīkara</s>, <s>jātarūpa</s>, <s>mahārajata</s>, and <s>kāñcana</s> [also denote gold]
(2.8.1364) <s>Rukma</s>, <s>kārtasvara</s>, <s>jāmbūnada</s>, and <s>aṣṭāpada</s> (not feminine) [also denote gold]
(2.8.1365) Ornamental gold is called <s>śṛṅgī</s>; <s>kanaka</s> is also [used] thus
(2.8.1366) <s>Durvarṇa</s>, <s>rajata</s>, <s>rūpya</s>, <s>kharjūra</s>, and <s>śveta</s> denote silver
(2.8.1367) <s>Rīti</s> (feminine) means brass; <s>ārakūṭa</s> (not feminine) [also means brass]; then <s>tāmraka</s> [means copper]
(2.8.1368) <s>Śulba</s>, <s>mlecchamukha</s>, <s>dvyaṣṭa</s>, <s>variṣṭa</s>, and <s>udumbara</s> also [denote copper]
(2.8.1369) <s>Loha</s> (not feminine) means iron; <s>śastraka</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, <s>piṇḍa</s>, <s>kālāyasa</s>, and <s>ayasī</s> [also mean iron]
(2.8.1370) <s>Aśmasāra</s> also [means iron]; then <s>maṇḍūra</s> and <s>siṃhāṇa</s> refer to its rust or impurity

children.text: (2.8.1371) sarvaṃ ca taijasaṃ lauhaṃ vikārastvayasaḥ kuśī
children.translated_text: (2.8.1371) Everything made of metal is <s>lauha</s>; a product made of iron is <s>kuśī</s>

children.text: (2.8.1372) kṣāraḥ kāco 'tha capalo rasaḥ sūtaśca pārade
children.translated_text: (2.8.1372) <s>Kṣāra</s> means alkali, [also] <s>kāca</s> (glass); then <s>capala</s>, <s>rasa</s>, and <s>sūta</s> denote mercury (<s>pārada</s>)
(2.8.1373) <s>Gavala</s> and <s>māhiṣa</s> denote buffalo horn; <s>abhraka</s> and <s>girijā</s> denote mica, [used as] a collyrium
(2.8.1374) <s>Srotoñjana</s> is called <s>mauvīra</s>; [the words] <s>kāpota</s> and <s>añjana</s> [denote another variety]
(2.8.1375) <s>Tutthāñjana</s> and <s>śikhigrīva</s> [denote blue vitriol]; <s>vitunnaka</s> and <s>māyūraka</s> [are synonyms]
(2.8.1376) <s>Karparī</s> [is a collyrium]; that produced from a forest fire is <s>tuttha</s> or <s>rasāñjana</s>
(2.8.1377) <s>Rasagarbha</s> and <s>tārkṣyaśaila</s> [are synonyms]; for sulphur (<s>gandhāśman</s>): <s>gandhika</s>
(2.8.1378) Also <s>saugandhika</s>; <s>cakṣuṣyā</s> and <s>kulālī</s> [are synonyms], also <s>kulatthikā</s>
(2.8.1379) <s>Rītipuṣpa</s> means verdigris; for flower-shaped [antimony]: <s>puṣpaka</s> and <s>kusumāñjana</s>
(2.8.1380) <s>Piñjara</s>, <s>pītana</s>, <s>tāla</s>, and <s>māla</s> denote orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>)
(2.8.1381) <s>Gaireya</s>, <s>arthya</s>, <s>girija</s>, <s>aśmaja</s> — and <s>śilājatu</s> (bitumen) [is another mineral]
(2.8.1382) <s>Vola</s>, <s>gandha</s>, <s>rasa</s>, <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>piṇḍa</s>, and <s>goparasa</s> are synonyms [for bdellium/guggulu]
(2.8.1383) <s>Ḍiṇḍīra</s>, <s>abdhikapha</s>, and <s>phena</s> [mean cuttle-bone/sea-foam]; <s>sindūra</s> means red lead, produced from <s>nāga</s> (lead)
(2.8.1384) <s>Nāga</s>, <s>sīsaka</s>, and <s>yogeṣṭa</s> [denote lead]; <s>vapra</s> [is also a synonym]; <s>piñcaṭa</s> is used in all three genders
(2.8.1385) <s>Raṅga</s> and <s>vaṅga</s> [denote tin]; then <s>picu</s> means cotton, [also] <s>tūla</s>; then <s>kamalottara</s>
(2.8.1386) means safflower (<s>kusumbha</s>), [also called] <s>vahniśikha</s> and <s>mahārajana</s>
(2.8.1387) <s>Meṣakambala</s> means wool; <s>ūrṇāyu</s> [also means wool]; <s>śaśorṇa</s> means rabbit fur

children.text: (2.8.1388) madhu kṣaudraṃ mākṣikādi madhūcchiṣṭaṃ tu sikthakam
children.translated_text: (2.8.1388) <s>Madhu</s>, <s>kṣaudra</s>, and <s>mākṣika</s> etc. [denote honey]; <s>madhūcchiṣṭa</s> (beeswax) is called <s>sikthaka</s>
(2.8.1389) <s>Manaḥśilā</s>, <s>manoguptā</s>, <s>manohvā</s>, and <s>nāgajihvikā</s> [denote realgar/red arsenic]
(2.8.1390) <s>Naipālī</s>, <s>kunaṭī</s>, and <s>golā</s> [also mean realgar]; <s>yavakṣāra</s> and <s>yavāgraja</s> [denote saltpeter]
(2.8.1391) <s>Pākya</s> [is also a synonym]; then <s>sarjikā-kṣāra</s> [means soda-ash]; <s>kāpota</s> and <s>sukhavarcaka</s> [are synonyms]
(2.8.1392) <s>Sauvarcala</s> means black salt, [also called] <s>rucaka</s>; <s>tvakkṣīrī</s> and <s>vaṃśarocanā</s> [denote bamboo camphor]
(2.8.1393) <s>Śigruja</s> and <s>śvetamārica</s> [denote white pepper from the moringa tree]; <s>moraṭa</s> means sugarcane root
(2.8.1394) <s>Granthika</s> means long pepper root (<s>pippalīmūla</s>), also called <s>caṭikāśira</s>
(2.8.1395) <s>Golomī</s> and <s>bhūtakeśa</s> are masculine; <s>patrāṅga</s> means red sandalwood

children.text: (2.8.1396) trikaṭu tryūpaṇaṃ vyopaṃ triphalā tu phalatrikam
children.translated_text: (2.8.1396) <s>Trikaṭu</s> (the three pungents) is [also called] <s>tryūṣaṇa</s> and <s>vyoṣa</s>; <s>triphalā</s> (the three fruits) is called <s>phalatrika</s>
Thus ends the <s>Vaiśyavarga</s> (section on the merchant class), the 9th [section]; it contains 111 root verses.
<s>Śūdravarga</s> (section on the laborer class):

children.text: (2.8.1397) śūdrāś cāvaravarṇāś ca vṛṣalāś ca jaghanyajāḥ | atha śūdravargaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1397) <s>Śūdra</s>, <s>avaravarṇa</s> (of lower caste), <s>vṛṣala</s>, and <s>jaghanyaja</s> (lowest-born) [are synonyms]. Now begins the <s>Śūdravarga</s>.
(2.8.1398) From [the union producing] a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> downward, the mixed castes are <s>Ambaṣṭha</s>, <s>Karaṇa</s>, and others
(2.8.1399) From a <s>Śūdra</s> [father] and a <s>Vaiśya</s> [mother] is born the <s>Karaṇa</s>; the <s>Ambaṣṭha</s> is from a <s>Vaiśya</s> [father] and a twice-born [Brāhmaṇa mother]
(2.8.1400) From a <s>Śūdra</s> [father] and a <s>Kṣatriya</s> [mother] is born the <s>Ugra</s>; the <s>Māgadha</s> is from a <s>Kṣatriya</s> [father] and a <s>Vaiśya</s> [mother]
(2.8.1401) The <s>Māhiṣa</s> is from an <s>Ārya</s> [Brāhmaṇa father] and a <s>Kṣatriya</s> [mother]; the <s>Kṣattṛ</s> is the son of an <s>Ārya</s> [Brāhmaṇa] woman and a <s>Śūdra</s> [man]

children.text: (2.8.1402) brāhmaṇyāṃ kṣatriyāt sūtas tasyāṃ vaidehako viśaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1402) From a <s>Kṣatriya</s> [father] and a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> [mother] is born the <s>Sūta</s>; from her [a Brāhmaṇī] and a <s>Vaiśya</s> is born the <s>Vaideha</s>

children.text: (2.8.1403) rathakāras tu māhiṣyāt karaṇyāṃ yasya saṃbhavaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1403) The <s>Rathakāra</s> (chariot-maker) is one whose origin is from a <s>Māhiṣya</s> [father] and a <s>Karaṇī</s> [mother]

children.text: (2.8.1404) syāc caṇḍālas tu janito brāhmaṇyāṃ vṛṣalena yaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1404) A <s>Caṇḍāla</s> is one who is born from a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> [mother] and a <s>Vṛṣala</s> (Śūdra) [father]

children.text: (2.8.1405) kāruḥ śilpī saṃhatais tair dvayoḥ śreṇiḥ sajātibhiḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1405) <s>Kāru</s> and <s>śilpin</s> mean an artisan; a group of them of the same caste is called a <s>śreṇi</s> (guild)

children.text: (2.8.1406) kulakaḥ syāt kulaśreṣṭhī mālākāras tu mālikaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1406) <s>Kulaka</s> means the head of a guild, [also] <s>kulaśreṣṭhin</s>; a garland-maker is <s>mālākāra</s> or <s>mālika</s>

children.text: (2.8.1407) kumbhakāraḥ kulālaḥ syāt palagaṇḍas tu lepakaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1407) A potter is <s>kumbhakāra</s> or <s>kulāla</s>; a plasterer is <s>palagaṇḍa</s> or <s>lepaka</s>

children.text: (2.8.1408) tantuvāyaḥ kuvindaḥ syāt tunnavāyas tu saucikaḥ
