children.translated_text: (2.8.1408) A weaver is <s>tantuvāya</s> or <s>kuvinda</s>; a tailor is <s>tunnavāya</s> or <s>saucika</s>
(2.8.1409) A dyer is <s>raṅgājīva</s>, a painter is <s>citrakara</s>; a sword-polisher is <s>śastramārja</s> or <s>asidhāvaka</s>
(2.8.1410) A shoemaker is <s>pādakṛt</s> or <s>carmakāra</s>; a blacksmith is <s>vyokāra</s> or <s>lohakāraka</s>
(2.8.1411) A goldsmith is <s>nāḍindhama</s> or <s>svarṇakāra</s>; [also] <s>kalāda</s> or <s>rukmakāraka</s>
(2.8.1412) A conch-worker is <s>śāṅkhika</s> or <s>kāmbavika</s>; a coppersmith is <s>śaulbika</s> or <s>tāmrakuṭṭaka</s>

children.text: (2.8.1413) takṣā tu vardhakis tvaṣṭā rathakāraś ca kāṣṭhataṭ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1413) A carpenter is <s>takṣan</s>, <s>vardhaki</s>, <s>tvaṣṭṛ</s>, and <s>rathakāra</s> — one who works with wood
(2.8.1414) One dependent on a village is <s>grāmatakṣa</s> (village carpenter); an independent one is <s>kauṭatakṣa</s>
(2.8.1415) <s>Kṣurin</s>, <s>muṇḍin</s>, <s>divākīrti</s>, <s>nāpita</s>, and <s>antāvasāyin</s> denote a barber
(2.8.1416) A washerman is <s>nirṇejaka</s> or <s>rajaka</s>; a distiller is <s>śauṇḍika</s> or <s>maṇḍahāraka</s>
(2.8.1417) <s>Jābāla</s> means a goatherd; one who lives by [serving] gods is <s>devājīva</s> or <s>devala</s>

children.text: (2.8.1418) syān māyā śāmbarī māyākāras tu pratihārakaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1418) <s>Māyā</s> is illusion, [also called] <s>śāmbarī</s>; a magician is <s>māyākāra</s> or <s>pratihāraka</s>
(2.8.1419) <s>Śailālin</s> means actors; those who live by their wives are <s>kṛśāśvin</s> (poor)

children.text: (2.8.1420) bharatā ityapi naṭāś cāraṇās tu kuśīlavāḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1420) <s>Bharata</s> is another [name]; <s>naṭa</s> means actors; <s>cāraṇa</s> and <s>kuśīlava</s> denote wandering performers
(2.8.1421) <s>Mārdaṅgika</s> and <s>maurajika</s> mean drum players; hand-drummers are <s>pāṇivāda</s> or <s>pāṇigha</s>

children.text: (2.8.1422) veṇudhmāḥ syur vaiṇavikā vīṇāvādās tu vaiṇikāḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1422) Flute players are <s>veṇudhmā</s> or <s>vaiṇavika</s>; lute players are <s>vīṇāvāda</s> or <s>vaiṇika</s>
(2.8.1423) A bird-catcher is <s>jīvāntaka</s> or <s>śākunika</s>; <s>vāgurika</s> and <s>jālika</s> (net-catcher) are a pair

children.text: (2.8.1424) vaitaṃsikaḥ kauṭikaś ca māṃsikaś ca samaṃ trayam
children.translated_text: (2.8.1424) <s>Vaitaṃsika</s>, <s>kauṭika</s>, and <s>māṃsika</s> (butcher) — these three are synonyms
(2.8.1425) <s>Bhṛtaka</s> and <s>bhṛtibhuk</s> mean a hired laborer; <s>karmakara</s> and <s>vaitanika</s> also [denote the same]
(2.8.1426) <s>Vārtāvaha</s> and <s>vaivadhika</s> [mean a porter]; <s>bhāravāha</s> and <s>bhārika</s> mean a burden-carrier

children.text: (2.8.1427) vivarṇaḥ pāmaro nīcaḥ prākṛtaś ca pṛthagjanaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1427) <s>Vivarṇa</s>, <s>pāmara</s>, <s>nīca</s>, <s>prākṛta</s>, and <s>pṛthagjana</s> mean a common or low person

children.text: (2.8.1428) nihīno 'pasado jālmaḥ kṣullakaś cetaraś ca saḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1428) <s>Nihīna</s>, <s>apasada</s>, <s>jālma</s>, <s>kṣullaka</s>, and <s>itara</s> also [denote the same]
(2.8.1429) For a servant: <s>dāsa</s>, <s>eradāseya</s>, <s>dāsa</s>, <s>gopya</s>, and <s>ceṭaka</s>
(2.8.1430) <s>Niyojya</s>, <s>kiṅkara</s>, <s>praiṣya</s>, <s>bhujiṣya</s>, and <s>paricāraka</s> [also mean servant]
(2.8.1431) <s>Parācita</s>, <s>pariskanda</s>, <s>parajāta</s>, and <s>paraidhita</s> [also mean servant — one reared or born in another's house]
(2.8.1432) <s>Mānda</s>, <s>tundaparimṛja</s> (licking the belly), <s>ālasya</s>, <s>śītaka</s>, <s>alasa</s>, and <s>anuṣṇa</s> denote a lazy person

children.text: (2.8.1433) dakṣe tu caturapeśalapaṭavaḥ sūtthāna uṣṇaś ca
children.translated_text: (2.8.1433) For a skillful person: <s>catura</s>, <s>apeśala</s>, and <s>paṭava</s> [are synonyms]; <s>sūtthāna</s> and <s>uṣṇa</s> also [mean diligent]
(2.8.1434) <s>Caṇḍāla</s>, <s>plava</s>, <s>mātaṅga</s>, <s>divākīrti</s>, and <s>janaṅgama</s> [are synonyms for outcaste]
(2.8.1435) <s>Nipāda</s>, <s>śvapaca</s>, <s>antevāsin</s>, <s>cāṇḍāla</s>, and <s>pukkasa</s> [also denote outcastes]
(2.8.1436) [These are their] subtypes. <s>Kirāta</s>, <s>Śabara</s>, and <s>Pulinda</s> are <s>mleccha</s> (barbarian) tribes
(2.8.1437) A hunter is <s>vyādha</s>, one who lives by killing deer, [also] <s>mṛgayu</s> and <s>lubdhaka</s>
(2.8.1438) <s>Kauleyaka</s>, <s>sārameya</s>, <s>kukkura</s>, and <s>mṛgadaṃśaka</s> [denote a dog]

children.text: (2.8.1439) śunako bhapakaḥ śvā syādalarkas tu sa yogitaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1439) <s>Śunaka</s> and <s>bhapaka</s> [also mean dog]; <s>śvan</s> is [the general term]; <s>alarka</s> means a rabid one
(2.8.1440) <s>Śvan</s> [is also called] <s>viśvakadru</s>; one skilled in hunting is [a hunting dog]; <s>Saramā</s> is a female dog

children.text: (2.8.1441) viṭcaraḥ sūkaro grāmyo varkaras taruṇaḥ paśuḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1441) <s>Viṭcara</s> and <s>sūkara</s> mean a pig; <s>grāmya</s> [means domestic]; <s>varkara</s> means a young animal
(2.8.1442) <s>Ācchodana</s> and <s>mṛgavya</s> mean hunting; <s>ākheṭa</s> and <s>mṛgayā</s> (feminine) [also mean hunting]
(2.8.1443) <s>Dakṣiṇāru</s> [denotes a decoy deer] trained by hunting; <s>dakṣiṇerma</s> and <s>kuraṅgaka</s> [are synonyms]
(2.8.1444) <s>Caura</s>, <s>ekāgārika</s>, <s>stena</s>, <s>dasyu</s>, <s>taskara</s>, and <s>mopaka</s> denote a thief
(2.8.1445) <s>Pratirodhī</s>, <s>parāskandin</s>, <s>pāṭaccara</s>, and <s>malimluca</s> [also denote a thief]

children.text: (2.8.1446) caurikā stainyacaurye ca steyaṃ loptraṃ tu taddhane
children.translated_text: (2.8.1446) <s>Caurikā</s> means theft; <s>stainya</s> and <s>caurya</s> also [mean theft]; <s>steya</s> and <s>loptra</s> mean the stolen property
(2.8.1447) <s>Vītaṃsa</s> means a snare; <s>upakaraṇa</s> means a device for trapping deer and birds
(2.8.1448) <s>Unmātha</s> and <s>kūṭayantra</s> denote a decoy trap; <s>vāgurā</s> means a net for catching deer

children.text: (2.8.1449) śulbaṃ varāṭakaṃ strī tu rajjus triṣu vaṭī guṇaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1449) <s>Śulba</s> and <s>varāṭaka</s> [mean cord]; <s>rajju</s> (rope) is feminine; in all three genders: <s>vaṭī</s> and <s>guṇa</s> (string)
(2.8.1450) <s>Udghāṭana</s> means a bucket-wheel device, a water-raising mechanism, [operated] by a lever

children.text: (2.8.1451) puṃsi vemā vāyadaṇḍaḥ sūtrāṇi nari tantavaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1451) <s>Vemā</s> (masculine) means a weaver's shuttle or loom-rod; <s>sūtrāṇi</s> (threads) [is neuter]; <s>tantava</s> (warp-threads) is feminine

children.text: (2.8.1452) vāṇir vyūtiḥ striyau tulye pustaṃ lepyādikarmaṇi
children.translated_text: (2.8.1452) <s>Vāṇi</s> and <s>vyūti</s> are feminine synonyms; <s>pusta</s> means work such as plastering and the like
(2.8.1453) <s>Pāñcālikā</s> or <s>puttrikā</s> means a doll, made of cloth, teeth [ivory], and other materials
(2.8.1454) For products made of lac or tin: <s>jātupa</s> and <s>trāpuṣa</s>, used in all three genders
(2.8.1455) <s>Piṭaka</s>, <s>peṭaka</s>, and <s>peṭā</s> mean a basket; <s>mañjūṣā</s> [means a chest]; then <s>vihaṅgikā</s>
(2.8.1456) <s>Bhārayaṣṭi</s> means a carrying pole; that which hangs from it is <s>śikya</s> (sling); <s>kāca</s> [means glass]; then <s>pādukā</s> (sandal)
(2.8.1457) <s>Pādū</s> and <s>upānat</s> (feminine) [mean sandal]; that same [sandal] when extended over the foot is <s>anupadīnā</s> and <s>padāyatā</s>

children.text: (2.8.1458) naddhnī vardhnī varatrā syādaśvādes tāḍanī kaśā
children.translated_text: (2.8.1458) <s>Naddhnī</s>, <s>vardhnī</s>, and <s>varatrā</s> are [synonyms for] a leather strap; <s>kaśā</s> is a whip for striking horses and the like.
(2.8.1459) <s>Cāṇḍālikā</s> is a <s>kaṇḍola</s> (a type of lute); <s>caṇḍālavallakī</s> is a lute [played by <s>Caṇḍālas</s>].

children.text: (2.8.1460) nārācī syādeṣaṇikā śāṇas tu nikaṣaḥ kaṣaḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1460) <s>Nārācī</s> is an iron probe (<s>eṣaṇikā</s>); <s>śāṇa</s> is a touchstone (<s>nikaṣa</s>, <s>kaṣa</s>).
(2.8.1461) <s>Vraścana</s> is a hatchet (<s>patraparaśu</s>); <s>ṛpikā</s> and <s>tūlikā</s> are synonymous [for a chisel or pointed tool].
(2.8.1462) <s>Taijasāvartanī</s> is a crucible (<s>mūṣā</s>); <s>bhastrā</s> is a leather bellows (<s>carmaprasevikā</s>).
(2.8.1463) <s>Āsphoṭanī</s> is a punch (<s>vedhanikā</s>); <s>kṛpāṇī</s> and <s>kartarī</s> are synonymous [for scissors or shears].
(2.8.1464) <s>Vṛkṣādanī</s> and <s>vṛkṣabhedī</s> [are synonyms]; <s>ṭaṅka</s> is a stone-chisel (<s>pāṣāṇadāraṇa</s>).
(2.8.1465) <s>Krakaca</s> (not feminine) is a saw (<s>karapatra</s>); <s>ārā</s> is an awl (<s>carmaprabhedhikā</s>, a leather-piercing tool).
(2.8.1466) <s>Sūrmī</s> is an iron pillar or anvil (<s>sthūṇā-yaḥpratimā</s>); <s>śilpa</s> is craft or skill (<s>karma</s>, <s>kalā</s>, etc.).
(2.8.1467) <s>Pratimāna</s>, <s>pratibimba</s>, <s>pratimā</s>, <s>pratiyātanā</s>, and <s>praticchāyā</s>,

(2.8.1468) <s>Pratikṛti</s>, and <s>arcā</s> [are synonyms for an image or idol]; in the masculine, <s>pratinidhi</s> [means a substitute]; <s>upamā</s> and <s>upamāna</s> [mean a comparison or standard of likeness].

children.text: (2.8.1469) vācyaliṅgāḥ samas tulyaḥ sadṛkṣaḥ sadṛśaḥ sadṛk
children.translated_text: (2.8.1469) Having the gender of the word they qualify: <s>sama</s>, <s>tulya</s>, <s>sadṛkṣa</s>, <s>sadṛśa</s>, <s>sadṛk</s>,
(2.8.1470) <s>sādhāraṇa</s>, and <s>samāna</s> [all mean 'equal' or 'similar']; but these [following words] occur as the latter member of a compound:
(2.8.1471) <s>nibha</s>, <s>saṃkāśa</s>, <s>nīkāśa</s>, <s>pratīkāśa</s>, <s>upama</s>, and the like [all mean 'resembling'].
(2.8.1472) For wages: <s>vidhā</s>, <s>abhṛti</s> (also <s>abhṛtā</s>), <s>bharma</s>, and <s>vetana</s>,

children.text: (2.8.1473) bharaṇyaṃ bharaṇaṃ mūlyaṃ nirveśaḥ paṇa ityapi
children.translated_text: (2.8.1473) <s>bharaṇya</s>, <s>bharaṇa</s>, <s>mūlya</s>, <s>nirveśa</s>, and <s>paṇa</s> — [all mean 'wages' or 'price'].
(2.8.1474) <s>Surā</s> (liquor): <s>halipriyā</s>, <s>hālā</s>, <s>parisrut</s>, <s>varuṇātmajā</s>,
(2.8.1475) <s>gandhottamā</s>, <s>prasannā</s>, <s>irā</s>, <s>kādambarī</s> [are synonyms]; <s>parisrutā</s> [is another synonym for liquor].
(2.8.1476) <s>Madirā</s> and <s>kaśya</s> are also [used for] liquor; <s>avadaṃśa</s> is a snack or appetizer (<s>bhakṣaṇa</s>).
(2.8.1477) <s>Śuṇḍā</s> is a drinking hall (<s>pāna</s>, <s>madasthāna</s>); <s>madhuvārā</s> and <s>madhukrama</s> [are synonyms for distilled honey-liquor].
(2.8.1478) <s>Madhvāsava</s>, <s>mādhavaka</s>, <s>madhu</s>, and <s>mādhvīka</s> — these two [pairs apply to honey-wine].
(2.8.1479) <s>Maireya</s>, <s>āsava</s> [are types of liquor]; <s>sīdhu</s>, <s>mandaka</s>, and <s>jagala</s> are synonymous [for another kind of fermented drink].

children.text: (2.8.1480) sandhānaṃ syādabhiṣavaḥ kiṇvaṃ puṃsi tu nagnahūḥ
children.translated_text: (2.8.1480) <s>Sandhāna</s> is fermentation (<s>abhiṣava</s>); <s>kiṇva</s> (masculine) is yeast; and <s>nagnahū</s> [is also yeast].
(2.8.1481) <s>Kārottara</s> is the scum of liquor (<s>surāmaṇḍa</s>); <s>āpāna</s> is a drinking party (<s>pānaghoṣṭhikā</s>).
(2.8.1482) <s>Capaka</s> (not feminine) is a drinking vessel (<s>pānapātra</s>); <s>saraka</s> is also [a cup]; <s>anutarṣaṇa</s> [is another synonym].
(2.8.1483) <s>Dhūrta</s>, <s>akṣadevī</s> (a dice-player), <s>kitava</s>, <s>akṣadhūrta</s>, and <s>dyūtakṛt</s> are synonymous [for a gambler].
(2.8.1484) <s>Lagnaka</s> and <s>pratibhū</s> [mean a surety or guarantor]; <s>sabhika</s> and <s>dyūtakāraka</s> [mean the keeper of a gambling house].
(2.8.1485) <s>Dyūta</s> (not feminine) is gambling; <s>akṣavatī</s> [is the same]; <s>kaitava</s> and <s>paṇa</s> are also [terms for gambling or a stake].

children.text: (2.8.1486) paṇo 'kṣeṣu glaho 'kṣās tu devanāḥ pāśakāś ca te
children.translated_text: (2.8.1486) <s>Paṇa</s> in the context of dice [means a wager]; <s>glaha</s> [is also a wager]; <s>akṣa</s> [means dice]; they are [also called] <s>devanā</s> and <s>pāśaka</s>.
(2.8.1487) <s>Pariṇāya</s> is the moving of chess-pieces all around [the board]; it is not feminine.
(2.8.1488) <s>Aṣṭāpada</s> is a chess-board; <s>śāriphala</s> is [the outcome of] a game of chess; <s>prāṇivṛtta</s> and <s>samāhvaya</s> [mean a wager or contest involving living beings].
(2.8.1489) Those [terms] that are derivable by etymology have been stated here because of their frequent usage in a single [meaning];
(2.8.1490) By analogy they may be applied in other contexts too, and even in other genders.
Thus ends the <s>Śūdravarga</s> (section on the <s>Śūdra</s> class), the 10th [section]. Here the root verses number 46. End of section.
(2.8.1491) Thus in the <s>Nāmaliṅgānuśāsana</s> composed by <s>Amarasiṃha</s>, the second <s>kāṇḍa</s> (chapter),
(2.8.1492) beginning with 'earth' (<s>bhūmyādi</s>), has been fully expounded together with its subdivisions. Here the root verses number 735.

children.translated_text: (2.8.1493) And all together 750. First <s>kāṇḍa</s> root verses 281. End-section verses 18, all together 299.

children.translated_text: <s>Amarakośa</s>, also known as <s>Nāmaliṅgānuśāsana</s>, <s>Kāṇḍa</s> 3. The third chapter, the <s>Sāmānyakāṇḍa</s> (General Chapter). Now begins the <s>Viśeṣyanighnavarga</s> (section on adjectival qualifiers).

children.translated_text: (3.1.102) Gods (<s>deva</s>) are born by spontaneous apparition (<s>upapāduka</s>); humans, cattle, and the like are born from the womb (<s>jarāyuja</s>).
(3.1.103) Worms, gnats, and the like are born from moisture (<s>svedaja</s>); birds, serpents, and the like are born from eggs (<s>aṇḍaja</s>).
Thus ends the <s>Prāṇivarga</s> (section on living beings). Here the root verses number 50.

(3.0.3-4) Whatever noun is qualified by such words as <s>strī</s> (woman), <s>dāra</s> (wife), etc. — words denoting qualities, substances, and actions serve as its differentiators. (3.1.5) [Now begins] the <s>Viśeṣyanighnavarga</s>. (3.1.6) <s>Kṣemaṅkara</s>, <s>ariṣṭatāti</s>, <s>śivatāti</s>, <s>śivaṅkara</s> [mean 'one who brings welfare']. (3.1.7) <s>Sukṛtī</s>, <s>puṇyavān</s>, <s>dhanya</s> [mean 'meritorious' or 'fortunate']; <s>mahecchas</s> is <s>mahāśaya</s> (magnanimous). (3.1.8) <s>Hṛdayālu</s> is tender-hearted (<s>suhṛdaya</s>); <s>mahotsāha</s> is one of great effort (<s>mahodyama</s>). (3.1.9) For one who is skilled: <s>nipuṇa</s>, <s>abhijña</s>, <s>vijña</s>, <s>niṣṇāta</s>, <s>śikṣita</s>. (3.1.10) <s>Vaijñānika</s>, <s>kṛtamukha</s>, <s>kṛtī</s>, and <s>kuśala</s> also [mean 'skilled' or 'learned']. (3.1.11) <s>Pūjya</s> means 'worthy of worship'; <s>pratīkṣya</s> means 'to be waited upon'; <s>sāṃśayika</s> is one whose mind has fallen into doubt. (3.1.12) <s>Dakṣiṇīya</s> and <s>dakṣiṇārha</s> [mean 'worthy of a gift']; in that sense <s>dakṣiṇya</s> is also [used]. (3.1.13) <s>Vadānya</s>, <s>sthūlalakṣya</s>, and <s>dānaśauṇḍa</s> [are synonyms] for one who gives abundantly. (3.1.14) <s>Jaivātṛka</s> means long-lived (<s>āyuṣmān</s>); <s>antarvāṇī</s> means one learned in the scriptures (<s>śāstravit</s>). (3.1.15) <s>Parīkṣaka</s> is an examiner (<s>kāraṇika</s>); <s>varada</s> means one who bestows boons (<s>samardhaka</s>). (3.1.16) <s>Harṣamāṇa</s> and <s>vikurvāṇa</s> [mean 'rejoicing']; <s>pramanā</s> and <s>hṛṣṭamānasa</s> [mean 'glad-hearted']. (3.1.17) <s>Durmanā</s> and <s>vimanā</s> [mean 'sad-hearted']; <s>antarmanā</s> means 'anxious' (<s>utka</s>, <s>unmanā</s>). (3.1.18) In [the sense of] 'upright': <s>sarala</s> and <s>udāra</s>; <s>sukala</s> [means] both a giver and an enjoyer. (3.1.19) <s>Tatpara</s>, <s>prasita</s>, <s>āsakta</s>, <s>iṣṭārtha</s>, <s>udyukta</s>, and <s>utsuka</s> [mean 'devoted to' or 'eager']. (3.1.20) For one who is well-known: <s>prathita</s>, <s>khyāta</s>, <s>vitta</s>, <s>vijñāta</s>, <s>viśruta</s>. (3.1.21) For one recognized by qualities: <s>kṛtalakṣaṇa</s> and <s>āhatalakṣaṇa</s>. (3.1.22) <s>Ibhya</s>, <s>āḍhya</s>, <s>dhanī</s>, <s>svāmī</s> [mean 'wealthy' or 'master']; <s>īśvara</s>, <s>pati</s>, <s>īśitṛ</s>, (3.1.23) <s>adhibhū</s>, <s>nāyaka</s>, <s>netṛ</s>, <s>prabhu</s>, <s>parivṛḍha</s>, and <s>adhipa</s> [mean 'lord' or 'ruler']. (3.1.24) <s>Adhikardhi</s> means 'prosperous' (<s>samṛddha</s>); one who is occupied with household affairs — (3.1.25) he is <s>abhyāgārika</s>; <s>upādhi</s> also [means 'manager']; this [word] is masculine. (3.1.26) One who possesses excellent bodily form is <s>siṃhasaṃhanana</s> (having a lion-like frame). (3.1.27) <s>Nirvārya</s> is one who gets things done; <s>saṃpanna</s> is one endowed with excellence of character. (3.1.28) <s>Avāc</s> and <s>mūka</s> [mean 'dumb']; <s>manojavasa</s> [means] 'swift as thought'; <s>pitṛsaṃnibha</s> [means 'resembling one's father']. (3.1.29) One who gives a daughter adorned and honored — he is <s>kūkuda</s>. (3.1.30) <s>Lakṣmīvān</s>, <s>lakṣmaṇa</s>, <s>śrīla</s>, <s>śrīmān</s> [mean 'prosperous']; <s>snigdha</s> means 'affectionate' (<s>vatsala</s>). (3.1.31) <s>Dayālu</s>, <s>kāruṇika</s>, <s>kṛpālu</s>, and <s>sūrata</s> are synonymous [for 'compassionate']. (3.1.32) <s>Svatantra</s>, <s>apāvṛta</s>, <s>svairī</s>, <s>svacchanda</s>, and <s>niravagraha</s> [mean 'independent' or 'free']. (3.1.33) <s>Paratantra</s>, <s>parādhīna</s>, <s>paravān</s>, and <s>nāthavān</s> also [mean 'dependent on another']. (3.1.34) <s>Adhīna</s>, <s>nighna</s>, <s>āyatta</s>, <s>asvacchanda</s>, and <s>gṛhyaka</s> also [mean 'dependent']. (3.1.35) <s>Khalapū</s> means one who does much work (<s>bahukara</s>); <s>dīrghasūtra</s> and <s>cirakriya</s> [mean 'procrastinator']. (3.1.36) <s>Jālma</s> means one who acts without deliberation; <s>kuṇṭha</s> and <s>manda</s> [mean] one who is slow in action. (3.1.37) <s>Karmakṣama</s> means capable of work; <s>alaṅkarmāṇa</s> and <s>kriyāvān</s> [mean 'active']; <s>karmasū</s> means 'diligent'. (3.1.38) <s>Kārma</s> is one who is habituated to work (<s>karmaśīla</s>); <s>karmaśūra</s> is <s>karmaṭha</s> ('industrious'). (3.1.39) <s>Bharaṇyabhuj</s> is a hired worker (<s>karmakara</s>); <s>karmakāra</s> means one who does [that very] work. (3.1.40) <s>Apasnāta</s> is one who has bathed after a death (<s>mṛtasnāta</s>); <s>āmiṣaśī</s> means a meat-eater (<s>śauṣkula</s>). (3.1.41) <s>Bubhukṣita</s>, <s>kṣudhita</s>, <s>jighatsur</s>, and <s>aśanāyita</s> [mean 'hungry']. (3.1.42) <s>Parānna</s> and <s>parapiṇḍāda</s> [mean 'one who eats another's food']; <s>bhakṣaka</s>, <s>ghasmara</s>, and <s>adbhara</s> [mean 'glutton']. (3.1.43) <s>Ādyūna</s> means a glutton (<s>audarika</s>); [it applies to one] devoid of the desire to conquer. (3.1.44) Both <s>ātmambhari</s> and <s>kukṣimbhari</s> [apply to] one who fills only his own belly. (3.1.45) <s>Sarvānnīna</s> is one who eats all kinds of food (<s>sarvānnabhojī</s>); <s>gṛdhnu</s> and <s>gardhana</s> [mean 'greedy']. (3.1.46) <s>Lubdha</s>, <s>abhilāpuka</s>, and <s>tṛṣṇaj</s> are synonymous; <s>lolupa</s> and <s>lolubha</s> are synonymous [for 'covetous']. (3.1.47) <s>Sonmāda</s> means 'with madness' (<s>unmadiṣṇu</s>); <s>avinīta</s> means 'arrogant' (<s>samuddhata</s>). (3.1.48) For one who is intoxicated: <s>śauṇḍa</s>, <s>utkaṭa</s>, <s>kṣība</s>; for one who is amorous: <s>kamitṛ</s> and <s>anuka</s>. (3.1.49) <s>Kamra</s>, <s>kāmayitṛ</s>, <s>abhīka</s>, <s>kamana</s>, <s>kāmana</s>, and <s>abhika</s> [all mean 'lover' or 'desirous']. (3.1.50) <s>Vidheya</s>, <s>vinayagrāhī</s>, <s>vacanesṭhita</s>, and <s>āśrava</s> [mean 'obedient']. (3.1.51) <s>Vaśya</s>, <s>praṇeya</s> [mean 'controllable']; <s>nibhṛta</s>, <s>vinīta</s>, and <s>praśrita</s> are synonymous [for 'modest' or 'humble']. (3.1.52) For one who is bold: <s>dhṛṣṇaj</s> and <s>viyāta</s>; <s>pragalbha</s> [applies to] one who has ready wit. (3.1.53) For one who is not bold: <s>śālīna</s>; <s>vilakṣa</s> [applies to] one who is amazed or embarrassed. (3.1.54) For one who is timid: <s>kātara</s>; for one who is frightened: <s>bhīru</s>, <s>bhīruka</s>, and <s>bhīluka</s>. (3.1.55) <s>Āśaṃsu</s> [applies to] one who expects; <s>gṛhayālu</s> [applies to] one who grasps. (3.1.56) <s>Śraddhālu</s> [applies to] one possessing faith; <s>patayālu</s> [applies to] one who is prone to falling. (3.1.57) <s>Apatrapiṣṇu</s> [applies to] one who is modest or bashful; <s>vandāru</s> [applies to] one who salutes. (3.1.58) <s>Śarāru</s>, <s>ghātuka</s>, and <s>hiṃsra</s> [mean 'violent']; <s>vardhiṣṇu</s> means 'one who increases' (<s>vardhana</s>). (3.1.59) <s>Utpatiṣṇu</s> means 'one who flies up' (<s>utpatitṛ</s>); <s>alaṅkariṣṇu</s> means 'one fond of adorning' (<s>maṇḍana</s>). (3.1.60) <s>Bhūṣṇu</s> and <s>śvaviṣṇu</s> [mean 'one who thrives']; <s>bhavitṛ</s> [means 'one who will be']; <s>vartiṣṇu</s> and <s>vartana</s> are synonymous [for 'one who exists or continues']. (3.1.61) <s>Nirākariṣṇu</s> and <s>kṣipnu</s> [mean 'one who rejects']; <s>sāndrasnigdha</s> means 'thick and smooth' (<s>medura</s>). (3.1.62) <s>Jñātṛ</s> is one who knows (<s>vidura</s>, <s>vindu</s>); <s>vikāsī</s> means 'one who blossoms' (<s>vikasvara</s>). (3.1.63) <s>Visṛtvara</s>, <s>visṛmara</s>, and <s>prasārī</s> [mean 'one who spreads']; also <s>visāriṇī</s>. (3.1.64) <s>Sahiṣṇu</s>, <s>sahana</s>, <s>kṣantṛ</s>, <s>titikṣu</s>, <s>kṣamitṛ</s>, and <s>kṣamī</s> [all mean 'patient' or 'forbearing']. (3.1.65) <s>Krodhana</s>, <s>amarṣaṇa</s>, and <s>kopī</s> [mean 'wrathful']; <s>caṇḍa</s> means 'extremely hot-tempered' (<s>atyantakopana</s>). (3.1.66) <s>Jāgarūka</s> and <s>jāgaritṛ</s> [mean 'wakeful']; <s>ghūrṇita</s> and <s>pracalāyita</s> [mean 'drowsy' or 'nodding']. (3.1.67) <s>Svapnaj</s> and <s>śayālu</s> [mean 'sleepy']; <s>nidrālu</s> [means 'drowsy']; <s>nidrāṇa</s> and <s>śayita</s> are synonymous [for 'asleep']. (3.1.68) <s>Parāṅmukha</s> and <s>parācīna</s> [mean 'turned away']; <s>avāṅ</s> means 'facing downward' (<s>adhomukha</s>). (3.1.69) <s>Devadryañc</s> [means 'facing the gods' — one who moves toward the gods]; <s>viśvadryañc</s> [means 'facing all directions']. (3.1.70) <s>Sadhryañc</s> is one who moves together [in the same direction]; <s>tiryañc</s> is one who moves across or diagonally. (3.1.71) <s>Vada</s>, <s>vadāvada</s>, <s>vaktṛ</s>, <s>vāgīśa</s>, and <s>vākpati</s> are synonymous [for 'eloquent speaker']. (3.1.72) <s>Vācoyuktipaṭu</s> and <s>vāgmī</s> [mean 'eloquent']; <s>vāvadūka</s> [applies to] an excessive talker. (3.1.73) <s>Jalpāka</s> means 'talkative' (<s>vācāla</s>); <s>vācāṭa</s> [means] one who speaks much that is blameworthy. (3.1.74) For one of foul mouth: <s>mukhara</s> and <s>abaddhamukha</s>; <s>śakla</s> [applies to] one who speaks pleasantly. (3.1.75) <s>Lohala</s> means one who speaks indistinctly; <s>kadvada</s> means one who speaks blame-worthily. (3.1.76) <s>Kuvāda</s> and <s>kucara</s> are synonymous [for 'ill-spoken']; one with an unpleasant voice is <s>asvara</s>. (3.1.77) <s>Ravaṇa</s> and <s>śabdana</s> [mean 'noisy']; <s>nāndīvādī</s> and <s>nāndīkara</s> are synonymous [for 'one who speaks auspiciously']. (3.1.78) <s>Jaḍa</s> and <s>ajña</s> [mean 'dull']; <s>eḍamūka</s> is one who is untrained in both speaking and hearing. (3.1.79) <s>Tūṣṇīṃśīla</s> is one who is habitually silent (<s>tūṣṇīka</s>); <s>nagna</s> and <s>avāsā</s> [mean 'naked'] — for a sky-clad [ascetic]: <s>digambara</s>. (3.1.80) <s>Niṣkāsita</s> means 'expelled' (<s>avakṛṣṭa</s>); <s>apadhvasta</s> means 'reviled' (<s>dhikkṛta</s>). (3.1.81) <s>Āttagarva</s> means one whose pride has been seized [i.e., humbled] (<s>abhibhūta</s>); <s>dāpita</s> and <s>sādhita</s> are synonymous [for 'made to pay' or 'subdued']. (3.1.82) <s>Pratyādiṣṭa</s> and <s>nirasta</s> [mean 'repelled']; <s>pratyākhyāta</s> and <s>nirākṛta</s> [mean 'rejected']. (3.1.83) <s>Nikṛta</s> means 'wronged' (<s>viprakṛta</s>); <s>vipralabdha</s> means 'deceived' (<s>vañcita</s>). (3.1.84) <s>Manohata</s>, <s>pratihata</s>, <s>pratibaddha</s>, and <s>hata</s> — he [is one who is dejected or struck down]. (3.1.85) <s>Adhikṣipta</s> and <s>pratikṣipta</s> [mean 'reproached']; for 'bound': <s>kīlita</s> and <s>saṃyata</s>. (3.1.86) <s>Āpanna</s> means 'one who has met with misfortune' (<s>āpatprāpta</s>); <s>kāndiśīka</s> means 'one fleeing in terror' (<s>bhayadruta</s>). (3.1.87) <s>Ākṣārita</s> and <s>kṣārita</s> [mean 'defamed']; <s>abhiśasta</s> [means 'accused']; <s>saṃkasuka</s> [means] 'unsteady'. (3.1.88) <s>Vyasanārta</s> and <s>uparakta</s> are synonymous [for 'afflicted by calamity']; <s>vihasta</s> and <s>vyākula</s> are synonymous [for 'agitated']. (3.1.89) <s>Viklava</s> means 'distressed' (<s>vihvala</s>); <s>vivaśa</s> means 'helpless'; <s>ariṣṭaduṣṭadhī</s> [means 'one of evil, corrupted mind']. (3.1.90) <s>Kaśya</s> [means] 'deserving of the whip'; for one who is armed or prepared for battle: <s>ātatāyī</s> [means] one who is intent on killing. (3.1.91) <s>Akṣigata</s> [means 'hateful, an eyesore']; <s>vadhya</s> and <s>śīrṣacchedya</s> are synonymous [for 'one who deserves death by beheading']. (3.1.92) <s>Viṣya</s> is one to be killed by poison; <s>musalya</s> is one to be killed by a club. (3.1.93) <s>Śiśvidāna</s> means 'one who does not perform black deeds' (<s>akṛṣṇakarmā</s>); <s>capala</s> and <s>cikura</s> are synonymous [for 'fickle']. (3.1.94) <s>Doṣaikadṛk</s> means 'one who sees only faults'; <s>purobhāgī</s> [means 'one who puts himself forward']; <s>nikṛta</s> means 'dishonest' (<s>anṛju</s>, <s>śaṭha</s>). (3.1.95) <s>Karṇejapa</s> means 'one who whispers in the ear' (<s>sūcaka</s>, an informer); <s>piśuna</s>, <s>durjana</s>, and <s>khala</s> [mean 'wicked person']. (3.1.96) <s>Nṛśaṃsa</s>, <s>ghātuka</s>, and <s>krūra</s> [mean 'cruel']; <s>pāpa</s> [means 'sinful']; <s>dhūrta</s> means 'a cheat' (<s>vañcaka</s>). (3.1.97) For an ignorant person: <s>mūḍha</s>, <s>yathājāta</s>, <s>mūrkha</s>, <s>vaidheya</s>, and <s>bāliśa</s>. (3.1.98) For a miser: <s>kṛpaṇa</s>, <s>kṣudra</s>, <s>kimpacāna</s>, and <s>mitampaca</s>. (3.1.99) <s>Niḥsva</s> means 'destitute' (<s>durvidha</s>); <s>dīna</s>, <s>daridra</s>, and <s>durgata</s> are also [synonyms for 'poor']. (3.1.100) <s>Vanīyaka</s>, <s>yācanaka</s>, and <s>mārgaṇa</s> [mean 'beggar']; <s>yācaka</s> and <s>arthin</s> [also mean 'suppliant']. (3.1.101) <s>Ahaṅkāravān</s> and <s>ahaṃyū</s> [mean 'proud']; <s>śubhaṃyū</s> means 'one endowed with auspiciousness' (<s>śubhānvita</s>).

children.translated_text: (3.1.104) Plants (<s>udbhid</s>) — trees, shrubs, etc. — [are called] <s>udbhid</s>, <s>udbhijja</s>, <s>udbhida</s>. (3.1.105–108) [Synonyms for 'beautiful':] <s>sundara</s>, <s>rucira</s>, <s>cāru</s>, <s>suṣama</s>, <s>sādhu</s>, <s>śobhana</s>, <s>kānta</s>, <s>manorama</s>, <s>rucya</s>, <s>manojña</s>, <s>mañju</s>, <s>mañjula</s>, <s>ramya</s>, <s>manohara</s>, <s>saumya</s>, <s>bhadraka</s>, <s>ramaṇīyaka</s>. <s>Āsecanaka</s> — that of which there is no end of satisfaction from seeing. (3.1.109) [Synonyms for 'desired':] <s>abhīpsita</s>, <s>hṛdya</s>, <s>dayita</s>, <s>vallabha</s>, <s>priya</s>. (3.1.110–111) [Synonyms for 'inferior/bad':] <s>nikṛṣṭa</s>, <s>pratikṛṣṭa</s>, <s>arva</s>, <s>repha</s>, <s>yāpya</s>, <s>avama</s>, <s>ādhama</s>, <s>kupūya</s>, <s>kutsita</s>, <s>avadya</s>, <s>kheṭa</s>, <s>garhya</s>, <s>āṇaka</s> — [these are] synonymous. (3.1.112) [Synonyms for 'dirty':] <s>malīmasa</s>, <s>malina</s>, <s>kaccara</s>, <s>maladūṣita</s>. (3.1.113) [Synonyms for 'pure':] <s>pūta</s>, <s>pavitra</s>, <s>medhya</s>; <s>vīdhra</s> means 'spotless.' (3.1.114) [Synonyms for 'cleansed':] <s>nirṇikta</s>, <s>śodhita</s>, <s>mṛṣṭa</s>, <s>niḥśodhya</s>, <s>anavaskara</s>. (3.1.115) [Synonyms for 'empty/worthless':] <s>asāra</s>, <s>phalgu</s>, <s>śūnya</s>, <s>vaśika</s>, <s>tuccha</s>, <s>riktaka</s>. (3.1.116–119) [Synonyms for 'chief/best':] <s>pradhāna</s> (neuter), <s>pramukha</s>, <s>praveka</s>, <s>anuttama</s>, <s>uttama</s>, <s>mukhya</s>, <s>varya</s>, <s>vareṇya</s>, <s>pravara</s>, <s>anavara</s>, <s>ardhyavat</s>, <s>parārdhya</s>, <s>agra</s>, <s>prāgrahara</s>, <s>prāgraya</s>, <s>agraya</s>, <s>agrīya</s>, <s>agriya</s>, <s>śreyān</s>, <s>śreṣṭha</s>, <s>puṣkala</s>, <s>sattama</s> — [meaning] most excellent. (3.1.120–121) In the latter part of compounds, <s>vyāghra</s> (tiger), <s>puṅgava</s> (bull), <s>ṛṣabha</s> (bull), <s>kuñjara</s> (elephant), <s>siṃha</s> (lion), <s>śārdūla</s> (tiger), <s>nāga</s> (elephant) etc. — in masculine, [denote] the meaning of 'best.' (3.1.122) <s>Aprāgraya</s> [means] 'deficient in both'; the two [words] <s>apradhāna</s> and <s>upasarjana</s> [mean 'secondary']. (3.1.123–124) [Synonyms for 'large/broad':] <s>viśaṃkaṭa</s>, <s>pṛthu</s>, <s>bṛhat</s>, <s>viśāla</s>, <s>pṛthula</s>, <s>mahat</s>, <s>vaḍra</s>, <s>uru</s>, <s>vipula</s>; <s>pīna</s> and <s>pīvan</s> [mean] 'fat/corpulent.' (3.1.125–127) [Synonyms for 'small':] <s>stoka</s>, <s>alpa</s>, <s>kṣullaka</s>, <s>sūkṣma</s>, <s>ślakṣṇa</s>, <s>dabhra</s>, <s>kṛśa</s>, <s>tanu</s>; in feminine: <s>mātrā</s>, <s>truṭi</s>; in masculine: <s>lava</s>, <s>leśa</s>, <s>kaṇa</s>, <s>aṇu</s>. In the superlative of 'very small': <s>alpiṣṭha</s>, <s>alpīyas</s>, <s>kanīyas</s>, <s>aṇīyas</s>. (3.1.128–129) [Synonyms for 'abundant':] <s>prabhūta</s>, <s>pracura</s>, <s>prājya</s>, <s>adabhra</s>, <s>bahula</s>, <s>bahu</s>, <s>puruhū</s>, <s>puru</s>, <s>bhūyiṣṭha</s>, <s>sphāra</s>, <s>bhūyas</s>, <s>bhūri</s>. (3.1.130) 'Beyond a hundred etc.' — those whose highest number is from a hundred upward. (3.1.131) [In the sense of] 'countable': <s>gaṇeya</s>; [of] 'counted': <s>gaṇita</s>. (3.1.131–133) [Synonyms for 'all/entire':] <s>sama</s>, <s>sarva</s>, <s>viśva</s>, <s>aśeṣa</s>, <s>kṛtsna</s>, <s>samasta</s>, <s>nikhila</s>, <s>akhila</s>, <s>niḥśeṣa</s>, <s>samagra</s>, <s>sakala</s>, <s>pūrṇa</s>, <s>akhaṇḍa</s> — [meaning] 'not deficient.' (3.1.134) [Synonyms for 'dense':] <s>ghana</s>, <s>nirantara</s>, <s>sāndra</s>; [for 'sparse':] <s>pelava</s>, <s>virala</s>, <s>tanu</s>. (3.1.135–138) [Synonyms for 'near':] <s>nikaṭa</s>, <s>āsanna</s>, <s>saṃnikṛṣṭa</s>, <s>sanīḍavat</s>, <s>sadeśa</s>, <s>abhyāśa</s>, <s>savidha</s>, <s>samaryāda</s>, <s>saveśavat</s>, <s>upakaṇṭha</s>, <s>antika</s>, <s>abhyarṇa</s>, <s>abhyagra</s>; also <s>abhitas</s> (indeclinable). [For 'contiguous':] <s>avyavahita</s>, <s>apadāntara</s>. (3.1.139–140) <s>Nediṣṭha</s> [means] 'nearest.' [Synonyms for 'far':] <s>dūra</s>, <s>viprakṛṣṭaka</s>, <s>davīyas</s>, <s>daviṣṭha</s>, <s>sudūra</s>, <s>dīrgha</s>, <s>āyata</s>. (3.1.141) [Synonyms for 'round':] <s>vartula</s>, <s>nistala</s>, <s>vṛtta</s>; <s>bandhura</s> [means] 'undulating.' (3.1.142–143) [Synonyms for 'tall':] <s>ucca</s>, <s>prāṃśu</s>, <s>unnata</s>, <s>udagra</s>, <s>ucchrita</s>, <s>tuṅga</s>. [For 'short':] <s>nyaṅ</s>, <s>nīca</s>, <s>kharva</s>, <s>hrasva</s>. (3.1.144–145) [Synonyms for 'crooked':] <s>arāla</s>, <s>vṛjina</s>, <s>jihma</s>, <s>ūrmimat</s>, <s>kuñcita</s>, <s>nata</s>, <s>āviddha</s>, <s>kuṭila</s>, <s>bhugna</s>, <s>vellita</s>, <s>vakra</s>. (3.1.146) [Synonyms for 'straight':] <s>ṛju</s>, <s>ajihma</s>, <s>praguṇa</s>; [for 'disordered':] <s>apraguṇa</s>, <s>ākula</s>. (3.1.147–149) [Synonyms for 'eternal':] <s>śāśvata</s>, <s>dhruva</s>, <s>nitya</s>, <s>sadātana</s>, <s>sanātana</s>, <s>sthāsnu</s>, <s>sthiratara</s>, <s>stheyas</s>. That which pervades time in one form is <s>kūṭastha</s>. <s>Sthāvara</s> [means] 'immovable.' (3.1.150–152) [Synonyms for 'moving':] <s>cariṣṇu</s>, <s>jaṅgama</s>, <s>cara</s>, <s>trasa</s>, <s>iṅga</s>, <s>carācara</s>. [For 'shaking':] <s>calana</s>, <s>kampana</s>, <s>kampra</s>, <s>cala</s>, <s>lola</s>, <s>calācala</s>, <s>cañcala</s>, <s>tarala</s>, <s>pāriplava</s>, <s>pariplava</s>. (3.1.153–154) <s>Atiriktaḥ</s> [means] 'surplus.' <s>Dṛḍhasandhi</s> [means] <s>saṃhata</s> (compact). [Synonyms for 'hard':] <s>khakkhaṭa</s>, <s>kaṭhina</s>, <s>krūra</s>, <s>kaṭhora</s>, <s>niṣṭhura</s>, <s>dṛḍha</s>. (3.1.155) <s>Jaraṭha</s> [means] 'having form'; <s>mūrtimat</s>, <s>mūrta</s>, <s>pravṛddha</s>, <s>prauḍha</s>, <s>edhita</s> [mean 'developed/grown']. (3.1.156) [Synonyms for 'ancient':] <s>purāṇa</s>, <s>pratana</s>, <s>pratna</s>, <s>purātana</s>, <s>cirantana</s>. (3.1.157–158) [Synonyms for 'new':] <s>pratyagra</s>, <s>abhinava</s>, <s>navya</s>, <s>navīna</s>, <s>nūtana</s>, <s>nava</s>, <s>nūtna</s>. [For 'tender':] <s>sukumāra</s>, <s>komala</s>, <s>mṛdula</s>, <s>mṛdu</s>. (3.1.159–162) [Synonyms for 'following':] <s>anvak</s>, <s>anuge</s>, <s>anupada</s> (neuter, indeclinable). [For 'perceptible':] <s>pratyakṣa</s>, <s>aindriyaka</s>; [for 'imperceptible':] <s>apratyakṣa</s>, <s>atīndriya</s>. [For 'concentrated':] <s>ekatāna</s>, <s>ananyavṛtti</s>, <s>ekāgra</s>, <s>ekāyana</s>, <s>ekasarga</s>, <s>ekāgrya</s>. (3.1.163–164) [For 'first':] <s>ādi</s> (masc.), <s>pūrva</s>, <s>paurastya</s>, <s>prathama</s>, <s>ādya</s>. [For 'last':] <s>anta</s>, <s>jaghanya</s>, <s>carama</s>, <s>antya</s>, <s>pāścātya</s>, <s>paścima</s>. (3.1.165–166) <s>Mogha</s> [means] 'vain'; <s>nirarthaka</s> [means the same]. [For 'clear':] <s>spaṣṭa</s>, <s>sphuṭa</s>, <s>pravyakta</s>, <s>ulbaṇa</s>. <s>Sādhāraṇa</s> [means] 'common'; <s>sāmānya</s> [means the same]. [For 'alone':] <s>ekākī</s>, <s>eka</s>, <s>ekaka</s>. (3.1.167–172) [Various terms:] <s>anyatara</s> [means 'either of two']; <s>uccāvaca</s> [means 'of various kinds']; <s>aruntuda</s> [means 'touching a vulnerable spot']; <s>abādha</s> [means 'unobstructed']; <s>prasavya</s> [means 'contrary']; in the body, <s>savya</s> means 'left' and <s>apasavya</s> 'right'; <s>saṅkaṭa</s> (neuter) but <s>saṃbādha</s> (masculine) [mean 'narrow/strait']; <s>kalila</s> and <s>gahana</s> [mean 'dense/impenetrable']. (3.1.173–228) [Continued lists of synonymous participles and adjectives describing various states: crowded, bound, spread, hidden, shaken, pushed, grown, ground, wrapped, broken, sharpened, dissolved, accomplished, split, woven, worshipped, heated, pleased, cut, fallen, obtained, sought, wet, protected, despised, abandoned, spoken, understood, promised, heard, praised, eaten — with their various synonymous forms; followed by superlative forms and their meanings.] Thus ends the <s>Viśeṣyanighnavarga</s> (Section on Adjectival Qualifiers) 1; here the original verses number 112.

(3.2.229) In the Mixed [Section], one should determine gender from the stem, suffix, meaning, etc.

Now begins the <s>Saṃkīrṇavarga</s> (Miscellaneous Section).
(3.2.230) <s>Karma</s>, <s>kriyā</s> are synonyms for 'action'; in the sense of continuous action, <s>gamya</s> applies; <s>aparasparāḥ</s> means 'unrelated to each other.'
(3.2.231) <s>Pārāyaṇa</s> and <s>parāyaṇa</s> denote completeness and non-attachment respectively in recitation.
(3.2.232) <s>Yadṛcchā</s>, <s>svairitā</s> mean 'spontaneity' or 'acting at will'; <s>hetuśūnyā</s> means 'causeless'; <s>āsthā</s> means 'regard'; <s>vilakṣaṇam</s> means 'anomalous' or 'embarrassed.'
(3.2.233) <s>Śamathaḥ</s>, <s>śamaḥ</s>, <s>śāntiḥ</s> are synonyms for 'tranquility'; <s>dāntiḥ</s>, <s>damathaḥ</s>, <s>damaḥ</s> are synonyms for 'self-restraint.'
(3.2.234) <s>Avadānam</s> means 'a deed' or 'meritorious action'; <s>karma</s> and <s>vṛttam</s> also mean 'action'; <s>kāmyadānam</s> and <s>pravāraṇam</s> mean 'a voluntary gift' or 'offering at will.'
(3.2.235) <s>Vaśakriyā</s> and <s>saṃvananam</s> mean 'subjugation' or 'winning over'; <s>mūlakarma</s> and <s>kārmaṇam</s> mean 'sorcery' or 'black magic.'
(3.2.236) <s>Vidhūnanam</s> and <s>vidhuvanam</s> mean 'shaking off'; <s>tarpaṇam</s>, <s>prīṇanam</s>, <s>avanam</s> mean 'gratification' or 'satisfying.'
(3.2.237) <s>Paryāptiḥ</s> means 'sufficiency' or 'protection'; <s>paritrāṇam</s> and <s>hastadhāraṇam</s> also denote 'protection' or 'holding by the hand.'
(3.2.238) <s>Sevanam</s> and <s>sīvanam</s> mean 'sewing'; <s>syūtiḥ</s> also means 'sewing'; <s>vidaraḥ</s>, <s>sphuṭanam</s>, <s>bhidā</s> mean 'splitting' or 'bursting open.'
(3.2.239) <s>Ākrośanam</s> and <s>abhīṣaṅgaḥ</s> mean 'abuse' or 'reviling'; <s>saṃvedaḥ</s> and <s>vedanā</s> mean 'sensation' or 'feeling' — not masculine.
(3.2.240) <s>Saṃmūrcchanam</s> and <s>abhivyāptiḥ</s> mean 'pervading' or 'spreading'; <s>yāñcā</s>, <s>bhikṣā</s>, <s>arthanā</s>, <s>ardanā</s> mean 'begging' or 'solicitation.'
(3.2.241) <s>Vardhanam</s> means 'cutting' (in this context); then two words <s>ānandanam</s> and <s>sabhājanam</s> mean 'pleasing' or 'honouring.'
(3.2.242) <s>Āpracchannam</s> means 'what is concealed'; <s>āmnāyaḥ</s> and <s>saṃpradāyaḥ</s> mean 'tradition' or 'sacred text handed down'; in the sense of destruction, <s>kṣiyā</s> is used.
(3.2.243) In seizing, <s>grāhaḥ</s>; <s>vaśaḥ</s> in subjection; <s>kāntiḥ</s> in beauty; <s>rakṣṇaḥ</s> and <s>trāṇam</s> in protection; <s>raṇaḥ</s> in sound; <s>kaṇaḥ</s> in a small particle.
(3.2.244) <s>Vyadhaḥ</s> in piercing; <s>vedhaḥ</s> in piercing; <s>pacā</s> in cooking; <s>pākaḥ</s> in cooking; <s>havaḥ</s> in offering; <s>hūtiḥ</s> in invocation; <s>varaḥ</s> in choosing; <s>vṛttiḥ</s> in livelihood.
(3.2.245) <s>Oṣaḥ</s> in burning; <s>ploṣaḥ</s> in scorching; <s>nayaḥ</s> in leading; <s>nāyaḥ</s> in leading; <s>jyāniḥ</s> in decay; <s>jīrṇau</s> in old age; <s>bhramaḥ</s> in wandering; <s>bhramau</s> in rotation.
(3.2.246) <s>Sphātiḥ</s> in increase; <s>vṛddhiḥ</s> in growth; <s>prathā</s> in fame; <s>khyātiḥ</s> in renown; <s>spṛṣṭiḥ</s> in touching; <s>pṛktiḥ</s> in mixing; <s>snavaḥ</s> in flowing; <s>sravaḥ</s> in oozing.
(3.2.247) <s>Edhā</s> in prosperity; <s>samṛddhiḥ</s> in abundance; <s>sphuraṇam</s> in throbbing; <s>sphuraṇā</s> in quivering; <s>pramā</s> in right measure or knowledge; <s>pramitiḥ</s> in correct notion.
(3.2.248) <s>Prasūtiḥ</s> in birth or production; <s>ścyotaḥ</s> in dripping; <s>prādhāraḥ</s> in pouring; <s>klamathaḥ</s> in fatigue; <s>klamaḥ</s> in weariness.
(3.2.249) <s>Utkarṣaḥ</s> in excellence; <s>atiśayaḥ</s> in surpassing; <s>sandhiḥ</s> in union; <s>śleṣaḥ</s> in adhesion; <s>viṣayaḥ</s> in domain; <s>āśrayaḥ</s> in support or refuge.
(3.2.250) <s>Kṣepaṇam</s> in throwing; <s>kṣipā</s> in hurling; <s>gīrṇiḥ</s> in swallowing; <s>giraḥ</s> in speech; <s>guraṇam</s> in effort; <s>udyamaḥ</s> in exertion.
(3.2.251) <s>Unnāyaḥ</s> in raising up; <s>unnayaḥ</s> in elevation; <s>śrāyaḥ</s> in resorting; <s>śrayaṇam</s> in taking refuge; <s>jayaḥ</s> in victory; <s>jayanam</s> in conquering.
(3.2.252) <s>Nigādaḥ</s> in speech; <s>nigadaḥ</s> in a fetter or recitation; <s>mādaḥ</s> in intoxication; <s>madaḥ</s> in pride; <s>udvegaḥ</s> in anxiety; <s>udbhramaḥ</s> in bewilderment.
(3.2.253) <s>Vimardanam</s> and <s>parimalaḥ</s> mean 'rubbing' or 'fragrance'; <s>abhyupapatti</s> and <s>anugrahaḥ</s> mean 'favour' or 'assistance.'
(3.2.254) <s>Nigrahaḥ</s> means 'restraint' — the opposite of the above; <s>abhiyogaḥ</s> and <s>abhigrahaḥ</s> mean 'attack' or 'seizure.'
(3.2.255) <s>Muṣṭibandhaḥ</s> and <s>saṃgrāhaḥ</s> mean 'clenching the fist' or 'grasping'; in the sense of tumult, <s>ḍamaraḥ</s> and <s>viplavaḥ</s> are used.
(3.2.256) <s>Bandhanam</s> means 'binding'; <s>prasitiḥ</s> means 'assault'; <s>cāraḥ</s> means 'movement' or 'spying'; <s>sparśaḥ</s> means 'touch' — one who touches or is affected.
(3.2.257) <s>Nikāraḥ</s> and <s>viprakāraḥ</s> mean 'ill-treatment' or 'insult'; <s>ākāraḥ</s> means 'form' or 'gesture'; <s>iṅgaḥ</s> and <s>iṅgitam</s> mean 'hint' or 'gesture.'
(3.2.258) <s>Pariṇāmaḥ</s> means 'transformation' or 'change'; two words <s>vikṛtiḥ</s> and <s>vikriyā</s> are synonyms meaning 'alteration' or 'modification.'
(3.2.259) <s>Apahāraḥ</s> and <s>apacayaḥ</s> mean 'removal' or 'diminution'; <s>samāhāraḥ</s> and <s>samuccayaḥ</s> mean 'collection' or 'aggregation.'
(3.2.260) <s>Pratyāhāraḥ</s> and <s>upādānam</s> mean 'withdrawal' or 'taking up'; <s>vihāraḥ</s> and <s>parikramaḥ</s> mean 'walking about' or 'recreation.'
(3.2.261) <s>Abhihāraḥ</s> and <s>abhigrahaṇam</s> mean 'attack' or 'seizing'; <s>nihāraḥ</s> and <s>abhyavakarṣaṇam</s> mean 'dragging down' or 'pulling away.'
(3.2.262) <s>Anuhāraḥ</s> and <s>anukāraḥ</s> mean 'imitation'; in the sense of loss of wealth, <s>vyayaḥ</s> is used.
(3.2.263) <s>Pravāhaḥ</s> and <s>pravṛttiḥ</s> mean 'continuous flow' or 'onward movement'; <s>pravahaḥ</s> means 'going forth' or 'outward motion.'
(3.2.264) <s>Viyāmaḥ</s>, <s>viyamaḥ</s> mean 'restraint' or 'extension'; <s>yāmaḥ</s>, <s>yamaḥ</s>, <s>saṃyāmaḥ</s>, <s>saṃyamaḥ</s> mean 'restraint' or 'self-control.'
(3.2.265) <s>Abhicāraḥ</s> means 'sorcery' or 'harmful rites'; <s>jāgaryā</s> and <s>jāṃgarā</s> mean 'wakefulness' — both forms are used.
(3.2.266) <s>Vighnaḥ</s>, <s>antarāyaḥ</s>, <s>pratyūhaḥ</s> are synonyms for 'obstacle' or 'hindrance'; <s>upághnaḥ</s> means 'one close by' or 'nearby support.'
(3.2.267) <s>Nirveśaḥ</s> and <s>upabhogaḥ</s> mean 'enjoyment' or 'requital'; <s>parisarpaḥ</s> and <s>parikriyā</s> mean 'moving about' or 'attendance.'
(3.2.268) <s>Vidhuram</s> means 'separation' or 'distress'; <s>abhiprāyaḥ</s>, <s>chandaḥ</s>, <s>āśayaḥ</s> mean 'intention' or 'desire.'
(3.2.269) <s>Saṃkṣepaṇam</s> and <s>samasanam</s> mean 'compression' or 'abridgement'; <s>paryavasthā</s> and <s>virodhanam</s> mean 'obstruction' or 'opposition.'
(3.2.270) <s>Parisaryā</s> and <s>parīsāraḥ</s> mean 'moving around' or 'attendance'; <s>āsyā</s>, <s>āsanā</s>, <s>sthitiḥ</s> mean 'sitting' or 'remaining.'
(3.2.271) <s>Vistāraḥ</s>, <s>vigrahaḥ</s>, <s>vyāsaḥ</s> mean 'expansion' or 'detail'; and <s>vyāsaḥ</s> also means 'the elaboration of a word' or 'exposition.'
(3.2.272) <s>Saṃvāhanam</s> and <s>mardanam</s> mean 'massaging' or 'rubbing'; <s>vināśaḥ</s> and <s>adarśanam</s> mean 'destruction' or 'disappearance.'
(3.2.273) <s>Saṃstavaḥ</s> and <s>paricayaḥ</s> mean 'acquaintance' or 'familiarity'; <s>prasaraḥ</s> and <s>visarpaṇam</s> mean 'spreading' or 'extension.'
(3.2.274) <s>Nīvākaḥ</s> and <s>prayāmaḥ</s> mean 'departure' or 'setting forth'; <s>saṃnidhiḥ</s> and <s>saṃnikarṣaṇam</s> mean 'proximity' or 'nearness.'
(3.2.275) <s>Lavaḥ</s> means 'cutting'; <s>abhilāṣaḥ</s> means 'desire'; <s>lavanam</s> means 'cutting' or 'reaping'; <s>niṣpāvaḥ</s> means 'winnowing'; <s>pavanam</s> and <s>pavaḥ</s> mean 'purification' or 'wind.'
(3.2.276) <s>Prastāvaḥ</s> means 'introduction' or 'prelude'; <s>apasaraḥ</s> means 'retreat'; <s>trasaraḥ</s> means 'the shuttle in weaving'; <s>sūtraveṣṭanam</s> means 'winding of thread.'
(3.2.277) <s>Prajanaḥ</s> and <s>upasaraḥ</s> mean 'procreation' or 'approach'; <s>praśrayaḥ</s> and <s>praṇayaḥ</s> are synonyms meaning 'modesty' or 'affection.'
(3.2.278) <s>Dhīśaktiḥ</s> means 'intellectual power'; <s>niṣkramaḥ</s> means 'departure' — not feminine; <s>saṃkramaḥ</s> means 'passage'; <s>durgasaṃcaraḥ</s> means 'traversing difficult terrain.'
(3.2.279) <s>Pratyutkramaḥ</s> means 'going forth to meet' (a purpose of courtesy); <s>prakramaḥ</s> and <s>upakramaḥ</s> mean 'commencement' or 'approach.'
(3.2.280) <s>Abhyādānam</s> means 'taking up'; <s>uddhātaḥ</s> means 'shaking' or 'rising'; <s>ārambhaḥ</s> means 'beginning'; <s>saṃbhramaḥ</s> and <s>tvarā</s> mean 'haste' or 'hurry.'
(3.2.281) <s>Pratibandhaḥ</s> and <s>praviṣṭambhaḥ</s> mean 'obstruction' or 'impediment'; <s>avanāyaḥ</s> and <s>nipātanam</s> mean 'bringing down' or 'felling.'
(3.2.282) <s>Upalambhaḥ</s> and <s>anubhavaḥ</s> mean 'perception' or 'experience'; <s>samālambhaḥ</s> and <s>vilepanam</s> mean 'anointing' or 'smearing.'
(3.2.283) <s>Vipralambhaḥ</s> and <s>viprayogaḥ</s> mean 'deception' or 'separation'; <s>vilambhaḥ</s> and <s>atisarjanam</s> mean 'delay' or 'release.'
(3.2.284) <s>Viśrāvaḥ</s> and <s>pratikhyātiḥ</s> mean 'fame' or 'reputation'; <s>avekṣā</s> and <s>pratijāgaraḥ</s> mean 'watchfulness' or 'vigilance.'
(3.2.285) <s>Nipāṭhaḥ</s> and <s>nipaṭhaḥ</s> apply in the sense of 'reading' or 'recitation'; <s>temaḥ</s> and <s>temaḥ</s> apply in the sense of 'moistening.'
(3.2.286) <s>Ādīnavaḥ</s> and <s>āsravaḥ</s> mean 'fault' or 'affliction'; in the sense of meeting, <s>saṅgaḥ</s> and <s>saṅgamaḥ</s> are used.
(3.2.287) <s>Saṃvīkṣaṇam</s>, <s>vicayanam</s>, <s>mārgaṇam</s>, <s>mṛgaṇā</s>, <s>mṛgaḥ</s> are synonyms for 'searching' or 'seeking.'
(3.2.288) <s>Parirambhaḥ</s>, <s>pariṣvaṅgaḥ</s>, <s>saṃśleṣaḥ</s>, <s>upagūhanam</s> are synonyms for 'embracing.'
(3.2.289) <s>Nirvarṇanam</s> and <s>nidhyānam</s> mean 'contemplation' or 'close examination'; <s>darśanam</s>, <s>ālokanam</s>, <s>īkṣaṇam</s> mean 'seeing' or 'beholding.'
(3.2.290) <s>Pratyākhyānam</s> and <s>nirasanam</s> mean 'rejection' or 'refusal'; <s>pratyādeśaḥ</s> and <s>nirākṛtiḥ</s> mean 'repudiation' or 'denial.'
(3.2.291) <s>Upaśāyaḥ</s> and <s>viśāyaḥ</s> are synonymous, meaning 'lying beside' or 'sleeping alongside' (<s>paryāyaśayana</s>).
(3.2.292) <s>Artanam</s>, <s>ṛtīyā</s>, and <s>hṛṇīyā</s> share the meaning of <s>ghṛṇā</s> (disgust, contempt, or compassion).
(3.2.293) <s>Vyatyāsaḥ</s>, <s>viparyāsaḥ</s>, and <s>vyatyayaḥ</s> are synonyms for 'reversal' or 'transposition' (<s>viparyaya</s>).
(3.2.294) <s>Paryayaḥ</s> and <s>atikramaḥ</s> mean 'transgression' or 'lapse'; in that same sense, <s>atipātaḥ</s> and <s>upātyayaḥ</s> are also used.
(3.2.295) <s>Preṣaṇam</s> means 'sending'; when one is summoned and then commanded, that is <s>pratiśāsanam</s> (a counter-command or instruction).
(3.2.296) That is called <s>saṃstāvaḥ</s> which is the platform of praise for the twice-born (<s>dvijanman</s>) in sacrificial rites (<s>kratu</s>).
(3.2.297) Where a piece of wood is placed and another is shaped upon it, that is called <s>uddhanaḥ</s> (a fire-churning base).
(3.2.298) <s>Stambaghnaḥ</s> and <s>stambaghanaḥ</s> mean 'that by which a clump or tuft (<s>stamba</s>) is struck down.'
(3.2.299) <s>Āvidhaḥ</s> is 'that by which something is pierced'; in the same sense, <s>nighaḥ</s> applies uniformly.
(3.2.300) <s>Utkāraḥ</s> and <s>nikāraḥ</s> are two words meaning 'winnowing' or 'tossing up grain.'
(3.2.301) <s>Nigāraḥ</s>, <s>udgāraḥ</s>, <s>vikṣāvaḥ</s>, <s>udgrāhaḥ</s> apply in the senses of swallowing, vomiting, scattering, and extracting respectively.
(3.2.302) <s>Ārati</s>, <s>avaratiḥ</s>, <s>viratiḥ</s> mean 'cessation' or 'desisting' (<s>uparāma</s>); and not feminine is <s>niṣṭhevaḥ</s>,
(3.2.303) <s>Niṣṭhyūtiḥ</s>, <s>niṣṭhevanam</s>, <s>niṣṭhīvanam</s> — these are synonymous, meaning 'spitting.'
(3.2.304) In the sense of speed, <s>jūtiḥ</s>; <s>sātiḥ</s> in completion; and in the sense of fever, <s>jūrtiḥ</s>.
(3.2.305) <s>Udajaḥ</s> means 'driving cattle'; <s>paśupreraṇam</s> also means 'urging animals'; <s>akaraṇiḥ</s> and similar words apply in the sense of 'cursing.'
(3.2.306) From words ending in <s>gotra</s> (family name), the collective meaning 'the group of such' yields forms like <s>aupagavaka</s> and so on.
(3.2.307) <s>Āpūpikam</s> (relating to cakes), <s>śāṣkulikam</s> (relating to pastries) — such forms denote 'a collection of' for inanimate things.
(3.2.308) For young students, the collective is <s>māṇavyam</s>; for companions, <s>sahāyatā</s> (companionship).
(3.2.309) <s>Halyā</s> is the collective for ploughs; <s>brāhmaṇyam</s> and <s>vāḍavyam</s> are collectives for the twice-born (<s>dvijanman</s>).
(3.2.310) Two words: for ribs (<s>parśuka</s>) the collective is <s>pārśvam</s>; for backs (<s>pṛṣṭha</s>), it is <s>pṛṣṭhyam</s> — in that order.
(3.2.311) For threshing floors (<s>khala</s>), the collectives are <s>khalinī</s> and <s>khalyā</s>; for humans (<s>nṛ</s>), the collective is <s>mānuṣyakam</s>.
(3.2.312) <s>Grāmatā</s> (for villages), <s>janatā</s> (for people), <s>dhūmyā</s> (for smoke), <s>pāśyā</s> (for snares), <s>galyā</s> (for drops) — each separately denotes a collective.
(3.2.313) Also <s>sāhasraka</s> (a collection of thousands), <s>kārīṣa</s> (a mass of dried dung), <s>vārmaṇa</s> (a collection of armour), <s>ātharvaṇa</s> (relating to the <s>Atharvaveda</s>) and so forth.
Thus ends the <s>Saṃkīrṇavarga</s> (Miscellaneous Section), the second section. Here the root verses number 42.

children.translated_text: (3.3.477) the sense organs (<s>indriyāṇi</s>), gems (<s>aśman</s>), material modifications (<s>vikṛti</s>), the origin of sound (<s>śabdayoni</s>) — all these are called <s>dhātu</s>.
(3.3.478) <s>Śuddhānta</s> means the inner apartments (<s>kakṣāntara</s>) or the domain not accessible to all (<s>asarvagocarā</s>) of a king.
(3.3.479) <s>Śakti</s> means ability (<s>sāmarthya</s>) in certain contexts. <s>Mūrti</s> means hardness (<s>kāṭhinya</s>) or the body (<s>kāya</s>).

(3.3.416) <s>Poṭā</s> means a female servant (<s>dāsī</s>); it is also used in both genders. <s>Ghṛṣṭī</s> means either grinding or a sow.
(3.3.417) <s>Ghaṭā</s> means an assembly (<s>ghoṣṭhī</s>) or a row of elephants. <s>Kṛpīṭa</s> means the belly or water.
(3.3.418) Thus end the words ending in <s>ṭa</s>.
(3.3.419) In the masculine, <s>koṣṭha</s> means the interior of the body (<s>antarjaṭhara</s>); <s>kusūla</s> means an inner chamber (<s>antargṛha</s>) likewise.
(3.3.420) <s>Niṣṭhā</s> means completion (<s>niṣpatti</s>) or destruction (<s>nāśa</s>) or end (<s>anta</s>). <s>Kāṣṭha</s> means excellence (<s>utkarṣa</s>), a state (<s>sthiti</s>), or a direction (<s>diś</s>).
(3.3.421) In all three genders, <s>jyeṣṭha</s> means the eldest or the most excellent; <s>kaniṣṭha</s> means the youngest or the smallest.
(3.3.422) Thus end the words ending in <s>ṭha</s>.
(3.3.423) <s>Daṇḍa</s> (not feminine) means also a staff (<s>laguḍa</s>). <s>Guḍa</s> means a ball or jaggery (sugarcane preparation).
(3.3.424) <s>Sarpa</s> means flesh (<s>māṃsa</s>) or cattle (<s>paśu</s>) or a ferocious beast (<s>vyāḍa</s>). The words <s>go</s>, <s>bhū</s>, and <s>vāc</s> are expressed by <s>iḍā</s> and <s>ilā</s>.
(3.3.425) <s>Nāḍī</s> means also a bamboo tube (<s>kṣveḍavaṃśaśalākā</s>) or a unit of time equal to six <s>kṣaṇas</s>.
(3.3.426) <s>Kāṇḍa</s> (not feminine) means a staff (<s>daṇḍa</s>), an arrow (<s>bāṇa</s>), water (<s>vāri</s>), a section (<s>varga</s>), or an occasion (<s>avasara</s>).
(3.3.427) <s>Bhāṇḍa</s> means a horse's trappings, a vessel (<s>amatra</s>), capital (<s>mūla</s>), a merchant (<s>vaṇij</s>), or wealth (<s>dhana</s>).
(3.3.428) Thus end the words ending in <s>ḍa</s>.
(3.3.429) <s>Bāḍham</s> means excessively (<s>bhṛśa</s>) or an affirmation (<s>pratijñā</s>). <s>Pragāḍha</s> means excessively (<s>bhṛśa</s>) or with difficulty (<s>kṛcchra</s>).
(3.3.430) <s>Piṇḍī</s> means a mass (<s>saṃghāta</s>) or a morsel (<s>grāsa</s>); in the masculine, both forms (<s>piṇḍa</s>) refer to the body (<s>kalevara</s>).
(3.3.431) <s>Gaṇḍa</s> means the cheek (<s>kapola</s>) or a boil (<s>visphoṭa</s>). <s>Muṇḍaka</s> in all three genders means one who is shaved.
(3.3.432) <s>Khaṇḍa</s> (not feminine) also means a type of sugarcane. <s>Śikhaṇḍa</s> means a peacock's tail (<s>barha</s>) or a crest (<s>cūḍā</s>).
(3.3.433) <s>Śakta</s> and <s>sthūla</s> both mean firm (<s>dṛḍha</s>) in all three genders. <s>Vyūḍha</s> means arranged (<s>vinyasta</s>) or compact (<s>saṃhata</s>).
(3.3.434) Thus end the words ending in <s>ḍha</s>.
(3.3.435) <s>Bhrūṇa</s> means a child (<s>arbhaka</s>) or a female embryo (<s>straiṇagarbha</s>). <s>Bāṇa</s> means the son of <s>Bali</s> or an arrow (<s>śara</s>).
(3.3.436) <s>Kaṇa</s> means something extremely minute or a grain of corn (<s>dhānyāṃśa</s>). <s>Gaṇa</s> means an assemblage (<s>saṃghāta</s>) or a troop of <s>Śiva's</s> attendants (<s>pramatha</s>).
(3.3.437) <s>Paṇa</s> means a stake wagered in gambling and such, wages (<s>bhṛti</s>), price (<s>mūlya</s>), or wealth (<s>dhana</s>).
(3.3.438) <s>Guṇa</s> means a bowstring (<s>maurvī</s>), a quality dependent on substance (<s>dravyāśrita</s>), or the properties such as <s>sattva</s> (goodness), <s>śaurya</s> (valor), <s>sandhyā</s> (juncture), and the like.
(3.3.439) <s>Kṣaṇa</s> means leisure or freedom from occupation (<s>nirvyāpāra</s>), a state (<s>sthiti</s>), a particular time (<s>kālaviśeṣa</s>), or a festival (<s>utsava</s>).
(3.3.440) <s>Varṇa</s> means a social class such as <s>dvija</s> (twice-born), a color such as white, or praise (<s>stuti</s>); but <s>varṇa</s> in the neuter means a syllable (<s>akṣara</s>).
(3.3.441) <s>Aruṇa</s> also means the sun (<s>bhāskara</s>), and in all three genders it also means a particular color.
(3.3.442) <s>Sthāṇu</s> also means <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>). <s>Droṇa</s> also means a crow (<s>kāka</s>). In battle (<s>āji</s>) and in the sun (<s>ravi</s>), the word <s>raṇa</s> is used.
(3.3.443) <s>Grāmaṇī</s> in the masculine means a barber (<s>nāpita</s>) or the chief among men; in all three genders, it means a village headman (<s>grāmādhipa</s>).
(3.3.444) <s>Ūrṇā</s> means the wool of sheep and other animals, or the curl (<s>āvarta</s>) between the eyebrows.
(3.3.445) <s>Hariṇī</s> means a doe (<s>mṛgī</s>), a golden image (<s>hemapratimā</s>), or she who is green (<s>haritā</s>).
(3.3.446) In all three genders, <s>hariṇa</s> also means pale (<s>pāṇḍu</s>). <s>Sthūṇā</s> means a pillar (<s>stambha</s>) or a post of a house (<s>veśman</s>).
(3.3.447) <s>Tṛṣṇā</s> means desire (<s>spṛhā</s>) or thirst (<s>pipāsā</s>) — these are two meanings. <s>Ghṛṇā</s> means disgust (<s>jugupsā</s>) or compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>).
(3.3.448) <s>Vipaṇi</s> means a market (<s>vaṇikpatha</s>). <s>Vāruṇī</s> means liquor (<s>surā</s>) or the western direction (<s>pratyak</s>).
(3.3.449) <s>Kareṇu</s> in both genders means a female elephant; in the neuter, it means a particular tree. <s>Draviṇa</s> means strength (<s>bala</s>) or wealth (<s>dhana</s>).
(3.3.450) <s>Śaraṇa</s> means a house (<s>gṛha</s>) or a protector (<s>rakṣitṛ</s>). <s>Śrīparṇa</s> also means a lotus (<s>kamala</s>).
(3.3.451) <s>Tīkṣṇa</s> in the neuter means poison (<s>viṣa</s>), a curse (<s>abhimara</s>), or iron (<s>loha</s>); in all three genders it means sharp (<s>khara</s>).
(3.3.452) <s>Pramāṇa</s> means a means of valid knowledge (<s>hetu</s>), a standard (<s>maryādā</s>), a scripture (<s>śāstra</s>), extent (<s>iyattā</s>), or a knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>).
(3.3.453) <s>Karaṇa</s> means the most efficient instrument (<s>sādhakatama</s>), a field (<s>kṣetra</s>), a limb (<s>gātra</s>), or a sense organ (<s>indriya</s>).
(3.3.454) <s>Saṃsaraṇa</s> means the birth of a living being (<s>prāṇyutpāda</s>), an unobstructed passage, or the marching of an army.
(3.3.455) <s>Ghaṇṭāpatha</s> means a highway. <s>Samudgiraṇa</s> means vomited food (<s>vāntānna</s>) or elevation (<s>unnaya</s>).
(3.3.456) Hence, in all three genders, <s>viṣāṇa</s> means the horn of an animal (<s>paśuśṛṅga</s>) or the tusk of an elephant (<s>ibhadanta</s>).
(3.3.457) <s>Pravaṇa</s> means a slope (<s>kramanimna</s>) on the earth or one who is humble (<s>prahva</s>); but as a masculine noun, it means a crossroads (<s>catuṣpatha</s>).
(3.3.458) <s>Saṃkīrṇa</s> means mixed or impure (<s>aśuddha</s>). <s>Viriṇa</s> means empty (<s>śūnya</s>) or barren (<s>ūṣara</s>).
(3.3.459) <s>Caraṇa</s> also means a bridge (<s>setu</s>). <s>Veṇī</s> means a confluence of rivers (<s>nadībheda</s>) or a braid of hair (<s>kacoccaya</s>).
(3.3.460) Thus end the words ending in <s>ṇa</s>.
(3.3.461) <s>Deva</s> and <s>Sūrya</s> are both called <s>Vivasvat</s>. <s>Sarasvat</s> means both a river and an ocean.
(3.3.462) <s>Tārkṣya</s> as a bird and <s>Garutmat</s> both refer to <s>Garuḍa</s>. <s>Śakunta</s> means the bird <s>Bhāsa</s> or any bird in general.
(3.3.463) <s>Dhūmaketu</s> means fire (<s>agni</s>) or a calamity (<s>utpāta</s>). <s>Jīmūta</s> means a cloud (<s>megha</s>) or a mountain (<s>parvata</s>).
(3.3.464) <s>Hasta</s> means the hand (<s>pāṇi</s>) or the <s>Hasta</s> lunar mansion (<s>nakṣatra</s>). <s>Marut</s> means the wind (<s>pavana</s>) or a god (<s>amara</s>).
(3.3.465) <s>Yantṛ</s> means an elephant driver (<s>hastipaka</s>) or a charioteer (<s>sūta</s>). <s>Bhartṛ</s> means a sustainer (<s>dhātṛ</s>) or a nourisher (<s>poṣṭṛ</s>).
(3.3.466) <s>Pota</s> means a vessel for travel (<s>yānapātra</s>) or a young animal (<s>śiśu</s>). <s>Preta</s> means another living being or one who has died (<s>mṛta</s>).
(3.3.467) <s>Ketu</s> means a particular planet (<s>grahabheda</s>) or a flag (<s>dhvaja</s>). <s>Suta</s> means one born of the earth (<s>pārthiva</s>) or a son (<s>tanaya</s>).
(3.3.468) <s>Sthapati</s> also means a type of artisan (<s>kārubheda</s>). <s>Bhūbhṛt</s> means a mountain (<s>bhūmidhara</s>) or a king (<s>nṛpa</s>).
(3.3.469) <s>Mūrdhābhiṣikta</s> also means a king (<s>bhūpa</s>). <s>Ṛtu</s> in the feminine means a season or also a flower (<s>kusuma</s>).
(3.3.470) <s>Ajita</s> and <s>Avyakta</s> also refer to <s>Viṣṇu</s>. <s>Sūta</s> means <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> (the divine craftsman) or a charioteer (<s>sārathi</s>).
(3.3.471) <s>Vyakta</s> means a wise person (<s>prājña</s>). <s>Dṛṣṭānta</s> — both meanings relate to a scriptural illustration (<s>śāstranidarśana</s>).
(3.3.472) <s>Kṣattṛ</s> means a charioteer (<s>sārathi</s>), a doorkeeper (<s>dvāḥstha</s>), or the offspring of a <s>Śūdra</s> father and a <s>Kṣatriya</s> mother.
(3.3.473) <s>Vṛttānta</s> means a subject matter (<s>prakaraṇa</s>), a manner (<s>prakāra</s>), completeness (<s>kārtsnya</s>), or news (<s>vārtā</s>).
(3.3.474) <s>Ānarta</s> means a battle (<s>samara</s>), a dancing stage (<s>nṛtyasthāna</s>), or a type of garment (<s>nīvṛdviśeṣa</s>).
(3.3.475) <s>Kṛtānta</s> means <s>Yama</s> (god of death), an established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>), fate (<s>daiva</s>), or misfortune (<s>akuśalakarma</s>).
(3.3.476) The <s>dhātus</s> (bodily constituents) include <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm) and so forth, <s>rasa</s> (chyle) and <s>rakta</s> (blood) and so forth, the great elements (<s>mahābhūtāni</s>), and their qualities (<s>guṇāḥ</s>),

(3.3.480) vistāra vallayor vratatir vasatī rātriveśmanoḥ
(3.3.481) kṣayārcayorapacitiḥ sātir dānāvasānayoḥ ||
children.translated_text:
(3.3.480) <s>Vistāra</s> and <s>vallī</s> — <s>vratati</s> means both. <s>Vasatī</s> means the night (<s>rātri</s>) or a house (<s>veśman</s>).
(3.3.481) <s>Apaciti</s> means decline (<s>kṣaya</s>) or worship (<s>arcā</s>). <s>Sāti</s> means giving (<s>dāna</s>) or conclusion (<s>avasāna</s>).

(3.3.859) cānvācayasamāhāretaretarasamuccaye
(3.3.860) svastyāśīḥ kṣemapuṇyādau prakarṣe laṅghane 'pyati
(3.3.861) svitpraśne ca vitarke ca tu syādbhede 'vadhāraṇe
(3.3.862) sakṛt sahaikavāre cāpyārāddūrasamīpayoḥ
(3.3.863) pratīcyāṃ carame paścādutāpyarthavikalpayoḥ
(3.3.864) punassahārthayoḥ śaśvat sākṣātpratyakṣatulyayoḥ
(3.3.865) khedānukampāsaṃtoṣavismayāmantraṇe bata
(3.3.866) hanta harṣenukampāyāṃ vākyārambhaviṣādayoḥ
(3.3.867) prati pratinidhau vīpsālakṣaṇādau prayogataḥ
(3.3.868) iti hetuprakaraṇaprakarṣādisamāptiṣu
(3.3.869) prācyāṃ purastātprathame purārthe 'grata ityapi
(3.3.870) yāvattāvacca sākalye 'vadhau māne 'vadhāraṇe
(3.3.871) maṅgalānantarārambhapraśnakārtsnyeṣvatho atha
(3.3.872) vṛthā nirarthakāvidhyor nānānekobhayārthayoḥ
(3.3.873) nu pṛcchāyāṃ vikalpe ca paścātsādṛśyayoranu
(3.3.874) praśnāvadhāraṇānujñānunayāmantraṇe nanu
(3.3.875) garhāsamuccayapraśnaśaṅkāsaṃbhāvanāsvapi
(3.3.876) upamāyāṃ vikalpe vā sāmi tvardhe jugupsite
(3.3.877) amā saha samīpe ca kaṃ vāriṇi ca mūrdhani
(3.3.878) ivetthamarthayorevaṃ nūnaṃ tarke 'rthaniścaye
(3.3.879) tūṣṇīmarthe sukhe joṣaṃ kiṃ pṛcchāyāṃ jugupsane
(3.3.880) nāma prākāśyasaṃbhāvyakrodhopagamakutsane
(3.3.881) alaṃ bhūṣaṇaparyāptiśaktivāraṇavācakam

(3.3.884) syātprabandhe cirātīte nikaṭāgāmike purā
(3.3.885) ūraryūrī corarī ca vistāre 'ṅgīkṛtau trayam
(3.3.886) svarge pare ca loke svar vārtāsaṃbhāvyayoḥ kila
(3.3.887) niṣedhavākyālaṅkārajijñāsānunaye khalu
(3.3.888) samīpobhayataśśīghrasākalyābhimukhe 'bhitaḥ
(3.3.889) nāmaprākāśyayoḥ pradur mitho 'nyonyaṃ rahasyapi
(3.3.890) tiro 'ntardhau tiryagarthe hā viṣādaśugartiṣu

children.translated_text:
(3.3.482) <s>Ārti</s> means pain and the tip of a bow. <s>Jāti</s> means genus and birth.
(3.3.483) <s>Rīti</s> means flow and going forth. <s>Ītir</s> means a plague and sojourning abroad.
(3.3.484) <s>Prāpti</s> means rising and attainment. <s>Tretā</s> means the three sacred fires and a <s>yuga</s> (age).
(3.3.485) <s>Mahatī</s> means a type of <s>vīṇā</s> (lute) as well. <s>Bhūti</s> means ashes and prosperity.
(3.3.486) <s>Bhogavatī</s> means a river and a city of the <s>Nāgas</s> (serpent-beings). Then, in battle—
(3.3.487) <s>Samiti</s> means an encounter, an assembly. <s>Kṣitī</s> means destruction and a dwelling as well.
(3.3.488) <s>Hetayaḥ</s> (the plural of <s>heti</s>) means the rays of the sun, a weapon, and the flame of fire.
(3.3.489) <s>Jagatī</s> means the world, a particular metre, and also the earth.
(3.3.490) <s>Paṅkti</s> means a metre as well as a row of ten. <s>Āyati</s> means influence and also the future.
(3.3.491) <s>Patti</s> means going and also a root. <s>Pakṣati</s> means a wing and a fortnight.
(3.3.492) <s>Prakṛti</s> means origin and grammatical base. <s>Vṛttayaḥ</s> such as <s>Kaiśikī</s> and others are dramatic styles.
(3.3.493) <s>Sikatāḥ</s> means sand. <s>Śruti</s> means the <s>Veda</s> and also the ear.
(3.3.494) <s>Vanitā</s> means a woman in whom intense love has been born, and also a woman in general.
(3.3.495) <s>Gupti</s> means concealment and also the earth. <s>Dhṛti</s> means holding and firmness.
(3.3.496) <s>Bṛhatī</s> means the small eggplant, a particular metre, and also something great.
(3.3.497) <s>Vāsitā</s> means a woman and a female elephant. <s>Vārtā</s> means livelihood and common report.
(3.3.498) <s>Vārta</s> (neuter) means healthy and free from disease; in the plural it means water, ghee, and nectar.
(3.3.499) <s>Kaladhautam</s> means silver and gold. <s>Nimittam</s> means cause and sign.
(3.3.500) <s>Śrutam</s> means sacred text and that which is ascertained. <s>Kṛtam</s> means an age and completion.
(3.3.501) <s>Atyāhitam</s> means great danger and also an action not caring for life.
(3.3.502) <s>Bhūtam</s> means what is combined, the earth, what is past, a living being, what is gone, and equal — used in all three genders.
(3.3.503) <s>Vṛttam</s> means verse-metre and conduct; in all three genders it means past, firm, and level ground.
(3.3.504) <s>Mahat</s> means a kingdom as well. <s>Avagītam</s> means censured; in all three genders it means blameworthy.
(3.3.505) <s>Rajatam</s> means silver; in the neuter it also means white. <s>Hemni rūpye site triṣu</s> — used for gold, silver, and white in all three genders.
(3.3.506) In all three genders beyond this: <s>raktam</s> means the world, a vowel, what is dyed, and having an attachment to indigo and the like.
(3.3.507) <s>Avadāta</s> means white, yellow, and pure. <s>Baddha</s> and <s>Arjuna</s> both mean white.
(3.3.508) <s>Abhinīta</s> means skilled, refined, and impatient. Then <s>saṃskṛtam</s>—
(3.3.509) means artificial and endowed with distinguishing marks. <s>Ananta</s> means also infinite and without limit.
(3.3.510) <s>Pratīta</s> means famous and joyful. <s>Abhijāta</s> means of noble birth and wise.
(3.3.511) <s>Vivikta</s> means both pure and solitary. <s>Mūrchita</s> means both stupefied and expanded.
(3.3.512) The pair <s>amla</s> (sour) and <s>paruṣa</s> (harsh) apply to <s>śukta</s> (vinegar). <s>Śitī</s> means white and dark.
(3.3.513) <s>Sat</s> means true, virtuous, existing, excellent, and worthy.
(3.3.514) <s>Puraskṛta</s> means honoured and placed before an enemy; also means appointed and placed in front.
(3.3.515) <s>Nivāta</s> means both sheltered and windless. That armour which is impenetrable by weapons is called <s>varma</s>.
(3.3.516) <s>Jāta</s>, <s>unnaddha</s>, and <s>pravṛddha</s> mean arisen, swollen, and grown. <s>Ucchrita</s> and <s>utthita</s> mean these as well.
(3.3.517) <s>Vṛddhimat</s>, <s>prodyata</s>, and <s>utpanna</s> mean prosperous, risen, and born. <s>Ādṛta</s> means both respectful and worshipped.
(3.3.518) <s>Jāta</s> applies to a multitude and to what is born. <s>Mahījit</s>, <s>Śrīpati</s>, and <s>Indra</s>—
(3.3.519) <s>Prapāta</s> means a precipice and also a nocturnal attack. <s>Avapāta</s> and <s>avaṭa</s> mean a cliff and a pit.
(3.3.520) <s>Samit</s> (feminine) means an encounter and battle. <s>Sthiti</s> means stability and also arrangement.
(3.3.521) <s>Artha</s> means signified meaning, wealth, thing, purpose, and cessation.
(3.3.522) <s>Tīrtha</s> means a watering-place, an approach, a place frequented by sages, water, and a teacher.
(3.3.523) <s>Samartha</s> in all three genders means capable, connected in meaning, and also beneficial.
(3.3.524) Those in the tenth stage: <s>kṣīṇarāga</s> means one whose passions are spent, <s>vṛddha</s> means aged. <s>Vīthī</s> means a path as well.
(3.3.525) <s>Āsthā</s> means a seat and effort. <s>Prastha</s> (not feminine) means a plateau and a measure.
(3.3.526) <s>Grantha</s> means a treatise and wealth. <s>Saṃsthā</s> means a support, a state, and death.
(3.3.527) Thus end the <s>tha</s>-ending words.
(3.3.528) <s>Chanda</s> means intention and will. <s>Abda</s> means a cloud and a year.
(3.3.529) <s>Apavāda</s> means censure and knowledge. <s>Dāyāda</s> means a son and a kinsman.
(3.3.530) <s>Pāda</s> means a ray, a foot, and a quarter part. <s>Tamonuda</s> means the moon, fire, and the sun.
(3.3.531) <s>Nirvāda</s> means public talk as well. <s>Śāda</s> means mud and fresh grass.
(3.3.532) <s>Ākranda</s> means weeping, calling for help, something terrible, and battle.
(3.3.533) <s>Prasāda</s> means favour and also affection. <s>Sūda</s> means a cook and also a condiment.
(3.3.534) <s>Govinda</s> also means a chief herdsman. <s>Mada</s> means joy and also intoxication.
(3.3.535) <s>Kakuda</s> (not feminine) means pre-eminence, a royal insignia, and the hump of a bull.
(3.3.536) <s>Saṃvid</s> (feminine) means knowledge, conversation, an action, a form, a battle, and a name.
(3.3.537) <s>Upaniṣad</s> means sacred teaching and secret doctrine. <s>Śarat</s> means a season and also a year.
(3.3.538) <s>Padam</s> means a position, a word, protection, a place, a mark, a foot, and a thing.
(3.3.539) <s>Goṣpadam</s> means a place frequented. <s>Pratiṣṭhā</s>, <s>kṛtya</s>, and <s>āspadam</s> mean fame, duty, and a seat.
(3.3.540) In all three genders: <s>iṣṭa</s> and <s>madhura</s> both mean sweet. <s>Mṛdu</s> means both not sharp and soft.
(3.3.541) <s>Manda</s> means foolish, little, unskilled, and unfortunate; the pair however means autumnal.
(3.3.542) <s>Viśārada</s> means both fresh and quick-witted, and also learned and very bold.
(3.3.543) Thus end the <s>da</s>-ending words.
(3.3.544) <s>Nyagrodha</s> means a banyan tree and a fathom. <s>Utsedha</s> means bodily height.
(3.3.545) <s>Vivadha</s> means both a transport-path and a road; <s>vīvadha</s> likewise.
(3.3.546) <s>Paridhi</s> means the branch of a sacrificial tree, a halo around the sun.
(3.3.547) <s>Ādhayaḥ</s> (the plural of <s>ādhi</s>) means bondage, misfortune, mental affliction, pain, and a foundation.
(3.3.548) <s>Samādhayaḥ</s> (the plural of <s>samādhi</s>) means justification, compensation, and a vow.
(3.3.549) <s>Anubandha</s> means a consequence of a fault, what is connected with the original, the beginning, and what is perishable.
(3.3.550) Also: a chief follower, a child, natural succession, and continuation.
(3.3.551) <s>Vidhu</s> means <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the moon. <s>Avadhi</s> means a limit, a hole.
(3.3.552) <s>Vidhi</s> means a rule and also fate. <s>Praṇidhi</s> means a prayer and a spy.
(3.3.553) <s>Budha</s> means the planet Mercury, an elder, and also a learned person. <s>Skandha</s> also means a multitude.
(3.3.554) <s>Sindhu</s> (masculine) means a country, a particular river, and the ocean; (feminine) it means a river.
(3.3.555) <s>Vidhā</s> means a mode and a kind. <s>Sādhu</s> in all three genders means good, pleasant.
(3.3.556) <s>Vadhū</s> means a wife, a daughter-in-law, and a woman. <s>Sudhā</s> means plaster, nectar, and the <s>snuhī</s> plant.
(3.3.557) <s>Sandhā</s> means a promise and a boundary. <s>Śraddhā</s> means faith, trust, and desire.
(3.3.558) <s>Madhu</s> means liquor, the juice of flowers, and honey. <s>Andham</s> means darkness as well.
(3.3.559) Hence in all three genders: <s>samunnaddha</s> means both conceited and arrogant.
(3.3.560) <s>Brahmabandhu</s> means reproach of a Brahmin; in the indicative sense, then <s>avalambita</s>—
(3.3.561) means not far and also firmly grasped. In renown: <s>khyāta</s> and <s>bhūṣita</s> both mean celebrated and adorned.
(3.3.562) <s>Gandha</s> means even a trace. <s>Saṃbādha</s> means both secret and crowded.
(3.3.563) <s>Bādhā</s> means prohibition and pain. <s>Budhāḥ</s> means kinsmen, those born under the moon, and the gods.
| Thus end the <s>dha</s>-ending words.
(3.3.564) <s>Citrabhānu</s> means the sun and fire. <s>Bhānu</s> means a ray and the sun.
(3.3.565) <s>Bhūtātman</s> means the soul and the body. <s>Pṛthagjana</s> means a fool and a low person.
(3.3.566) <s>Grāvāṇau</s> means a mountain and a stone. <s>Patriṇau</s> means an arrow and a bird.
(3.3.567) <s>Śikhariṇau</s> means a tree and a mountain. <s>Śikhinau</s> means fire and a peacock.
(3.3.568) <s>Pratiyatna</s> means both effort and desire. <s>Upagraha</s> means both.
(3.3.569) The pair <s>sādin</s> means a charioteer and a horseman. <s>Vājin</s> means a horse and also a bird.
(3.3.570) <s>Abhijana</s> means also a family. <s>Janma</s> means birth and also the earth.
(3.3.571) <s>Hāyana</s> means a year, a ray, and a type of rice. <s>Virocana</s> means the moon, fire, and the sun.
(3.3.572) <s>Vṛjina</s> also means hair. <s>Viśvakarman</s> means the sun and the divine architect of the gods.
(3.3.573) <s>Ātman</s> means the self, effort, firmness, intellect, nature, <s>Brahman</s> (the Absolute), and the body.
(3.3.574) <s>Śakra</s> means a slayer, a maddened elephant. <s>Varṣuka</s> means a year. <s>Ghana</s> and <s>aghana</s> mean a cloud.
(3.3.575) <s>Abhimāna</s> means pride in objects and the like, knowledge, love, and injury.
(3.3.576) <s>Ghana</s> means a cloud and a quality of solidity; in all three genders it means solid and uninterrupted.
(3.3.577) <s>Ina</s> means the sun, a lord, and a king. <s>Rājan</s> means the moon, a <s>Kṣatriya</s> (warrior), and a king.
(3.3.578) <s>Vāṇī</s> (dual) means a dancing-girl and a messenger-woman. <s>Vāhinī</s> means also a river.
(3.3.579) <s>Hlādinī</s> (dual) means a thunderbolt and lightning. <s>Kāminī</s> means also a worshipping woman.
(3.3.580) <s>Tanu</s> means skin and body. <s>Sūnā</s> means a slaughter-house and also the tongue.
(3.3.581) <s>Vitānam</s> (not feminine) means a sacrifice and an expanse; in all three genders it means worthless.
(3.3.582) And slow. Then <s>ketanam</s> means an act; <s>ketu</s> means a banner and an invitation.
(3.3.583) <s>Brahman</s> means the <s>Veda</s>, truth, <s>tapas</s> (austerity); <s>Brahmā</s> means the creator-god, a Brahmin, and <s>Prajāpati</s> (lord of creatures).
(3.3.584) <s>Gandhanam</s> means also exertion, injury, and informing.
(3.3.585) <s>Ātañcanam</s> means a flavoring addition, and also running and refreshing.
(3.3.586) <s>Vyañjanam</s> means a mark, a moustache, and also limbs; <s>niṣṭhā</s> means ending and completion.
(3.3.587) <s>Kaulīnam</s> means public talk and also a fight among cattle, snakes, and birds.
(3.3.588) <s>Udyānam</s> means going out, a type of garden, and also a purpose.
(3.3.589) <s>Sthānam</s> means an open space, a position. <s>Devanam</s> means play and the like.
(3.3.590) <s>Vyutthānam</s> means opposition and also departing from proper conduct.
(3.3.591) <s>Utthānam</s> means enterprise, independence, rising from an assembled position, and also arising.
(3.3.592) <s>Sādhanam</s> means killing, funeral rites for the dead, going, substance, producing wealth,
(3.3.593) accomplishment, means, instruments, and following as well.
(3.3.594) <s>Niryātanam</s> means revenge, giving, returning a deposit, and also offering.
(3.3.595) <s>Vyasanam</s> means calamity, downfall, a fault, and passion born of desire or anger.
(3.3.596) <s>Pakṣman</s> means an eyelash, a filament, and also a thread; also means something very fine.
(3.3.597) <s>Parvan</s> means a division of a lunar month, a moment. <s>Vartman</s> means an eyelid and a road.
(3.3.598) <s>Kaupīnam</s> means a shameful secret and a loincloth. <s>Maithunam</s> means union and sexual intercourse.
(3.3.599) <s>Pradhānam</s> means the supreme self and the intellect. <s>Prajñānam</s> means wisdom and a mark.
(3.3.600) <s>Prasūnam</s> means a flower and a fruit. <s>Nidhanam</s> means a family and destruction.
(3.3.601) <s>Krandanam</s> means crying and calling out. <s>Varṣman</s> means the body and its measure.
(3.3.602) <s>Dhāma</s> means a house, a body, splendour, and power. Also at a crossroads—
(3.3.603) and a settlement: <s>saṃsthānam</s> means form. <s>Lakṣman</s> means a mark and what is chief.
(3.3.604) <s>Saṃvidhānam</s> and <s>apavāraṇam</s> both mean covering and arranging.
(3.3.605) <s>Ārādhanam</s> means accomplishment, attainment, and also pleasing.
(3.3.606) <s>Adhiṣṭhānam</s> means a governing seat, a chariot, a city, authority, and a throne.
(3.3.607) <s>Ratnam</s> means the best of its kind. <s>Vanam</s> means water and a forest.
(3.3.608) <s>Talinam</s> means thin and small — used in its expressed gender; likewise <s>uttaram</s>.
(3.3.609) <s>Samānāḥ</s> means equal and alike. <s>Piśuna</s> means both a rogue and an informer.
(3.3.610) <s>Hīna</s> and <s>nyūna</s> mean deficient. <s>Ūna</s> means deficient and contemptible. <s>Tarasvin</s> means swift and brave.
(3.3.611) <s>Abhipanna</s> means one who has transgressed, one who is afflicted, and one who has met with misfortune.
| Thus end the <s>na</s>-ending words.
(3.3.612) <s>Kalāpa</s> means an ornament, a peacock's tail, a quiver, and a collection.
(3.3.613) <s>Parīvāpa</s> means a covering, sowing, and staying in water.
(3.3.614) <s>Gopa</s> (dual) means a milker of cows and a lord of cowherds. <s>Vṛṣākapī</s> (dual) means <s>Hara</s> (Shiva) and <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
(3.3.615) <s>Bāṣpa</s> means steam and tears. <s>Kaśipu</s> means food and clothing — both as a pair.
(3.3.616) <s>Talpam</s> means a bed, a turret, and wives. <s>Viṭapa</s> (not feminine) means also a bush.
(3.3.617) <s>Prāptarūpa</s>, <s>svarūpa</s>, and <s>abhirūpa</s> mean wise and handsome.
(3.3.618) These are of variable gender: <s>kūrmī</s> means a female tortoise, and <s>kacchapī</s> means a type of <s>vīṇā</s> (lute).
(3.3.619) <s>Kutapa</s> means a blanket made of deer-hair, and also the eighth part of the day.
| Thus end the <s>pa</s>-ending words.
(3.3.620) <s>Śiphā</s> means a crest, a river, a muscular woman, and a mother.
(3.3.621) <s>Śapham</s> means the root of trees and also the hoof of cattle and the like.
(3.3.622) <s>Gulpha</s> means an ankle-joint, a bracelet of the arm, and is also an ornament.
(3.3.623) <s>Repha</s> (masculine) means the letter 'ra'; in a contemptuous sense it is used in any gender.
| Thus end the <s>pha</s>-ending words.
(3.3.624) <s>Gandharva</s> means an intermediate being, a horse, and a divine musician.
(3.3.625) <s>Kambu</s> (masculine) means a bracelet and a conch. <s>Dvijihva</s> (dual) means a serpent and an informer.
(3.3.626) <s>Pūrva</s> is of variable gender; it means eastern and prior. In the masculine plural it also means ancestors.
(3.3.627) <s>Kādamba</s> means also a variegated arrow. <s>Nitamba</s> means a mountain-slope and the hip.
(3.3.628) <s>Darvī</s> also means a serpent's hood. <s>Bimba</s> (not feminine) means also a disc.
| Thus end the <s>ba</s>-ending words.
(3.3.629) <s>Kumbha</s> (dual) means a pot and the frontal globe of an elephant. <s>Ḍimbha</s> (dual) means a child and a fool.
(3.3.630) <s>Stambha</s> (dual) means a pillar and stupefaction. <s>Śambhu</s> (dual) means <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Trilocana</s> (three-eyed <s>Śiva</s>).
(3.3.631) <s>Garbha</s> means the belly, a foetus, and a child. <s>Visrambha</s> also means affection.
(3.3.632) <s>Dundubhi</s> (masculine) means a kettledrum; <s>dundubhi</s> (feminine) means a die.
(3.3.633) <s>Kusumbha</s> (neuter) means great silver; <s>kusumbha</s> (masculine) means a water-pot.
