(3.3.811) <s>Dhvāṅkṣa</s> (dual) means a crow and a fish-eating bird. <s>Kakṣa</s> means also grass and a creeper.
(3.3.812) <s>Abhīpu</s> means a rein and a ray. <s>Praiṣa</s> means a command and a punishment.
(3.3.813) <s>Pakṣa</s> also means an ally. <s>Uṣṇīṣa</s> means a turban and a crown.
(3.3.814) <s>Vṛṣa</s> means semen, a rat, the best, meritorious, and a bull.
(3.3.815) <s>Kośa</s> (not feminine) means a bud, a sword-sheath, a treasury of wealth, and a lexicon.
(3.3.816) <s>Ākarṣa</s> means in gambling, a die, and a game-board. Then <s>akṣa</s> means a sense-organ;
(3.3.817) as masculine it means a die in a game, a weight measure, a wheel, a legal proceeding, and the <s>kali</s> tree.
(3.3.818) <s>Karṣū</s> means a report. <s>Karīṣāgni</s> means a dung-fire. <s>Karṣa</s> means a measure called <s>kulyā</s>.
(3.3.819) <s>Pauruṣam</s> means manhood and also its associated activity; <s>viṣam</s> also means water.
(3.3.820) <s>Āmiṣam</s> also means a bribe. <s>Kilbiṣam</s> also means an offence.
(3.3.821) <s>Varṣam</s> (not feminine) means rain, a region, the earth, and a year.
(3.3.822) <s>Prekṣā</s> means a dance, seeing, and wisdom. <s>Bhikṣā</s> means service, begging, and wages.
(3.3.823) <s>Tviṣ</s> also means beauty. In all three genders, <s>nyakṣam</s> means entirely and low.
(3.3.824) <s>Adhyakṣa</s> means perceptible and a superintendent. <s>Rūkṣa</s> means unkind and rough.
(3.3.825) <s>Lakṣam</s> means a pretext, a number, and a target. <s>Ghoṣa</s> (dual) means a sound and a herd.
(3.3.826) <s>Kapiśīrṣam</s> means a wall-top ornament. <s>Anutarṣa</s> means a cup and liquor.
(3.3.827) <s>Doṣa</s> means a bodily humour like wind and the like. <s>Doṣā</s> (feminine) means night. <s>Dakṣa</s> also means a rooster.
(3.3.828) <s>Gaṇḍūṣa</s> means the tip of an elephant's trunk; both meanings also include a mouthful.
| Thus end the <s>ṣa</s>-ending words.
(3.3.829) <s>Haṃsa</s> (dual) means the sun and a goose. <s>Vibhāvasu</s> (dual) means the sun and fire.
(3.3.830) <s>Vatsa</s> (dual) means a calf and a year. <s>Sāraṅga</s> means also the gods.
(3.3.831) <s>Rasa</s> means a dramatic sentiment, poison, potency, a quality, passion, and juice.
(3.3.832) <s>Uttaṃsa</s> and <s>avataṃsa</s> (dual, masculine) mean an ear-ornament and also a crest.
(3.3.833) <s>Vasu</s> means a divine being, fire, a ray; <s>vasu</s> (neuter) means a gem, wealth, and goods.
(3.3.834) <s>Vedhās</s> means <s>Viṣṇu</s> as well. <s>Āśīḥ</s> (feminine) means a blessing, a good wish, and a serpent's fang.
(3.3.835) Greed means desire and eagerness. <s>Hiṃsā</s> means injury and also acts like theft.
(3.3.836) <s>Prasū</s> also means a mare. <s>Bhū</s> and <s>dyau</s> — <s>rodasī</s> (dual) means heaven and earth.
(3.3.837) <s>Arcis</s> (not masculine) means a flame and light. <s>Jyotis</s> means a firefly and also sight.
(3.3.838) <s>Āgas</s> means sin and transgression. <s>Vayas</s> means a bird and also youth.
(3.3.839) <s>Varcas</s> means splendour and excrement. <s>Mahas</s> means a festival and brilliance.
(3.3.840) <s>Rajas</s> means a quality (of nature) and also menstrual blood. <s>Tamas</s> means <s>Rāhu</s>, darkness, and a quality.
(3.3.841) <s>Chandas</s> means a metre and also desire. <s>Tapas</s> means austerity and also severe penance.
(3.3.842) <s>Sahas</s> means strength. <s>Sahā</s> means a road. <s>Nabhas</s> means the sky and the month of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>. <s>Nabhāḥ</s> likewise.
(3.3.843) <s>Okas</s> means a house and a refuge. <s>Aukāḥ</s> as well. <s>Payas</s> means milk and also water.
(3.3.844) <s>Ojas</s> means lustre and strength. <s>Srotas</s> means a sense-organ and a river-course.
(3.3.845) <s>Tejas</s> means splendour, brilliance, strength, and semen — not feminine, in all three genders.
(3.3.846) <s>Vidvān</s> and <s>vidan</s> mean a learned person; <s>bībhatsa</s> means disgusting and cruel; also superlative in degree.
(3.3.847) <s>Jyāyān</s> means elder and more praiseworthy. <s>Kanīyān</s> means younger and smaller.
(3.3.848) <s>Varīyān</s> means wider and better. <s>Sādhīyān</s> means more virtuous and more intense.
| Thus end the <s>sa</s>-ending words.
(3.3.849) <s>Barham</s> also means a leaf. <s>Graha</s> means an obstinate hold, an eclipse, and planets like the sun.
(3.3.850) <s>Āpīḍa</s> means a door and a decoction. <s>Niryūha</s> means an elephant-tusk ornament.
(3.3.851) <s>Pragrāha</s> (also <s>pragraha</s>) means the string of a balance and a rein for horses.
(3.3.852) <s>Parigraha</s> means a wife, attendants, an acceptance, a root, and a curse.
(3.3.853) <s>Gṛha</s> in the plural also means wives. <s>Āroha</s> means the hip and also a noble woman.
(3.3.854) <s>Vyūha</s> also means a multitude. <s>Ahi</s> also means the demon <s>Vṛtra</s>. <s>Tamopaha</s> means the sun, fire, and the moon.
(3.3.855) <s>Paribarha</s> means a covering and a royal possession.
| Thus end the <s>ha</s>-ending words.
(3.3.856) The prefix <s>ā</s> means a little, an extent, a boundary, and is used in connection with verbal roots.
(3.3.857) <s>Ā</s> is considered an indeclinable particle; in speech also. <s>Āḥ</s> means anger and pain.
(3.3.858) <s>Ku</s> means sin, contempt, and a little. <s>Dhik</s> means censure and blame.
(3.3.859) <s>Ca</s> means addition, aggregation, mutual connection, and combination.
(3.3.860) <s>Svasti</s> means a blessing, welfare, and merit. <s>Ati</s> means excess and also transgression.
(3.3.861) <s>Svit</s> means a question and also a doubt. <s>Tu</s> means distinction and restriction.
(3.3.862) <s>Sakṛt</s> and <s>saha</s> mean once. <s>Ārāt</s> means both far and near.
(3.3.863) In the west and in the last: <s>paścāt</s>. <s>Utāpi</s> means an alternative proposition.
(3.3.864) <s>Punar</s> means also and again. <s>Śaśvat</s> means always. <s>Sākṣāt</s> means directly and equivalently.
(3.3.865) <s>Bata</s> expresses sorrow, compassion, satisfaction, surprise, and an address.
(3.3.866) <s>Hanta</s> means joy and compassion, and also the beginning of a sentence and despair.
(3.3.867) <s>Prati</s> means a substitute, distribution, a distinguishing mark, and is used by usage.
(3.3.868) <s>Iti</s> is used for cause, topic, emphasis, and conclusion.
(3.3.869) In the east, before, in the first, and in the sense of a city: <s>purastāt</s> and <s>agrataḥ</s> likewise.
(3.3.870) <s>Yāvat</s> and <s>tāvat</s> mean totality, a limit, a measure, and restriction.
(3.3.871) <s>Atho</s> and <s>atha</s> are used for auspiciousness, what follows, beginning, a question, and totality.
(3.3.872) <s>Vṛthā</s> means pointlessly and improperly. <s>Nānā</s> means many, both, and in both senses.
(3.3.873) <s>Nu</s> means a question and also an alternative. <s>Anu</s> after: means similarity.
(3.3.874) <s>Nanu</s> means a question, an ascertainment, a permission, a persuasion, and an address.
(3.3.875) Also censure, aggregation, a question, doubt, and possibility.
(3.3.876) In a comparison and an alternative, or <s>sāmi</s> means partially and in contempt.
(3.3.877) <s>Amā</s> means together and near. <s>Kam</s> means water and also the head.
(3.3.878) <s>Iva</s> means thus and in this manner. <s>Evam</s> likewise. <s>Nūnam</s> means in reasoning and in certainty.
(3.3.879) <s>Tūṣṇīm</s> means in sense and in comfort. <s>Joṣam</s> likewise. <s>Kim</s> means in a question and in contempt.
(3.3.880) <s>Nāma</s> means disclosure, possibility, anger, approach, and contempt.
(3.3.881) <s>Alam</s> expresses ornamentation, sufficiency, ability, and prohibition.
(3.3.882) <s>Hum</s> means deliberation and a counter-question. <s>Samaya</s> means nearness and the middle.
(3.3.883) <s>Punar</s> means again, at first, and in distinction. <s>Niḥ</s> means certainty and negation.
(3.3.884) <s>Purā</s> means in a narrative, long ago, and in the near past and near future.
(3.3.885) <s>Ūrari</s>, <s>ūrī</s>, and <s>corarī</s> — all three mean expansion and acceptance.
(3.3.886) <s>Svar</s> means heaven and the other world. <s>Kila</s> means rumour and possibility.
(3.3.887) <s>Khalu</s> is used in prohibition, a statement, an ornamental word, inquiry, and persuasion.
(3.3.888) <s>Abhitaḥ</s> means near, on both sides, quickly, entirely, and facing.
(3.3.889) <s>Pradur</s> means both name and disclosure. <s>Mithaḥ</s> means mutually and also secretly.
(3.3.890) <s>Tiraḥ</s> means concealment and in a crosswise direction. <s>Hā</s> expresses grief, danger, and pain.
(3.3.891) <s>Ahaha</s> expresses wonder and sorrow. <s>Hi</s> means a reason and an emphasis.
| Thus ends the <s>Nānārthavarga</s> (section on homonyms), the third section. Herein are 256 root verses.
End of the Homonyms Section, comprising 24 root verses.
The Section on Indeclinable Words (<s>avyayavarga</s>).

(3.4.892) '<s>cirāya</s>' (for a long time), '<s>cirarātrāya</s>' (for a long night), '<s>cirasya</s>' and others are synonymous with 'long duration.'
(3.4.893) '<s>muhuḥ</s>' (repeatedly), '<s>punaḥ punaḥ</s>' (again and again), '<s>śaśvat</s>' (perpetually), '<s>abhīkṣṇam</s>' (frequently), '<s>asakṛt</s>' (not once, i.e. repeatedly) are synonymous.
(3.4.894) '<s>srāk</s>' (at once), '<s>jhaṭiti</s>' (instantly), '<s>añjasā</s>' (directly), '<s>āhnāya</s>' (immediately), '<s>drāk</s>' (quickly), '<s>maṅkṣu</s>' (swiftly), '<s>sapadi</s>' (on the spot), '<s>drute</s>' (speedily) [are synonymous].
(3.4.895) '<s>balavat</s>' (strongly), '<s>suṣṭhu</s>' (well), '<s>kimuta</s>' (how much more), '<s>svati</s>', '<s>atīva</s>' (exceedingly) — these [mean] 'in excess.'
(3.4.896) '<s>pṛthak</s>' (separately), '<s>vinā</s>' (without), '<s>antareṇa</s>' (except) [mean] 'apart from'; '<s>hiruk</s>', '<s>nānā</s>' also [mean] 'exclusion.'
(3.4.897) '<s>yat</s>' (because), '<s>tat</s>' (therefore), '<s>yataḥ</s>' (whence), '<s>tataḥ</s>' (thence) [express] cause; but '<s>cit</s>' and '<s>cana</s>' [express] incompleteness.
(3.4.898) '<s>kadācit</s>' (sometimes) and '<s>jātu</s>' (ever) [are synonymous]. '<s>sārdham</s>' (together with), '<s>sākam</s>' (along with), '<s>satrā</s>' (jointly), '<s>samam</s>' (equally), '<s>saha</s>' (with) [are synonymous].
(3.4.899) '<s>prādhvam</s>' [means] 'in a favorable manner.' For uselessness: '<s>vṛthā</s>' (in vain) and '<s>mudhā</s>' (fruitlessly).
(3.4.900) '<s>āho</s>' (or), '<s>utāho</s>' (or else), '<s>kimuta</s>' (whether) [express] alternative; '<s>kim</s>' (what) and '<s>kimūta</s>' also.
(3.4.901) '<s>tu</s>', '<s>hi</s>', '<s>ca</s>', '<s>sma</s>', '<s>ha</s>', '<s>vai</s>' [are used as] metrical fillers (<s>pādapūraṇa</s>). '<s>svati</s>' [is used] in honoring.
(3.4.902) '<s>divā</s>' [means] 'by day'; then '<s>doṣā</s>' and '<s>naktam</s>' both [mean] 'at night.'
(3.4.903) '<s>sāci</s>' and '<s>tiraḥ</s>' [mean] 'crosswise' or 'sideways.' Then, [words] meaning 'address' or 'vocative':
(3.4.904) '<s>pyāṭ</s>', '<s>pāṭ</s>', '<s>aṅga</s>', '<s>he</s>', '<s>hai</s>', '<s>bhoḥ</s>' [are exclamations of address]. '<s>samayā</s>' (near), '<s>nikaṣā</s>' (close by) — '<s>hiruk</s>' [means] 'near.'
(3.4.905) '<s>sahasā</s>' [means] 'unexpectedly.' '<s>puraḥ</s>' (in front), '<s>purataḥ</s>' (before), '<s>agrataḥ</s>' (ahead) [are synonymous].
(3.4.906) '<s>svāhā</s>' [is used when] offering oblations to the gods. '<s>śrauṣaṭ</s>', '<s>vauṣaṭ</s>', '<s>vaṣaṭ</s>' [are ritual exclamations]. '<s>svadhā</s>' [is the oblation call for ancestors].
(3.4.907) '<s>kiñcit</s>' (a little), '<s>īṣat</s>' (slightly), '<s>manāk</s>' (a bit) [mean] 'in small measure.' '<s>pretya</s>' (after death), '<s>amutra</s>' (in the other world), '<s>bhavāntare</s>' (in another life) [are synonymous].
(3.4.908) '<s>va</s>', '<s>vā</s>', '<s>yathā</s>', '<s>tathā</s>', '<s>iva</s>', '<s>evam</s>' [express] similarity. '<s>aho</s>' and '<s>hī</s>' [express] astonishment.
(3.4.909) '<s>tūṣṇīm</s>' and '<s>tūṣṇīkām</s>' [mean] 'in silence.' '<s>sadyaḥ</s>' (immediately), '<s>sapadi</s>' (at once), '<s>tatkṣaṇe</s>' (that very moment) [are synonymous].
(3.4.910) '<s>diṣṭyā</s>' (by good fortune) and '<s>samupajoṣam</s>' [express] joy. Then '<s>antare</s>' (between) and '<s>antarā</s>' (in the midst),
(3.4.911) '<s>antareṇa</s>' (in between) — these [mean] 'in the middle.' '<s>prasahya</s>' [means] 'forcibly' (<s>haṭhārthakam</s>).
(3.4.912) '<s>sāmpratam</s>' [means] both 'at the present time' and 'fittingly.' '<s>abhīkṣṇam</s>' (frequently) and '<s>śaśvat</s>' (constantly) [mean] 'without cessation.'
(3.4.913) '<s>na</s>' (not), '<s>hi</s>', '<s>no</s>' (nor), '<s>na api</s>' (not even) [express] absence. '<s>mā</s>' (don't), '<s>sma</s>', '<s>mā alam</s>' (enough!) also [express] prohibition.
(3.4.914) '<s>ced</s>' (if) and '<s>yadi</s>' [express] an alternative condition. '<s>tu</s>' and '<s>addhā</s>' — both [express] truth. '<s>añjasā</s>' [means] 'directly.'
(3.4.915) '<s>prādur</s>' and '<s>āviḥ</s>' [mean] 'manifestly.' '<s>om</s>' and '<s>evam</s>' [mean] 'so be it' — [expressing] agreement. '<s>paramam</s>' [means] 'excellent' — [expressing] approval.
(3.4.916) '<s>samantataḥ</s>' (on all sides), '<s>paritaḥ</s>' (around), '<s>sarvataḥ</s>' (everywhere), '<s>viṣvak</s>' (in all directions) [are synonymous].
(3.4.917) '<s>kāmam</s>' [expresses] unwilling assent. '<s>asūya</s>' [expresses] grudging acceptance — these [take] '<s>tu</s>' and '<s>ca</s>' [as particles].
(3.4.918) '<s>nanu</s>' and '<s>ca</s>' [express] contradiction or objection. '<s>kaścit</s>' and '<s>kāma</s>' [express] disclosure of desire.
(3.4.919) '<s>niḥṣamam</s>' and '<s>duḥṣamam</s>' [express] censure. '<s>yathāsvam</s>' [means] 'each according to his own,' and '<s>yathāyatham</s>' [means] 'as appropriate.'
(3.4.920) '<s>mṛṣā</s>' (falsely) and '<s>mithyā</s>' (wrongly) [express] untruth. '<s>yathārtham</s>' [means] 'truly,' and '<s>yathātatham</s>' [means] 'according to fact.'
(3.4.921) '<s>evam</s>' (thus), '<s>tu</s>', '<s>punar</s>' (again), '<s>vai</s>', '<s>vā</s>' — these are emphatic particles (<s>avadhāraṇavācakāḥ</s>).
(3.4.922) '<s>prāk</s>' [means] 'in the past.' '<s>nūnam</s>' (certainly) and '<s>avaśyam</s>' (inevitably) — both [express] certainty.
(3.4.923) '<s>saṃvat</s>' [means] 'year.' '<s>avare</s>' [means] 'hither' — '<s>arvāk</s>' (on this side) and '<s>ā</s>' (up to). '<s>evam</s>' (thus), '<s>svayam</s>' (oneself), '<s>ātmanā</s>' (by oneself) [are synonymous].
(3.4.924) '<s>nīcaiḥ</s>' [means] 'in small measure'; '<s>uccaiḥ</s>' [means] 'in great measure.' '<s>prāyaḥ</s>' (mostly) [expresses] abundance. '<s>adrute</s>' [means] 'not quickly,' i.e. '<s>śanaiḥ</s>' (slowly).
(3.4.925) '<s>sanā</s>' [means] 'always.' '<s>bahiḥ</s>' [means] 'outside.' '<s>sma</s>' [expresses] past tense. '<s>astam</s>' [means] 'disappearance' or 'setting.'
(3.4.926) '<s>asti</s>' [expresses] existence. '<s>ruṣā</s>' [expresses] 'in anger.' '<s>uktau</s>' [means] 'in speech.' '<s>ūm</s>' [is used] in questioning. '<s>anunaye</s>' [means] 'in conciliation.' '<s>tvayi</s>' [means] 'in you.'
(3.4.927) '<s>hum</s>' [expresses] deliberation. '<s>uṣā</s>' [means] 'at dawn.' '<s>rātreḥ</s>' [means] 'of the night.' '<s>avasāne</s>' [means] 'at the end.' '<s>namaḥ</s>' [means] 'obeisance' — [used] in bowing.
(3.4.928) '<s>punar</s>' [means] 'again.' '<s>aṅga</s>' [expresses] censure. '<s>duṣṭhu</s>' [means] 'badly.' '<s>suṣṭhu</s>' [means] 'well' — [used] in praising.
(3.4.929) '<s>sāyam</s>' [means] 'in the evening.' '<s>sāye</s>' [is a variant]. '<s>prage</s>' and '<s>prātaḥ</s>' [mean] 'in the morning.' '<s>prabhāte</s>' [means] 'at dawn.' '<s>nikaṣā</s>' [means] 'nearby.'
(3.4.930) '<s>amā</s>' [means] 'together' or 'at home.' '<s>nuguṇye</s>' [means] 'in accordance.' '<s>smaraṇe</s>' [means] 'in remembrance.' '<s>hum phaṭ</s>' [is used for] dispelling obstacles.
(3.4.931) '<s>aṅgīkṛtau</s>' [means] 'in acceptance.' '<s>arthe</s>' [means] 'in meaning.' '<s>hūm</s>' [expresses agreement]. '<s>hīna</s>' [means] 'inferior.' '<s>saṃbodhate</s>' [means] 'in addressing.' '<s>tvare</s>' [means] 'in haste.'
(3.4.932) '<s>parut</s>' [means] 'last year.' '<s>parārtha</s>' [means] 'the year before.' '<s>eṣamaḥ</s>' [means] 'this year.' '<s>abde</s>' [means] 'in the year.' '<s>pūrve</s>' [means] 'in the former.' '<s>pūrvatare</s>' [means] 'in the earlier.' '<s>yati</s>' [is a suffix].
(3.4.933) '<s>adya</s>' [means] 'today.' '<s>atra ahni</s>' [means] 'on this day.' Then the terms for the previous and following days, from '<s>pūrva</s>' (former) and '<s>uttara</s>' (later) and '<s>apara</s>' (other):
(3.4.934) likewise '<s>adhara</s>' (lower) and '<s>anya</s>' (another) and '<s>itara</s>' (the other) and '<s>atara</s>' (another) — from '<s>pūrvedyuḥ</s>' and so on [are formed the terms for relative days].
(3.4.935) '<s>ubhayadyuḥ</s>' and '<s>ubhayedyuḥ</s>' [mean] 'on both days.' '<s>pare</s>' [means] 'on the next day' — '<s>paredyavi</s>' [is its form].
(3.4.936) '<s>hyaḥ</s>' [refers to] the past day; '<s>śvaḥ</s>' [refers to] the coming day. '<s>paraśvaḥ</s>' [means] 'the day after tomorrow' — literally 'on the further day.'
(3.4.937) '<s>tadā</s>' (then), '<s>tadānīm</s>' (at that time), '<s>yugapat</s>' (simultaneously), '<s>ekadā</s>' (once), '<s>sarvadā</s>' (always), '<s>sadā</s>' (ever) [are synonymous time-words].
(3.4.938) '<s>etarhi</s>' (now), '<s>samprati</s>' (at present), '<s>idānīm</s>' (now), '<s>adhunā</s>' (currently), '<s>sāmpratam</s>' (presently) — likewise [are synonymous].
(3.4.939) For direction, place, and time, the prefixes '<s>pūrva</s>' (east/before) etc. [produce]: '<s>prāk</s>' (eastward/before), '<s>udak</s>' (northward), '<s>pratyak</s>' (westward) and so on.
